abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gently and carefully evening out dental flaws for a carefree smile

bloecke.text: A radiant smile exudes vitality and draws people towards us. Yet straight, even, white teeth are often a rarity. Life leaves its marks on our teeth too. The result can be worn or chipped teeth, gaps, misaligned teeth or teeth that appear too short. Discolouration, damage and misalignment can cloud the first impression. With dental veneers from KU64 Berlin, you can conceal these flaws and give your teeth a new shine along with a natural look.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers: wafer-thin facings for aesthetically beautiful teeth

bloecke.text: Veneers, also known as facings, are wafer-thin ceramic or composite shells that the dentist bonds onto the front teeth or the side of the dentition. This conceals discolouration, unevenness or other flaws in the teeth, while the natural look of the tooth is preserved. The result is an even row of white teeth, without the unsightly metal margins seen with crowns.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Uses of veneers: small corrections for maximum results

bloecke.text: Discover the secret behind the Hollywood stars' radiant smiles. Beautiful white, healthy teeth are a dream that, nowadays, can become reality thanks to dental treatments with veneers.
These wafer-thin facings are the ideal solution to simply make the following aesthetic flaws in your teeth disappear:
tooth discolouration, for example from smoking, coffee, tea or red wine
damage from accidents, such as chipped tooth corners
a filling on the front teeth that repeatedly falls out
cracks in the front teeth
minor orthodontic corrections and misaligned teeth, such as crooked teeth
gaps caused by teeth that are set too far apart
short teeth, for example due to grinding
unattractive tooth shapes and deformities
metal-coloured margins on crowns and bridges
rough tooth surfaces due to damaged enamel

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which types of veneers does KU64 Berlin offer?

bloecke.text: Depending on the type of dental correction, KU64 Berlin uses different veneers, which differ in their method of application, thickness and material. In a personal consultation, we discuss together which veneers are suited to your dental correction. As a KU64 patient, you can choose from the following types of veneer:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prep veneers

bloecke.text: Most of our patients opt for prep veneers. Prep veneers are up to one millimetre thick and are permanently bonded to the tooth. For this, the tooth surface is prepared and the enamel is reduced. A temporary then protects the tooth being treated until the dentist fits the final facing at a further appointment. For the temporary provision, we use composite veneers made of resin. Prep veneers offer excellent durability and can be worn for 10 to 20 years.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Non-prep veneers

bloecke.text: Compared with conventional veneers, non-prep veneers require no grinding of the tooth surface. The roughly 0.3-millimetre-thick transparent facings are bonded directly onto the tooth surface using a special adhesive. Instead of grinding, only a professional clean beforehand is necessary. Local anaesthetic and a temporary are also not required. Fitting non-prep veneers is completely painless and poses no risk to the teeth. This is why they are often used for children with dental injuries. Non-prep veneers last on average 5 to 15 years before your dentist needs to replace them.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Lumineers

bloecke.text: A well-known type of non-prep veneer is Lumineers, manufactured in the USA. Lumineers are made from Cerinate, a patented ceramic. Compared with other non-prep veneers, Lumineers offer above all the advantage of a brand system proven over many years, with very thin ceramic shells and a firmly defined manufacturing process in specialised laboratories, which allows for a high degree of predictability in aesthetics and fit.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers-to-Go: the fast route to a Hollywood smile

bloecke.text: Veneers-to-Go, also known as instant veneers, are the ideal solution for a quick aesthetic dental correction. Veneers-to-Go are made of composite and require only one appointment. Up to ten veneers per jaw can be fitted within an hour. Unlike conventional prep veneers, Veneers-to-Go are not custom-made. This means the colour and shape of the veneers cannot be individually matched to the patient's tooth. They generally last 5 to 8 years.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: New at KU64: injectable veneers without grinding

bloecke.text: Improving the look of your front teeth has never been as simple as it now is at KU64 – thanks to the Flowable Injection Technique. Also known as injectable veneers, these are a novel method of enhancing teeth, offered by only a few dentists.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are injectable veneers suited to?

bloecke.text: Injectable veneers can be used to treat a wide range of aesthetic dental issues. These include brightening naturally dark tooth colour, unevenness in tooth shape, closing gaps between teeth and treating minor fractures in the front teeth. They offer a quick, painless alternative to ceramic or composite veneers and require no grinding, anaesthetic or painkillers.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Precise shaping using a template instead of laborious layering

bloecke.text: Conventional ceramic veneers are painstakingly layered from ceramic by dental technicians. Composite veneers, too, require laborious modelling by the dentist. By contrast, injectable veneers using the Flowable Injection Technique are injected onto the teeth in a stable shape via a template. A special resin designed specifically for this technique (reinforced with a high proportion of ceramic) is used. It is available in various colours and shades to allow a perfect match to the natural tooth colour. In most cases, there is no need to grind the teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How does treatment with injectable veneers proceed?

bloecke.text: After the initial consultation, the dental technician produces a perfectly aesthetic, well-fitting wax model in the form of a template, which the dentist uses for the injection technique. The template is filled with the special resin using special cannulas. The special resin is finished with a specially developed polish to guarantee the highest-quality aesthetic result!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Advantages of injectable veneers summarised:

bloecke.text: no grinding required (with few exceptions)
quick aesthetic result in a single appointment, using a robust special resin
more affordable than ceramic veneers (under 1,000 euros per tooth)
with good care and regular preventive check-ups, they generally last 5 to 6 years
repairs are possible without having to remake the entire veneer

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Proven quality: veneers made from ceramic or composite

bloecke.text: At KU64 in Berlin and Potsdam, you choose the material for your Hollywood smile that best suits your requirements. We offer you veneers made from full ceramic or composite. If you have any questions, the dentists at KU64 are happy to advise you in detail at a personal appointment on the advantages and disadvantages of the various materials:

Full ceramic: our KU64 Berlin dental specialists produce conventional veneers from full ceramic. Ceramic comes closest to natural tooth substance. The material can be worked very well and, despite its natural translucency, is very robust. Classic ceramic veneers generally last 10 to 20 years.

Composite: composite is a compound material made up of several substances. It consists of a combination of ceramic, glass and quartz particles embedded in a resin matrix. Your dentist applies composite veneers directly onto the tooth surface in layers and hardens them in several steps. This tooth-coloured, easily mouldable material is also used for classic fillings. Composite veneers last on average 5 to 10 years. Due to their thin surface, discolouration tends to show through more quickly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: With veneers, you gain more than just a beautiful smile

bloecke.text: Choose an aesthetic dental correction with veneers and benefit from the following advantages:
Ceramic, the base material of veneers, is very well tolerated by the body. Allergies caused by veneers are very rare.
Veneers are durable and, depending on the material, can sometimes last a lifetime.
Deposits and stains from coffee or tea do not adhere to the ceramic surface, thanks to the particular nature of veneers.
Treatment with non-prep veneers is minimally invasive, protects the tooth structure and causes no pain.
Veneers are firmly bonded to the tooth surface and are stable and abrasion-resistant, even under strong chewing forces.
Veneers do not discolour or lose their shape, and retain their original brightness and form. White, straight teeth are thus assured.
Thanks to their translucency, veneers are light-permeable and give the tooth surfaces a natural appearance. The transition between tooth and veneer is not noticeable.

Support the sparkle in your eyes with a radiant smile! Our veneers are the perfect solution to fulfil your dream of beautiful, white, healthy teeth. The dentists and dental technicians at KU64 in Berlin and Potsdam are happy to advise you in person about veneers, the materials and costs, as well as all other cosmetic dentistry services. On request, we are happy to prepare a detailed overview of the treatment process for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A perfect treatment requires optimal preparation

bloecke.text: Detailed diagnostics and planning are essential for achieving the best possible aesthetic result with veneers. During treatment, patients, dentists and dental technicians at KU64 Berlin and Potsdam work closely together. In our practice, this process is further supported by digital low-radiation x-rays, digital photographs and models of the starting situation. This is because the best treatment results can only be achieved if the situation can be 'tested' beforehand on models or even directly in the mouth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Natural aesthetics with maximum protection of your teeth

bloecke.text: Aesthetics and the protection of patients' valuable natural tooth material are top priorities in all veneer treatments at KU64 Berlin. In planning and carrying out treatment, we pay equal attention to precision, optimal tolerability, functionality and durability of the restoration, as well as its perfect interplay with the tooth and surrounding gum. Your smile benefits as a result! The dental technicians at KU64 Berlin make all veneers by hand in our own laboratory and fit them individually to your teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Step by step: how your veneer treatment proceeds
Consultation and cost information

bloecke.text: At the first appointment, your dentist discusses with you what you would like to achieve visually. They examine your teeth, gums and bite and explain which type of veneer (prep, non-prep or Veneers-to-Go) suits your wishes and your teeth. At the same time, you receive transparent information about the costs, coordinated with the dental technician team who will later make your veneers individually for you. Please note that the cost of veneers is generally not covered by statutory health insurance, and supplementary dental insurance will only partially reimburse the costs, or not at all, depending on the tariff and scope of cover.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Diagnostics and aesthetic planning

bloecke.text: This is followed by photographs, x-rays and impressions or scans, from which your dentist creates models and an aesthetic treatment concept. This lets you see in advance the direction the shape and colour of your veneers will take. Veneers are planned so that they match the neighbouring teeth harmoniously in colour. Your dentist carries out a precise shade determination and selection together with the laboratory for this purpose.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Preparing the teeth and fitting a temporary

bloecke.text: With classic prep veneers, the tooth surface is minimally ground down and a temporary veneer is fitted so that you can already test the new shape in everyday life. With many non-prep veneers and Veneers-to-Go, this grinding is either not needed at all or is considerably reduced.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fitting the veneers

bloecke.text: The final veneers from the dental laboratory are checked for fit, colour and effect on the face, then permanently bonded to the tooth and polished to a high shine. The bite and contact points are finally adjusted so that speaking and chewing feel as natural as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Check-up and aftercare

bloecke.text: After a short settling-in period, a check-up appointment follows, at which your dentist examines fit, bite, sensitivity and cleaning. At the same time, you receive individual guidance on caring for your veneers and on sensible intervals for prevention and check-ups.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When veneers are not (yet) right for you

bloecke.text: Veneers are not the first choice in every situation. What matters is how healthy the teeth, gums and bite are, and whether an aesthetic restoration can be achieved with long-term stability.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers are generally well suited if …

bloecke.text: your front teeth are largely healthy and stable.
you mainly want to correct discolouration, minor defects, slight misalignments or gaps.
your oral hygiene is good and you attend regular preventive appointments, including professional teeth cleaning.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers are less suitable (for now) if …

bloecke.text: your teeth are severely damaged or already loose.
your gums are inflamed or you have periodontitis.
your oral hygiene is significantly impaired and plaque and inflammation form frequently.
you grind or clench heavily without wearing a protective splint.
you have pronounced dental misalignment, for which orthodontic treatment should be considered first.

In these situations, we first recommend establishing a stable foundation instead of veneers, meaning treatment for decay, gums and bite. We then decide together whether and when an aesthetic restoration with veneers makes sense for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What to bear in mind when wearing veneers

bloecke.text: After your veneers are fitted, it is mainly your everyday habits that determine how stable and well cared for your new smile remains. A few habits help keep teeth and veneers in good condition long-term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Daily care

bloecke.text: Brush your teeth two to three times a day with a soft toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste.
Clean between your teeth with dental floss or interdental brushes, so that plaque does not settle at the junctions between tooth and veneer.
Avoid highly abrasive whitening toothpastes where possible, to protect the polished surfaces of your veneers.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prevention and check-ups

bloecke.text: Arrange regular preventive appointments and professional teeth cleaning so that teeth, gums and veneer margins are thoroughly checked.
Ask the dentists and prevention teams at KU64 to show you how to look after your veneers at home.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Protection from overload and damage

bloecke.text: Avoid 'cracking' very hard foods such as nuts, hard crusts or ice cubes with your front teeth, or using your teeth as a 'tool'.
If you grind or clench your teeth, wear an individually fitted splint to protect veneers and teeth from overload.
For contact or ball sports, use an individually fitted mouthguard to protect your front teeth and veneers from impacts.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers or alternatives: what suits you?

bloecke.text: Veneers are not the first choice in every situation. Depending on your starting point, other cosmetic dentistry procedures may also be sensible, often even in combination with veneers.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers or whitening?

bloecke.text: If colour and brightness are the main concern but the tooth shape is fine, whitening (tooth bleaching) is often sufficient. Veneers come into play when discolouration is very strong or deeply embedded in the tooth, or when shape, position and surface also need correcting.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers or composite bonding

bloecke.text: Smaller corners, edges or gaps can often be treated with high-quality composite bonding (resin build-ups). Veneers are the right option when several teeth are affected, when particularly high consistency of shape and colour is desired, or when several old fillings already exist in the front tooth area.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers or orthodontics?

bloecke.text: For more pronounced misalignments or crowding, orthodontic treatment is recommended first, for example with Invisalign or other orthodontic systems. Veneers can then take care of fine corrections, such as the shape, length or colour of the teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers or crowns and implants?

bloecke.text: If teeth are badly damaged, heavily filled or have already had root canal treatment, (partial) crowns or other restorations often offer more stability than veneers. If teeth are missing entirely, dental implants are used as a foundation, on which aesthetic restorations are then built. In a consultation at KU64, we decide together which form of restoration best suits your situation, both functionally and aesthetically.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about veneers
How many veneers make sense – is 2 enough, or should it be 4, 6, 8 or 10?

bloecke.text: Whether you need 2, 4, 6, 8 or 10 veneers mainly depends on which teeth are visible when you smile and how pronounced the differences between the teeth are. In some cases, two veneers on the central incisors are enough. Often, though, the result looks more harmonious if the visible front area, for example 4 or 6 teeth, is treated uniformly. The dentists at KU64 plan together with you how many veneers are needed so your smile looks natural and balanced.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much do veneers cost per tooth?

bloecke.text: The cost of veneers depends mainly on the type of veneer, the number of teeth treated and your individual findings. A distinction is made, for example, between classic ceramic veneers, non-prep veneers (Lumineers), Veneers-to-Go and injectable veneers. Prices vary considerably depending on the technique and material.
As a rough guide for veneers, you can expect the following costs:
Ceramic veneers: usually around €900–1,500 per tooth
Injectable veneers: generally under €1,000 per tooth, often around €600–900 per tooth
This results, for example, in the following total amounts (without guarantee):
2 ceramic veneers on the front teeth: usually in the lower to mid four-figure range
4 ceramic veneers on the upper jaw: often in the mid to upper four-figure range
6 injectable veneers on the upper jaw: generally in the mid four-figure range

In addition, preliminary treatments such as treating decay, gum therapy or replacing old fillings, as well as the planning and laboratory work involved, can affect the total sum. At KU64, you receive an individual treatment and cost plan before treatment begins, in which the veneer costs for your specific case are laid out transparently. Should your supplementary dental insurance partially reimburse the cost of veneer treatment, we are happy to support you with our service and provide all the necessary documents for the reimbursement.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does insurance cover the cost of veneers?

bloecke.text: The use of veneers is not a medically necessary treatment but serves to enhance the appearance of the teeth. Veneers are therefore considered a purely cosmetic treatment. Statutory and private health insurance generally does not cover the cost of veneers. Supplementary dental insurance also does not automatically reimburse the cost of cosmetic treatment with facings. Whether and to what extent costs are covered depends on the particular tariff and scope of cover of the supplementary dental insurance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does preparing for and fitting veneers hurt?

bloecke.text: With classic prep veneers, the tooth is minimally ground, which is generally done under local anaesthetic and is therefore well tolerated. Non-prep veneers (Lumineers) and many injectable veneers often require no grinding and frequently no anaesthetic either, so usually only a slight feeling of pressure or tension is noticeable. After fitting, some mild sensitivity may occur for a short while, which usually subsides quickly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do veneers end up looking artificial, or can you tell they are there?

bloecke.text: Modern veneers are designed to blend harmoniously into the natural row of teeth in terms of shape, colour and translucency, so they are not recognisable as dental restorations. At KU64, extremely thin, translucent ceramic veneers from our own laboratory are used for this purpose, mimicking the natural translucency of tooth enamel and appearing almost invisible even at the edges. Thanks to precise planning and minimally invasive treatment, discolouration, small gaps or slight misalignments can be corrected aesthetically – with a result that looks like your own teeth and often provides a gentle alternative to whitening.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are the risks and downsides of veneers?

bloecke.text: Veneers are a well-proven and very attractive treatment, but they do have limits if not carried out properly. With classic prep veneers, some of the enamel is removed, which cannot be fully reversed. The tooth will therefore always need some form of restoration, whether veneers or crowns, in the long term.
Good oral hygiene is also important: if teeth and the spaces between them are not cleaned carefully, plaque can build up at the margins between veneer and tooth, which can lead to decay at the edges.
With non-prep veneers, the tooth remains largely unground. However, the additional material can make the teeth appear a little fuller – which is not ideal in every starting situation.

Veneers generally have to be paid for privately, and any repairs or replacements can involve costs that are not always fully covered by supplementary dental insurance either. The dentists at KU64 take these points carefully into account during diagnosis and planning, and work together with an experienced specialist team to avoid possible downsides and achieve a stable, reliable result.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are cheap veneers abroad a good alternative?

bloecke.text: Veneer offers abroad often seem very attractive due to aggressive package prices, since the costs appear much lower at first glance. However, it is often not clear what these costs actually include – for example, what diagnostics are carried out, what materials are used, how much time is allowed for planning and fitting, and how follow-up work is handled. If complaints, breakages or the need for adjustments arise later, additional travel, time and treatment costs quickly follow. This significantly increases what initially seemed like a bargain, and this is not covered by supplementary dental insurance either.

KU64 therefore advises against such cut-price packages and recommends treatment with transparent planning, a clear cost structure and long-term care close to home. In Berlin and Potsdam, you receive comprehensive service with traceable diagnostics and high-quality materials from our own dental laboratory. The KU64 team is always by your side, supporting you with check-ups, corrections or repairs even years later.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can teeth decay underneath veneers?

bloecke.text: Yes, teeth underneath veneers can be damaged if they are not well cared for or if the fit is not tight. The veneers themselves do not decay, but plaque can build up at the margins between veneer and tooth and cause decay at the edges. This then damages the tooth beneath the veneer. Careful oral hygiene, regular preventive care in the form of professional teeth cleaning, and precisely crafted transitions are key. The dentists at KU64 check these areas specifically at follow-up appointments to spot and prevent damage early, without your veneer needing to be removed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long do veneers last?

bloecke.text: The durability of veneers depends on material, load and care. With good oral hygiene and regular preventive care, ceramic veneers generally achieve a stable lifespan of around 10 to 20 years, or even longer. Composite and injectable veneers generally last somewhat less and often need to be removed and replaced a little earlier, after 5 to 8 years, if necessary. The key factors for the durability of veneers are careful care, individual load such as grinding, and regular dental check-ups.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What do I need to bear in mind day-to-day with veneers?

bloecke.text: In everyday life, you can generally eat normally with veneers, but should avoid 'cracking' very hard foods such as nuts, hard crusts or ice cubes with your front teeth. For sport, an individual mouthguard is recommended, especially for contact or ball sports. If you grind or clench, you should wear a grinding splint to protect veneers and teeth from overload.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What happens if a veneer chips or comes off?

bloecke.text: If a veneer comes loose or a piece chips off after some years, you should contact your dentist at KU64 as soon as possible. Depending on the material and the damage, the veneer can be re-bonded, repaired or, if necessary, completely removed and remade. With injectable veneers in particular, targeted repairs are often possible without replacing the entire restoration. The dentists at KU64 will decide, after an examination, which solution makes sense in your case.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are veneers possible even with severe teeth grinding?

bloecke.text: Yes, veneers can be fitted in many cases even if you grind your teeth. However, planning needs to be especially careful in this case. A functional analysis of the bite is important, and generally wearing an individually fitted grinding splint to protect veneers and teeth from overload. In some cases, preliminary functional treatment may make sense before your dentist plans your veneers.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: From what age do veneers make sense?

bloecke.text: In adults, veneers can be fitted once teeth, gums and bite are stable and there are no acute conditions present. In children and adolescents, non-prep solutions or composite build-ups tend to be used instead, for example following dental injuries, in order to protect the tooth substance. Whether veneers make sense in an individual case is always assessed by the KU64 practice team on a case-by-case basis.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are veneers advisable during pregnancy or breastfeeding?

bloecke.text: During pregnancy and breastfeeding, larger non-urgent treatments are generally planned with more caution. Smaller diagnostic steps or preliminary planning can usually still be carried out, while more extensive procedures – especially those involving longer sessions – are often postponed until afterwards. The dentists at KU64 will discuss with you which measures are sensible and safe in your situation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I have my veneers removed or 'reversed' later on?

bloecke.text: Prep veneers require enamel to be removed, and this step cannot be reversed. The tooth will therefore always need some form of restoration long-term, for example new veneers or a crown. Non-prep veneers and certain injection methods can sometimes be carried out without any grinding. In theory, reversal is more feasible here, but this must be carefully assessed on a case-by-case basis. In consultation, your dentist will explain which option is planned for you, what the long-term consequences are, and to what extent insurance may contribute to the costs.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The essentials at a glance
Replacement for missing teeth

bloecke.text: A denture replaces missing teeth and restores chewing function, speech and appearance. Depending on your starting situation, there are removable and fixed variants – from partial dentures to All-on-4 solutions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Stability and comfort in everyday life

bloecke.text: A well-fitting denture prevents the remaining teeth from shifting, preserves the natural shape of your face and protects the jawbone from deteriorating. It gives you back the freedom to eat, speak and laugh without a worry.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Individually made in our own laboratory

bloecke.text: At KU64, we make your denture with over 20 years of experience in our own dental laboratory – individually, precisely and with the latest technology, without any detour via an external laboratory.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth loss doesn't have to be permanent

bloecke.text: Teeth are rarely lost all at once. It's usually a gradual process. Tooth decay, periodontal disease, an accident or simply age: over the course of a lifetime, the loss of individual teeth can't always be prevented. What begins as a small gap can widen over time, until eventually an entire row of teeth needs replacing. Many people only realise how much missing teeth affect everyday life, confidence and enjoyment of life once they start avoiding certain sides when eating, feel unsure in conversations, or have to give up favourite meals. A well-fitting denture gives you back exactly that: the freedom to eat, speak and laugh without a worry.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is a denture?

bloecke.text: A denture is a permanent dental replacement for lost teeth that helps restore chewing function, appearance and speech. In everyday language, dentures are often referred to as "false teeth" or a "set of teeth". Dentures are mainly used when fixed solutions such as bridges aren't enough or aren't possible. They can either be attached to your own remaining teeth or held in place by one or several dental implants, depending on your individual starting situation. Your dentist decides which type of denture is suitable for you on an individual basis, according to your diagnosis, your wishes and your budget.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Partial or full denture – for a carefree smile

bloecke.text: Whether it's individual missing teeth or a completely toothless jaw – there is a suitable prosthetic solution for every case of tooth loss. A distinction is made between different types of dentures, in particular the partial denture and the full denture. Depending on the individual situation, dentists also use combined solutions, for example using dental implants to anchor the denture or stabilising it with fixed elements such as crowns to further improve stability and function.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Full denture – when no natural teeth remain

bloecke.text: If we can no longer preserve all the teeth in your jaw, a full denture replaces your entire row of teeth. It consists of a pink acrylic base designed to look like gum tissue, with artificial teeth made of acrylic or ceramic attached to it. In higher-quality variants, the base is reinforced with a metal framework. The full denture rests directly on the mucous membrane and is held in place in the upper jaw by natural suction, and in the lower jaw by the jaw muscles and, if needed, adhesive cream.

Full dentures are used either as a permanent solution or as an immediate denture straight after tooth extraction as a temporary measure. If you still have enough bone volume and would like more chewing comfort and better hold in the long term without adhesive cream, implants often provide a better foundation for full dentures.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Partial denture – when some natural teeth remain

bloecke.text: If you're missing several teeth but still have healthy remaining teeth, a partial denture is the obvious solution. It consists of three components: a pink acrylic base modelled on the gums, the artificial teeth attached to it, and attachment and support elements. Depending on the type of partial denture, it's anchored either with visible clasps or invisible precision attachments on the remaining teeth. With flexible partial dentures, soft, springy, elastic acrylic takes on this role – without any metal parts at all.

A partial denture is suitable when a fixed bridge isn't possible. However, it isn't an option if your remaining teeth are badly damaged or weakened by periodontal disease and can't offer a stable base for anchoring.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: More stability, more quality of life: types of dentures at a glance

bloecke.text: Maximum wearing comfort, a natural appearance or a long-term stable solution: depending on your individual wishes, at KU64 we offer you the following high-quality types of denture:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Cast partial denture / clasp denture

bloecke.text: The cast partial denture is the most common form of partial denture and is considered the standard solution for several adjacent missing teeth. This removable denture is anchored to the remaining teeth with metal clasps. In the upper jaw, a palatal plate – a flat metal structure that spans the palate – provides additional hold and stability. In the lower jaw, a so-called lingual bar takes on this role: a narrow metal bar that runs beneath the tongue and stabilises the denture.
Both elements take some getting used to for many patients, as they can affect speech and wearing comfort during the settling-in period.

Anyone with high aesthetic expectations can opt for tooth-coloured clasps instead of visible metal clasps on the front teeth. These are far less noticeable, though they do come with slightly higher costs.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Interim denture

bloecke.text: If you need a quick temporary solution, the interim denture is the right choice. It's used when teeth have just been extracted, the final denture is still being made in the laboratory, or during implant treatment. It consists of a simple acrylic base with wire clasps and can be made quickly and cost-effectively. This means you don't have to go without teeth in the meantime and can speak and chew as usual.

Because the acrylic base gives slightly under chewing pressure, an interim denture sits less securely than a cast partial denture and can put strain on the tooth bed of the remaining teeth if worn for a long period. It's therefore explicitly not intended as a permanent solution.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Precision attachment denture

bloecke.text: The precision attachment denture is a combination of fixed and removable dental replacement. It's mainly used in the area of the back teeth, when several or all teeth are missing there and stable remaining teeth are still available as anchor points. Your dentist crowns these anchor teeth and builds an invisible attachment system into the crowns – consisting of an anchor point in the crown and a matching counterpart on the removable denture.

The denture is simply slid on and clicks securely into place. From the outside, neither clasps nor connecting elements are visible. In many cases, it works without a palatal plate in the upper jaw and allows good chewing function. However, it's more complex to make and therefore considerably more expensive than a cast partial denture.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Telescopic denture

bloecke.text: With a telescopic denture – also known as a double crown denture – fixed and removable dental replacement are combined. Fixed crowns – the primary crowns – are first cemented onto the remaining teeth. The removable denture contains precisely made outer crowns, the secondary crowns. These are slid over the primary crowns like a telescope and click securely into place thanks to the exact fit – without any visible clasps. For daily care, you simply take the telescopic denture out.

Telescopic dentures are used in both the upper and lower jaw. Implants as well as natural remaining teeth serve as anchors for the telescopic crowns. The result is a natural-looking, aesthetically high-quality appearance combined with good chewing function. Should you lose further teeth, the telescopic denture can easily be extended. This makes it a particularly future-proof solution.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bar-retained denture

bloecke.text: The bar-retained denture can be used as either a partial or a full denture and combines fixed and removable dental replacement in one solution. A fixed metal bar is cemented between two or more remaining teeth, serving as a stable base for the removable denture. The denture has a matching recess on its underside and clicks securely onto the bar with a noticeable click. This construction distributes chewing forces evenly across the jaw, which makes the bar-retained denture particularly stable as a form of dental replacement.

The bar-retained denture is mainly used when several teeth in a row are missing in the lower jaw and stable remaining teeth are available as anchor points. Implants can also support the bar-retained denture when no suitable remaining teeth are available. From the outside, neither clasps nor connecting elements are visible. A palatal plate in the upper jaw is also not necessary. For daily care, you simply take the denture out. The exposed bar can then be cleaned thoroughly and easily.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: All-on-4 – fixed dental replacement as an alternative to a removable denture

bloecke.text: Have you lost all or almost all of your teeth and would like a fixed solution that feels like your own teeth? All-on-4 makes this possible: a bridge is anchored on just four strategically placed implants per jaw and replaces the entire row of teeth. It's firmly screwed in place and allows you to speak, eat and laugh without any restrictions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A carefree smile: the benefits of a denture

bloecke.text: A denture can visibly and functionally replace missing teeth, especially when only a few natural teeth remain or several teeth are already badly weakened. While implants and implant-supported dental replacement are now often seen as the more modern, comfortable and long-term stable solution, since they feel especially firm and natural, a denture remains a well-established solution when implants aren't medically possible, aren't currently wanted, come with too high a cost, or when a quick solution is needed. A denture also offers further benefits:
Prevents the remaining teeth from shifting: when teeth are missing, the remaining teeth gradually drift into the gap. A denture holds them in place.
Restores chewing function: a gap in the teeth can significantly limit chewing function. With a denture, patients can bite firmly again.
Preserves facial appearance: lips and cheeks that have sunken in due to tooth loss regain their natural appearance with a denture.
Restores speech function: limited speech, especially caused by gaps in the front teeth, can be corrected again with a denture.
Protects the jawbone: implant-supported dentures transfer chewing forces to the bone and so slow down the natural bone loss that follows tooth loss.
Optimal wearing comfort: the denture is individually adapted to the patient's mouth and therefore offers a high level of wearing comfort.
Restores your smile and confidence: a well-fitting denture gives you back not only your chewing function, but also your natural smile and, with it, a piece of your quality of life.
High stability: a steel metal framework provides high stability for the denture when strong chewing forces are at work.
Gentle and quick treatment: while implants need several months to fully integrate into the bone, removable dentures on your own remaining teeth avoid the surgical healing phase.
Natural hold: saliva usually creates a suction bond between the denture base and the oral mucosa, so dentures sit firmly in the mouth even without adhesive.
Simple and easy cleaning: unlike fixed dental replacement, the denture can be taken out of the mouth for daily cleaning.
Repairable and adjustable: if your jaw changes over time, the denture can be adjusted or relined without needing an entirely new solution.
Long lifespan: with careful care, a denture can last ten years or considerably longer.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Step by step: how your denture treatment at KU64 works

bloecke.text: At KU64, we support you from the initial consultation right through to the finished denture – individually, precisely and with the latest technology from our own dental laboratory. In total, around four to six appointments are needed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Consultation and examination

bloecke.text: In a detailed initial consultation, we analyse your situation together: how many teeth are missing, what condition are your remaining teeth and jawbone in? Which solution suits your diagnosis, your wishes and your budget? We discuss all the options with you in detail, so that you can make a decision you'll be happy with in the long run.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Planning and impressions

bloecke.text: Based on the diagnosis, we draw up an individual treatment plan, which you can then submit to your health insurer. We then take a precise impression of your jaw, either the classic way with impression material in a tray, or with our digital intraoral scanner, which works quickly, without contact and without any unpleasant gag reflex. The data gathered forms the exact basis for making your denture.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Individual manufacture in our own dental laboratory

bloecke.text: Your denture is made directly in our own dental laboratory – from high-quality materials, precisely matched to your jaw. Through close collaboration between dentist and dental technician, a denture is created step by step that fits your oral situation exactly. The base is made of gum-coloured acrylic, and the teeth of ceramic or high-quality acrylic. At KU64, we use modern CAD/CAM technology for this: your denture is precisely milled or produced using 3D printing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Fitting and settling in

bloecke.text: If an implant-supported solution is planned – for example with a telescopic or bar-retained denture – we first place the implants. Your dentist then attaches the already completed denture onto the implant. With tooth-supported solutions too, the necessary crowns are cemented onto the anchor teeth before the denture is fitted. In both cases, we carefully check the fit, bite and appearance, and make fine adjustments if needed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 5. Aftercare and check-ups

bloecke.text: Regular check-up appointments ensure that your denture continues to fit well and that your jaw doesn't change. If needed, we adjust or reline the denture, so that you remain satisfied in the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What to bear in mind after your denture is fitted

bloecke.text: After your new denture is fitted, there's a settling-in period during which your jaw, gums and muscles adapt to the new dental replacement. It's normal for speaking and eating to feel unfamiliar at first, and for the first sore spots to appear – these usually disappear on their own. With a few simple measures, you can support this process and help ensure your denture fits well for as long as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Straight after fitting:

bloecke.text: Wait to eat until any anaesthetic has fully worn off. Start with soft foods and gradually increase the firmness. Cut food into small bites and chew evenly on both sides. This helps prevent the denture from tipping. You should avoid sticky or very hard foods such as caramel or nuts in the early days. With upper jaw dentures, take particular care with hot food and drinks: since the palate is covered, your sense of temperature is reduced. There's a risk of burning yourself.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Settling-in period:

bloecke.text: Reading aloud helps you get used to the new denture more quickly and trains your speech. Bring the denture into the correct position by swallowing before you speak. Should the denture press or cause pain persistently, please come and see us – we'll make the necessary correction straight away.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Long-term care:

bloecke.text: Clean your denture carefully every day and attend regular check-up appointments. This way, we can work together to make sure your denture continues to fit well and respond early to any changes in your jaw.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – frequently asked questions about dentures
What's the difference between a denture and false teeth?

bloecke.text: The term denture is the medically correct name for all forms of artificial dental replacement. This includes both removable and fixed solutions, such as partial dentures, full dentures, or solutions supported by dental implants.
False teeth, on the other hand, is a colloquial term and usually refers to a removable full denture, meaning the complete dental replacement for one jaw.
In short: any full denture can colloquially be called "false teeth", but the term denture covers all types of dental replacement.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much does a denture cost?

bloecke.text: The cost of a denture depends on the type and the amount of work involved. Simple full dentures start from around €4,500 per jaw, while high-quality partial dentures can start from around €2,000. More elaborate dentures supported by dental implants can be considerably more expensive and cost several thousand euros. Patients usually need to expect co-payments and cover part of the cost themselves. Supplementary dental insurance is a sensible addition to statutory health insurance and significantly reduces the cost of dental replacement, especially when a dental implant is needed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much do I have to pay myself for a denture?

bloecke.text: The amount you have to pay yourself for a denture depends on the type of solution and your individual diagnosis. It can be considerably higher if, for example, dental implants need to be placed first, as these costs are usually not covered by statutory health insurers.

As a rule, statutory health insurers cover a fixed subsidy of around 60 per cent of the standard treatment for dentures, which can rise to up to 75 per cent if you've regularly kept up your bonus record book.

Patients cover the remaining costs themselves, so you're usually left with a share of around 25 to 40 per cent. However, with higher-quality or more elaborate dentures, your share can be considerably higher, since the subsidy only applies to the basic treatment. Supplementary dental insurance for dentures covers up to 100 per cent of the cost, depending on the policy.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is it worth having supplementary dental insurance for dentures?

bloecke.text: Supplementary dental insurance can be helpful if you already have a denture or foresee needing dental replacement. Adjustments, repairs or a new denture can involve costs you have to cover yourself, since statutory health insurance usually only pays a fixed subsidy. How much a supplementary policy actually helps depends on the tariff, the benefits, waiting periods and your individual diagnosis. Before taking out a policy, patients should therefore check carefully which costs are actually covered and whether, for example, a dental implant is included too.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which denture is the best?

bloecke.text: There's no general answer to which denture is the "best", as the right solution always depends on your individual starting situation. Key factors include, among others, the number and condition of your remaining teeth, your jawbone, and your personal requirements for comfort and appearance.

As a general rule: fixed solutions often offer the highest wearing comfort and feel closest to your own teeth, while removable dentures are more flexible and usually more affordable. Your dentist will decide together with you which option best suits you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I wear a denture even without any of my own teeth?

bloecke.text: If no teeth remain at all, the full denture is the classic solution with comparatively low costs. It replaces the entire row of teeth, rests on the jaw, and stays in place thanks to suction and the support of the mouth muscles.

For more hold and comfort, dentures can also be attached to a dental implant. The implant serves as a stable base to securely anchor the dental replacement. If no teeth remain at all, there's the All-on-4 solution. Here, the dental replacement is attached to several dental implants in the upper or lower jaw.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can a denture stay in place without adhesive cream?

bloecke.text: Yes, a denture such as a full denture can generally stay in place without adhesive cream. What matters most is that the denture is precisely fitted and sits well on your jaw.

Adhesive cream can provide additional hold in some cases, for example with dry oral mucosa or slight inaccuracies in fit. However, it's usually only a supporting solution and not a substitute for a well-fitting denture.
If your denture only stays in place with adhesive cream over the long term, you should have your dentist check the fit.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Should I wear my denture at night too?

bloecke.text: Whether you should wear your denture at night depends on your individual situation. In many cases, it's recommended to take the denture out at night, so that the gums and jaw can recover and blood flow to the oral mucosa improves.

In certain cases, however, it can make sense to wear the denture at night too, for example to help with settling in or for functional reasons. You should always discuss the right approach for you individually with your dentist.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What should I never do with a denture?

bloecke.text: There are a few things you should avoid with a denture, to prevent damage and problems in your mouth. This includes biting on very hard or sticky foods, as these can damage or loosen the denture. Repairing or gluing the denture yourself isn't recommended either, as this can permanently worsen the fit. You should also avoid using hot water for cleaning, as the material can warp. Regular, thorough cleaning is also important. Take the denture out at night – if recommended by your dentist – so that the gums can recover.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How do I make sure my denture lasts a long time?

bloecke.text: Alongside daily cleaning at home, regular professional check-ups are essential: we check whether the denture still fits well, whether your jaw has changed, and whether your teeth and gums are healthy. This way, small problems can be spotted and fixed early, before they grow and require more involved treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How many teeth do I need for a telescopic denture?

bloecke.text: There's no minimum number of remaining teeth required for a telescopic denture. However, several stable remaining teeth are usually still needed, typically around four to eight anchor teeth per jaw. These serve as retention elements for the double crown technique.

If not enough natural teeth are available for the dental replacement, telescopic dentures can also be supplemented with one or more dental implants. Each implant then serves as a stable base, on which the dental replacement is anchored using telescopic crowns.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I eat everything with a telescopic denture?

bloecke.text: In general, a telescopic denture allows significantly better chewing function than many other removable dentures. You can eat most everyday foods well with it. Even firmer foods such as fresh bread, apples or steak can be bitten comfortably with a telescopic denture.

At first, a certain settling-in period is often needed until the new feeling in your mouth and when chewing feels secure. During this transition phase, soft, easy-to-chew foods such as soup, pasta or mashed potato are helpful, until a confident chewing feeling has developed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are the disadvantages of a telescopic denture?

bloecke.text: Telescopic dentures offer many benefits, but also come with some disadvantages. Compared to simple dentures, they involve higher costs, as their manufacture requires several elaborate treatment steps.

First, existing anchor teeth are ground down so that they can serve as a stable base for the telescopic crowns – this step is permanent and cannot be undone. The dentist then fits precisely made inner crowns onto these teeth, onto which the outer denture is later placed exactly.

For the telescopic denture to hold securely, the telescopic crowns must be manufactured very precisely and matched exactly to one another. It's only through this interplay that a stable and functional dental replacement is created.
In addition, regular follow-up check-ups and, if necessary, adjustments are required to ensure a good long-term fit for the telescopic denture.

Getting to know you before treatment

bloecke.text: At your first appointment at the KU64 practice, there's no drilling. The focus is on a personal conversation, your wishes and concerns, and a thorough assessment of your entire mouth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Holistic diagnostics from the very start

bloecke.text: At your first visit, we don't just look at individual teeth but also your gums, jaw joints, chewing muscles and oral mucosa. This gives us a complete picture as the basis for any further treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: From findings to treatment plan

bloecke.text: If treatment is indicated following the initial examination, you'll receive a clear treatment plan with concrete measures, priorities and costs. This way you know exactly what to expect.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The first step towards healthy teeth and a dentist you can trust

bloecke.text: A first visit to a new dentist can mean many things: perhaps you've switched practices, haven't been to the dentist in a while, or finally want to tackle a specific problem. Or maybe you simply want to know how your teeth are doing? Whatever brings you to us: at KU64 we want to get to know you and your ideas and needs first. We take time for your concerns, your history and your wishes, especially if you're anxious about the dentist. We examine thoroughly, explain what we see – without time pressure and without you having to make an immediate decision. Together we lay the foundation for a long-term dentist-patient relationship. Only in the case of acute pain do we, of course, take care of relief straight away.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dentistry you can rely on
Anxious patients welcome

bloecke.text: Dental anxiety is no obstacle at KU64. You set the pace for your first appointment. We support you with calm procedures and empathetic explanations – and treat nothing until you're ready.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: All specialists under one roof

bloecke.text: If your first appointment reveals an acute need for treatment, all specialists at KU64 are directly on site: dentists, implantologists, orthodontists and prosthetists all work hand in hand here. This way, your findings end up exactly where they're best looked after.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Here for you 7 days a week

bloecke.text: Our practice is open seven days a week. Book your first appointment whenever it suits your daily routine, without having to wait long for an available slot.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: State-of-the-art diagnostics on site

bloecke.text: Digital X-rays, an intraoral camera, periodontal screening: even for your first appointment at KU64 we use the most modern diagnostic tools – for a complete picture of your mouth at a glance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Family-friendly practice

bloecke.text: At KU64, appointments for the whole family can be cleverly combined: come for your first appointment and bring your children along for a check-up at the same time.
Take the right care home straight after your first appointment: in our prophylaxis shop you'll find suitable products for your dental health – tailored to what we've found at your first appointment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The KU64 gold standard for your first appointment

bloecke.text: Before you even reach the treatment room, your first appointment at KU64 begins in the waiting area. Instead of a sterile setting, you'll find an atmosphere where you can truly arrive: with a fireplace, lounge music and fresh coffee. Our team welcomes you personally, explains the procedure and takes time for your questions. This way you enjoy the KU64 VIP service from the very first minute.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Welcome and medical history: your concerns at the centre

bloecke.text: Before any instruments come into play, the conversation takes priority, without you having to lie in the treatment chair straight away. Together we go through the medical history form, which you'll have already filled in on the iPad in the waiting area. We want to understand what brought you to KU64: why are you looking for a new dentist? Are there acute complaints or a fear of the dentist? And what is your aesthetic goal? Only once we know your dental history and expectations does the examination begin.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Examination: from the jaw joints to the oral mucosa

bloecke.text: Now the actual examination begins – painless and systematic. We examine not just your teeth but your entire mouth:

Extraoral check: first we palpate your jaw joints and lymph nodes from the outside and check whether your chewing muscles are tense – a common sign of jaw problems such as teeth grinding or jaw joint complaints, which we call craniomandibular dysfunction (CMD).
Intraoral check: we then examine every single tooth for decay, fractures and leaking filling margins.
Periodontal screening (PSI): with the periodontal screening index (PSI), we measure your gum pockets to detect gum disease early.
Mucosa check: finally, we check your tongue and oral mucosa for any noticeable changes.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Digital diagnostics: looking beneath the surface

bloecke.text: To complete the picture of your oral health, we need to look beneath the surface using digital X-rays. For this, we take an orthopantomogram (OPG), a digital panoramic image of the entire jaw, or targeted bitewing images to assess decay between the teeth and the condition of your jawbone. With the intraoral camera, we take images directly inside your mouth and transfer them to the monitor in real time. This way you can watch live what we're examining.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Discussion and consultation: your findings explained clearly

bloecke.text: Afterwards, your dentist explains what the examination has shown: in plain terms, without jargon. Together we clarify what your teeth need, which steps take priority and what treatment options are available.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 5. Treatment plan and prevention: what happens after your first appointment

bloecke.text: At the end, we record the results of the examination digitally and discuss together how to proceed. If treatment is needed, we draw up a written treatment and cost plan in consultation with our colleagues from implantology, periodontology, oral surgery, orthodontics and aesthetic dentistry, covering all further steps. In this plan, we set out all costs transparently so you can make a well-informed decision about the right treatment – without any pressure. Based on the treatment plan, we can also always tell you exactly what has been achieved so far and roughly how much longer the treatment will take.

At almost every first visit, we recommend a professional teeth cleaning to create a clean starting point for any further treatments, such as whitening or veneers. We arrange follow-up appointments together, at whatever pace suits you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Checklist: documents you should have ready for your first visit

bloecke.text: So that your first appointment at KU64 runs smoothly from the start and we can focus entirely on you, we ask you to bring the following documents:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Your insurance card

bloecke.text: Your electronic health or health insurance card proves your membership of a statutory health insurance scheme. All your personal details are stored on the chip. If you have private insurance, please bring your identity card instead.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Registration and risk-assessment questionnaire

bloecke.text: Before your first dental examination, we ask you to fill in a registration form. Using this registration or medical history form, we collect your contact details as well as information about your general state of health. This includes illnesses, allergies and any medication you're taking that could affect dental treatment. This information allows us to identify risk factors early and prevent complications. You'll receive the registration form from our dental assistants at reception during your first visit.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bonus booklet

bloecke.text: Your bonus booklet gives us an overview of the preventive dental check-ups you've had so far. With your initial examination, you'll receive another stamp in your bonus booklet from us. To keep the booklet complete without gaps, you need to attend a preventive appointment at least once a year, and children even twice a year. If you haven't missed a preventive appointment within five to ten years, your health insurance will give you a bonus contribution towards dentures. We take this information into account in your individual cost and treatment plan.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Examination records

bloecke.text: Have you had X-rays or 3D scans, so-called CBCT images, of your teeth taken within the last few years? Please ask your dentist to make all the relevant material available to you, if possible. Our dentists can take these images into account when assessing your dental health, meaning additional X-rays may not be needed. Please also bring your X-ray record card to the check-up, if you have one.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Splints and braces

bloecke.text: If you use a splint or brace, for example a grinding splint, bite splint or retainer, feel free to bring it along to your appointment. This allows us to assess its current condition directly and take it into account in further planning.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment and cost plans

bloecke.text: Has another dentist already drawn up a treatment and cost plan for upcoming treatment? We recommend bringing it along to your first dental examination. It contains all the details on the condition of your teeth, the planned care, the intended therapy and the expected costs, and can be used by our dentists as a guide for further arrangements.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Medication record and cardiac device card

bloecke.text: Please let us know if you are currently taking, or regularly take, any medication. Looking at your medication record or the package insert for your medication helps us anticipate any unwanted interactions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Implant record

bloecke.text: Do you already have dentures, dental implants, prostheses or other implants such as a pacemaker? Please let us know, and bring your cardiac device card, if you have one, to your initial examination at our practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Allergy record

bloecke.text: Do you have allergies and have you been given an allergy record by your doctor? A properly functioning immune system is an important factor, especially with dentures. Using the allergy record, we can rule out or take into account any contact allergies to denture materials during our treatments.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Referral

bloecke.text: If you have received a referral from your dentist to one of our specialists, please bring it along to your initial examination as well. Your treating dentist will then be informed of the findings from our examinations afterwards.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Toothbrush

bloecke.text: If you don't have time to brush your teeth beforehand, you can simply do so at our practice before your appointment. Toothbrushes and toothpaste are available for you. However, if you use a special toothpaste, please remember to bring it with you. Please also allow a few extra minutes for brushing your teeth at our practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prevention for a lifelong smile

bloecke.text: Even if no treatment is currently due, we recommend that our patients arrange regular check-up appointments with their dentist after the initial examination. This allows us to detect and treat general illnesses early, before they get worse. An inadequate diet, eating disorders, poor oral hygiene, stress or a misaligned jaw can also harm your health in the long run. During your first examination, we give you concrete information and tips for healthy teeth. We also inform you about prevention and professional teeth cleaning. All of this helps not only to prevent complex procedures but also to reduce your treatment costs in the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The cost of the initial examination at KU64

bloecke.text: For new patients with statutory health insurance, the initial examination is a covered service and is paid for once a year by your health insurance provider. Most statutory health insurers accept the consultation, the clinical examination and the periodontal screening as reimbursable services. It's worth checking your insurer's exact terms beforehand. X-rays aren't always necessary – but if they are, they're not covered by the insurer and are billed separately. At KU64, this costs around 150 to 200 euros. In return, you receive 3D-quality images, taken with ultra-modern equipment that uses particularly low radiation levels.

For private patients, billing follows the official schedule of fees for dentists (GOZ). Depending on the scope of the examination and individual findings, the extent of services may vary. We disclose all costs in advance so you know what to expect before anything is done.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The service you can rely on at KU64
High-tech diagnostics

bloecke.text: For your first appointment, we work with digital photography, digital X-rays and an intraoral camera for precise findings that leave nothing to chance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Specialist team

bloecke.text: Rely on dentists who train continuously, so that at your first appointment you benefit from the most modern diagnostic methods and up-to-date knowledge.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 20 years of experience

bloecke.text: Build on more than 20 years of experience in holistic dentistry and thousands of initial examinations that have laid the foundation for long-term patient relationships.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Interdisciplinary team

bloecke.text: The findings from your first appointment go straight to the right specialists – thanks to a team that works closely across disciplines and brings all specialities together under one roof.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – Frequently asked questions about the initial examination
What is the routine dental check-up called?

bloecke.text: In dentistry, there are various terms for the regular dental check-up: the check-up examination refers to the annual routine check for existing patients. During the prevention examination, our team focuses on prevention and early detection.

The initial examination at KU64 is something different: it's the first comprehensive look at your entire mouth, including a medical history, holistic assessment of findings and personal consultation with our colleagues. For new patients, it's the starting point of long-term dental care at our practice. We're happy to give you an initial overview. You can call us or book an appointment directly online.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much does a dental check-up cost as a private patient?

bloecke.text: Private patients pay according to the official schedule of fees for dentists (GOZ). This applies both to the initial examination and to every subsequent check-up appointment. The exact amount depends on the scope of the examination, for example whether X-rays are needed or extended diagnostics are required. We set out all relevant details and costs transparently in advance, so you have a full overview of the content and scope of your treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What happens during a routine dental check-up?

bloecke.text: During a routine check-up, we examine every single tooth for decay, fractures and leaking fillings, measure gum pockets and check the jaw joints as well as the oral mucosa. The content of this examination is the same at every appointment and follows a fixed standard. The initial examination at KU64 goes further: new patients also receive a detailed medical history, a holistic assessment of findings and individual tips for their dental health – all following a fixed checklist, so nothing is overlooked at the first visit.

All data and findings are recorded digitally with us, so that the information is available to you and our team at any time. If the initial examination shows a need for further treatment, the right colleagues are on site straight away, whether in periodontology, orthodontics, implantology or prevention. This service is part of our holistic treatment concept.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How often does health insurance pay for a dental check-up?

bloecke.text: Statutory health insurers cover the cost of a check-up examination once a year. Anyone new to KU64 starts with the initial examination. This also counts as an annual covered service and is accepted without any issue by most insurers. We recommend making consistent use of this entitlement and keeping your bonus booklet regularly updated, since a complete record of preventive care is later a requirement for higher insurance contributions towards more extensive treatments, such as dental implants.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long are the waiting times at KU64 Berlin?

bloecke.text: If you've arranged an appointment for an initial examination at our dental practice, you'll hardly have to wait at all. Especially if you're anxious about the dentist, we don't want you to have to wait long at KU64. That's why we do our best to offer anxious patients an appointment as quickly as possible. If you have acute tooth pain or a filling has fallen out, you can also visit our practice without an appointment. In this case, please get in touch with us beforehand. This allows us to plan your pain treatment better and reduce your waiting time.

zahnschmuck.titel: Tooth Gems at the Dentist in Berlin – sparkling accents for your smile

bloecke.text: Would you like a little eye-catcher that makes your smile shine even more? At KU64, we fit tooth gems professionally and gently. Whether it's a subtle gemstone, a sparkling tooth gem or a small gold motif: our dentists first check your tooth surface, advise you on the right position and attach the tooth gem with special dental adhesive – no drilling and no pain. This way, you set an aesthetic highlight without losing sight of your dental health.
