abschnitte.ueberschrift: The most important facts at a glance
An extra sparkle for healthy teeth

bloecke.text: Tooth jewellery is especially suitable for people with healthy, decay-free teeth and good oral hygiene who would like to give their smile an individual accent. Tooth jewellery on clearly visible front teeth is particularly popular – whether subtle or a little more eye-catching and sparkly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gentle attachment to the tooth

bloecke.text: Tooth jewellery is attached to the tooth surface. To do this, we clean the tooth, gently prepare the desired spot and fix the gemstone, twinkle or tooth gem with a special dental adhesive.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: With good care, tooth jewellery brings joy for a long time

bloecke.text: How long tooth jewellery lasts depends on the material, position, care and everyday wear. With good oral hygiene and careful handling, professionally attached tooth jewellery can last several years. Should it become bothersome, loosen or simply no longer suit your taste, we remove it professionally and polish the tooth surface so that no traces remain.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A little sparkle that suits your smile

bloecke.text: You speak, laugh, turn your head into the light – and suddenly a small detail flashes on your teeth. That's exactly what makes tooth jewellery so special. It's not a big statement, but a subtle eye-catcher that makes your smile feel more personal and, depending on the gemstone, tooth gem or gold motif, can look either understatedly elegant or deliberately on-trend.

In the beauty and fashion world, tooth jewellery is experiencing a comeback and is being reinterpreted in a modern way today. At KU64, we combine this trend with dental care. We check your tooth surface, advise you on position, size and shape, and fit the tooth jewellery so that it suits your tooth colour, your smile line and your everyday life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dentistry you can rely on
Anxious patients welcome

bloecke.text: Even a small appointment like fitting tooth jewellery can trigger uncertainty. At KU64, we take the time for calm explanations and transparent procedures – especially for anxious patients who want to know exactly what's going to happen. From choosing the gemstone to attaching it to the tooth, we guide you step by step.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Aesthetics and dental health under one roof

bloecke.text: Tooth jewellery needs a healthy foundation. That's why we check the tooth surface, enamel and gums beforehand. If a professional teeth cleaning, treatment for decay, gum treatment or whitening is advisable before fitting the jewellery, we have the right specialists on hand.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Here for you 7 days a week

bloecke.text: Whether before work, after office hours or at the weekend: at KU64, your appointment for tooth jewellery can be flexibly fitted into your everyday life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: In-house dental laboratory

bloecke.text: Benefit from short lines of communication between dentistry and dental technology. This allows us to realise your individual wishes for your tooth jewellery quickly and precisely.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Family-friendly practice

bloecke.text: At KU64, you can cleverly combine appointments for yourself and your family, for example tooth jewellery, a check-up and preventive care all on one visit.

After your appointment, KU64 can provide you with the right care products for home use straight away, if you wish. In our preventive care shop, you'll find a selection of products to help you keep your teeth and the area around your tooth jewellery thoroughly clean.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is tooth jewellery and what types are there?

bloecke.text: Tooth jewellery is a small decorative element that is visibly attached to the tooth surface. Unlike dentures, tooth jewellery has no functional role. It creates a purely aesthetic accent on the tooth surface. Tooth jewellery is often fitted on the upper front or canine teeth, as it stands out particularly well there when speaking and laughing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth gems and gemstones

bloecke.text: Tooth gems are small gemstones that are stuck onto the tooth. Depending on your preference, they can look very subtle or noticeably sparkly, for example with a crystal, diamanté, zirconia or diamond-like appearance. They are especially suitable for people who would like to give their smile a small flash of light.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Twinkles, dazzlers and gold motifs

bloecke.text: Twinkles and dazzlers are small motifs, often made of gold or gold-coloured material. Popular choices include stars, hearts, circles or other symbols. They tend to look a little more eye-catching than many classic gemstones.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Other forms of tooth jewellery

bloecke.text: In addition to classic gemstones and small motifs, there are other variants such as temporary tooth tattoos – small stuck-on or applied motifs – decorative films as thin, ornamental foils for the tooth surface, or more elaborate solutions such as grillz. These differ significantly in attachment, feel, level of care required and everyday practicality.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The right option for your smile

bloecke.text: Which option suits you depends on your style, tooth shape, tooth colour and the effect you'd like to achieve. A small stone can look very elegant on a front tooth, while a motif stands out more. With visible front teeth, your current tooth colour can also play a role. We're happy to discuss with you whether whitening beforehand would make sense.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Healthy teeth as the basis for beautiful tooth jewellery

bloecke.text: Sparkling tooth jewellery looks especially beautiful when it's attached to a smooth, well-cared-for and healthy tooth surface. That's why, at KU64, we pay attention not only to the right shape, size and position of the decorative element, but also to whether the tooth, enamel and gums are suitable for it.

Before attaching the jewellery, we check for decay, plaque, gum inflammation or other abnormalities. If the tooth surface is healthy, tooth jewellery can usually be attached gently. If there's something to treat first, we take care of your oral health first, so the jewellery sits on a stable and clean foundation. If you'd like whitening, this should be done before the tooth jewellery is fitted, as the tooth colour can no longer be evenly lightened around the decorative element once it's attached.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth jewellery is suitable when…

bloecke.text: your teeth are healthy and free of decay
your gums are free of irritation
your tooth surface is clean and smooth.
Tooth jewellery looks especially harmonious on a clean tooth surface – for example, after a professional teeth cleaning or, if you'd like an overall brighter look, after whitening.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth jewellery is less suitable when…

bloecke.text: there is decay at the desired spot
the enamel is damaged
the gums are inflamed
you grind your teeth heavily,
there are known intolerances to certain materials.
In these cases, we'll discuss with you what preliminary treatment makes sense so that your tooth jewellery can be fitted safely and harmoniously.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How fitting tooth jewellery works at KU64

bloecke.text: We carefully check your teeth and gums beforehand and make sure the foundations are right for teeth whitening.
Together with you, we decide how white your teeth should become. The result is matched to your skin type, facial expressions and any existing dentures.
We work with professional whitening systems, carefully matched concentrations and clearly defined treatment times.
We specifically protect sensitive areas so that comfort and results remain in balance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Consultation and selection

bloecke.text: First, we discuss what kind of tooth jewellery you'd like: a subtle little stone, a sparkling tooth gem or a small motif. Together, we choose the position, size and effect so that the jewellery suits your tooth shape, tooth colour and smile line.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Checking and cleaning the tooth surface

bloecke.text: We then carefully examine the chosen tooth. The tooth surface must be clean, smooth and healthy for the tooth jewellery to bond well. We thoroughly remove any plaque before attaching it. We'll also discuss with you whether a professional teeth cleaning beforehand would be advisable.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Attachment with special dental adhesive

bloecke.text: The desired spot is professionally prepared so that the special dental adhesive can bond reliably. We then place the tooth jewellery precisely on the tooth. The adhesive cures right there in the dental practice, so the jewellery sits firmly on the tooth afterwards.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Check and care instructions

bloecke.text: Finally, we check that the tooth jewellery sits comfortably and is neatly finished. We then explain what to look out for in the first few hours and how best to clean the area around the jewellery. That way, you can start off safely and well informed with your new little detail in your smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Have your tooth jewellery fitted professionally rather than sticking it on yourself

bloecke.text: Tooth jewellery seems small and uncomplicated – yet its attachment belongs in experienced hands. On the tooth, every millimetre counts: the jewellery needs to hold securely, sit comfortably and not put unnecessary strain on the tooth surface. Self-adhesive kits or unsuitable adhesives, on the other hand, can damage the enamel, irritate the gums or leave residue.
Professionally attached tooth jewellery has a whole range of advantages:

Lower risk of decay: In the dental practice, the tooth surface is carefully prepared so that the jewellery sits cleanly and as little food debris or bacteria as possible collects underneath the stone.
Better hygiene: Professional materials and clean procedures reduce the build-up of germs around the tooth jewellery.
Lower risk of irritation and allergies: We use suitable dental materials and check beforehand for any known intolerances.
Longer lifespan: A professionally attached gemstone usually sits more securely than tooth jewellery stuck on at home.
More safety in everyday life: If the stone sits reliably, it's less likely to come loose and be accidentally swallowed.
A more harmonious result: Position, size and shape are chosen so that the tooth jewellery suits your teeth, your smile and your everyday life.
Safe removal: If you no longer like your tooth jewellery or would like to replace it, we remove it professionally, dissolve any adhesive residue and polish the tooth surface.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The right care: enjoy your tooth jewellery for longer

bloecke.text: How long tooth jewellery lasts depends on several factors: the material, the position on the tooth, your oral hygiene and the daily strain from eating, brushing and chewing. Professionally attached tooth jewellery can last several months to several years with good care. It's important that the tooth surface around the jewellery stays clean and doesn't build up plaque. If you follow the care instructions below, you'll enjoy your tooth jewellery for a long time:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Straight after the appointment

bloecke.text: In the first few hours after fitting, you shouldn't rub or pull at the tooth jewellery, or play with it with your tongue. Also avoid very hard, sticky or strongly staining foods for the time being. This allows the special adhesive to fully cure, keeping the jewellery securely in place.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Everyday care

bloecke.text: Brush your teeth thoroughly as usual and clean the area around the tooth jewellery especially carefully. A soft toothbrush, floss or interdental brushes can help remove plaque without putting unnecessary strain on the jewellery. If you notice that the tooth jewellery is loosening, bothering you, or the tooth surface is changing, please make an appointment at our practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Check-ups and professional teeth cleaning

bloecke.text: Regular check-ups help keep an eye on how the tooth jewellery sits and on the tooth surface. During a professional teeth cleaning, we also remove plaque from hard-to-reach spots and let you know if the jewellery is loosening, causing bother, or if care around the attachment is becoming more difficult.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – Frequently asked questions about tooth jewellery
What do dentists say about tooth gems?

bloecke.text: Most dentists are generally open to tooth gems – provided the small stones are attached professionally and dental health remains the priority. Tooth jewellery is now a fashion accessory for many people, similar to press-on nails, piercing jewellery or other beauty trends that emphasise an individual look or personality.

However, it's important that tooth gems aren't attached at home or in a beauty studio without dental training. Various studios do offer such treatments, but not every training course covers the necessary knowledge about tooth surfaces, bonding techniques and oral health. Dentists therefore point out that tooth jewellery is ideally fitted in a dental practice.

When professionally attached, the stones are glued onto the tooth surface without drilling into the tooth. Certain areas around the tooth jewellery need a little extra attention during daily oral hygiene. That's why, before treatment at our practices in Berlin and Potsdam, you'll receive detailed information on care and durability.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much do tooth gems cost at the dentist?

bloecke.text: The cost of tooth gems at the dentist depends mainly on the decorative element, the material and the effort involved in fitting it. A simple gemstone is often in the double-digit euro range. On top of this come the costs for consultation, preparing the tooth surface and professional attachment. Higher-quality motifs made of gold or sparkling diamond-look designs can be more expensive, as material value, workmanship and placement increase the price.

Additional costs may arise if the tooth needs to be cleaned or treated beforehand. A professional teeth cleaning can be worthwhile so the tooth surface is clean and the jewellery holds well. If decay, inflamed gums or other findings are present, we treat these first, for example with a filling or, if medically necessary, a root canal treatment. Tooth jewellery is not a dental prosthesis but an aesthetic service, and is therefore usually not covered by statutory health insurance.

At KU64, we discuss costs transparently before treatment. Please feel free to get in touch with our dental practice. We'll advise you personally on choice, attachment, durability and how the tooth jewellery can later be removed professionally.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does tooth jewellery last at the dentist?

bloecke.text: Tooth jewellery professionally attached by a dentist usually lasts several months to several years. Exactly how long depends on the attachment, the material, the position on the tooth and your oral hygiene. A gemstone on a heavily strained spot can come loose more quickly than tooth jewellery sitting in a more protected position.

For the jewellery to last as long as possible, the tooth surface should be clean and healthy before it's attached. That's why, at our dental practice, we check beforehand for plaque, decay or inflamed gums. If the tooth jewellery loosens, becomes bothersome or you simply no longer like it, your dentist will remove it professionally and painlessly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does fitting tooth jewellery hurt?

bloecke.text: Compared to treatments such as veneers, dentures or orthodontics, tooth jewellery is a small aesthetic service with very little treatment involved. Fitting is usually painless, as the jewellery is only attached to the surface of the tooth. No drilling, injection or anaesthetic is needed for this.

Before treatment, we clean the desired spot, gently prepare the tooth surface and attach the gemstone, gold motif or diamond-look design with a special dental adhesive. During this, you'll usually feel, at most, slight pressure or contact on the tooth, but no pain.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can tooth jewellery also be attached to dentures?

bloecke.text: Whether tooth jewellery can be attached to dentures depends on the material and the surface. Jewellery can usually be attached more securely to natural teeth than to crowns, bridges or veneers. What matters is whether the adhesive bonds reliably to the relevant material without damaging the surface. At KU64, we check in advance whether the desired spot is suitable for tooth jewellery, or whether another position on a natural tooth would make more sense.

Does a stern or tired face sometimes look back at you from the mirror – one that doesn't match how you actually feel? Our facial expressions, lifestyle and age all leave their mark on our faces – for many people, the forehead is affected first. Many find the frown line between the eyebrows particularly bothersome. Fortunately, this doesn't have to be the case: modern, gentle methods of aesthetic medicine can smooth out such lines gently and effectively. In our treatments with botulinum toxin (Botox), we focus on the highest precision, exact dosing and a natural result that doesn't freeze your facial features, but relaxes them harmoniously and removes your frown line. We're happy to inform you about the options that suit you best!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: From frown lines to crow's feet: why do wrinkles form?

bloecke.text: Every wrinkle tells a story – of moments of laughter, focused thinking, sunny or stressful days. At some point, we notice that the lines remain visible even when the face is relaxed, and deepen over time. While some people notice their first lines in their twenties, others retain youthfully firm skin well into their forties. But why is this the case? Let's take a look at the causes.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Facial expressions, stress and the natural ageing process

bloecke.text: Every time we laugh or squint, our facial muscles move. Over the years, these contractions leave their mark on the skin. The forehead is particularly affected, as we tense these muscles especially often here. Alongside horizontal forehead lines, the frown line is therefore often the first to become clearly visible.

As we age, the production of collagen and elastin, which are responsible for the skin's firmness and elasticity, also slows down. As these proteins break down, the skin can no longer fully smooth itself out after a movement. Fine lines that were initially only visible with certain expressions gradually become permanent.

Stress intensifies this process further. Those who are often tense tend to frown or knit their eyebrows together – a habit that deepens the frown line over time. Stress also releases hormones such as cortisol, which further accelerate the breakdown of collagen and elastin and weaken your skin's ability to regenerate.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Genetic factors and external influences on the skin

bloecke.text: Alongside facial expressions and natural skin ageing, genetic predisposition also plays a major role in wrinkle formation. Some people naturally have thicker, more resilient skin, in which it takes comparatively longer for permanent wrinkles to form. Others tend towards a finer, more sensitive structure, in which the signs of time become visible earlier. Those who are genetically predisposed to produce less collagen also develop wrinkles more quickly – even with good skincare and a healthy lifestyle.

But it's not just genes that determine how quickly wrinkles form – external influences play a role too. A major cause of premature skin ageing is UV radiation. It accelerates the breakdown of collagen and elastin, causing the skin to lose firmness. It also damages both the skin barrier and deeper skin layers, impairing your skin's ability to regenerate. So the best way to slow down skin ageing is: use sun protection every day!

Environmental pollution, lack of sleep and an unbalanced diet also contribute to the skin losing its freshness more quickly. Free radicals, which arise from exhaust fumes and other pollutants, attack skin cells and accelerate the ageing process.

So there are many factors that influence wrinkle formation. Fortunately, you can actively influence many of them. And there's more good news: thanks to modern aesthetic treatments, such as the targeted use of botulinum toxin, wrinkles can be significantly reduced.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Removing frown lines and more – what wrinkle treatment methods are available?

bloecke.text: As natural as wrinkles are, not everyone wants to accept them. Would you like to gently smooth your forehead or other areas of your face and remove wrinkles, but plastic surgery and a forehead lift aren't an option for you? Then aesthetic medicine has various non-invasive or minimally invasive solutions for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Botulinum toxin – the most effective solution for a smooth forehead

bloecke.text: When it comes to the targeted treatment of forehead lines and particularly the frown line, an injection with botulinum toxin (Botox) is usually the first choice. The active ingredient relaxes the muscles responsible for wrinkle formation. This not only allows the skin above to smooth out again, but also prevents deepening and the formation of further wrinkles. The great advantage: with the right dosage, your facial expressions are preserved. Only the unconscious, permanent tension in the muscles that leads to wrinkle formation is reduced.

The effect of botulinum toxin begins in the first few days after treatment and develops fully within a week. After just a few days, your forehead looks more relaxed, the frown line visibly recedes, and your entire facial expression appears softer and fresher. Since the body only slowly breaks down the active ingredient, the result usually lasts three to six months. The treatment of the frown line can then be repeated without any problem, if desired.

Another advantage of minimally invasive treatments such as a wrinkle injection with botulinum toxin: unlike plastic surgery, there are no lengthy recovery or downtime periods here. After the treatment, you should only take it a little easy, but can return directly to your everyday life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Further methods for removing forehead lines: hyaluronic acid, laser and more – a comparison

bloecke.text: Is directly plumping up certain bothersome wrinkles more important to you than muscle relaxation? Then hyaluronic acid can be a good alternative. This naturally occurring substance in the body binds moisture and provides more volume beneath the skin. To achieve the best possible result, especially for deeper lines, a combination of botulinum toxin and hyaluronic acid can be useful.

Modern laser treatments can also help reduce wrinkles. They stimulate the body's own collagen production and improve skin structure in the long term. However, several sessions are usually needed for a visible result.

If you want a permanent result, plastic surgery can be a solution. However, a surgical procedure such as a forehead lift involves greater effort, higher risks and a longer recovery period. So be sure to get comprehensive advice and information from your doctor.

Ultimately, the right wrinkle treatment depends on the results you want and how much time and budget you'd like to allow for treatment and recovery. In a personal consultation, we'll work together to find out which solution suits you best. Why not arrange an appointment straight away!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Botulinum toxin against the frown line – why it's so popular

bloecke.text: Botulinum toxin is usually the first choice, for both doctors and patients, when it comes to treating wrinkles and, in particular, removing the frown line. Injection with botulinum toxin is an effective and proven method, especially for forehead and frown lines.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How does botulinum toxin work?

bloecke.text: The frown line and horizontal forehead lines mainly arise from excessive activity of the muscles on the forehead or between the eyebrows. Through frequent frowning – whether from concentration, stress or simply as an unconscious habit – the skin over these muscles contracts again and again. Over time, this creates wrinkles that no longer disappear even when the face is relaxed.

This is where botulinum toxin comes in: the active ingredient specifically inhibits the signal transmission between nerve and muscle. This means that the muscle treated with botulinum toxin relaxes, so the skin above it appears smoother. This makes it an extremely effective treatment for removing a frown line.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The treatment with botulinum toxin – fast, precise and gentle

bloecke.text: A wrinkle injection with botulinum toxin usually takes no longer than 15 to 20 minutes. After an analysis of the facial muscles, the active ingredient is injected into the affected areas using a fine needle.
At KU64 Berlin, we place great importance on exact dosing and precise application. This is how our doctors achieve a natural result: your forehead doesn't appear rigid, but relaxed and smoother.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Results: when will I see the effect, and how long does it last?

bloecke.text: You'll see changes within the first three to four days after treatment. After around a week, the full effect of the botulinum toxin injection develops: your frown line appears smoothed, and your entire facial expression looks softer and more relaxed.

Depending on individual factors such as metabolism, skin condition and lifestyle, the result of a botulinum toxin treatment usually lasts between three and six months. With regular top-ups, you can maintain the effect long-term, preventing wrinkles from becoming deeply etched in again in the first place.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Relaxed in every area: further aesthetic treatments with botulinum toxin

bloecke.text: Treating the frown line is one of the most popular applications of botulinum toxin – but by no means the only one. Whether it's forehead lines, crow's feet or drooping corners of the mouth – many signs of skin ageing can be gently corrected with botulinum toxin, without your face losing any expression. Fine lines can be reduced, facial features harmonised, and even certain muscle tensions specifically influenced.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gentle smoothing of forehead lines and crow's feet

bloecke.text: Not just the frown line area, but the whole forehead is one of the most mobile zones of the face. Whether raising your eyebrows or concentrating intensely, the skin here is heavily used every day. Over time, this creates horizontal lines: the typical forehead lines.
Our facial expressions also create what are known as crow's feet – the fine lines at the outer corners of the eyes. They appear mainly when smiling or blinking and can deepen over the years.

Botulinum toxin specifically relaxes the affected muscles in these areas, allowing the skin above to smooth out. The result: the forehead looks more rested, the eye area appears fresher – and your face looks more relaxed and youthful overall.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Easing lip lines and lifting the corners of the mouth – for a radiant smile

bloecke.text: Fine lines around the lips mainly form in people with pronounced facial expressions and comparatively thin skin. Smokers also tend to develop vertical lines above the upper lip – so-called smoker's lines.
At the same time, over the years, the corners of the mouth can droop slightly. Many of our patients find this bothersome, as it can make them look grumpy or in a bad mood, even when they're not.

With precise botulinum toxin injections, these lines around the mouth and lips can be softened, and the corners of the mouth lifted slightly. This makes your smile look more positive and open again, without losing any naturalness.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gummy smile, masseter and more – botulinum toxin for a harmonious facial profile

bloecke.text: Besides wrinkle injections, there are other aesthetic applications of botulinum toxin that are less well known but highly effective. These include correcting a gummy smile – a smile in which too much gum tissue is visible. Through targeted muscle relaxation, the ratio between lips and teeth can be harmonised.

The shape of the face can also be gently sculpted with botulinum toxin. Those who are bothered by a very pronounced chewing muscle (masseter) can relax it with a targeted injection. This makes the lower part of the face appear slimmer and softer – ideal for anyone who wants a narrower jawline.

So botulinum toxin can be used very versatilely. Whether for finer facial features, a fresher appearance or more harmonious proportions – the possibilities are diverse and offer a gentle yet effective alternative to plastic surgery. Our specialists are happy to advise you on which application is best suited to achieve your desired result. Why not arrange an appointment straight away!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Safety and tolerability of botulinum toxin

bloecke.text: If you're considering an aesthetic treatment with botulinum toxin, you're probably also asking yourself about safety. After all, it's an active ingredient that specifically relaxes muscles – an intervention in your body's natural function.

As with any medical procedure, there is a certain risk of side effects with a botulinum toxin injection. The good news: botulinum toxin has been used in aesthetic and medical treatment for decades and is considered one of the safest and best-tolerated methods for reducing wrinkles, when dosed and applied professionally.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Side effects and risks of botulinum toxin

bloecke.text: Botulinum toxin is injected in minimal amounts and remains active exclusively in the treated region. Serious side effects are therefore extremely rare. Nevertheless, as with any injection, short-term reactions can occur. These include slight redness, swelling or small bruises at the injection site – these usually disappear within a few days.

In rare cases, temporary weakening of neighbouring muscles can occur. This can manifest as a slight drooping of the eyebrows or an asymmetrical result. However, such effects are not permanent, as the body fully breaks down the active ingredient again within a few months.

To ensure the best possible result, you should follow a few guidelines after the injection. Avoid intense physical exertion, direct sunlight and sauna visits for a few days after treatment. This allows the active ingredient to distribute ideally within the muscles and develop its full effect.
Our doctors at KU64 in Berlin will, of course, inform you about all possible risks before treatment and answer all your questions. Feel free to contact us for an initial consultation!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is a botulinum toxin treatment suitable for me?

bloecke.text: In principle, treatment with botulinum toxin is suitable for most people who want a gentle reduction of wrinkles or a subtle correction of certain facial features. However, there are some cases in which treatment is not recommended. We advise against it if you:
are pregnant or breastfeeding
have a neuromuscular condition that affects muscle activity
are allergic to any of the ingredients in the injection.
If none of these points apply to you, a botulinum toxin treatment carried out by an experienced professional is a well-tolerated method for gently smoothing wrinkles and relaxing your face.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about botulinum toxin
Can frown lines disappear again?

bloecke.text: With the right treatment, frown lines can be significantly reduced. Whether complete smoothing is possible depends on how deeply the frown line is already established.

Early treatment with botulinum toxin relaxes the muscles between the eyebrows, allowing the skin above to smooth out and preventing further wrinkle formation. For deeper frown lines, a combination with hyaluronic acid can be useful. Hyaluronic acid plumps up the line so it becomes much less visible. Regular use of botulinum toxin can prevent your frown line from becoming pronounced again in the long term. Feel free to visit us for a personal consultation!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much do botulinum toxin treatments cost?

bloecke.text: The cost of a botulinum toxin injection can vary depending on the treatment area, the amount of active ingredient required and individual factors such as muscle activity. For smaller areas such as the frown line, prices are usually between 150 and 350 euros, while larger treatments, for example for several areas or the entire forehead, can cost up to 600 euros. At KU64 in Berlin, you'll of course receive a transparent and detailed cost breakdown for your desired treatment after a personal consultation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does Botox last in the frown line?

bloecke.text: The effect of botulinum toxin in the frown line usually lasts three to six months. The exact duration depends on individual factors such as your muscle activity, metabolism and lifestyle.

Once the effect wears off and your frown line becomes more visible again, you can easily refresh the effect with a further treatment. With regular injections, the duration of the effect can also increase, as the treated muscle becomes accustomed to relaxing over time.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What's the difference between hyaluronic acid and botulinum toxin?

bloecke.text: Hyaluronic acid and botulinum toxin (Botox) are two different methods for treating the frown line. Hyaluronic acid fills the line, plumping up the skin from within, and is suitable for already deeply etched, static wrinkles. Botox relaxes the forehead muscles, prevents the eyebrows from contracting, and thus reduces the formation of new wrinkles. A combination of both methods is often used to effectively smooth and treat the frown line.

parodontitis-behandlung.titel: Periodontology Berlin: Treating Periodontitis and Protecting Your Teeth

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Periodontitis in Berlin: Prevention, Treatment AND Aftercare FOR Periodontal Disease

bloecke.text: You can do something about gum inflammation, receding gums or gum loss! Periodontal disease (also called periodontitis or gingivitis) – the everyday term for gum inflammation that can lead to the loss of a tooth – is cured by thoroughly tackling its bacterial causes. At our dental practice KU64 Berlin, systematic gum treatment is carried out by our periodontology specialists.

Patients who see a dentist in the early stages of periodontitis / periodontal disease (bacterial gum inflammation) can, in the long run, be spared the need for dentures such as implants, bridges or crowns altogether. Treatment of the gums, together with the patient keeping up their own oral hygiene, is often necessary and can help preserve the teeth, avoiding more serious dental procedures where possible.
The prophylaxis assistants and dental hygienists at KU64 Berlin are happy to advise you in detail on the subject of prevention for periodontitis!
Our prophylaxis assistants and dental hygienists are happy to give you further, more detailed advice!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Recognising Periodontal Disease

bloecke.text: Although gum inflammation is a widespread condition among the German population, it is rarely recognised in time. This is partly because the symptoms are only mildly uncomfortable in the early stages. On the other hand, those affected rarely associate these symptoms with a serious gum disease. This is mainly due to a lack of health education.

Periodontitis is the most widespread form of gum inflammation. It is now responsible for more tooth loss than tooth decay. The task of periodontology (the systematic treatment of periodontitis) is to maintain or restore the health of the gums, making the use of artificial teeth unnecessary wherever possible. Unfortunately, this is not always possible, which is why high-quality implants are sometimes the best solution.

Early detection of periodontitis is particularly important for anyone with dental implants. To make our prevention programme for your implants as successful as possible, it makes sense to also check your bone metabolism. This can be negatively affected by undetected diabetes and low vitamin D levels. We can now test for both.
The Implant Safe Test costs 64 euros, the vitamin D test 49 euros, and the diabetes test also 49 euros.
Do mention this if you're interested at your next prevention appointment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW Periodontitis Develops

bloecke.text: More and more people suffer from chronic inflammation of the periodontium and gums. It is caused by certain bacteria living in dental plaque. These bacteria are also responsible for the build-up of tartar and plaque. They first colonise the root surface and then migrate towards the root tip. As the body defends itself, not only are the bacteria killed, but the periodontium is also broken down. The tooth loosens and eventually falls out. Fortunately, this development can be recognised early on and even prevented by treating the affected gums.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prevention IS THE Best Protection FOR Your Teeth

bloecke.text: Inflammation of the gums and gum pockets (periodontal disease/gingivitis) can be prevented through careful prevention and good oral hygiene! Periodontitis can be quickly detected during a dental check-up and even during a prevention appointment as part of a professional teeth cleaning. Dentists recommend regular preventive care to detect receding gums in good time! Bleeding gums can be an early warning sign.
At our dental practice, we are one of the few practices in Berlin to offer the PerioSafe® test – the world's first test for the reliable early detection of hidden breakdown processes in the gums.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Early Signs OF Periodontitis / Gingivitis, I.E. A Gum Disease:

bloecke.text: Please note: as early-stage periodontitis is barely painful, these symptoms are often not noticed or not taken seriously:
Dark red colouring
Bleeding gums (bleeding when touched)
Slight swelling
Bad breath

abschnitte.ueberschrift: THE Causes OF Periodontitis:

bloecke.text: The possible causes of gum inflammation are varied. Poor oral hygiene, infrequent professional teeth cleaning (prevention) by prophylaxis assistants, dietary mistakes, aggressive bacteria, overloading or incorrect loading of the teeth, misaligned teeth or jaws, disorders of the immune system, and genetic predisposition – all these factors can lead to periodontal disease and defects at the tooth neck.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Innovative Periodontitis Treatment WITH Emundo – THE Photothermal Therapy

bloecke.text: As a rule, dentists treat periodontitis with antibiotics. An alternative to medication is periodontitis treatment with EmunDo and laser. It is particularly suitable for stubborn cases of the disease. EmunDo is a colouring substance that, when activated by laser, can fight germs even more effectively. The best part: EmunDo acts selectively on the relevant germs, regardless of antibiotic resistance. Your teeth and your health will thank you!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs about periodontology

bloecke.text: To give you a thorough understanding of this important topic, we have put together comprehensive information about periodontitis for you below:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Periodontitis and general health

bloecke.text: Numerous scientific studies show possible links between periodontitis (gum inflammation) and the risk of developing the following conditions:
Heart attack
Stroke
Premature birth
Obstructive lung disease
Bowel disease
As an aside: bad breath is also often caused by the breakdown products of periodontitis bacteria.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Periodontitis and smoking

bloecke.text: Here, as dentists, we can agree with our medical colleagues: smoking is harmful – to your teeth too!

Smoking makes gum inflammation (periodontitis) worse and reduces the effectiveness of gum treatment. Patients who smoke therefore need even better oral hygiene and receive more intensive care from the dental hygienists at KU64 Berlin.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Systematic gum treatment at KU64 Berlin

bloecke.text: The aim of systematic gum treatment at KU64 Berlin is to remove the bacterial colonies beneath the gums and in the gum pockets, thereby eliminating the cause of the inflammation.
Systematic gum treatment as part of periodontology can be divided into four stages:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Preliminary treatment (2 to 3 sessions):

bloecke.text: This involves thoroughly removing all deposits above the gum line – both by hand and by machine. We will show you the tips and tricks that will help you maintain this plaque-free state at home too. Your cooperation is, incidentally, crucial to the success of the actual gum treatment: we can only achieve the best result together.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment (1 to 2 sessions):

bloecke.text: The actual gum treatment at our dental practice involves removing the bacterial colonies that have built up deep down, along with their hard deposits (known as calculus), from the root surfaces. This is usually done under local anaesthetic using special hand instruments, ultrasound, medical rinsing solutions and laser. Our periodontologists at KU64 Berlin use a special laser for this purpose. It works with a fluorescence-guided feedback system that detects bacteria and calculus deep within the gum pockets and vaporises them precisely with small laser light pulses until the pocket is sterile. The laser also stimulates microcirculation and speeds up healing. Please note: some teeth may experience temporary sensitivity to hot and cold, as well as sensitivity when biting. This is nothing to worry about.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Possible regeneration (bone rebuilding):

bloecke.text: In certain cases, it is possible to rebuild and regenerate bone and periodontium lost to periodontitis. Through special minimally invasive microsurgical procedures and biologically active substances, your own bone is stimulated to form new bone mass. This does, of course, require that systematic gum treatment has been completed and that the patient maintains good oral hygiene.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Aftercare and recall:

bloecke.text: With gum treatment, the dentist removes bacteria from the gum pockets as thoroughly as possible. However, this does not eliminate the underlying susceptibility to these bacteria. This means that gum disease can, under certain circumstances, return. To prevent this, it is essential that a critical amount of bacteria cannot build up again along the gum line and in any remaining pockets. This requires careful brushing on your part and regular aftercare appointments. The ultimate aim is to maintain the improved gum condition achieved after treatment on a lasting basis. To counter the risk that bacteria in the mouth pose to the gums, ongoing aftercare following gum treatment is of the greatest importance. This aftercare consists of regular professional teeth cleaning, which ensures that new bacterial colonies cannot settle even in hard-to-reach areas. In addition, medicated rinses are used, which protect against tooth decay as well as helping prevent periodontitis. These measures are virtually painless and are carried out at our dental practice in Berlin by prophylaxis assistants at intervals of one to three months. The intervals between individual sessions depend on the severity of the condition.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Regeneration and rebuilding of the periodontium in periodontitis

bloecke.text: In certain cases, it is possible to rebuild or regenerate the bone and periodontium lost to periodontitis.

Through special minimally invasive microsurgical procedures and biologically active substances, your own bone is stimulated to re-form. This does, of course, require that systematic gum treatment has been completed and that you maintain good oral hygiene.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gum grafting and covering exposed tooth necks

bloecke.text: If you have exposed tooth necks, this can affect not only your lovely smile but also cause unpleasant sensitivity.
At KU64 Berlin, we can rebuild your gums using minimally invasive microsurgery with your own tissue, restoring your smile to perfection. This also successfully prevents that troublesome sensitivity.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treating periodontitis pain-free: minimally invasive periodontal surgery

bloecke.text: As the term "minimally invasive" suggests, the dentist treats your gums with particular gentleness during this type of treatment. This spares you pain, shortens healing times, and improves treatment outcomes.
We achieve this using particularly fine instruments and suture materials originally developed for vascular surgery, along with modern techniques such as magnifying loupes and a surgical microscope.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental implants and periodontitis

bloecke.text: If you have lost one or more teeth due to periodontitis, you should consider the option of dentures. Implants are often the best way to fill gaps in your teeth without grinding down the neighbouring teeth.
For implants to work well for you, and to avoid gum inflammation developing around the implant, the following conditions must be met:
Systematic gum treatment of your teeth must be complete
Your oral hygiene must be good
Our dental hygiene team (professional teeth cleaning/recall) is happy to advise you on this topic.
Book a consultation

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Periodontitis or saliva risk test

bloecke.text: If you have existing gum pockets, it can be worthwhile examining the bacteria living deep within them. Such an analysis of certain key germs can help predict how the disease is likely to progress. Your dentist can also use the results of this analysis to determine a suitable antibiotic for systematic gum treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Periodontitis and gum grafting

bloecke.text: An attractive smile only comes about through the perfect interplay between the gums ("red aesthetics") and the teeth ("white aesthetics").

Thin, delicate gums can recede under excessive strain or in the case of gum inflammation. Such gum recession leads to exposed tooth necks, which disrupt the harmony of your smile and cause tooth sensitivity.
Through microsurgical gum grafting, the gum specialists at KU64 Berlin can cover exposed tooth necks and create resilient gum tissue. The harmony of your smile is restored – go ahead and smile!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Periodontal disease and gut flora
What does periodontitis have to do with an unhealthy gut?

bloecke.text: Many bowel conditions lead to a deficiency of minerals and vitamins, as these vital substances can no longer be absorbed from food in sufficient quantities by the diseased gut. However, since minerals and vitamins are essential for building bone and teeth as well as the periodontium, a deficiency in these substances can, for example, lead to periodontitis.

In addition, a large part of the immune system – around 80 percent of immune cells – is located in the gut and depends on a healthy gut to function properly. Bowel conditions therefore disrupt the immune system. The result: periodontitis and other inflammations may heal poorly or not at all. Restoring gut health helps strengthen the immune system.

You can find more information on "gut restoration" at www.darmflora-analyse.de. We would be happy to tell you more about periodontitis treatment – a holistic treatment concept from KU64 and MDL – at our periodontology practice in Berlin Charlottenburg.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Sinus lift and bone augmentation for an implant

bloecke.text: A good supply of bone is essential for the successful, long-lasting placement of implants. In implantology, the general rule is: the stronger the bone, the better the hold for the implant. However, if the bone does not meet the necessary requirements, bone augmentation is recommended before the actual implantation. Various bone augmentation procedures, such as a sinus lift, can improve the quality of the jawbone or maxillary sinus. The effort and cost involved can vary drastically between individual procedures.

Bone loss in the jaw is usually caused by periodontitis, tooth loss, or the high chewing pressure placed on the sinus floor by a denture. Factors such as genetics, general health conditions, medication, age and, for example, smoking also influence the extent of bone loss.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bone augmentation for an implant: requirements

bloecke.text: For implants to be held securely, sufficient bone height is needed, as well as sufficient bone width in the jaw, depending on the implant. Rebuilding bone width is generally less problematic than increasing bone height.

The lower jaw generally has a higher bone density and quality than the upper jaw, which improves implant success. In the upper jaw, however, the curved maxillary sinus often means there isn't enough natural bone to securely anchor a dental implant. In this case, a so-called sinus lift can help.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: External sinus lift & internal sinus lift

bloecke.text: A sinus lift generally refers to the surgical thickening or raising of the maxillary sinus floor. There is a distinction between an external and an internal sinus lift. A sinus lift can only be performed on the upper jaw. In this procedure, either the patient's own bone or a bone substitute material is surgically placed beneath the maxillary sinus. This creates greater bone height which, after a healing period of around four months, provides sufficient support for a dental implant.

The external and internal sinus lift differ in that the external sinus lift is the more involved procedure. It is only used when the existing bone height is very low and several millimetres of bone height need to be gained. To do this, the wall of the maxillary sinus must be exposed with the greatest precision and care. The bone material is then placed in the cavity between the mucous membrane and the bone.

An internal sinus lift is a minimally invasive procedure in which access to the sinus floor is gained through the drill channel for the future implant. The advantage here is that no second surgical site needs to be opened. This procedure also requires patience and great precision from the dentist, particularly as visibility through the drill hole can sometimes be quite limited.

kinderzahnarzt.titel: Paediatric Orthodontics in Berlin – gentle and low-pain

bloecke.text: When your child's teeth and jaw are a bit out of line, it's about more than just a nice smile. Recognising and treating jaw misalignments early on also supports healthy chewing, breathing and growth. That's why, in KU64's paediatric orthodontics department, we look closely and holistically from an early age – with plenty of empathy, modern diagnostics and a child-friendly atmosphere. Together, we lay the groundwork so your child can develop without worry and grow up with a healthy smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The Most Important Facts at a Glance
Specialised Paediatric Orthodontics

bloecke.text: Paediatric orthodontics deals with the prevention and treatment of dental and jaw misalignments in children and teenagers.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Early Detection, Gentle Guidance

bloecke.text: We check early on whether your child's jaw and teeth are developing healthily. This often allows us to correct misalignments gently and with less effort.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A Holistic View of Your Child

bloecke.text: We look not only at your child's tooth position but also at breathing, posture and chewing – for treatment that keeps both function and aesthetics equally in view.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When Orthodontic Treatment Is Necessary

bloecke.text: Sometimes parents simply notice: "Something's not quite right here." Your child only chews on one side, keeps their lips closed when smiling, or avoids certain foods. Older children and teenagers also develop a sense, sooner or later, of when their jaw, tooth position or chewing apparatus doesn't look or function normally. During puberty, comments from classmates often add to this – crooked teeth or a protruding jaw can quickly become a burden.
In such cases, don't hesitate to book an appointment with our specialists. Seeing a paediatric and adolescent orthodontist becomes especially important if you notice the following:
persistent harmful habits in younger children, such as thumb-sucking, prolonged dummy or bottle use, or tongue thrusting
functional abnormalities such as predominantly mouth breathing, frequent snoring or unusual head and body posture
crowding of teeth that have too little space in the jaw or are even crooked
gaps between the teeth, such as spaces that don't fill out the jaw
mismatched jaws, where the upper and lower jaw don't fit together properly when biting
overbite, where the upper front teeth protrude too far over the lower teeth
underbite, where the lower teeth sit too far forward or the upper teeth too far back
crossbite, where the upper and lower teeth don't meet properly on the sides
open bite, where there's a gap at the cutting edge of the front teeth and/or the chewing surfaces of the back teeth when the back teeth are bitten together
front teeth without a symmetrical midline, when the centre of the upper front teeth doesn't align with the centre of the lower front teeth

An early orthodontic assessment in children and a timely start to treatment makes the best use of the growth phase to adjust jaw and tooth misalignments as gently as possible. This often allows more extensive interventions later on to be avoided. Only an orthodontist can determine whether the issues described actually require orthodontic treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Benefits of Paediatric Orthodontics for Children and Teenagers at KU64
Expertise at the Highest Level

bloecke.text: Every set of teeth is as individual as the person. That's what makes an individual, precisely tailored treatment plan so essential for successful treatment. Regular further training and continuing education for our orthodontists and practice team guarantee expertise at the highest level and orthodontic treatment that considers the whole person.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: High-Tech and Know-How

bloecke.text: Our dental specialists are in constant exchange with each other to create the best possible treatment plan for your child. Here, our young patients benefit from our unique concept of close coordination and the latest high-tech equipment. The ongoing development of techniques and materials, for example, has made near-metal-free, invisible braces possible – which are, of course, also used at KU64. We only use tested, well-tolerated materials and provide long warranties – well beyond what's usual.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: In-House Dental Laboratory

bloecke.text: In our dental laboratory, we ensure the highest quality using biocompatible materials and many years of experience. Our high-tech laboratory guarantees dental prosthetics of German master craftsman quality and relies on state-of-the-art CAD/CAM technology for precise, well-fitting appliances. This means children and teenagers get accurately fitted appliances for their orthodontic treatment quickly and with short coordination times.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Does Paediatric Orthodontics Offer?

bloecke.text: Orthodontics for children and teenagers deals with preventing and treating dental and jaw misalignments in children. Left untreated, these lead to serious problems in the mouth. Protruding teeth, for example, are particularly vulnerable to irreparable damage in a fall or blow. Crowded teeth are difficult to clean properly, which can lead to tooth decay and gum disease. A deep bite causes lasting damage to teeth and tooth roots over time.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Happens If Misalignments Aren't Treated?

bloecke.text: Untreated misalignments of teeth and jaw lead to prolonged complications well into old age. That's why it's enormously important for orthodontists to always keep the whole person in view, as the effects of misalignments can impact the entire body. At KU64, we try to address this with a holistic treatment concept.

The symptoms reach far beyond the mouth: incorrect bite function, such as a crossbite, can lead to facial asymmetry and imbalance throughout the whole body. Poor chewing and biting function is often the cause of chronic conditions such as stomach and intestinal problems, postural damage and resulting back pain. Tension caused by jaw misalignments frequently leads to headaches. This is why it's especially important for children and teenagers to identify and correct a tooth misalignment early on.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Does Treatment at the Orthodontist Proceed?

bloecke.text: The first step in finding the right treatment method is always the initial assessment. This requires a complete medical and dental history, a clinical examination, dental impressions, special X-rays and photographic images. Based on the data gathered and the resulting diagnosis, we at KU64 decide whether paediatric orthodontic treatment is recommended in the specific case, and develop the right treatment plan for our young patients.

There are many different fixed and removable appliances that we at KU64 can use to guide existing misalignments in the teeth into the correct position as gently as possible. With their help, light pressure on the jaw and teeth allows correction and retraining of the muscles as well as influencing jaw growth. The type and severity of the particular problem determines which orthodontic treatment promises the greatest success in each case. The approach to treatment also depends on whether the child still has milk teeth or already has permanent teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Orthodontics for the Baby Teeth

bloecke.text: In rare cases, orthodontic treatment is already necessary at a very young age, while the milk teeth are still present. This is the case, for example, with:
open bites caused by sucking habits, which impair biting function
crossbites, which can hinder the growth of a jaw
premature loss of milk teeth
severe crowding, preventing permanent teeth from growing in

Milk teeth can usually be adjusted with simple, removable braces. This allows the orthodontist to have a very positive influence, affect the body's overall posture and thus support your child's wellbeing. The braces come in child-friendly cases with various designs to choose from and are worn in the afternoons and at night.
When using removable braces, the treating team needs your support as parents to ensure the orthodontic appliance is worn consistently.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Orthodontics During the Mixed Dentition Phase

bloecke.text: In most cases, it's sufficient to begin orthodontic treatment when the second phase of tooth changing starts. This happens in children at around nine to ten years of age. In some situations, orthodontic treatment is also needed for older teenagers and adults. This can be the case, for example, following sports injuries involving jaw damage.

The goal of orthodontic treatment is to create space for all permanent teeth and correctly align the relationship between the upper and lower jaw. This can also help prevent jaw joint problems and back pain.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which Appliances and Accompanying Therapies Are Used?

bloecke.text: At KU64, we use removable braces, functional orthodontic appliances, fixed appliances placed on the inside (Incognito) or outside of the teeth, and clear aligners (Invisalign) to help your child achieve a natural, healthy bite.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Removable Appliances

bloecke.text: Removable appliances are used mainly during the milk-teeth or mixed-dentition phase for gentle correction, exerting light pressure on the jaw and teeth. They're particularly suitable for young children.
Active plates / expansion plates: Loose plastic braces with screws and springs, used mainly to widen the dental arches, gently move individual teeth and create space.
Twin plates: These well-known functional orthodontic appliances consist of a forward-and-backward twin plate for the upper and lower jaw, mainly used to correct the position of the lower jaw.
Removable space maintainers: These appliances are used to keep gaps open after premature loss of milk teeth, so permanent teeth have enough space later on.

Vestibular plate / habit breaker: A plastic plate positioned in front of the front teeth helps reduce harmful habits such as thumb-sucking, heavy dummy use or mouth breathing, and trains the lip muscles.
Aligners: These transparent plastic trays move the teeth step by step and are used mainly for teenagers with permanent teeth and mild to moderate misalignments.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fixed Appliances

bloecke.text: Fixed appliances are attached to the teeth and cannot be removed by the patient, which guarantees a steady, reliable effect. Their main use is the precise alignment of permanent teeth, often during the second phase of tooth changing in older children and teenagers.
Fixed braces (multibracket appliance): Metal or ceramic brackets are bonded to the teeth and connected with archwires. These are now a standard method for precisely aligning permanent teeth.
Palatal expander: This appliance is fitted in the upper jaw with a screw in the middle; it's used for rapid or slow widening of a narrow upper jaw.
Transpalatal arch / Nance appliance: Fixed arches between the back teeth in the upper jaw, used for stabilisation, anchoring or gentle tooth movement (e.g. widening or rotating back teeth).
Distalisation and non-compliance appliances: These systems are used to move the upper back teeth backward.

Headgear (external brace): Combines an inner arch in the mouth with a strap around the neck or head; used less often nowadays, but still applied in selected cases to reposition or stabilise back teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Retention Appliances (For Stabilisation After Treatment)

bloecke.text: Treatment with removable or fixed appliances doesn't mark the end of orthodontic therapy. It's followed by the important retention phase, during which so-called retention appliances are used. They serve to stabilise the treatment result and prevent the teeth from shifting back into their original misaligned position.
Removable retainers: Plates or trays worn after active treatment is complete, to stabilise the result and prevent the teeth from "drifting back".

Fixed retainers: A thin wire behind the front teeth, usually bonded from canine to canine on the inside of the front teeth; provides long-term security for tooth position, particularly in the lower front area.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Speech Therapy and Osteopathy

bloecke.text: Alongside orthodontic treatment, speech therapy may be necessary to bring the functional pattern of the tongue and muscles into balance. Osteopathic treatment is also sometimes recommended as a supplement, to address dysfunctions in the body, tension patterns in the fascial system and postural issues.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently Asked Questions About Paediatric Orthodontics
From What Age Does a First Orthodontic Appointment Make Sense?

bloecke.text: A first check-up appointment in orthodontics often makes sense as early as primary school age, when the first permanent teeth come through or you notice something about your child's bite or chewing. This allows the orthodontist to assess early on whether treatment is needed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does My Child Always Get Braces Straight Away?

bloecke.text: No, not every child automatically needs braces straight away for problems with tooth or jaw position. In many cases, we first monitor development at regular intervals in orthodontics and only begin treatment once the right point in growth has been reached and treatment truly becomes necessary.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are Teenagers and Adults Also Treated with Braces?

bloecke.text: Yes, alongside children, we also treat teenagers and adults in orthodontics when removable or fixed braces are appropriate. This means misalignments noticed during the teenage years or later can also be specifically corrected.
