zahnimplantate.titel: Dental Implants Berlin – High-quality Dentures CLOSE TO Nature

bloecke.text: When we lose a tooth, it's often not just our health that suffers, but also our quality of life. With an implant, missing teeth, bridges and entire rows of teeth can be replaced – permanently. The specialists at KU64 Berlin accompany you with high-quality dentures on the way to an open, aesthetic smile and greater joy in life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental Implants Berlin – New Roots FOR Strong Teeth Instead OF Dentures

bloecke.text: Whether it's tooth migration, a broken tooth or unsightly aesthetics, the reasons a tooth needs replacing are just as varied as the ways the replacement can look. Professional dental implants are the highest-quality dentures in dentistry because they serve as a long-term replacement for a single tooth or several teeth. For example, a single gap can be closed with a tooth that becomes truly 'your own'. There's then no need to grind down healthy neighbouring teeth for a bridge. The aesthetics and natural comfort of chewing are fully preserved. Implants thus offer an ideal solution for a better quality of life without gaps, for all patients.

Thanks to the most modern techniques and procedures, as well as excellently trained specialists – highly qualified oral and maxillofacial surgeons and implantologists – the implantology department at the KU64 practice in Berlin Charlottenburg guarantees results of the highest standard and the long-term durability of all dental implants, even after many years.

Implants can also sensibly complement existing dentures or help ensure that a denture sits firmly in the mouth. Through what's known as pillar augmentation, it's often even possible to do away with a classic 'denture' altogether. The palate remains free of materials such as plastic or metal, and the teeth sit firmly, allowing for confident chewing, biting and smiling.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Advantages OF Implants

bloecke.text: A dental implant looks and functions like your own tooth.
Implants allow for a much firmer bite than dentures and make chewing easier in many cases.
With professional dental implants, your speech remains unchanged or is improved and restored compared with other types of dentures.
Unlike many bridges and dentures, implants prevent the jawbone from continuing to recede.
Neighbouring teeth remain untouched when implants are placed.
An implant cannot develop tooth decay.
Artificial tooth roots (implants) can also stabilise a removable denture again or support a fixed bridge.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Long-lasting AND Stable: Our Implant Material

bloecke.text: Nearly all dental implants nowadays are made of titanium, as bone attaches to this material best of all. Titanium is extremely well researched, stable over the long term and completely biocompatible. Our implants come from renowned manufacturers and additionally feature a bioactive surface, which further speeds up healing. Aside from titanium, there are various other materials, such as zirconium. Zirconium is a ceramic material with particularly high biocompatibility that is primarily used for dentures. These ceramic implants guarantee the highest aesthetics and look very natural.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Implant Treatment Proceeds AT Our Practice IN Berlin

bloecke.text: A gentle tooth extraction should be followed by implantation as soon as possible. The prerequisite: teeth, gums and periodontium – in short, everything 'around' the tooth – must be in good order. There's no point placing an expensive implant if, for example, gum inflammation or a lack of preventive care would jeopardise long-term success. These things should therefore be checked before implant treatment.
As a general rule: the stronger the bone, the more securely the implant will hold in the patient's jaw.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Sinus Lift: Bone Augmentation for Stable Roots

bloecke.text: Ahead of dental implant treatment, minor bone deficiencies – such as a very thin jawbone – often need to be compensated for by adding the patient's own bone or a bone substitute. In other words, special bone augmentation takes place before the actual implantation. This is often referred to as a 'sinus lift'.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Placing the Implant

bloecke.text: To insert the implant once bone augmentation has been successfully completed, the gum in the area intended for the implant is carefully detached from the jaw. In several steps, a cavity that exactly matches the shape of the implant is then drilled into the jaw. The implant is then screwed into place. Finally, the gum is closed securely so that the implant can heal undisturbed.

Aside from a feeling of soreness, the pain following implantation can, in most cases, be managed with mild painkillers. Depending on the extent of the procedure, mild to pronounced swelling and bruising are possible in the first week after surgery. In the following period, the implant fuses with the jawbone (osseointegration). This process takes around eight weeks in the lower jaw and about twelve weeks in the upper jaw – there are individual variations from patient to patient.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fitting the Denture

bloecke.text: In a third step, the implant is exposed again and the dentist fits the tooth replacement onto the artificial tooth root. This can be individual ceramic crowns, bridges or dentures. In some cases, the dentist connects the individual implants with a bar, onto which the denture is then fitted.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Bone Augmentation Works

bloecke.text: Thanks to the most modern procedures in oral surgery, it's now possible for almost every patient to have implants firmly anchored in bone. So if there isn't enough bone in the jaw, augmentation under anaesthetic is necessary. This augmentation can be carried out in various ways and using different methods:
using the patient's own bone
using what are known as bone substitute materials
Should there be too little space in the area of the maxillary sinus, it's possible to gently raise the sinus floor using what's called a sinus lift (targeted bone augmentation).

By raising the sinus floor (lift), an artificial cavity can be created above the jawbone. This cavity is filled with the patient's own bone or a bone substitute material and ossifies within around four months. This method gives implants in the upper jaw (sinus lifts are only used in the upper jaw) the stability they need.

Our team of experienced dentists and specially trained oral surgeons and implantologists are happy to advise you at our dental practice on your individual dental situation. Overall planning for dental implants – from the materials used through to bone augmentation – is generally carried out jointly by the treating dentist and the implantologist. The in-house dental laboratory at KU64 Berlin is also involved in the planning from an early stage.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: All Experts Under One Roof

bloecke.text: In particularly complex cases, we also offer patients at our dental practice the option of a 3D X-ray, to ensure that surrounding anatomical structures such as neighbouring teeth, the sinus and nerves can be factored into the planning. Your advantage here lies in the close collaboration of all specialists under one roof, right here at our dental practice in Berlin. This means you don't need to visit additional doctors while your dental implants are being planned.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Pain-free Dentures Thanks TO Anaesthesia

bloecke.text: Your wellbeing is also taken care of during longer procedures. At our dental practice in Berlin, having our own operating area is just as much a given as the option of twilight sleep or general anaesthesia during your surgery. The wellbeing of our anxious patients is a particular concern of ours: we take your individual needs into account and do everything we can to make the time before, during and after surgery at our practice as pleasant as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Preventive Implant Diagnostics AT KU64 – A Rarity AMONG Berlin Dental Practices

bloecke.text: For the best possible use of dental implants, we recommend prior diagnostics to minimise individual risk before implantation, with our specialist in oral, maxillofacial and facial surgery and implantologist Dr Jan Wagner, or our specialist dentist in oral surgery Dr Surian Herrmann. Implant diagnostics refers to determining immunological (inflammatory), osteological (bone-related) and genetic risks that could jeopardise the long-term success of implants. Modern preventive medicine makes it possible to identify at-risk patients through detailed diagnostics and to treat them with individual treatment concepts.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently Asked Questions ABOUT Dental Implants AND Implantology
Can the body develop allergies to titanium dental implants?

bloecke.text: Titanium contains no allergenic components and behaves neutrally within the body. This makes it perfectly suited for professional dental implants.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Who are dental implants suitable for?

bloecke.text: For treatment with implants, bone growth should be complete. This is generally the case from around 18 years of age. You're never too old for implant treatment!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is implant treatment carried out on an outpatient basis?

bloecke.text: Yes, the procedure is carried out on an outpatient basis under local anaesthetic. Placing several dental implants at the same time is also possible!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do health insurers cover the cost of treatment?

bloecke.text: Normally, the cost of treatment isn't covered by statutory health insurers. However, there may be the option of receiving a fixed subsidy. In rare cases, a health insurer may nonetheless cover the cost of the treatment – for example, if particular medical conditions make dental implants necessary.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does treatment take?

bloecke.text: Treatment generally involves five appointments. In total, it takes around eight to twelve weeks for the dental implants to heal within the bone. This is followed by exposure of the implant by the dentist. Fourteen days later, our dentists can take the impression for our laboratory and determine the colour for the denture. A further ten days after that, the final step – fitting the crown – takes place. All in all, the denture takes around four to six months.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does the healing phase of a dental implant take: will I be without teeth for weeks?

bloecke.text: No, you needn't worry about going about your daily life without teeth during the healing phase of your dental implant. Generally, your existing removable denture is extended and adjusted. In some cases, a temporary travel denture is made. Long-term temporary restorations are also used until the final denture can be fitted.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is the injection enough for the anaesthetic?

bloecke.text: Yes, implantation is a procedure for which local anaesthetic is sufficient. You may feel vibration or pressure, but no pain! If you'd rather 'sleep through it', that's no problem: on Wednesdays, KU64 Berlin offers the option of treatment under general anaesthesia. Preliminary consultations for this take place with the anaesthetist on Mondays from 5 to 6pm.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What other anaesthetic options are there?

bloecke.text: In addition to local anaesthetic, general anaesthesia or what's known as sedation – also referred to as twilight sleep – can be used. During sedation, the patient is put into a sleep-like state in which they perceive their surroundings only to a limited extent. Unlike with general anaesthesia, the patient remains responsive throughout sedation, doesn't need to be artificially ventilated, and wakes up considerably more quickly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are dental implants suitable for diabetics?

bloecke.text: Yes, diabetics can also receive implants. However, their condition must be well controlled beforehand. Patients with diabetes should please consult their GP.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do dental implants set off alarms at the airport?

bloecke.text: No, dental implants are not magnetic. Should an alarm sound regardless, please present your implant pass.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What do dental implants feel like?

bloecke.text: Allow yourself and your teeth a little time after implantation. The tooth no longer has any nerves and feels different. You'll notice this when speaking, eating and laughing. It can take up to six months to get used to an implant.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are there any issues with pacemakers?

bloecke.text: No, implants have no electromagnetic effect.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Will I be signed off work?

bloecke.text: You'll probably be signed off work for a short time. However, you'll be able to return to work relatively quickly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are there any issues with medication?

bloecke.text: There can be interactions between implantation and existing medication! Cortisone, for example, can alter the body's metabolism and immune response. Blood-thinning medication may need to be paused temporarily.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are there any risks with implantation?

bloecke.text: Implantation is a minor surgical procedure. Injury to nerves and blood vessels is possible. For this reason, the procedure is carried out by an experienced oral surgeon. In addition, 3D X-rays (CBCT) can largely rule out risks in advance. Rejection reactions of dental implants by the jaw are also fairly rare.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is it painful?

bloecke.text: After implantation, you'll have a feeling of soreness, and any discomfort that occurs can, in most cases, be managed with mild painkillers. Swelling is possible during the first week after surgery. There's no need to be afraid of severe pain following implant treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is whitening advisable before implantation?

bloecke.text: Yes. It's definitely advisable to whiten your natural teeth first and then determine the new tooth shade for the denture! This ensures that the dental implants can't later be visually distinguished from your other teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Am I allowed to do sport after implantation?

bloecke.text: In the first few days after implants have been fitted, patients should avoid strenuous physical exertion!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much do dental implants cost?

bloecke.text: The cost of implants varies. In an initial consultation, we'll discuss your wishes regarding a dental implant. The price of treatment is then made up depending on the scope of the implantation – that is, depending on the number of dental implants desired or required. Drawing up a cost plan for you is entirely free of charge.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What should I bear in mind when caring for my teeth after implantation?

bloecke.text: After an implant has been fitted, you should brush your teeth as usual and use mouth rinses! Generally, there's no need to worry about your implant. Titanium and ceramic implants are highly stable.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is immediate implantation?

bloecke.text: Immediate implantation is a type of dental implant treatment in which an artificial tooth root is placed immediately after the natural tooth is removed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are the alternatives to a dental implant?

bloecke.text: An alternative to dental implant treatment is root canal treatment, such as an apicoectomy. In this case, however, the patient must live with a tooth that is natural but dead. An apicoectomy only really buys time, though, since a dead tooth generally cannot remain in the mouth permanently, meaning implant treatment becomes unavoidable in the long run. Root canal treatment therefore tends to be more of a temporary solution.

keramik-kronen.titel: Dental Crowns in Berlin – Your Practice for High-Quality, Long-Lasting Dental Crowns

bloecke.text: A healthy, radiant smile matters a great deal to how we see ourselves. It's all the more distressing when a tooth is damaged or breaks and your smile is left with a gap. Besides the aesthetic side of things, it's important not to forget that a damaged tooth is also a health risk. Dental crowns offer a quick and lasting solution here. When a tooth is damaged, a crown is fitted over it like a cap, acting as a chewing aid, a protective shield and a cosmetic replacement all at once. With a crown, even severely damaged teeth can often be saved. For lighter damage, a partial crown is also an option, replacing just the damaged portion of the tooth. Crowns are so effective because they don't just replace part of the tooth – they protect it at the same time.
Do you need a dental crown? We're happy to take the time to advise you in detail.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When are dental crowns necessary?

bloecke.text: Many conditions can make a dental crown necessary. A crown is often the best way to preserve an individual tooth. If several teeth in a row are damaged or missing, a dental bridge should be considered instead.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth decay

bloecke.text: Severe tooth decay can also make a crown necessary. Wherever possible, the treatment for decay should of course be a filling, which seals the damaged areas. But when decay has weakened the tooth so much that its overall stability is no longer assured, a crown may become necessary.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Root canal treatment

bloecke.text: Teeth that need root canal treatment are usually already quite weakened by what led to it. Once a tooth has had root canal treatment, it is no longer supplied by the body and becomes even more prone to injury and infection. Although a filling may be sufficient for some root-treated teeth, a crown is generally needed to preserve the tooth long-term. It supports the tooth and protects it from outside influences.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Mechanical fracture

bloecke.text: Here, part or all of the crown of the tooth has broken off. This can happen from biting on something hard, such as a small stone in a salad. Accidents can also easily lead to a broken tooth. The dental crown stabilises what remains of the tooth and protects it from further injury, preserving the remaining tooth structure. Important: if your tooth breaks, you should see a dentist straight away. Within the first few hours, it may be possible to repair the break with dental adhesive. To make this possible, keep any broken pieces and bring them with you to your dentist.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Aesthetic reasons

bloecke.text: A dental crown doesn't always have to be medically necessary – it can also come from the patient's own sense of aesthetics. Ultimately, wellbeing and satisfaction with your own smile are what matter most in any dental treatment. A crown is therefore a good choice for correcting misalignments such as crooked teeth, for filling gaps between teeth, or for covering discoloured teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Protecting and preserving teeth with quality crowns

bloecke.text: Sometimes a knock or an awkward bite is all it takes to injure a tooth. What's more, such an injury often isn't even recognised as one, since a chip or crack in a tooth can occur without any pain or discomfort. The consequences of such a dental injury depend on how severe it is.

Cracks and damage to the enamel are often harmless, but should still be examined by a dentist. If the damage reaches down into the underlying dentine layer, bacteria can enter the tooth and attack the root. Such an injury must be treated as quickly as possible and the affected area sealed. Otherwise, root inflammation or infection often follows, usually accompanied by severe pain.
Root resorption refers to the breakdown of tooth structure around the root – a result of inflammatory reactions that seriously attack the tooth substance.

When a tooth is lost, whether fully or partially, its chewing function is naturally lost too. The jawbone at that point suddenly no longer experiences any mechanical load, which leads to poorer blood flow and bone loss. In severe cases, this can even change the shape of the face.
Injuries often lead to inflammation of the tooth. If a gap like this isn't sealed, it can result in the total loss of the tooth.

After a dental injury, chewing and biting habits often change. Patients subconsciously adopt a protective posture to shield the damaged tooth. This frequently leads to uneven strain on the jaw joints and chewing muscles, which in turn can cause back or neck pain.

When a tooth is lost, the neighbouring tooth suddenly loses the counter-pressure that a healthy tooth exerts on its neighbour. As a result, the adjacent teeth can tilt or shift into the gap. A similar effect occurs with the opposing tooth, which suddenly has no counter-pressure when biting down – it can begin to grow into the resulting gap.

In general, damaged or missing teeth can have far-reaching consequences for your whole smile. Repairing and correcting such damage with dental crowns is essential for preserving your smile and your dental health.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Invisible replacement teeth for a radiant smile

bloecke.text: Replacement teeth don't have to be visible. Our replacement teeth are made in our own dental laboratory, so we can be sure our crowns fit precisely into each patient's smile. Alongside shape, colour matching is crucial here. Our high-quality crowns blend perfectly with the natural colour and form of your existing teeth, so they're visually indistinguishable from your natural teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: We'll advise you individually!

bloecke.text: KU64 stands for quality. That's why it matters to us that every patient feels thoroughly and completely informed. Do you have a dental treatment coming up? Get in touch with us – we're happy to give you detailed information.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Replacement teeth of the highest quality – from our own dental laboratory

bloecke.text: KU64 stands for replacement teeth of German master craftsmanship. While many dental practices nowadays rely on mass-produced products, KU64 takes the opposite approach. We make our replacement teeth individually in our own dental laboratory. This is the only way we can be certain our crowns meet our own high standards of quality.
Because of our high standards, we have the utmost confidence in the quality and longevity of our replacement teeth – which is why we can offer guarantee periods of up to 10 years.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Every crown is one of a kind

bloecke.text: Our dental crowns are produced using computer-assisted 3D modelling. This process is significantly more precise and less error-prone than manual, hand-made production. Ultimately, precision is the decisive factor for the correct fit and appearance of any replacement tooth. Our dental technicians check every single crown individually and give it the finishing touches, because every crown we make is one of a kind.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Types of dental crowns

bloecke.text: Dental crowns come in many forms and can vary considerably in size and function depending on where they're used. Alongside choosing the right material, choosing the right type of crown is the most important decision for the rest of the treatment and for preserving the tooth in the long run.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Replacement crown

bloecke.text: The most common type of crown. It completely encloses the top of the tooth, replacing the tooth's natural crown. It's generally used for more extensive tooth damage.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Anchor crown

bloecke.text: An anchor crown serves as an attachment point for replacement teeth, for example for dental bridges or dentures.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Protective crown

bloecke.text: A protective crown is only used when the tooth's enamel has been damaged to the point where its protective function is compromised, but the tooth is otherwise intact. The dentine, the soft layer beneath the enamel, is very sensitive. In this case, a crown is fitted to take over the protective role that the enamel normally plays.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Partial and full crowns

bloecke.text: One way to distinguish between crowns is by dividing them into partial and full crowns. As the name suggests, partial crowns replace only part of the tooth's crown. This is useful, for example, with severe decay, when a filling is no longer enough to stabilise the tooth. A full crown, by contrast, replaces the entire natural crown of the tooth. The aim of this type of crown is to restore chewing function, preserve the appearance of your smile, and protect the remaining tooth structure.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Crown materials – gold, silver, ceramic and more
Full-cast crowns or metal crowns

bloecke.text: Metal crowns are usually made from precious metals (such as gold) or non-precious alloys (such as chromium or cobalt). They're particularly well suited to less visible areas, such as the back teeth, where their natural colour doesn't disrupt the look of your smile, while their advantages can really come into their own. Metal crowns are, after all, exceptionally sturdy and relatively affordable. However, they are also quite sensitive to temperature, which some patients with sensitive teeth may find uncomfortable.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Ceramic crowns

bloecke.text: Ceramic is a very popular material for dental crowns and offers a number of advantages: the colour of a ceramic crown can be matched precisely to the patient's natural tooth shade. In both look and feel, ceramic is very close to natural teeth. This material makes it possible to produce a replacement tooth that is practically invisible. Although slightly less durable than metal crowns, a high-quality ceramic crown should still last many years. Our ceramic crowns are made for you within just a few hours using our unique CEREC technology.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneer crown

bloecke.text: A veneer crown, also known as a porcelain-fused-to-metal crown, consists of a metal framework with a ceramic coating. This type of crown is exceptionally sturdy and long-lasting. The ceramic coating gives it a fairly natural look, although metal edges are often still visible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Composite (plastic) crown

bloecke.text: Composite is the most affordable material for replacement teeth. However, the drawbacks are correspondingly significant: crowns made this way discolour quickly, are fairly brittle and don't last very long.

Choosing the right material for your crown depends on many factors. It's best to speak to us directly – we're happy to advise you thoroughly and individually on the crown material that suits you best.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fitting your crown – the treatment process

bloecke.text: We take our time with our patients. Even so, the process from your first diagnosis to your finished replacement tooth is quick with us – thanks to our own in-house dental laboratory, we're able to avoid long waiting times.
Here's how a typical crown treatment usually goes:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Diagnosis and preliminary treatment

bloecke.text: Once damage to a tooth has been identified, your dentist needs to determine the right course of treatment. Our aim is generally to preserve the tooth wherever possible. We always try to work as minimally invasively as we can and make full use of whatever strength remains in the tooth. Any parts of the tooth that can't be saved need to be removed before treatment continues. The tooth is then built up with a filling and prepared to receive the crown.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Measuring and taking impressions

bloecke.text: To fit the crown perfectly into your existing smile, a precise impression is taken of the whole mouth, capturing the shape of your teeth and the damaged tooth in detail. This forms the basis for designing the new crown. Before the new crown is fitted, patients are given a temporary crown, which allows normal chewing and protects what remains of the tooth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Fitting

bloecke.text: Once the crown has been made, it needs to be fitted precisely onto the tooth. The fit of the crown on the tooth must be checked carefully, as must its shape, since a poorly fitting crown can lead to gum inflammation and other problems. Ultimately, it's also essential that the finished crown blends into your smile exactly as intended.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Follow-up check

bloecke.text: A follow-up appointment should take place a few weeks after the crown has been fitted. This is to make sure no problems have arisen with the new crown, and that the patient is happy with how their replacement tooth looks and feels.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: No need to be afraid of your crown

bloecke.text: Feeling anxious or nervous about visiting the dentist is nothing unusual. As many as one in five people can be classed as anxious patients, with strong symptoms such as shortness of breath and panic attacks. Our aim is to take away that fear and make even a stress-free treatment possible for patients with severe dental phobia.
That's why we offer a uniquely comprehensive approach:
Avoiding that typical “dental practice feeling” through the design and colour scheme of our rooms
A pleasant atmosphere free of the usual dental practice smell
Specially trained staff
Particularly short waiting times
Visual and audio distraction with video glasses during treatment
For patients with severe anxiety, we offer treatment under general anaesthetic
Are you nervous about visiting the dentist? Get in touch with us! We'll talk you through how we can make your visit as stress-free as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Would you like to know more?

bloecke.text: Our dental experts are happy to help with any questions. Get in touch with us and arrange a no-obligation consultation. For example, send us an email at info@ku64.de, or call us directly on 030 8647320 for our practice on Kurfürstendamm, or on 030 509304280 for our practice in BERLIN-MITTE.

bloecke.text: Feel free to get in touch with us on our social media pages on Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn and Instagram too. There you'll always find the latest news on dentistry and KU64.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about dental crowns
How much does health insurance cover for dental crowns?

bloecke.text: Health insurance generally covers 60% of the cost of dental crowns. With a well-kept bonus book, this cover can rise to as much as 75%.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which material is best for dental crowns?

bloecke.text: The different materials each offer their own advantages. Alongside appearance, durability and tolerance also play a role – and, of course, so does cost. Ceramic crowns are very popular as replacement teeth because they look so much like natural teeth and are very well tolerated.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How is an old crown removed?

bloecke.text: An old crown can be removed without damage, or by breaking or bending the old crown. Exactly how it's removed depends on the condition of the crown and the material it's made from. Removing a crown made of composite materials in particular can be quite a technical challenge. Ultimately, the goal is always to preserve the remaining tooth, if it isn't already damaged, and potentially fit it with a new crown.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does a crown last?

bloecke.text: On average, a crown lasts 10 years or more. Metal crowns tend to last longer than ceramic crowns. But many factors influence how long a crown lasts. The quality of the crown, how well the dentist fits it, the amount of biting pressure it's under, and oral hygiene can all have a significant effect on how long a replacement tooth lasts.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What should you do if a crown has fallen out?

bloecke.text: If a crown falls out, you should arrange a dentist's appointment straight away. Clean the crown and keep it safe to bring with you to your appointment. Avoid hot, cold and acidic drinks. Don't try to put the crown back in yourself – a loose crown is a potential choking hazard.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can you eat with a temporary crown?

bloecke.text: As a rule, you can eat normally with a temporary crown. It's best to chew mainly on the other side of your mouth. You should also avoid hot and cold drinks, as well as very hard or sticky foods.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When can a tooth no longer be crowned?

bloecke.text: For a crown to make sense, the remaining tooth stump, the root and the surrounding gum need to be healthy. If a tooth is loose or the root badly damaged, a crown no longer makes sense – in these cases, a dental implant or a bridge should be considered instead.

dentosophie.titel: Dentosophy Treatment in Berlin – Breathing and Bite in Balance

bloecke.text: Do you often breathe through your mouth, grind your teeth, snore or suffer from tension in your jaw? Dentosophy is based on the recognition that teeth and jaw have a significant influence on health and wellbeing. With a gentle, holistic approach, we support children and adults in changing unfavourable patterns, helping them gain more balance, relief and wellbeing in everyday life. Dentosophy can also be helpful for complaints such as incorrect tongue posture, postural problems, and as a complementary approach for tinnitus or migraine, when the cause lies in the functional interplay of mouth, jaw and muscles.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Contents

bloecke.text: The essentials at a glance When mouth, jaw and body fall out of balance Holistic dentistry at the highest level What is Dentosophy? Areas of application for Dentosophy Step by step: How your Dentosophy treatment works Interview with dentist and naturopath Clara-Constanze Meinberg What you can rely on at KU64 Your Dentosophy specialists at KU64 Contact and advice: Still have questions about Dentosophy? We're happy to help! Already read? FAQ: The most important questions about Dentosophy

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The essentials at a glance
Gentle support for grinding, clenching and jaw joint complaints

bloecke.text: Dentosophy therapy helps when your jaw is permanently under tension, when you clench or grind your teeth, and when jaw joint complaints are affecting your everyday life. The method gently addresses the functional patterns that place stress on the jaw.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Training devices and exercises for wellbeing

bloecke.text: The Balancer, or Activator, is a soft training device we use to train your natural functions of breathing, swallowing and chewing, so that processes in the mouth as well as your overall wellbeing improve step by step.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Breathe more calmly, sleep better, experience less pain

bloecke.text: Dentosophy treatment has a positive effect on the muscles, jaw joint, posture and nervous system. This is because breathing, swallowing and chewing can throw the entire system out of balance, cause sleep problems, and play a role in recurring pain.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When mouth, jaw and body fall out of balance

bloecke.text: Sometimes it isn't major pain but many small signs that show the body has fallen out of balance: a frequently open mouth, restless sleep, grinding, tension in the jaw, unusual swallowing, or the feeling that breathing and mouth function aren't working together in harmony.

This affects people of all ages: in children, such patterns show up as mouth breathing, snoring, lisping, an unfavourable tongue posture, or early signs of jaw and tooth misalignment. In adults, they are often only consciously noticed once complaints such as clenching, grinding, jaw joint problems, craniomandibular dysfunction (CMD), neck and shoulder tension, or chronic snoring start affecting everyday life.

Dentosophy takes a holistic view of these connections and addresses the root of many complaints: breathing, tongue posture, mouth closure, chewing and swallowing. This relatively new therapeutic approach looks at the interplay between the jaw, muscles, posture and general wellbeing.

The therapy is gentle and activating. Using a training device, accompanying exercises and regular support, we change unconscious patterns step by step. This leads to improved mouth closure, promotes nasal breathing, relaxes the muscles and re-establishes the natural function of the mouth and jaw.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Holistic dentistry at the highest level
Anxious patients welcome

bloecke.text: Dentosophy treatment is especially well suited to anxious patients, as the therapy method is very gentle and requires no apparatus.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Open 7 days a week

bloecke.text: Avoid long waiting times and flexibly fit your Dentosophy sessions around work, family and life. Our opening hours, seven days a week, make this possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Family appointments with a play paradise

bloecke.text: Simply combine your appointment with your children's check-up – thanks to family appointments and our spacious, lovingly designed KU64 play paradise.
Support the long-term success of your regained balance in the mouth with suitable products from our in-house prophylaxis shop.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is Dentosophy?

bloecke.text: Dentosophy is a functional form of support for children and adults who want to do more than merely suppress their complaints – who want to better understand the underlying causes in the interplay of mouth, jaw and body, and gently change them. It does not view the mouth in dentistry in isolation, but as part of a larger interplay of breathing, tongue posture, swallowing, chewing, muscles and body posture. At its core is the idea that disturbances in these basic functions can affect not only the teeth and jaw but also general wellbeing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treating causes, not symptoms

bloecke.text: Unlike purely symptom-focused approaches, Dentosophy – similar to osteopathy – aims to identify and gently change functional patterns that can be the underlying cause of a wide range of problems. Breathing, swallowing and chewing are not trivial matters – they are neurologically controlled functions that influence your entire regulatory system. This means the condition of your teeth and jaw affects your health and wellbeing.

Unlike conventional orthodontic treatments involving braces or surgical procedures, Dentosophy uses gentle impulses to guide the body back into its natural balance. This leads to a lasting correction of tooth misalignment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Restoring balance with the Balancer

bloecke.text: Using a soft training device – the so-called Balancer or Activator – our therapist helps rebalance your system. This aid is designed to support correct tongue posture, promote physiological swallowing, establish bilateral chewing, and encourage nasal breathing.

The treatment is complemented by myofunctional exercises, aimed at correcting any existing muscle imbalance. Regular check-ups and close therapeutic support are also part of the process. The active participation of patients is a central part of the concept, as new movement and functional patterns need to be practised. In this way, Dentosophy can help children and adults better coordinate their mouth functions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Areas of application for Dentosophy

bloecke.text: Dentosophy is suitable for all age groups. What matters for the success of the therapy is not age, but the improvement of current movement patterns. Dentosophy treatment should always be considered when certain mouth functions involved in breathing, chewing and swallowing are not working harmoniously. The method aims to gently optimise these movement patterns. The positive effects extend far beyond the mouth:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gently supporting tooth misalignment in growing children

bloecke.text: Dentosophy can help with tooth and jaw misalignment when functional patterns such as mouth breathing, incorrect tongue posture or an unfavourable swallowing pattern are affecting the development of children and adolescents. The aim is to promote natural balance in the mouth and to support the early management of developmental issues.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Relieving the jaw joints and CMD

bloecke.text: For tension, jaw joint pain or CMD, Dentosophy can address the underlying functional processes. By working on the muscles, jaw movement and mouth function, the therapy gently relieves the jaw area.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Better regulating grinding and clenching

bloecke.text: When teeth grinding or clenching is linked to persistent tension in the jaw, Dentosophy can help bring these patterns into conscious awareness and change them. The Balancer and accompanying exercises aim to regulate muscle tension and reduce unconscious pressure in the mouth and jaw area.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Improving snoring and airway problems

bloecke.text: Dentosophy is a good aid for snoring and sleep-related breathing problems. This is because mouth closure, tongue posture and nasal breathing are closely linked and can influence airway function. With successful therapy, sleep quality improves.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Correcting swallowing disorders and incorrect tongue posture

bloecke.text: An unusual swallowing pattern or an incorrect resting tongue posture can place lasting strain on teeth, jaw and muscles. Dentosophy addresses this directly, helping to bring swallowing, mouth closure and tongue position into better alignment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Supporting developmental issues in children early on

bloecke.text: Many developmental issues in children – such as an open mouth, incorrect tongue posture, incorrect swallowing, lisping, recurring ENT infections, snoring, and tooth or jaw misalignment – are typical areas of application for Dentosophy. It helps identify the underlying unfavourable patterns early and gently correct them.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Reducing the risk of tooth decay and gum problems

bloecke.text: When impaired mouth function leads to dry mouth, the natural balance within the mouth changes. Bacteria find it easier to thrive, increasing the risk of tooth decay and gum problems. Dentosophy promotes a healthy oral environment and is therefore often a sensible, strengthening complementary therapy.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treating postural problems holistically

bloecke.text: For many people affected, there is a connection between jaw function, resting tongue posture and body posture. When complaints in the mouth and jaw area occur alongside altered body statics or poor posture, Dentosophy should be part of a holistic treatment concept.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Considering tinnitus and muscular tension

bloecke.text: Tinnitus is a possible area of application for Dentosophy, particularly when jaw joint problems and muscular tension in the head and neck area are contributing factors. This is because the jaw joint and the inner ear are anatomically connected.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Considering migraine and chains of tension

bloecke.text: Like tinnitus, migraine is a possible area of application for Dentosophy when tension or misalignment in the jaw plays a role as a trigger or aggravating factor. By improving jaw function and relieving the muscles, it can provide complementary support in the treatment of migraine.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Improving back and neck pain

bloecke.text: If you suffer from pain in the back and neck, this is often connected to clenching, incorrect loading, or persistent muscle tone. Here, Dentosophy can be a sensible complementary approach to improving these complaints.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Supporting athletes

bloecke.text: For physically active people, Dentosophy can offer valuable support. A more favourable jaw and tongue position supports nasal breathing and contributes to more efficient breathing. This can have a positive effect on athletic performance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Step by step: How your Dentosophy treatment works

bloecke.text: Holistic Dentosophy therapy works with a special training device: the Balancer. This elastic training device, made of soft rubber in the shape of a dental arch, is worn in the mouth daily for a limited period. Its purpose is not to move teeth using pressure, but to activate functional processes in the mouth and bring them into conscious awareness. Combined with targeted chewing, swallowing and breathing exercises, the Balancer helps gently improve tongue function, mouth closure and nasal breathing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Initial diagnosis

bloecke.text: Treatment begins with a detailed diagnostic assessment at our practice, in order to discuss functional findings as well as your individual goals and wishes, and to establish an overall treatment concept.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Active phase with daily Balancer training and wear

bloecke.text: The active phase of Dentosophy treatment begins with around five minutes of daily training with the Balancer, guided by our expert. This training is supplemented by a relaxed wearing period of the Balancer of around one hour a day, without active exercises.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Extending wearing time and adjusting the exercises

bloecke.text: Once you have become well accustomed to the exercises and the wearing time, therapy is gradually extended by wearing the Balancer overnight. Our therapist adjusts the exercises together with you according to your progress.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Check-ups and osteopathic support

bloecke.text: At intervals of six to eight weeks, you attend check-up appointments to review the overall progress of your Dentosophy treatment. Depending on your needs and situation, our expert provides targeted manual-therapeutic or osteopathic support to help reinforce the success of the therapy.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQ: The most important questions about Dentosophy
Who is Dentosophy suitable for?

bloecke.text: The method is suitable both for children and adolescents still developing, and for adults. It is a gentle approach for a wide range of physical complaints where functional issues such as mouth breathing, incorrect tongue posture, unusual swallowing, grinding, clenching or jaw misalignment play a role. It is often also used alongside other dental measures such as orthodontics or the treatment of tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is the Balancer?

bloecke.text: The Balancer is an elastic training device made of plastic, shaped like a dental arch, used in Dentosophy. Among other things, it is designed to support tongue function, lip closure, swallowing and nasal breathing, thereby having a positive effect on your health. It is worn regularly during the therapy phase and used together with accompanying exercises.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does Dentosophy treatment take?

bloecke.text: The duration depends on the findings, age and treatment goal. It typically covers an overall period of around six to twelve months. In individual cases, ongoing Dentosophy support may also be sensible for longer.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does health insurance cover the costs?

bloecke.text: Statutory health insurers generally do not cover the costs of Dentosophy treatment. For privately insured patients and those with supplementary private dental insurance, cost coverage depends on the respective tariff. Our team will advise you in detail before treatment begins and provide you with all the information on the process and costs.

bloecke.text: Immaculately white teeth look vital, attractive and are a sign of our health. Yet over time, the bright white of our teeth gradually fades. abschnitte.ueberschrift: When Brushing Is No Longer Enough: Find Your Way Back to Your Natural Radiance

bloecke.text: It's not just pigments from food and drink that leave a grey veil on our teeth over the course of our lives. Medication or a dead tooth nerve can also dull a bright smile. Our teeth become darker. The enamel takes on a blotchy, yellowish-brown or greyish colour.

Polishing pastes or air-polishing devices usually only remove surface staining. In the case of discolouration caused by a dead tooth nerve, superficial cleaning is almost entirely ineffective. Only professional bleaching at the dentist can successfully remove deep-seated staining. Together with our bleaching specialists, you decide on your individual method of teeth whitening and your new tooth colour. Which procedure is right for you depends, among other things, on the degree of your discolouration.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Method 4: Whitening Individual Dark Teeth Through Internal Bleaching

bloecke.text: If, after a root canal treatment or an accident, only a single tooth becomes discoloured grey or brownish, internal bleaching may be an option. Unlike classic bleaching, we do not apply the whitening agent to the enamel but inside the tooth, in a tooth that has already had root canal treatment. Through a small access point, the tooth is opened, part of the filling removed and a special bleaching gel inserted. This remains inside the tooth for a few days, is usually renewed over two to three sessions and the tooth is then sealed again with a filling.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gentle Bleaching Options at KU64

bloecke.text: For sensitive teeth, we mainly rely on bleaching methods that

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prophylaxis – The Foundation of Every Teeth Whitening

bloecke.text: Whichever bleaching method you choose as a patient: before whitening, an examination of your teeth for any disease should be carried out and any decay treated. For an even better, more aesthetic result, we recommend professional teeth cleaning (prophylaxis) by the prophylaxis assistants at KU64 in Berlin and Potsdam. The reason: with professional teeth cleaning, we remove deposits such as plaque or tartar, so that the bleaching gel can work more effectively on the tooth. Professional teeth cleaning at the dentist should be done within six weeks before bleaching.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How a Bleaching Treatment Works

bloecke.text: With teeth whitening, also called bleaching, we professionally lighten your teeth at the dental practice in just a few steps, all in one session:
Preparation and protection First, the lips, cheeks and gums are carefully protected, so that only the areas actually intended to be whitened are treated.

Applying the bleaching gel Next, your dentist applies a bleaching gel to the teeth. Depending on the manufacturer, it contains hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide – active ingredients that chemically break down pigments in the enamel.

Activation with a special lamp The gel is activated with a special lamp. This produces so-called nascent oxygen, which penetrates the tooth surface and lightens the discoloured substances without damaging the tooth structure. Studies show that the lamp can increase the effectiveness of the gel by at least 26 per cent, with lightening of up to eight shades.

Several rounds in one session The gel, and where applicable the light treatment, is repeated in several rounds within the same treatment session until the planned degree of whitening is reached. This produces an even, controlled result.

Check, fluoridation and repeat interval To finish, your dentist removes the gel completely, checks the result and fluoridates the teeth or provides other care products. From a dental point of view, this kind of power bleaching should not be repeated any sooner than after a year.
Arrange your bleaching appointment at KU64 now and take the next step towards a visibly brighter, naturally beautiful smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When Can I Have Teeth Whitening

bloecke.text: Bleaching is an effective way of improving tooth colour, but it isn't always the first step. It's important that your teeth and gums are healthy and that whitening can be carried out in a way that makes dental sense and is stable in the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bleaching Is Well Suited If …

bloecke.text: your teeth are free of decay and you have no acute toothache.
your gums are healthy and there is no untreated periodontitis.
your fillings, crowns and bridges are sound and show no gaps at the edges.
you are willing to have a check-up beforehand and, ideally, a professional teeth clean.
you wish for a natural lightening by a few shades and have realistic expectations of the result.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bleaching Is Less Suitable (For Now) If …

bloecke.text: you are pregnant or breastfeeding. In this case, we recommend avoiding purely cosmetic treatments, as the effects of bleaching agents during pregnancy and breastfeeding have not been sufficiently researched.
you are a patient who is still very young, such as children and adolescents whose teeth have not yet fully matured.
you have active decay, leaking fillings, inflamed gums or untreated periodontitis.
your teeth are highly sensitive or you have a lot of exposed tooth necks.
you wish for a 'pure white' result that no longer suits your look, or that is meant to override your natural tooth structure.
Together, we then decide whether and when professional teeth whitening is sensible and safely possible for you. Make use of our service and arrange an appointment!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bleaching for Sensitive Teeth and Exposed Tooth Necks

bloecke.text: Sensitive teeth or exposed tooth necks are not an automatic reason to rule out bleaching. However, they are a clear sign to take a closer look. At KU64, we first check where the sensitivity is coming from and whether there is decay, leaking fillings or inflamed gums. Once the cause has been clarified and treated from a dental point of view, and your teeth are otherwise stable, we plan the teeth whitening in a way that enhances your smile without putting extra strain on your teeth and gums.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bleaching with KU64: Look Forward to a Smile That Suits You

bloecke.text: At KU64, it's not just about making your teeth brighter, but about making your smile as a whole look harmonious:
We carefully check your teeth and gums beforehand and make sure that the foundation for teeth whitening is right.
Together with you, we decide how bright your teeth should become. The result is matched to your skin tone, expressions and any existing dental prosthetics.
We work with professional bleaching systems, carefully matched concentrations and clearly defined treatment times.
We specifically protect sensitive areas, so that comfort and result remain in balance.

Whitening toothpastes from the chemist, home strips or treatments at a beauty salon can freshen up your smile in everyday life. As a supplement, they are mainly suitable for evening out minor discolouration between two professional treatments and preserving the result of a bleaching treatment in the long term. However, if you wish for a targeted result that truly suits you, you are in the best hands with professional bleaching at our KU64 dental practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bleaching and Dental Prosthetics: How to Keep a Consistent Tooth Colour

bloecke.text: Bleaching is a great option if you want to freshen up your natural tooth colour. However, as soon as fillings, crowns, bridges or veneers are involved, it's always about the overall picture – in other words, how well your natural teeth and your dental prosthetics match in colour.

Composite fillings, crowns, bridges and veneers cannot be lightened by bleaching. If only the natural tooth is whitened, it can happen that older restorations in the front area appear noticeably darker afterwards and 'stand out'.

That's why, at KU64, we check beforehand exactly what dental prosthetics are present in the visible area and how they can be colour-matched. In some cases, it's necessary for us to replace individual, noticeably darker restorations after bleaching, so that they match the overall picture in colour again.
If you're already planning new dental prosthetics in the front tooth area, we generally recommend: bleaching first, then adjusting the prosthetics.
This allows us to:
first bring your natural tooth colour to the desired lighter shade
then match crowns, bridges or veneers exactly to this shade.
This way, a harmonious overall picture is achieved, without the need for further adjustments later on.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When Bleaching Alone Isn't Enough

bloecke.text: Sometimes, whitening alone isn't enough – for example, when teeth are heavily worn, discoloured due to fillings, crooked, or clearly disproportionate in shape and size. In such cases, we combine bleaching with other aesthetic solutions where needed:
veneers, to improve the shape, colour and position of the front teeth
high-quality implants, crowns or bridges, if teeth are already severely damaged
professional teeth cleaning and polishing, if plaque and surface staining are the main issue
In a personal consultation at KU64, we will discuss with you whether bleaching alone is enough, or whether a combined aesthetic treatment is the better, more stable long-term solution for your smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What to Keep in Mind After Bleaching

bloecke.text: So that your bleaching result lasts as long as possible and your teeth can recover well, the first few hours and days after treatment are particularly important:
Avoid strongly colouring food and drink such as coffee, tea, red wine, cola, berries, intense sauces and nicotine for the first 24 to 48 hours.
Opt for water, light-coloured foods and a mild, non-abrasive toothpaste.
Continue brushing your teeth carefully, but without too much pressure, to avoid further irritating the gums.
For temporary sensitivity, use a desensitising toothpaste or special products recommended by KU64.
If discomfort persists or you have any questions, arrange a short check-up appointment so we can review the result and your dental health.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: This Is What Your Bleaching Costs at KU64 Berlin

bloecke.text: A whiter smile is always an investment in how you present yourself, and should remain something you can plan for. That's why, at KU64, we place great importance on transparent costs rather than blanket promises. The price of your bleaching treatment comes from a number of clearly definable factors, which we go through with you in the consultation and set out in a personal cost plan.

Type of bleaching method Whether you choose intensive in-office bleaching in our bleaching lounge or home bleaching has a direct effect on the cost. Professional bleaching at the practice takes up more of the team's treatment time and makes use of high-tech equipment and specially protective materials. As a result, the price is higher than for a home-bleaching kit that you use yourself at home.

Extent of the teeth whitening The area treated also determines the cost: are only the visible front teeth being whitened, or the whole upper and lower jaw? The more teeth we include, the more material and treatment time is needed, and the greater the investment you should plan for your new smile.

Starting shade and desired degree of whitening Mild discolouration can often be corrected with fewer rounds than deep-seated, long-standing staining. If you wish for particularly noticeable whitening, more bleaching rounds or a longer treatment period are usually needed. Each additional round increases the effort involved and, with it, the cost of your teeth whitening.

Preliminary treatment and dental health Bleaching is only an option on healthy teeth and healthy gums. Necessary preliminary treatments, such as professional teeth cleaning, treating decay or replacing leaking fillings, make dental sense or are medically necessary, but are not always covered by health insurance and are added to the actual bleaching costs.

Durability and touch-ups Depending on the method, the result remains stable, on average, for around one to eighteen months. Anyone wanting a lasting, naturally white smile should factor these touch-up treatments into their personal cost planning as well.

At the same time: the longer-lasting the result, the more cost-effective your bleaching becomes 'per month of smiling', compared with short-term solutions. Instead of repeatedly reaching for chemist products, you invest once in a professional whitening treatment with a predictable effect. That way, you benefit day after day, whether looking in the mirror, at work, or in every photo.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently Asked Questions About Bleaching
Who Is Bleaching Suitable For?

bloecke.text: In principle, bleaching is suitable for anyone who wants whiter teeth – provided your teeth and gums are healthy, there is no acute decay or inflammation, you are not pregnant or breastfeeding, and you don't have highly sensitive teeth or significantly exposed tooth necks. In these cases, treatment isn't ruled out entirely, but is postponed for the sake of your dental health and planned for a later date.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do Many People Have Their Teeth Whitened?

bloecke.text: More people than you might think already have whitened teeth – often subtly, but with a great effect. A radiant smile and brighter teeth make a noticeable difference compared with a smile with darker, discoloured teeth, as they stand for freshness, vitality and a confident, well-groomed appearance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is There a Risk with Bleaching?

bloecke.text: Bleaching isn't a 'wellness' treatment, but when carried out professionally, it's considered a well-studied and generally safe procedure. Key factors are healthy teeth and gums, approved materials and clearly defined application times.

The most common side effect is temporary tooth sensitivity, as the enamel reacts slightly more sensitively for a short time. That's why dentists recommend avoiding highly acidic and strongly colouring food and drink in the first few days after treatment. Saliva, appropriate care and a final fluoride application support remineralisation, so sensitivity usually returns to normal after a short time.
Gum irritation mainly occurs when the gums aren't sufficiently protected. At KU64, we ensure your bleaching treatment is gentle and safe through careful shielding and precisely dosed bleaching gel.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Long Does the Bleaching Effect Last?

bloecke.text: With good oral hygiene and mindful eating habits, the result remains stable on average for around one to eighteen months. In general, your teeth will remain brighter than before the treatment for several years. To maintain the brilliance of your teeth, you should take care with thorough oral hygiene. Brush your teeth twice daily, use dental floss and visit your dental practice regularly for professional teeth cleaning. The dentists at KU64 in Berlin and Potsdam generally recommend a teeth clean before every bleaching treatment. This helps optimise the result of the teeth whitening.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Is the Difference Between Tooth Discolouration and Plaque?

bloecke.text: Plaque on the teeth can usually be removed during a professional teeth clean. Tooth discolouration, on the other hand, is more stubborn. It develops from the permanent build-up of pigments within the tooth substance itself. In this case, thorough oral hygiene alone isn't enough to bring back the natural white of the teeth. Over-the-counter whitening products also don't remove this deeper discolouration.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Is the Difference Between Bleaching and Professional Teeth Cleaning?

bloecke.text: Professional teeth cleaning removes plaque, tartar and surface staining. Teeth often already look fresher as a result, but they aren't specifically lightened by several shades. Bleaching goes deeper and chemically changes the tooth's colour. The ideal approach is to combine the two: first professional teeth cleaning as a foundation, then bleaching for the desired brightening effect.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Where Does Tooth Discolouration Come From?

bloecke.text: Tooth discolouration has many causes. Among the most common reasons are ageing and the consumption of substances such as coffee, tea, cola, tobacco, red wine and so on. Their pigments settle into the enamel and cause discolouration there. Certain antibiotics or too much fluoride during tooth formation can also cause tooth discolouration. So-called dental fluorosis, for example, is caused by drinking water very high in fluoride, fluoride tablets, or frequently swallowing fluoride toothpaste during childhood.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is Teeth Whitening Possible Despite Dental Prosthetics?

bloecke.text: In principle, bleaching can only lighten the shade of natural teeth. Dental prosthetics such as implants, veneers, crowns and fillings do not change colour during bleaching. Our expert team in implantology recommends carrying out bleaching before new dental prosthetics are fitted. If this isn't possible, fillings, crowns, veneers and bridges can be replaced after bleaching.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can a Single Dark Tooth Be Bleached?

bloecke.text: In principle, even just one single tooth can be bleached by a dentist, for example, a tooth that has had root canal treatment and become dark. Dentists often use so-called internal bleaching for this. The tooth is whitened from the inside. Whether this method is suitable is clarified after a thorough examination, and we'll explain the procedure and alternatives to you in detail. Get in touch, make use of our service and book an appointment today.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Does Bleaching Cost in Berlin at KU64?

bloecke.text: The price of bleaching depends on the chosen bleaching method, the number of teeth being whitened, the desired degree of whitening, and any preliminary treatments or other services, such as professional teeth cleaning. Before treatment, you always receive a transparent, individual cost plan, so you know exactly what costs to expect.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do Health Insurance Providers Cover the Cost of Bleaching?

bloecke.text: Teeth bleaching at the dentist is a purely cosmetic and not a medical procedure. For this reason, health insurance providers don't cover the cost of the treatment. Things are different with supplementary dental insurance: it usually covers the cost of bleaching at the dentist every two years.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which Is Better: Home Bleaching or Bleaching at the Practice?

bloecke.text: Whether bleaching at the practice or home bleaching is more suitable for you depends on your personal preferences.

In most cases, we recommend teeth bleaching at the practice if you want a quickly visible, optimally controlled result. Here, we evaluate your dental data, such as dental health, starting shade and sensitivity, and can adapt the concentration and process very precisely to suit.
Home bleaching is a good option if your discolouration is milder, if you have sensitive teeth, or if you'd prefer to carry out whitening step by step at home.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is Digital Smile Design?

bloecke.text: Digital Smile Design is a dental treatment concept that originated in the USA and Brazil. In these countries, aesthetic dentistry has been developed with particular rigour for many years. At KU64, we combine this international concept with our commitment to quality and a clear focus on natural-looking results.

Our team regularly undergoes further training in modern DSD workflows, directly with the developers of the concept, Dr Christian Coachman and Dr Michael Apa, on site in Miami, in order to bring current methods and standards straight into practice. For you as a patient, this means comprehensible planning and a result that doesn't just look beautiful. It also feels right, because it suits you as well as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The right time: before a major change is carried out

bloecke.text: Digital Smile Design is particularly useful when a major restoration or overhaul of the teeth is planned – and when several measures in the mouth are being carried out by the dentist. This can include, for example, veneers, crowns, bridges or implants. Often, various treatment options and materials need to be weighed up, and decisions made that will change and improve the appearance of your smile for many years to come.

Rather than relying solely on a feeling or a rough idea, at KU64 we begin with structured planning. Using photos, video recordings and digital scans, Digital Smile Design creates a simulation as a test run of your possible result. This gives you, as a patient, a kind of trial run before the first step is carried out. This creates confidence and reduces uncertainty. In this way, it helps us jointly define a target image that you truly feel comfortable with.
With Digital Smile Design, you gain planning confidence, precision and a result with real presence – one that lets you come across exactly as you wish.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Nervous patients welcome

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Step by step to the perfect smile with Digital Smile Design

bloecke.text: Together with your dentist, you design your new smile directly on the computer in our practice. The KU64 specialists plan your dental restoration step by step and offer you optimal care for your dental issues.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Getting to know each other & preliminary examination

bloecke.text: A comprehensive dental restoration must be carefully prepared and tailored to the needs of the patient. First, we get to know you and discuss your ideas before the dental treatment begins. The dentist takes time for your concerns and addresses your wishes individually.

After the personal conversation, a thorough examination follows so that your dental status and oral health can be closely assessed. Depending on your needs, dental X-rays and models of your teeth are made in order to tailor the later steps of a dental restoration or cosmetic improvement precisely to your dental profile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Personal photo session

bloecke.text: Next, we take you to our photo studio. In a short photo session, we take pictures of you and your smile. These images are evaluated by the KU64 specialists in collaboration with our dental technicians.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Professional Digital Smile Design

bloecke.text: Using a special process, we design your smile on the computer with the help of professional software and compare it to your current situation. The Digital Smile Design result is then prepared for you as a wax-up (a removable trial mock-up).

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Individual wax model

bloecke.text: At your next visit, the wax-up is tried in and the cosmetic test drive can begin. Photos and videos are taken of this so you can see for yourself how your new smile looks. Together with you, we analyse shape, colour and overall impression. Changes are made directly on the wax-up until your desired smile is achieved.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 5. Preparing for the smile transformation

bloecke.text: Together with you, we discuss the necessary treatment steps and costs, as well as possible alternatives for the new dental restoration. Whether ceramic veneers (also known as porcelain laminates or ceramic facings), crowns, bridges, inlays, fillings, teeth whitening or tooth correction using a splint – at our KU64 practice, we cover the entire spectrum of dental treatment at the highest quality!
