abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQ: The most important questions about Digital Smile Design
What is the Digital Smile System?

bloecke.text: In aesthetic dentistry, the term Digital Smile System (DSS) refers to a digital planning and visualisation system that uses facial photos and videos, often together with additional 3D scan data, to virtually design and verify a planned smile. This provides an authentic visual impression of various treatment options before veneers, crowns or other dental restorations are carried out. A typical workflow involves a 2D smile analysis (photo/video) that is then translated into 3D planning, in order to better align and communicate the aesthetics and later implementation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How does Digital Smile Design differ from normal aesthetic dental treatment?

bloecke.text: With Digital Smile Design, the result is first digitally planned and visualised before any treatment is carried out. This makes the outcome more predictable and allows patients to actively participate in designing their own smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much does treatment with Digital Smile Design cost?

bloecke.text: The costs of Digital Smile Design cannot be stated as a flat rate, as they depend on the scope of planning and, above all, on the subsequent implementation of planned measures such as veneers or dentures. The scope, duration and chosen materials are decisive, so prices can vary considerably depending on the starting situation. You will receive a binding treatment and cost plan listing all costs and any personal contribution after the examination and individual planning during your consultation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which treatments can be planned using Digital Smile Design?

bloecke.text: DSD is often used as a planning tool for various aesthetic treatments, such as:
Veneers
Teeth whitening (bleaching)
Dentures
Orthodontic tooth correction

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is Digital Smile Design permanent?

bloecke.text: No – Digital Smile Design (DSD) is not a permanent treatment, but a digital planning concept. How long-lasting the result is depends on the treatment that is planned and initiated with DSD (for example, veneers, crowns, whitening or orthodontics): some solutions last many years with good care, but are generally not permanent and require regular checks and maintenance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does treatment with Digital Smile Design take?

bloecke.text: The duration depends on the planned treatment. Digital planning usually takes just a few appointments, while the subsequent implementation – for example with veneers or dentures – can take several weeks.

prophylaxe-4-0.titel: Early Detection of Periodontal Disease with the Periosafe Test (aMMP-8 Test)

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Implant Safe Centre

bloecke.text: Periodontal degeneration progresses gradually and often goes unnoticed for a long time. KU64 is a certified Implant Safe Centre. To detect tissue breakdown in the gums at an early stage, the experts at KU64 use the Periosafe test. This helps prevent disease and improve dental hygiene.

For over 30 years, KU64 has supported you in prevention and prophylaxis for oral health. In keeping with our values, we focus on prevention through professional, modern teeth cleaning (No-Pain Prophylaxis) and regular check-ups by our specialists.

Current research shows just how important this is. Experts estimate that around 28 million people in Germany have periodontitis requiring treatment. One in two people over 40 is affected. Yet only around one million people are actually receiving treatment.

The PerioSafe rapid test detects undiscovered periodontal inflammation before any tissue breakdown even occurs in the structures supporting the teeth. This allows our specialists to initiate treatment at an early stage and use follow-up tests to check and confirm the success of treatment.
Our practice team, and especially our dentists, are happy to advise you about PerioSafe and how you can banish the troublesome issue of periodontitis from your life for good.
Book an appointment for the test now on 030-8647320 or use our online booking system!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The health risk of inflammation around implants

bloecke.text: Implant wearers in particular should have their inflammation levels checked regularly. A recent study in the field of periodontology shows that a quarter of all implants already show signs of inflammation (peri-implantitis) after just nine years. Nearly 70 per cent of all implant patients, it turns out, suffer largely unnoticed from inflammation (periodontitis, gingivitis) and the early stages of bone loss around their implants.

This bone loss is triggered by metalloproteinase, a proteolytic enzyme involved in the breakdown of collagen. This enzyme can therefore also be used to prove that the breakdown process has already begun, long before any symptoms appear.

As a certified Implant Safe Centre, we have the know-how to support you fully in keeping your implants healthy. With new technology in oral diagnostics and tailor-made prophylaxis, the Implant Safe concept ensures healthy implants for life and spares you inconvenience and follow-up costs for your high-quality dental restorations. The new, modern rapid tests from Dentognostics are an extremely effective way for us to look after you comprehensively when it comes to your dental restorations.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does the Periosafe test/aMMP-8 test do?

bloecke.text: PerioSafe from Dentognostics is the world's first rapid test for the early detection of hidden breakdown processes in the gums. PerioSafe can be particularly helpful for at-risk groups, revealing previously undetected periodontal inflammation together with the granulocytes involved. Otherwise, these might not become obviously visible via probing or X-ray until months or even years later. This gives you a quick overview of the state of your oral hygiene, and our dentists can start treatment early, ideally long before symptoms would appear.

For the first time, we can carry out this enzyme diagnostic test in just 20 minutes, right there in the treatment chair, and use it to determine the need for treatment quickly and precisely with a Periodontal Screening Index (PSI). Afterwards, and as part of follow-up care, a repeat test can provide evidence that the tissue breakdown process has been reduced through the therapeutic measures taken.
The German Dental Association (DZV) has reviewed the scientific basis and benefits of this method and, as a result, explicitly recommends that it be reimbursed by insurers.

To make our prophylaxis programme for your implants as successful as possible, it also makes sense to check your bone metabolism. This is negatively affected by potentially undetected diabetes and by too low a vitamin D level. We can now test for both.

Early detection is particularly important for dental implant wearers. To make our prophylaxis programme for your implants as successful as possible, it also makes sense to check your bone metabolism. This is negatively affected by potentially undetected diabetes and by too low a vitamin D level. We can now test for both.
We charge 64 euros for the Implant Safe test, 49 euros for the vitamin D test, and 49 euros for the diabetes test as well.
If you're interested, just mention this at your next prophylaxis appointment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The connection between mouth and body

bloecke.text: Numerous clinical studies, as well as close interdisciplinary collaboration between doctors of various specialities, demonstrate and confirm the link between periodontal inflammation (periodontitis) in the mouth and the following conditions:
diabetes
endocarditis and cardiovascular disease
rheumatoid arthritis
osteoporosis
inflammation around endoprostheses, such as artificial hip joints
respiratory conditions and chronic lung disease
but also unfulfilled wishes to have children and premature birth

This shows just how significant these issues are for your health: monitoring your oral hygiene using suitable products such as the Periosafe rapid test is an important factor in actively preventing chronic disease and supporting a healthy immune system. In practice, this means our oral health experts near you should regularly check the health of your mouth and teeth. It's best to ask about an appointment for advice and active prevention today.

Of course, the foundation for maintaining the health of your mouth and teeth is regular brushing with toothpaste, and perhaps also using mouthwash as part of your daily personal care. This removes the harmful bacteria that attack the gums and can lead to tissue breakdown. Exercise and getting enough vitamins in your diet also help support good periodontal health. Even so, this is only the foundation for comprehensive prevention, so that serious damage to teeth, dental restorations and gums can be avoided. Regular testing is essential for this.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prevention-focused dentistry – early detection saves teeth and saves money

bloecke.text: We recommend that all patients over the age of 35 have regular tests, since early periodontal detection significantly reduces the risk of tooth loss too. Oral health and regular prevention are important, and more affordable than dental restorations. While periodontal treatment is covered by most health insurers, you often have to pay for dental restorations yourself.

If your test result is positive, you can be enrolled in our Perio-Prevention Programme. Here, an interdisciplinary team of experts works intensively to reduce your periodontitis risk factors, so that you either recover quickly, or better still, stay healthy and never become ill in the first place!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Especially important for people with chronic conditions

bloecke.text: People with chronic conditions, such as
diabetics,
people with rheumatism, and
cardiovascular patients

develop periodontitis more often, and when they do, the disease tends to progress far more severely than in people without these risk factors. With the PerioSafe oral health test, which our specialists can carry out for you conveniently in just 5 minutes, aMMP-8 technology lets you find out at an early stage whether tissue or bone loss is taking place. This is of immense value.

If your test result is positive, you can discuss and take suitable measures with your dentist at KU64 at an early stage, so that periodontitis doesn't destroy any further valuable tissue, and so that any gum pockets are identified and treated.

In principle, you can carry out the test yourself at home, obtaining it from a pharmacy with a prescription from us that you can redeem there. However, we're happy to carry out the rapid test directly at the practice and discuss the next steps with you straight away afterwards.
Incidentally, our prevention programme also reduces your risk of heart attack and stroke, and improves the treatability of rheumatoid arthritis and diabetes.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Unfulfilled wishes to have children and premature birth

bloecke.text: Couples hoping to have children in particular benefit enormously from our comprehensive prevention programme. Not only can it save teeth, it can also significantly improve overall health, to the point where a long-awaited pregnancy can then occur. This is because oral health is a key factor in overall health.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: KU64 is Germany's first Implant Safe Centre

bloecke.text: In 2022, KU64 became the first dental practice in Germany to receive "Implant Safe Centre" certification from the Deutsche Mundgesundheitsstiftung (German Oral Health Foundation, DMS). We are now Berlin's first PerioPrevention Centre, and one of only a few in the whole of Germany. This is a certification in the field of immunological diagnostic technology.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What were we recognised for?

bloecke.text: A simple saliva test with a marker can now reliably detect impending inflammation around an implant up to 24 months before any damage appears, with a predictive accuracy of 94 per cent. Clinical studies show that targeted treatment and individual prophylaxis can prevent serious consequences. This stops, or significantly slows, inflammation around the implant.

This is scientifically proven: researchers at the universities of Marburg, Rome and Helsinki have provided scientific evidence for the effectiveness of the Implant Safe concept in clinical studies. Long-term studies from the Netherlands show that inflammation around implants could be stopped, or at least significantly slowed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about the Periosafe test
WHAT IS the Periosafe test?

bloecke.text: This is a rapid test to improve oral health. We therefore offer this biomarker test to every patient at low cost with every prophylaxis appointment. The rapid test with the perio marker even provides early detection of diabetes. And best of all, it doesn't hurt at all – just a little saliva is enough! Naturally, it's part of our service to carry out the test right here at our practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT does the test do FOR MY oral health AND oral hygiene

bloecke.text: The patented, state-of-the-art saliva diagnostic technology behind this test helps you preserve your teeth, protect your implants and maintain your overall health. It allows periodontal disease to be detected and treated extremely early, well before tissue damage with long-lasting consequences can occur.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT does aMMP-8 mean?

bloecke.text: The abbreviation aMMP-8 stands for "activated matrix metalloproteinase 8". This is the name for a naturally occurring enzyme in the body that breaks down collagen. Detecting this enzyme in the mouth using the aMMP-8 test is an indication that periodontitis is developing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT IS a biomarker?

bloecke.text: A so-called biomarker, as measured by the Periosafe test, is a general medical term for physical characteristics that can be determined. Many examinations carried out at a doctor's surgery or hospital are, in fact, biomarker tests. The best-known biomarker is body temperature, which you've probably measured yourself to check whether you have a fever.

More complex disease relationships require rapid tests or laboratory tests that can detect specific proteins and messenger substances in bodily fluids. In the case of the aMMP-8 test, it's a particular enzyme that indicates a potentially harmful inflammatory reaction has started in the mouth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW does the test work?

bloecke.text: The test is very straightforward to carry out. It's performed quickly and painlessly by our qualified staff. A saliva sample is taken from the mouth, and the result is available just 5 minutes later.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHO NEEDS the Periosafe test?

bloecke.text: As a rule, we recommend that all our patients aged 35 and over have their oral inflammation levels checked regularly. Depending on your condition and any pre-existing conditions, this should be done more often, or may only be needed occasionally.

Early diagnosis of periodontitis is especially important for patients with implants. In the most severe cases, degeneration of periodontal tissue can lead to the loss of the implant. However, the earlier it is detected, the better it can be treated.

Tissue degeneration is also a very important issue for people with chronic conditions, as they suffer from this disease more often and experience more severe progression. But here too, the same applies: with timely diagnosis, treatment options are very good.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW OFTEN should I get tested?

bloecke.text: How often you should be tested depends on your individual situation, based on the condition of your teeth and mouth. Your dentist will discuss all of this with you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT does this test cost?

bloecke.text: The cost for NHS-equivalent and private-paying patients is 64 euros. Private patients have the invoice reimbursed. The medical profession has recommended that the cost be covered, but unfortunately statutory health insurers have so far not followed this recommendation.

Early detection is particularly important for dental implant wearers. To make our prophylaxis programme for your implants as successful as possible, it also makes sense to check your bone metabolism. This is negatively affected by potentially undetected diabetes and by too low a vitamin D level. We can now test for both.
We charge 64 euros for the Implant Safe test, 49 euros for the vitamin D test, and 49 euros for the diabetes test as well.
If you're interested, just mention this at your next prophylaxis appointment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: ARE THERE prescriptions FOR this test?

bloecke.text: It is possible to obtain the test as a private prescription, similar to non-prescription medicines, either by mail order or in person at a pharmacy. However, we keep it in stock at our practice and can carry it out on the spot, so this isn't necessary.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW can implants NOT BE "safe"?

bloecke.text: Implants have the great advantage that they can never develop decay. They also never need root canal treatment. The only condition that can prove their undoing is so-called peri-implantitis, an inflammation around the implant. If detected too late, this can lead to the loss of the implant.

The innovation in treatment and prevention lies in the fact that new technology has allowed us to significantly improve diagnostics for you. Even before any damage has occurred, it's now possible to determine whether bone loss is likely to happen soon.
As a qualified Implant Safe Centre, we combine systematic early detection with prophylaxis tailored to you individually, to keep your implants healthy for life!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT IS Dentognostics?

bloecke.text: This is the name of the company that developed and markets the Periosafe test. The German manufacturer is based in Solingen. Dentognostics GmbH specialises in diagnosing inflammatory reactions that can attack and damage the structures supporting the teeth. Thanks to the rapid tests and laboratory tests they offer, these can be detected at a very early stage and treated accordingly. The tests are sold under the trade name "Periosafe".

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHO IS the Deutsche Mundgesundheitsstiftung?

bloecke.text: The Deutsche Mundgesundheitsstiftung GmbH (German Oral Health Foundation, DMS) is committed to the public good. It carries out educational work for German doctors, patients and consumers on the subject of inflammatory conditions of the oral cavity. In this context, it awards the "Implant Safe Centre" certificate to dental practices that can meet the high scientific standards required for comprehensive prevention among patients with implants.

bloecke.text: For precise results and fewer appointments, we plan All-on-4 treatment at our KU64 practice with digital precision – efficiently and predictably.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When eating, speaking and smiling become a struggle – All-on-4 restores confidence

bloecke.text: Does this sound familiar? Wobbly dentures, sore spots, constant frustration with adhesive cream. You avoid crunchy foods, speak more cautiously and smile less often, worried that someone might "notice something". Perhaps you still have a few remaining teeth that keep causing problems: inflammation, very loose fit, some needing to be extracted. Everything revolves around temporary fixes and appointments, while your wish for a stable, fixed solution for your dental restoration keeps growing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is All-on-4?

bloecke.text: The registered treatment concept All-on-4 is the original oral surgery treatment concept, developed at the MALO CLINIC in Lisbon, for rehabilitating toothless or soon-to-be toothless jaws with dental implants. Unlike standard therapy, the method requires very few implants to fully restore your set of teeth.

The concept is internationally established, and medium- to long-term clinical data has documented the impressive longevity of fixed dental restorations following All-on-4 treatment. Only partner clinics are permitted to carry out the treatment, in order to ensure and monitor the highest treatment standards and long-term benefit for patients.

The core principle of the All-on-4 method: a full-arch bridge fixed in place by dental implants, serving as the dental restoration. It fully restores the chewing function and appearance of the entire jaw. This is made possible by the strategic implant distribution that gives the method its name. Two implants are placed in the front tooth area, and two more in the back tooth area. Depending on the situation, six implants are sometimes required in the lower jaw, which is why the concept is occasionally also referred to as All-on-6. Often, no prior bone augmentation is required for patients.

Under certain conditions, such as sufficient stability, the All-on-4 treatment concept allows for immediate provision with a screwed-in, fixed temporary bridge – often fitted on the very day of the surgery.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is All-on-4 the right solution for?

bloecke.text: Are you tired of loose, removable dentures or hopelessly advanced periodontitis affecting your remaining teeth? With implants supporting your new dental restoration, the All-on-4 procedure can make your wish for a beautiful smile and a fixed set of teeth come true. The All-on-4 treatment was developed precisely for these situations: four strategically placed implants in the upper jaw, or six implants in the lower jaw, support a fixed full-arch bridge as a complete replacement for your teeth – planned digitally in 3D and carried out gently.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are the benefits for patients?

bloecke.text: The full-arch bridge fully restores your row of teeth with a dental restoration. In very many cases, you receive a temporary restoration on the very first day of treatment, which is also already fixed in place. You regain stability, appearance and confidence in everyday life: with a firm bite when eating and clear speech.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are the benefits of implant-supported dental restorations?

bloecke.text: Dental implants are among the most proven solutions for fixed dental restorations in modern implantology. Implant placement enables a stable, aesthetic restoration even in complex cases. The benefits range from a secure bite and natural speech to the preservation of bone. In implant-supported restorations, surgical precision is just as important as prosthetic planning.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What materials are used for All-on-4 restorations?

bloecke.text: The temporary full-arch bridge is often made from the thermoplastic polymer polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA). The final dental restoration can, for example, be made from zirconium oxide or titanium/acrylic constructions. The choice depends on the findings, aesthetics, load-bearing requirements and care.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are the requirements?

bloecke.text: Before any treatment, our dental team at KU64 in Berlin or Potsdam checks the individual requirements for this treatment. The All-on-4 method is only the treatment of choice for patients with a toothless or soon-to-be toothless jaw. Your jawbone must be healthy enough to support several implants. Stable general health is also a requirement, so that the implants have a good chance of healing successfully. Reliable oral hygiene and a willingness to attend follow-up care are also essential for the success of the treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How does the treatment for fixed teeth in one day work?

bloecke.text: At KU64, the All-on-4 concept is based on precise digital 3D planning, which allows us to individually tailor each implant to your jaw and ensure the best possible outcome. This precise preparatory work ensures that the dental implants in the upper and lower jaw are optimally positioned to support a stable, fixed bridge – often on the very same day!

The digital workflow in implantology saves time and increases the precision of the procedure, as every step from planning to fitting the dental restoration is perfectly coordinated. This means less strain on you and a quicker return to your everyday life – with a radiant smile!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment process step by step

bloecke.text: Contact and appointment: initial consultation at our practice in Berlin or Potsdam, medical history, goals, preliminary cost information.
Diagnostics: clinical examination, CBCT/3D X-ray, intraoral scan/photos, bite analysis.
3D planning and suitability check: virtual implant positions, checking bone availability, decision on whether immediate provision is possible or bone augmentation is required.
Consultation and surgical planning: procedure, sedation/anaesthesia options, medication; scheduling the surgery date.
Preparation: professional preliminary treatment, digital data/impressions for the temporary bridge, starting the laboratory workflow.
Surgery day: extraction of any remaining teeth if necessary, placement of the implants, screwing in the fixed temporary full-arch bridge, checking occlusion and fit.
Post-surgery instructions: pain management/oral hygiene plan, dietary recommendations, emergency contact, follow-up appointment.
Early check-up in the first few days: wound check, bite adjustment, hygiene coaching.
Healing phase: gentle diet, regular check-ups.
Final restoration after a few months: fabrication and fitting of the final bridge.
Aftercare: professional implant maintenance, X-ray check-ups, interdental hygiene, night guard if needed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The benefits of All-on-4 treatment at KU64

bloecke.text: Fixed teeth in one day: in most cases, we can fit a temporary dental restoration directly after implant placement, until the implants have integrated.
State-of-the-art technology: thanks to digital planning, we can carry out the procedure with particular precision and individual care.
Fewer sessions: thanks to the minimally invasive approach and high planning reliability, fewer dental appointments are often needed, which reduces costs.

Longevity and stability: the patented procedures used for the dental restoration from Straumann (Smile in a Box and Comfour) stand for quality and offer you a long-lasting solution for your dental restoration.
Individual consultation: we show you the options based on your personal situation and help you find your new smile with All-on-4!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Contact and consultation

bloecke.text: Say goodbye to wobbly dentures. With the evidence-based All-on-4 concept, you get a fixed dental restoration at KU64 quickly and safely. In many cases, you benefit from fixed temporary teeth on the very same day, which immediately gives you back more quality of life, and confidence when eating, speaking and smiling. Don't wait any longer for your new smile: book your initial consultation now and check all the information and details!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQ: The most important questions about All-on-4
Do you offer the All-on-4 method in Berlin?

bloecke.text: Yes. Our practice in Berlin offers the All-on-4 method as a plannable treatment for patients with toothless or soon-to-be toothless jaws. Through this treatment, all teeth can be replaced by the dentist with a fixed bridge anchored to the jawbone. Our specialists will individually assess whether this modern method is suitable for you. Simply get in touch with us. Book an appointment online around the clock or by phone seven days a week for a consultation and any further information.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does the All-on-4 procedure cost?

bloecke.text: The cost of the procedure depends on your individual findings, the number of dental implants, the materials used, and the extent of preparatory and follow-up treatment; a transparent cost estimate provides clarity. The cost of your All-on-4 treatment is individual and depends on the findings. The procedure combines reliable processes with plannable results – from preparation through to implant placement. This means costs can also be calculated very reliably in advance.
The total cost is made up of the costs for:
diagnostics and digital 3D planning
surgical steps such as extraction of any remaining teeth
bone augmentation, if required
the implant placement
the anaesthesia
laboratory and material costs per implant, as well as for the temporary and final bridge

Statutory health insurers usually contribute towards the cost of dental restorations. The costs of implantology services usually have to be paid privately, or can be covered by private supplementary insurance if you have one. After your initial examination at our practice in Berlin, our dentist will give you a transparent cost estimate for the procedure, breaking down the parts covered by your health insurer and the share you need to pay yourself.

bloecke.text: You can get in touch with our practice either by phone or online to arrange an appointment. Feel free to use our round-the-clock appointment booking via Doctolib. Our team will discuss any previous findings with you, answer your questions about the method and arrange a suitable appointment in Berlin or Potsdam. This allows patients to begin treatment without any detours. Our practice in Berlin is open to patients seven days a week.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What exactly does All-on-4 mean?

bloecke.text: All-on-4 is the oral surgery concept developed at the MALO CLINIC for a full-arch bridge covering the entire jaw. A fixed bridge is supported by four implants – straight at the front, angled at the back – replacing the entire set of teeth in the jaw.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How does All-on-4 differ from a full denture?

bloecke.text: Unlike a regular denture, All-on-4 is fixed in the mouth using dental implants, aiming for a stable bite on the artificial teeth with a very high level of comfort for speaking and eating.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is All-on-4 a protected term?

bloecke.text: Yes. All-on-4 is the complete medical treatment concept in oral surgery. A fixed four-implant solution generally makes it possible to restore the entire set of teeth in the jaw with an implant-supported dental restoration. The concept is registered as a protected trademark by the MALO CLINIC in Lisbon. This ensures consistent treatment standards and standardised monitoring of treatment success and aftercare across all practices permitted to offer the concept.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Who is All-on-4 suitable for?

bloecke.text: The procedure is suitable for patients who are toothless or soon-to-be toothless, including those with remaining teeth that cannot be preserved. It offers those affected a fixed alternative to a full denture. Our experts individually assess suitability for the dental implants required, based on your findings, the condition of your jawbone and your general health.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do I need bone augmentation for this?

bloecke.text: Artificial bone augmentation is often not required for fitting the new teeth: by placing the rear implants at an angle, existing bone can be used optimally. However, augmentation may still be necessary in individual cases.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is general anaesthesia required for the treatment?

bloecke.text: General anaesthesia is not necessarily required. Depending on the case, local anaesthesia, intravenous sedation or general anaesthesia may be used for the surgery. Your treating doctor will discuss all the options and the treatment process with you in detail and is available to answer any questions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What risks and complications are possible?

bloecke.text: As with any dental restoration, problems that can occur after fitting include bacterial infections such as mucositis/peri-implantitis and mechanical wear such as loosening of screws, material wear and denture wear. The biggest risk factors for these are inadequate oral hygiene and smoking. Daily care and regular follow-up appointments significantly reduce the risk of these problems.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does the dental restoration last?

bloecke.text: Long-term data from the MALO CLINIC show very good durability for the All-on-4 concept. Up to 98.8 per cent of the dentures and around 93 per cent of the implants were reportedly still functioning after an 18-year study period.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How do I care for an All-on-4 bridge?

bloecke.text: Cleaning is similar to that of natural teeth: brushing twice a day, plus cleaning between teeth with special dental floss or interdental brushes. You should also have your dental restoration examined by a dentist at regular intervals. X-ray check-ups are generally recommended every one to two years as well.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental filling – explained simply

bloecke.text: A filling, commonly also called a 'plomb', is used to seal a damaged tooth or a defect that has formed in the tooth. After the dentist has removed the diseased tooth tissue, the resulting cavity is filled with a special material. This artificial filling replaces the lost tooth structure, stabilises the tooth, and restores its natural shape as well as its function when chewing. Without treatment, bacteria could continue to penetrate the tooth and cause more severe pain or inflammation in the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When your tooth needs a filling

bloecke.text: Fillings are used when:
your tooth has a hole or a spot of decay
small fractures such as breaks, cracks or chips exist in your tooth
your old filling has fallen out
your existing filling is leaking or damaged
parts of your tooth structure have been lost due to wear or erosion

When such damage occurs, typical problems and symptoms such as pain when chewing, sensitivity to cold, heat or sweetness, as well as a rough or unfamiliar feeling on the tooth, can become noticeable. Therefore, have affected teeth examined and treated by a dentist as early as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The right filling for every defect

bloecke.text: A hole in the tooth or a chipped corner on a front tooth is no cause for concern and can be treated gently and unobtrusively without immediately requiring dentures. Depending on the size of the defect, the position of the tooth, and the desired durability, we choose the right treatment together with you – from temporary solutions to direct fillings to individually made inlays.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Direct fillings

bloecke.text: With a direct filling, the filling material is placed straight into your tooth. After the decay has been removed, your dentist shapes the filling directly in the tooth and hardens the material there.
Advantages:
treatment is usually possible in just one appointment
tooth-coloured materials ensure an unobtrusive result
gentle treatment, as only a small amount of healthy tooth structure needs to be removed

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Indirect fillings (inlays)

bloecke.text: For indirect fillings, so-called inlays, we first make the filling individually for your tooth outside the mouth in our dental laboratory, similar to dentures, and then fit it precisely afterwards. An inlay is usually used for larger defects in the tooth, when a simple direct filling would no longer provide sufficient stability.
Advantages:
very precise fit due to individual manufacture
particularly long-lasting and stable, even for larger defects
highly aesthetic result that closely resembles the natural tooth

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Provisional fillings

bloecke.text: With a provisional filling, your tooth is temporarily sealed. This solution is used when a final treatment is being prepared, for example before an inlay is fitted, or when the tooth is to be observed for a while after treatment.
Advantages:
quick and straightforward treatment of the tooth
protection of the tooth until the final treatment
bridges the gap until a permanent filling is fitted

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The right filling materials for your tooth

bloecke.text: Are you looking for a suitable filling? When treating decay or damaged tooth structure, we offer you various materials for your filling. We decide together which filling is best for you, depending on the condition of your tooth and your personal requirements regarding durability and aesthetics. We would be happy to advise you individually at our practice on the various options.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Composite or plastic filling

bloecke.text: The composite or plastic filling is one of the most commonly used fillings today. It consists of about 80 percent very fine ceramic, glass and quartz particles, which provide stability, plus around 20 percent plastic content for flexible processing. The material is placed directly into the tooth and hardened in layers using UV light, allowing it to adapt very well to the natural tooth shape. For an aesthetically optimal result, we make composite or plastic fillings in your natural tooth colour.
Particularly suitable for: small to medium-sized defects as well as visible areas such as front teeth
Advantages: unobtrusive appearance, gentle treatment, and treatment is usually possible in just one session, immediately load-bearing
Durability: 6 to 8 years

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Ceramic filling

bloecke.text: The ceramic filling is one of the highest-quality fillings and is an aesthetic alternative to composite fillings. Compared to plastic fillings, ceramic stands out mainly through its high stability and shape retention, even under heavy chewing loads, as well as its natural tooth appearance.

Ceramic can be used both as a direct filling and – especially for larger defects – in the form of inlays or onlays. At KU64, we make the inlays individually in our own dental laboratory using the modern CEREC procedure and then fit them precisely into your tooth. Thanks to the precise manufacturing, an exact fit is achieved, while the tooth-coloured ceramic blends almost invisibly into your smile. The material is also particularly biocompatible and well tolerated.
Particularly suitable for: medium to large defects, especially in the back teeth as well as where high aesthetic demands apply
Advantages: very long-lasting, similarly stable to natural teeth and therefore largely resistant to breakage and wear, perfect fit, excellent aesthetics, very good tolerability
Durability: 10 to 15 years or longer

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gold filling

bloecke.text: Gold fillings are among the particularly long-lasting treatments if your tooth needs to remain highly load-bearing permanently. In most cases, we repair your tooth with an individually made gold inlay or onlay: like ceramic fillings, we make your gold filling to fit precisely in our own dental laboratory and then fit it firmly into your tooth. In rare cases, gold can also be worked directly into the tooth.

Compared to other materials, gold offers very high stability and seals your tooth very tightly and reliably, resulting in a dependable treatment in the long term. Due to its visible colour and higher cost, we recommend gold fillings mainly for the non-visible back teeth area and will advise you individually on this.

Particularly suitable for: medium to large defects in the back teeth, especially with high chewing loads or teeth grinding. Advantages: very long durability, high stability, reliable marginal seal, very good tolerability. Durability: 10 to 30 years or longer

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Cement and glass ionomer filling

bloecke.text: We use cement and glass ionomer fillings (GIC) when your tooth needs to be treated quickly and easily – for example as a long-term provisional, for tooth-neck defects, root decay, or in baby teeth. Cement and glass ionomer fillings (GIC) consist of a combination of glass particles (including silicate glass) and a special cement acid that hardens directly in the tooth.

The material also continuously releases fluoride, which additionally protects your tooth from decay. At the same time, it adheres well to the tooth surface and allows for gentle treatment. These fillings also represent a cost-effective alternative to high-quality plastic or ceramic fillings.
Particularly suitable for: temporary treatments, baby teeth, tooth-neck areas or root decay
Advantages: quick application, additional protection against decay through fluoride, good adhesion to the tooth, subtle tooth-coloured appearance, good biological tolerability
Durability: approximately 2 to 3 years

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Compomer filling

bloecke.text: Compomer fillings combine properties of plastic (composite) and glass ionomer cement and are used mainly when a tooth-coloured, well-tolerated, and at the same time straightforward treatment is desired, for example in baby teeth or for smaller defects. The material is easy to work with and hardens under light.

Similar to glass ionomer cements, compomers release fluoride and can thus additionally help protect against decay. At the same time, they offer better aesthetics than classic cement fillings and blend visually unobtrusively into the tooth.
Particularly suitable for: baby teeth, smaller defects, low-load areas. Advantages: tooth-coloured appearance, fluoride release, good tolerability, gentle application
Durability: approximately 3 to 5 years

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Alkasite filling

bloecke.text: Alkasite fillings are a relatively new, metal-free filling material and are mainly used in the back teeth area – especially for larger defects. The material combines properties of plastic and cement, has a tooth-like colour and blends unobtrusively into the tooth. When hardening, alkasite releases minerals such as fluoride and calcium, which can additionally strengthen the tooth and protect against new decay. At the same time, the material offers good stability and is well tolerated. As a modern alternative to amalgam, alkasite combines functionality with a more discreet aesthetic.

Particularly suitable for: larger defects in the back teeth area, high chewing loads. Advantages: metal-free, tooth-like appearance, mineral release, good tolerability, straightforward application. Durability: approximately 5 to 10 years

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Amalgam filling

bloecke.text: The amalgam filling consists of a metal alloy with mercury and was long used as the standard in the back teeth area, as it is particularly durable and resilient. However, due to health and environmental concerns, amalgam is viewed critically today. Amalgam fillings have no longer been used in the EU since 1 January 2025. Mercury is also very noticeable in the mouth due to its metallic, dark colour.

At KU64, we have never used amalgam since our founding in 2005, relying instead on modern, tooth-coloured materials. If you still have amalgam fillings, we would be happy to advise you – if needed, we offer gentle removal of amalgam under protective measures.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment process: how your filling procedure works

bloecke.text: The dentists at KU64 guide you step by step through the treatment – precisely, gently and clearly:
Examination and consultation First, your tooth is thoroughly examined and, together with you, a decision is made about which filling material is most suitable.
Removal of damaged tooth structure We then carefully remove damaged areas of the tooth and decay, to create a stable base for the filling.
Preparation of the tooth The tooth is then carefully cleaned and dried, and the surface is specifically prepared so that the filling material can adhere securely and permanently.

Placing the filling The dentist then precisely places the filling in the tooth. Plastic is built up and hardened in layers. For an inlay, the individually made restoration is fitted precisely and permanently secured in the tooth.
Adjustment & check In the next step, we adjust the filling exactly to your bite and check that everything feels natural when biting.
Polishing Finally, the surface is smoothed and polished – for a pleasant feel and long durability.

The treatment usually takes 20 to 60 minutes and, thanks to modern methods, involves little pain. Do you have concerns about the treatment? Talk to us. Especially if you suffer from dental anxiety, you are in good hands at KU64. We specialise in treating anxious patients. Your dentist will guide you step by step in a calm, trusting atmosphere.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Your benefits for fillings at KU64
Precise planning with modern technology

bloecke.text: For your filling, we use digital diagnostics at KU64 such as 3D X-rays and modern analysis methods. This allows us to precisely assess the defect and optimally adapt the filling to your tooth and bite.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Specialised dentists for high-quality fillings

bloecke.text: Our dentists specialise in modern filling therapies and continuously further their training. This means you benefit from up-to-date materials and gentle treatment methods.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Experience for long-lasting results

bloecke.text: With over 20 years of experience, we ensure that your filling is functional, stable and aesthetically convincing – from diagnosis to the final adjustment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment tailored to you

bloecke.text: Our interdisciplinary and multilingual team enables clear consultation and individually tailored treatment, so that you always feel well looked after.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Experiencing pain during or after a filling?

bloecke.text: After a filling, the tooth may react temporarily with sensitivity. Patients report increased sensitivity to cold, heat or pressure. This pain occurs because the tooth first has to adjust to the new material.

Pain when chewing after a filling can also occur temporarily. Usually these complaints subside within a few days with thorough care. Even if a filling is too high, this can lead to noticeable discomfort when biting down. Typical symptoms are pressure pain, an unfamiliar bite sensation, or pain when chewing. In this case, the filling can usually be adjusted quickly and painlessly. Should the toothache after the filling last longer or even become more intense – especially pain after months – we recommend having the tooth checked.
If you are unsure how long pain after a filling is normal, get in touch with us – we will help you quickly and without complications.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Help your filling last a long time

bloecke.text: After your treatment, you can do a lot yourself to help your tooth settle down quickly after a filling:
Eating: Do not eat again until the anaesthetic has fully worn off. This helps you avoid injuries.
Smoking: Avoid smoking during the first few hours as much as possible, so as not to irritate the treated area.
Sport: Light activity is fine, but you should avoid intense exertion directly after treatment.
Dental care: Brush your teeth thoroughly as usual, but gently.

By the way: regular professional teeth cleaning is also worthwhile if you have fillings, as it keeps the filling margins clean and thus supports the durability and tightness of the restoration. If you have any questions about the health of your teeth, we are here for you at any time and are happy to help.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Costs and reimbursement for fillings

bloecke.text: The costs of a filling depend mainly on which material is best suited to your tooth and how large the defect is. At KU64, we discuss transparently with you before treatment what your filling will cost and which portions of the cost will be covered.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which filling does statutory health insurance pay for?

bloecke.text: Statutory health insurance covers a filling as a standard benefit if it is medically necessary. In the front and visible tooth area, a tooth-coloured plastic filling is usually free of charge. In the back teeth area, the insurer covers the cost of the standard treatment. This includes alternative, durable materials such as modern glass ionomer cements, compomers, or special self-adhesive plastics. If you choose higher-quality materials or techniques, you will need to make a co-payment for the filling.
If you are unsure which filling your statutory health insurer will pay for, we are happy to advise you personally and offer you comprehensive information and services on all options.

Until 2025, amalgam, which contains mercury, was also part of the standard treatment covered by statutory health insurers for the back teeth area. Today, however, amalgam is no longer used for health and environmental reasons and has been replaced by alternative materials.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – Frequently asked questions about fillings
What can I do if my filling has fallen out?

bloecke.text: If a filling has fallen out, provisional fillings from the pharmacy (e.g. Cavit) or home remedies are often considered as short-term solutions. These measures can temporarily cover the tooth, but do not provide a permanent or secure seal and do not reliably protect the tooth from further damage or bacteria. If an old amalgam filling has fallen out, this is usually not harmful to health in itself. However, it is important not to swallow loose pieces of amalgam fillings or continue chewing on them. Instead, have the tooth treated by your dentist as soon as possible. At KU64, you get an appointment quickly and a professional, long-term solution.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What types of fillings are there?

bloecke.text: Fundamentally, a distinction is made between direct and indirect fillings. Direct fillings are built up directly in the tooth and are suitable mainly for smaller to medium-sized defects. Indirect fillings are individually made outside the mouth and then fitted precisely afterwards. They are suitable for larger tooth damage.

The materials used are mainly plastic (composite), ceramic, gold, and cement or glass ionomer fillings. Amalgam fillings, which contain mercury, were commonly used in the past. Since 2025, amalgam is only provided in medically necessary exceptional cases. For children under 15, pregnant women and breastfeeding women, amalgam has already been banned since 2018. Which filling is suitable for you depends on the size of the defect, the position of the tooth, and your individual requirements.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which filling is best for teeth?

bloecke.text: There is no universal 'best' filling – what matters is what makes sense for your situation. Composite fillings are a proven, tooth-coloured solution for many smaller and medium-sized defects. Ceramic fillings offer particularly high aesthetics and durability, especially for larger defects. Gold fillings are considered very robust and long-lasting, but are usually used in the back teeth area. Health aspects such as tolerability and biocompatibility also play an important role in choosing the material. Your dentist at KU64 will advise you individually on which filling offers the best combination of function, durability, health, and aesthetics for your tooth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does it hurt to have a filling replaced?

bloecke.text: Replacing a filling is usually low-pain to painless. If needed, we anaesthetise the tooth locally so that you feel almost nothing during treatment. Only a slight pressure may be noticeable. After the procedure, the tooth may react temporarily with sensitivity, for example to cold or when chewing – these symptoms usually subside quickly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When can I eat again after a filling?

bloecke.text: After a filling, you can usually eat again once the anaesthetic has fully worn off. This helps you avoid accidentally biting your tongue or cheek. With plastic fillings, the tooth is usually immediately load-bearing. Nevertheless, we recommend chewing carefully in the first few hours and avoiding very hard or sticky foods.

If you are wondering how long you should avoid eating after a filling, the rule is: wait at least until the feeling in your mouth has fully returned – usually about 1 to 2 hours. For other materials or larger treatments, your dentist can give you an individual recommendation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does a filling last?

bloecke.text: The durability of a filling depends mainly on the material, the size of the defect, and your oral hygiene.
Plastic fillings (composite): approx. 6 to 8 years
Ceramic fillings: approx. 10 to 15 years or longer
Gold fillings: approx. 10 to 30 years or longer
Cement or glass ionomer fillings: approx. 2 to 3 years
Important: regular check-ups and good care of your teeth contribute significantly to your filling lasting as long as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Who covers the costs of a filling?

bloecke.text: For patients with statutory health insurance, the costs of a filling are covered by the health insurer if it is a medically necessary basic treatment. In the front tooth area, a tooth-coloured plastic filling is usually fully covered. In the back teeth area, the health insurers cover the standard treatment. If you choose a higher-quality or more aesthetically demanding material (e.g. ceramic or a more elaborate composite technique), you pay the difference as a co-payment.

For private patients, cost coverage depends on the respective tariff. Depending on the insurance, high-quality fillings are reimbursed fully or partially. Supplementary dental insurance can – depending on the tariff – also cover a large part of the costs of higher-quality fillings for statutorily insured patients, or significantly reduce the co-payment. At KU64, we advise you transparently on all costs and possible reimbursements before treatment.

wurzelkanalbehandlung.titel: Endodontics Berlin: Saving Your Own Teeth with Root Canal Treatment

bloecke.text: Severe toothache, swelling, sensitivity to pressure when biting, or heightened sensitivity to hot and cold foods can indicate inflammation of the tooth root. This is caused by bacteria that have infected the root canal system, usually as a result of decay or an accident. Root canal treatment can help remove the harmful germs and save the tooth. The endodontists at KU64 Berlin are here to support you with confidence, from clarifying your symptoms right through to treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Does Endodontics Mean?

bloecke.text: The term endodontics describes the systematic, expert treatment of inflamed tooth nerves and dead teeth. The tooth nerves lie inside (endo) the tooth, within what are known as root canals. This root canal system branches out finely, rather like the branches of a tree. Root canal treatment is correspondingly delicate and demanding.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gentle and Precise: Root Canal Treatment at KU64 Berlin

bloecke.text: During root canal treatment, the dentist uses specialist instruments to remove the nerve and any inflamed or dead tissue completely and thoroughly from the complex root canal system. The canal system is then widened so it can be sealed against bacteria with a filling made using gutta-percha (tree resin). As this procedure is highly intricate, the endodontics specialists at KU64 Berlin work with magnifying loupes fitted with integrated LED lighting and a surgical microscope. This gives our patients the highest level of precision and the reassurance that the dentist can truly identify and treat every canal — without unpleasant after-effects. For precise diagnostics in unclear situations, the dentists at KU64 Berlin use modern imaging techniques such as digital volume tomography (DVT) for 3D X-rays.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Signs of Nerve Inflammation

bloecke.text: Sensitivity to cold
Sensitivity when eating, especially with sweet foods
Pulling pain, sometimes radiating to other areas of the head
A feeling of pressure
The tooth feels too high when biting

Inflammation of the nerve tissue causes the affected tooth to die. The result is a dead tooth. Root canal treatment, or endodontic treatment, prevents this kind of tooth loss caused by inflammation. Instead, patients benefit from long-term preservation of the tooth, even after many years, and can avoid the need for dentures or other tooth replacement.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Causes of Inflamed Root Canals

bloecke.text: Tooth decay: Since decay is a bacterial condition, deep decay can allow bacteria to travel through the dentinal tubules into the tooth nerve and trigger inflammation there.
Gum pockets: Deep gum pockets, sometimes caused by periodontitis, can allow bacteria to penetrate the periodontal ligament space. An inflamed root tip can result.
Overloading: Physical strain, such as strong forces from grinding or clenching, can also irritate the nerve and lead to inflammation.

Disturbances in other body systems: As every tooth is connected via certain meridians to organs in the body, disturbances, for example in the intestines, can also be linked to an inflamed or dead tooth.

Discolouration of dead teeth, particularly a grey tinge, is caused by oxidised blood components that become deposited in the remaining dentine. The dentist can lighten such teeth again using so-called internal bleaching.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When Does Root Canal Treatment Become Necessary?

bloecke.text: At the centre of a healthy tooth lies the dental pulp, made up of blood vessels and nerves. If decay is deep, or if a large piece of the tooth breaks off, bacteria can reach the pulp. In rare cases, the pulp can become infected via a deep gum pocket. This leads to inflammation, which can be quite painful and irreversibly destroys the tissue. As the bacteria advance further, and as the breakdown products of the dying pulp — known as toxins — spread, the body mounts a defensive response around the root tip. This inflammation at the root can persist painlessly and unnoticed over a long period, acting as a so-called interference field that affects the relevant meridian. What's more, the inflammation can trigger symptoms — that is, a chronic inflammatory process — in far-flung parts of the body. The site of inflammation can turn acute at any time, ranging from severe discomfort when biting down to a painful abscess with swelling around the root tip.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Apicoectomy for Lasting Results

bloecke.text: The only way to preserve an affected tooth in the long term is root canal treatment, also known as endodontic treatment. Only a complete cleaning of the intricate root canal system, along with the thorough removal of harmful bacteria, metabolic by-products and remnants of the decayed pulp, will ensure the treatment succeeds in the long run. If bacteria remain in the root canal after endodontic therapy is complete, the site of inflammation in the jawbone around the root tip will often persist or even grow.
Apicoectomy in Berlin — precise, gentle, and aimed at saving your tooth

Sometimes even careful root canal treatment isn't enough to fully clear a deep-seated infection within the tooth. When our experienced endodontics specialists cannot resolve the cause through conventional root canal treatment alone, an apicoectomy is the final — but highly effective — step in treatment.

At our practice here on the Ku'damm, this microsurgical procedure is carried out by our highly qualified oral surgeons, maxillofacial surgeon Dr Dr Surian Herrmann and Dr Jiotis Hondralis MSc, specialist dentist for oral surgery. During an apicoectomy, under local anaesthetic, they remove the inflamed root tip and the surrounding infected tissue with particular thoroughness and care.

This is followed by a precise root filling to seal the root canal permanently and keep it bacteria-tight. This prevents germs from entering again — with the clear aim of preserving your natural tooth in the long term.

Thanks to state-of-the-art technology, extensive experience and a caring team, we're able to carry out this treatment in most cases with minimal pain and a swift recovery. So if you're looking in Berlin for a reliable, lasting solution to treat inflammation of the tooth root, you're in the best possible hands with us.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Our Goal: Healing and Preserving the Tooth

bloecke.text: Based on today's knowledge, there should be no compromises when it comes to root canal treatment. If the dentist doesn't carry out the treatment with absolute thoroughness, this inevitably worsens the prognosis for the affected tooth.

With the following professional measures used in modern root canal treatment, the endodontics team at KU64 Berlin achieves the greatest possible freedom from bacteria within the root canal system, giving the best prospects for long-term success:
Creating a sterile working field with a rubber dam, using sterile, single-use rotary canal preparation instruments made from highly flexible nickel-titanium
alloy, guided by a computer-controlled stepper motor that measures and optimally adjusts torque 300 times per second
Ultrasonically activated cleaning of the root canal to clear side canals
Use of additional medical, disinfecting irrigation solutions to loosen and flush out organic debris within the root canal
Supplementary electronic measurement of root canal length, to prevent the canals being under- or over-filled

Root filling: once the root canals have been cleaned, elaborate root-filling techniques are used, such as lateral condensation or the thermal filling technique, using gutta-percha, a natural material obtained from the sap of the gutta tree.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQ

bloecke.text: Today's modern endodontic treatments are far more comfortable and gentle than they used to be. Even so, root canal treatment at KU64 Berlin is usually carried out over several sessions, each lasting an hour or longer.

Making full use of everything modern root canal treatment has to offer gives an excellent chance that the affected tooth can be kept healthy and free of inflammation for the long term. Only very rarely does a root canal run in a simple S-shape; more often, it branches out or is otherwise impossible to prepare mechanically. Such cases cannot be entirely ruled out before treatment begins.

The alternative to root canal treatment is tooth replacement. This involves surgically removing the tooth and closing the gap afterwards with a bridge, consisting of two crowns and a replacement tooth. An alternative to a bridge is a dental implant (an artificial tooth root) fitted with a crown. The implantology experts at KU64 Berlin will be happy to talk you through other forms of tooth replacement.

Root canal treatment itself considerably weakens the tooth, making it somewhat more brittle. Some degree of grey discolouration is a natural result. For this reason, such teeth should always be fitted with a crown or partial crown. This offers the best protection against the tooth breaking apart, as well as against reinfection with bacteria.

Please bear in mind: a tooth that has been optimally root-treated and then fitted with a ceramic restoration can go on doing its full job in the mouth for a lifetime, without developing into an interference field. Further surgical measures, such as an apicoectomy, are also highly unlikely to be needed.
