karies-behandlung.titel: Professional Tooth Decay Treatment in Berlin

bloecke.text: Tooth decay is one of the most widespread dental conditions, affecting people of all ages. Recognising and treating decay in good time is crucial to prevent further damage and to maintain healthy teeth. At KU64, we offer a wide range of treatment options to restore your dental health and wellbeing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Watch out, tooth decay! But what exactly is it?

bloecke.text: Tooth decay is a pathological change to the tooth tissue and dentine, commonly known as caries or a cavity. The development of decay is a complex microbiological process in which bacterial acid production attacks the tooth surface. This leads to the breakdown of enamel and dentine, resulting in holes or cavities in the teeth. The symptoms of tooth decay include throbbing toothache, bleeding gums, increased tooth sensitivity, and the typical discolouration of the tooth surface.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth decay treatment – lastingly beautiful teeth

bloecke.text: There are numerous ways to treat tooth decay effectively. Which treatment makes sense always depends on the severity and extent of the decay. The first step is usually to prevent things from getting worse, as decay generally begins with quite small and rather superficial lesions. It is therefore advisable to attend regular dental appointments in order to detect decay at an early stage. The earlier tooth decay is treated, the better the outlook for dental health and the fewer the follow-on problems.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment options for tooth decay

bloecke.text: For small to medium-sized decay, the dentist can remove the affected area and close the resulting hole with a filling. This prevents the decay from spreading further and restores the normal tooth structure. Commonly used filling materials include composite resin and amalgam.
Info: An amalgam filling, colloquially also known as a “filling”, is a dental filling made from mercury alloys.

If the decay has reached the tooth pulp, this can cause severe pain and inflammation. In such cases, root canal treatment is necessary. In the course of this, the affected pulp – the soft tissue of the tooth – is removed, the root canal is cleaned and disinfected, and the tooth is then sealed.

If a large part of the tooth has been damaged by decay, a dental crown is required in most cases. During this treatment, the affected tooth is prepared and a custom-made crown made from metal, porcelain or ceramic is then placed over the tooth. This protects it and preserves its function.

In extremely advanced cases, where the tooth unfortunately can no longer be saved or it is simply not advisable to preserve it for other reasons, extraction is recommended. Here, the tooth is removed by the dentist. In normal circumstances, however, this is really only considered as a last resort. In such a case, our team at KU64 will be happy to advise you on tooth replacement and provide you with plenty of information on treatment options.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment options for preventing tooth decay

bloecke.text: There are many ways to protect yourself from tooth decay and to prevent the condition. At KU64, we recommend the following points to our patients to help prevent tooth decay:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Good brushing routine & healthy oral hygiene

bloecke.text: Healthy oral hygiene and dental care, along with the associated daily brushing routine, are crucial for preventing tooth decay. This includes thorough brushing at least twice a day, ideally morning and evening, with fluoride toothpaste. Regular brushing and good dental care help remove plaque, which harbours bacteria. These bacteria are responsible for producing the acid that causes decay. In addition, dental floss or interdental brushes should be used to clean between the teeth, where plaque can easily build up. A healthy oral hygiene routine, combined with regular dental check-ups, is the key to avoiding tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: You are what you eat: the right diet against tooth decay

bloecke.text: A healthy diet plays a crucial role in preventing tooth decay. This is because a diet high in sugar encourages the growth of decay-causing bacteria in the mouth. To prevent tooth decay, you should limit your sugar intake and focus on a balanced diet rich in fresh fruit, vegetables and lean protein. Fluoridated drinking water can also help strengthen the teeth and protect against decay. It is advisable to reduce or avoid sugary drinks and snacks and to choose water or other alternatives instead. A healthy diet is an essential part of preventing tooth decay and helps maintain your dental health.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth decay treatment in children

bloecke.text: Treating tooth decay in children differs in several respects from treating it in adults. As particularly good care and oral hygiene lay the foundation for children's future dental health, this requires special attention and care. The best method for treating tooth decay in children is to prevent it from the outset. This includes encouraging good oral hygiene, educating parents about the right diet, and using fluoride to strengthen the teeth.

Our specially trained children's dentists are experienced in detecting tooth decay at an early stage, often at a very early phase. This allows for timely treatment before the decay can worsen. Our team is always keen to create a particularly child-friendly and pleasant atmosphere in our dental practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Holistic dentistry at KU64

bloecke.text: The KU64 dental practice brings together dentists from every dental specialism. From oral hygiene tips, through tooth decay treatment, to fillings of every kind – with us, you will find a team of dentists with sensitivity, precision and highly professional expertise. Whether a damaged or old filling needs replacing, you are suffering from unexplained toothache, or you even have the odd blackened tooth – our dental experts at KU64 will help you achieve a healthy, beautiful set of teeth as quickly as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Detecting tooth decay quickly after it develops and acting as soon as possible

bloecke.text: The damage caused by tooth decay is often underestimated, or the person affected may not notice their diagnosis because they feel no pain, or only mild toothache. At KU64, we are well aware of how dangerous decay damage and its consequences can be, and so we act immediately. That is why even seemingly healthy teeth are thoroughly checked with us – this is the only way to detect decay in good time, carry out its removal, and prevent serious consequences before it's too late.
Depending on the size of the tooth defect, the appropriate filling is chosen. At the end, you will also receive tips on preventing further tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Make an appointment now

bloecke.text: You can find further information about the service and treatments offered by our dental practice for beautifully healthy teeth on our social media channels Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn and Instagram.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW Quickly Does Tooth Decay Need To Be Treated?

bloecke.text: Once tooth decay has been diagnosed, it should be treated as soon as possible. This helps prevent it from spreading further and ensures that dental health is preserved as far as possible. To ensure the earliest possible diagnosis, it is important to look out for the typical symptoms of tooth decay and to contact your dentist immediately.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW Painful IS Tooth Decay Treatment?

bloecke.text: How much pain is felt during tooth decay treatment varies from person to person. The modern dental techniques and anaesthetic methods used in our practice aim to reduce pain during treatment to a minimum. Our team at KU64 always strives to make treatment as pleasant as possible for our patients.

How much pain is involved also always depends on the type of treatment, as more extensive procedures such as root canal treatment can potentially cause more pain than fillings. Talk to us about your concerns and worries – we will be happy to advise you and stand by your side.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW Much Does IT Cost To Remove Tooth Decay?

bloecke.text: The cost of treating tooth decay can vary considerably and depends on several factors. First and foremost, it is crucial which treatment is required. While removing decay and filling a small cavity is fairly inexpensive, the costs rise for more extensive procedures such as root canal treatment or fitting a crown. In cases of advanced decay or complications, additional treatments are often required, which can increase the overall cost. Naturally, you will discuss all available payment options with our team at KU64 in advance, before deciding on a treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can Tooth Decay BE Removed Without Drilling?

bloecke.text: Yes, in some cases tooth decay can be removed without drilling. There are various minimally invasive treatment methods and techniques for this, which can be used depending on the size and depth of the decay lesions. In most cases, these treatments are preferred, as they help preserve healthy tooth structure. After a thorough examination and diagnosis, your dentist will recommend the most suitable treatment option. The following options are available:

Fluoride treatment: Early, and therefore rather superficial, decay lesions can be treated with fluoride-containing gels or varnishes. The fluoride helps to remineralise the enamel and harden the decay lesions.

Caries infiltration: In this method, a special gel is applied to the decay lesion to stop acid formation and remineralise the tooth enamel. This technique is often used for very early and rather small decay lesions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can A Tooth Affected BY Decay Still BE Saved?

bloecke.text: The good news first: yes! A tooth affected by decay can, in most cases, be saved, provided it is detected and treated in good time. However, this depends on various factors, such as the extent of the decay and the overall condition of the teeth, or of the affected tooth in particular. The options for saving the tooth include:
Fillings: The affected area is removed and the hole is closed with a filling.
Dental crowns: If the tooth is already weakened or there is a deeper decay lesion, a dental crown becomes necessary.
Root canal treatment: If the decay has reached the tooth pulp and caused an infection, treatment of the root is required.

Recognising the symptoms of tooth decay in good time is essential in order to save the affected tooth, or at least keep the consequences of the condition to a minimum. It is therefore advisable to attend regular dental check-ups and to seek medical help immediately at the first signs of tooth decay or dental problems. Your dentist will assess the condition of your tooth and recommend the most suitable treatment options.

cmd-behandlung.titel: Bite Raising in Berlin – Minimally Invasive Methods for a Relaxed Smile

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do you bite your way through life too?

bloecke.text: Are your teeth worn down through grinding or clenching? Then you may well be suffering from a lowered bite. A lowered bite doesn't just affect facial aesthetics. Pain in the jaw, back, hips or knees is often the result. Are you affected too? Our KU64 specialists in aesthetic dentistry and functional diagnostics in Berlin are here for you: with a bite raising, they restore your natural bite height and bring your whole body back into balance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When tooth substance disappears: reasons for a lowered bite

bloecke.text: You are not alone with a lowered bite. More and more patients, even young ones, suffer from worn teeth, known as an abrasion dentition. The most common causes of progressive tooth wear are teeth grinding and clenching (bruxism). The following factors can also contribute to a lowered bite:

Stress Many people come under pressure when stressed. It's not only the nervous system that becomes tense, but often the chewing muscles too. Psycho-emotional stress is usually released at night through grinding and clenching. Enormous forces occur in the process. Over time, this wears away not only the enamel but also the dentine beneath it.

Misaligned teeth and uneven strain on the chewing system Congenital misalignments or gaps between teeth can also encourage tooth abrasion. In this case, we recommend getting in touch with our orthodontic specialists. They will develop a tailored plan that corrects misalignments in the long term. Poorly fitted dental restorations can likewise lead to unnatural tooth wear. Ill-fitting crowns, implants, bridges, fillings, dentures or temporary restorations can cause uneven strain on the chewing system and damage the surrounding teeth.

Insufficient preventive care Inadequate oral hygiene and conditions such as tooth decay and periodontal disease can prematurely destroy tooth structure and the supporting tissues. Stomach acid is a dangerous factor (acid reflux, vomiting), but cola and even a very healthy diet (raw food) can also contain a lot of acid. Poor eating habits likewise contribute to an abrasion dentition. Acidic foods in particular can, if oral care is lacking, impair chewing function and lead to a loss of bite height.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Recognising early signs & treating in good time

bloecke.text: You are in good hands at our dental practice in Berlin: our dentists specialising in functional diagnostics are experts at recognising and treating a lowered bite right from its onset. Together we look at the underlying causes and advise you on the treatment that makes sense for you. This allows us to specifically prevent consequential damage, because nightly grinding and clenching affects the whole body.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bruxism and its consequences

bloecke.text: Worn teeth are often more sensitive to all stimuli (cold, heat, sweetness, pressure). A lowered bite can also cause imbalances throughout the whole body, because clenching and grinding places the chewing and facial muscles under constant strain. They become tense and hardened. Toothache, jaw joint pain and muscle tension (myopathy) are often the first warning signs of a lowered bite. The discomfort usually radiates from the teeth to other parts of the body, where the following symptoms often appear:
Tension headaches
Neck, shoulder and back pain
Earache
Tinnitus
Visual disturbances such as eye flickering, double vision accompanied by dizziness
Morning swallowing difficulties due to poor circulation
Pelvic misalignment

If left untreated, bruxism can, in the long term, lead to problems with the jaw joint (arthropathy), changes to the jaw muscles (myoarthropathy) and even chronic, inflammatory craniomandibular dysfunction (CMD).

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bite raising: holistic and individual for better balance

bloecke.text: If the upper and lower jaw are too far apart, a bite raising can help restore the balance between aesthetics, stability and function. Our dental specialists at KU64 Berlin take great care to include all the teeth of a jaw in the treatment plan, because every change to a single tooth automatically affects the position and function of the jaw joints. That's why, at the first signs of a 'faulty bite' and CMD, our dentists place great value on a holistic approach that takes the patient's entire body posture into account. Depending on your individual situation, we offer the following treatment options:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Help from the Dros splint (stabilisation splint)

bloecke.text: In cases of a severely lowered bite, we recommend a therapeutic trial phase for our patients before the definitive bite raising. One option for this is the Dros stabilisation splint. It lifts the problematic premature contacts between the upper and lower teeth and trains the jaw joints for the new, healthy bite height. Your dentist has the Dros splint made to individual specifications in our own certified in-house dental laboratory, once the muscles have been relaxed through preliminary treatment (JIG/Aqualizer, osteopathy).

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Reconstruction with dental restorations

bloecke.text: Once the jaw joints have adjusted to the new position, our dental specialists fit the permanent restoration. Depending on the degree of tooth abrasion, we use crowns, partial crowns, bridges, inlays and onlays, or veneers made of full ceramic for the build-up. These provide not only a natural-looking aesthetic but also lasting function. Where there is only slight abrasion of the front teeth, veneers or partial crowns are sufficient for the bite raising. A bite raising will only be successful in the long term if it is embedded in a holistic treatment concept. For this reason, our dentists work together with various interdisciplinary specialists (such as osteopaths, physiotherapists, orthopaedists, psychologists) on your behalf! This way, our patients learn techniques that can help achieve lasting relaxation of the muscles.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Precise craftsmanship for a smooth bite

bloecke.text: A bite raising calls for a fine touch from everyone involved: at our dental practice, dentists, implantologists and dental technicians work hand in hand, coordinating each treatment step perfectly with one another. For precise diagnostics and preparation of your teeth, our dentists use magnifying loupes with at least 4x magnification. The Smile Design dental laboratory also meets the highest standards of precision. For planning your dental restoration, the dental technicians use the latest 3D software.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Complete service: a strong team of specialists for every case

bloecke.text: A bite raising is an extremely complex procedure. That's why, at our dental practice, we involve doctors and specialists from a wide range of fields in the treatment. Our team of specialists includes not only dentists, dental technicians, orthodontists and implantology experts, but also radiologists, orthopaedists, ENT doctors, alternative practitioners, osteopaths and physiotherapists, who support us at every single step of treatment. This is how we enable our patients to receive a holistic, promising course of treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is a lowered bite?

bloecke.text: In a healthy set of teeth, the upper and lower jaw are in a balanced relationship to one another. The jaw joints are stably positioned, and the chewing muscles are relaxed. All the back teeth, canines and front teeth move harmoniously together when the lower jaw opens and closes. Typically, the distance between the upper and lower jaw at rest is two to four millimetres. The two only touch briefly during swallowing. When tooth structure is lost, the distance between the upper and lower jaw also increases. When they are more than eight millimetres apart, this is referred to as a lowered bite. The teeth then often no longer have contact with their opposing counterparts. In some cases, the inside of the tooth becomes exposed. The result: shortened front teeth and canines can no longer guide the bite harmoniously. Healthy occlusion is disrupted. The consequence: the chewing pattern develops from a functional vertical pattern into a horizontal one, similar to a ruminant animal.

Contact points in a healthy set of teeth turn into contact surfaces. It helps to know that 'chewing performance = force per surface area'. The larger the surface, the harder the chewing muscles have to work to generate the same chewing performance. This causes the chewing muscles (and the accessory chewing muscles too) to enlarge. A self-reinforcing vicious circle is set in motion.
What's the solution? => Turn back time!

Hardly any other field of medicine can truly do what's possible for teeth at KU64. We can give you back what is practically a virgin chewing surface at the original height, with perfect contact points. As a result, the muscles are put under far less strain. The vicious circle is broken!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For the health and wellbeing of your teeth

bloecke.text: Our experienced dentists are on hand with advice and support, and are happy to advise you individually on the options for a bite raising. Whether through orthodontic treatment or the use of splints – together we'll find a solution perfectly tailored to your needs, ensuring you a well-shaped set of teeth as well as straight teeth.

zahnsanierung.titel: Dental Restoration in Berlin – for a lasting radiant smile

bloecke.text: Healthy teeth well into old age – that's what many people wish for. But teeth grow older too: conscientious dental care and prevention are necessary, but often aren't enough to preserve dental health in the long term. A complete dental restoration at KU64 in Berlin and Potsdam gives you the chance for a fresh start: we renew your teeth from the ground up, so you can head into your best years with a radiant smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The essentials at a glance
Aesthetics and function in harmony

bloecke.text: A dental restoration is ideal if you'd like a visible glow-up while also valuing stable function. We bring aesthetics and bite into harmony: from a targeted upgrade of individual teeth to a comprehensive dental restoration.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental restoration with dentures made by KU64

bloecke.text: Receive high-quality solutions such as veneers, inlays, crowns, bridges or implants, perfectly matched to you through our in-house dental laboratory with digital planning.

bloecke.text: Before you start, you'll know which steps are needed, roughly how long treatment will take and what costs to expect. We tailor every process as closely as possible to your preferences and circumstances.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Beautiful, healthy teeth for a lifetime

bloecke.text: A radiant smile is more than dental health – it means presence. For many patients, it's simply a natural part of their personal look: in meetings, on video calls, at dinner, whilst travelling, or just in everyday life. If you'd like your smile to feel fresh again, look more natural, or simply match your style perfectly, a dental restoration can be exactly the right step – at any age.

Life leaves its marks – and sometimes you can see them in your smile too: small edges that gradually round off over the years, or older restorations in the mouth that no longer look quite so fresh. Damage from minor or major mishaps, from sport, from misalignment, decay or teeth grinding. Discolouration from foods such as coffee, tea, red wine. None of this can always be avoided – and it tells the story of a life lived. A dental restoration is then like a glow-up for your teeth: it brings back clarity, harmony and freshness, without looking artificial.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: World-class dentistry
Interdisciplinary specialist team

bloecke.text: At KU64, dentists, oral surgeons, prosthetists and periodontists work hand in hand to carry out your dental restoration at the highest level. Our interdisciplinary team ensures that every detail of your treatment is precisely planned and carried out. This holistic expertise guarantees the best possible care.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Modern technology for optimal results

bloecke.text: We rely on the latest technological methods to carry out your dental restoration precisely and with minimal invasiveness. With innovative methods such as 3D X-ray, Digital Smile Design and CAD/CAM technology, we offer you precise planning and execution that meets the highest standards, both aesthetically and functionally. This gives you a result that fits perfectly with your face and expressions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Individual treatment with personal care

bloecke.text: Your dental restoration at KU64 is as unique as you are. We take the time to discuss your wishes and concerns, and create a bespoke treatment plan for you. We accompany you step by step and ensure you feel comfortable throughout the entire process. Our personal care is at the centre of every treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Anxious patients welcome – stress-free treatments

bloecke.text: For many people, going to the dentist is associated with anxiety. At KU64, we offer special treatment options for anxious patients, such as calming sedation and treatment under general anaesthetic. This allows you to have your dental restoration carried out stress-free, in an atmosphere of calm and trust, without pain or fear.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When a dental restoration is sensible and necessary

bloecke.text: A dental restoration can be worthwhile for any patient when teeth lose their function and aesthetics over time. This often happens as a result of decay, dental accidents, gum disease or age-related wear. A dental restoration is not merely a cosmetic measure – it also contributes to improving quality of life by restoring or improving chewing function, speech and overall wellbeing. Whether individual teeth or the whole set is affected: a dental restoration creates a harmonious, aesthetic overall picture and a stable, long-term solution.
A dental restoration is strongly recommended, in particular, in the following cases:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When aesthetic flaws affect your quality of life

bloecke.text: A healthy, beautiful smile is an important feature of beauty for many people. Unattractive teeth, whether due to discolouration, gaps or irregularities, can affect self-confidence. If your teeth no longer visually match the smile you want – whether due to ageing, discolouration, smoking or defects – a dental restoration is the perfect way to fix these problems and regain a harmonious, natural smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When your teeth are weakened by ageing or external influences

bloecke.text: Over the years, everyday stresses such as stress, poor diet or inadequate dental care leave their mark. But the perfectly normal ageing process also affects your smile. Tooth enamel can wear down, decay can damage the tooth structure, and old fillings or dental restorations lose their function. Dental accidents, grinding and bite problems also frequently lead to damage to the teeth. A dental restoration is especially worthwhile when teeth are badly damaged and a single treatment isn't enough to repair them.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When your overall dental health is at risk

bloecke.text: Dental restorations aren't just an aesthetic decision, but also a preventive measure for your dental health. When decay, periodontitis or other dental diseases progress, they can lead to serious health problems that affect the entire chewing system. In such cases, a dental restoration serves not only to restore functionality, but also to preserve the health of the teeth and gums.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When the condition of your teeth limits your quality of life

bloecke.text: If your teeth are affecting your quality of life because your ability to speak and chew is impaired, it is high time for a dental restoration. Such a condition in the mouth often leads to discomfort and social insecurity. Chewing hurts, certain foods can no longer be eaten, and spoken words no longer sound natural. By restoring the tooth structure and chewing function, we bring about a significant improvement in your quality of life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which methods and measures are available for a dental restoration?

bloecke.text: With your dental restoration, you've decided on a comprehensive treatment. It will give you a natural and healthy look for many, many years to come and bring your teeth the best possible appearance. Accordingly, in a complete restoration, almost all departments in our practice are involved, giving everything for a perfect result. Depending on the findings and the current condition of the teeth and gums, endodontics and periodontics, oral surgery and orthodontics, as well as our dental laboratory, work hand in hand for your perfected smile.

As a rule, before the dental restoration, we first carry out preparatory measures to ensure impeccable oral health, such as a professional teeth cleaning or treatment of any existing gum inflammation and tooth roots. Crowns can stabilise teeth, veneers can aesthetically refine small flaws in shape or colour, and dental implants replace missing teeth to a very high standard.

Here you'll find an overview of all the treatments we can carry out as part of a complete dental restoration. Your dentist uses these methods as needed and in combination to achieve the best result for you. Which solution suits you, and which methods and measures are required for it, depends on the condition of your teeth and the desired result.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Decay treatment

bloecke.text: Decay is one of the most common dental diseases and can affect people of any age. The complete removal of existing decay is a crucial precondition for the success of your dental restoration. At KU64, a broad spectrum of treatment options is available, which we use depending on the extent and severity of the damage.
All information on decay treatment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Professional teeth cleaning

bloecke.text: Professional teeth cleaning, for the thorough removal of plaque and tartar, is the first step towards keeping your teeth healthy in the long term and creating a solid foundation for all further restorative measures. It also reliably helps prevent periodontitis and decay and should be carried out regularly to ensure your newly regained smile is preserved.
All information on professional teeth cleaning

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Periodontitis treatment

bloecke.text: Comprehensive periodontitis treatment is often unavoidable when dental restorations become necessary. Periodontitis, an inflammation of the tooth-supporting structures, leads to receding gums and loose teeth. In a complete dental restoration, treatment therefore often begins with eliminating periodontitis in order to stabilise dental health. Targeted treatment can save teeth and prevent further damage before more serious restorative procedures, such as dental implants, become necessary.
All information on periodontitis treatment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Root canal treatment

bloecke.text: If a tooth root becomes inflamed due to decay or other damage, a root canal treatment by the dentist may become necessary in order to save the tooth. Removing the inflamed tissue and subsequently sealing the tooth prevents the tooth from being lost. In the course of the dental restoration, we resolve all existing problems with tooth roots, which is also an important preparatory measure for the next treatment steps, such as dentures.
All information on root canal treatment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bone augmentation

bloecke.text: Bone augmentation is required for a dental restoration when the jawbone has been weakened by tooth loss or periodontitis. For those affected, this measure is necessary before we can restore your rows of teeth with dentures. In a surgical procedure, we restore your jawbone to its original shape using artificial materials and help it regain full stability, so that dental implants or dentures can later be securely anchored.
All information on bone augmentation

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers

bloecke.text: Veneers are natural-looking facing shells and an ideal option for patients who want an aesthetically pleasing, radiant smile. They can be used in the front tooth area without requiring extensive dentures. In a dental restoration, veneers are therefore often used to correct minor defects, discolouration or gaps in the front tooth area. They offer a quick, minimally invasive way to improve the appearance of the teeth and boost self-confidence.
All information on veneers

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fillings

bloecke.text: Fillings are a central part of any dental restoration, used to repair teeth damaged by decay. We use tooth-coloured materials such as composites or ceramics, which are convincing both functionally and aesthetically. They also serve to preserve teeth and can prevent the need for dentures later on. That's why, in a dental restoration, we also renew old fillings if they are defective. Replacing existing fillings is also possible for aesthetic reasons.
All information on fillings

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Amalgam removal

bloecke.text: Removing old amalgam fillings is an important step as part of a dental restoration. Amalgam has a dark, metallic colour and is therefore often no longer desired for aesthetic reasons. In addition, it raises health concerns for many patients due to the toxic mercury it contains, and it is now no longer permitted for use.
All information on amalgam removal

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Inlays

bloecke.text: We use inlays to restore damaged teeth when fillings are no longer sufficient due to the size of the damage. They are particularly useful in dental restorations that require a long-lasting and aesthetic solution. At the same time, an inlay allows the tooth to be largely preserved, retaining its functionality and natural appearance.
All information on inlays

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Crowns

bloecke.text: We use crowns to stabilise badly damaged teeth and restore their functionality. Crowning the tooth is also usually required after a root canal treatment. The dentist places an artificial tooth, made precisely in our laboratory, onto the root, which is hardly distinguishable from a real tooth in shape and appearance. In the course of your dental restoration, crowns offer a lasting and aesthetically pleasing way to restore the tooth structure and secure the natural bite.
All information on crowns

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Implants

bloecke.text: Dental implants are the preferred choice in a dental restoration when teeth have been lost. They fully replace missing teeth, including the root, and offer a stable, functional and aesthetic solution to significantly improve patients' quality of life. Implants are particularly beneficial because they protect healthy gums and jawbone without affecting neighbouring teeth.
All information on implants

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bridges

bloecke.text: Bridges are a solution in a dental restoration when one or more teeth are missing and neighbouring teeth are still intact. They close the gaps with dentures that look as natural as possible and are attached to the neighbouring teeth. Bridges are a tried-and-tested method that restores both the function and the aesthetic appearance of the teeth, when implants are not desired or not possible.
All information on bridges

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dentures

bloecke.text: Full dentures are necessary for patients who are missing many teeth or even the entire row of teeth, and for whom implants cannot be placed for medical reasons, for example due to the condition of the jawbone. Dentures are also a more cost-effective solution than implants and offer a complete denture solution to ensure bite and speech capability. Thanks to the latest methods and materials, we can give you a largely natural smile with these.
All information on dentures

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Your dental restoration at KU64

bloecke.text: At KU64, we combine aesthetic dentistry with a clear, high-quality treatment concept: we start with thorough diagnostics, plan your result digitally and coordinate every detail to your wishes.

With a complete restoration, the specialist dental team at KU64 designs a fresh start for your teeth! Veneers (ceramic facing shells), dental implants, bridges, dentures or high-quality inlays, aesthetic all-ceramic crowns and the restoration of your amalgam fillings (amalgam removal under triple protection) provide optimal dentures that are barely distinguishable from perfect natural teeth.

High-quality dentures are created in our in-house dental laboratory – and our interdisciplinary team works hand in hand to ensure shape, colour and function work together harmoniously. The Smile Design dental laboratory meets best practice standards: all success-critical work steps are carried out under a microscope. This makes beautiful teeth a systematically plannable pleasure.

The experienced dentists at KU64 make sure that the complete dental restoration goes as smoothly as possible: we carry out comprehensive complete tooth restorations under general anaesthetic or sedation, where needed. This also offers patients who suffer from dental anxiety the best possible care and a relaxed treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How the dental restoration at KU64 works

bloecke.text: Our process is clearly structured: first an appointment for diagnostics and consultation with your dentist, then planning, followed by implementation in well-coordinated steps. In our practice, it's important to us that you always know what's coming next.

When it comes to planning, the aim is to make sure the result and the treatment steps really fit together: we start with a comprehensive analysis and coordinate shape, colour and bite with one another. This creates a concept that suits your wishes – with the individual details that ultimately make a smile look natural.

With Digital Smile Design (DSD), we offer you a modern method of dental visualisation that will impress you! Even before your dental treatment, you can see the planned result in a video and take a cosmetic test drive with your new smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Risks and complications

bloecke.text: A dental restoration can significantly improve your dental health, function and aesthetics. As with all treatments, complications can occur with the associated dental and surgical procedures. However, these are generally rare and, in most cases, can be treated well. Careful planning, hygiene control and coordination with the entire KU64 health team by the dentist minimise risks and ensure that your dental restoration proceeds safely and successfully.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Swelling and pain

bloecke.text: After surgical steps such as tooth extractions, implantations or bone augmentation, many patients temporarily experience swelling, pain, slight secondary bleeding or a feeling of pressure. These are normal healing reactions and can generally be well controlled with cooling, rest and the measures, painkillers or other supportive medications recommended by the practitioner. They usually subside after a few days.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Infections and inflammation

bloecke.text: After medical procedures, wounds can sometimes become infected. Signs of this include persistent redness, swelling, pain or the formation of pus. We treat infections following dental restorations – for example, around an implant or bone augmentation material – with early antibiotic therapy and/or follow-up treatment to disinfect and clean away pus.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Nerve injuries and functional limitations

bloecke.text: With surgical measures in the jaw area, there is a small risk of irritating or injuring neighbouring nerves – for example, during implantation or bone augmentation. This can lead to temporary or, in rare cases, longer-lasting sensory disturbances (for example, numbness, tingling) in the lips, chin or tongue.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Problems with implants and dentures

bloecke.text: With dental implants, specific risks such as peri-implantitis (an inflammatory reaction around an implant), implant loosening or – very rarely – failure to heal ("non-osseointegration") can occur afterwards. Poor oral hygiene, smoking or certain medical conditions increase the risk of such problems. With dentures, wearing them can cause tissue irritation, pressure sores or changes to the jawbone, meaning the denture may need to be adjusted again.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Complications with bone augmentation and sinus lift

bloecke.text: Measures such as bone augmentation or a sinus lift to prepare the implant site are very effective, but in some cases also carry risks such as infections, perforation of the sinus membrane, severe swelling or delayed healing. We carefully assess such risks before initiating treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQ: The most important questions about dental restoration
What does "dental restoration" mean?

bloecke.text: A dental restoration is a holistic update for your teeth: we bring aesthetics, stability and wellbeing in the mouth back together. In modern holistic dentistry, this means looking at causes, function and appearance together, and coordinating everything sensibly with one another.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When is a complete dental restoration necessary?

bloecke.text: A complete dental restoration may be necessary for you when several areas need attention at the same time – for example, because old dentures no longer fit ideally, or the bite no longer feels harmonious. Whether a complete restoration is really required, or whether individual measures are sufficient, is best clarified after a thorough examination at our dental practice with the treating dentist.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which treatments and measures typically form part of a dental restoration?

bloecke.text: Depending on the starting situation, various treatments and measures can be part of it – from renewal to aesthetic optimisation. Common building blocks include high-quality dentures such as ceramic crowns, veneers or dental implants, always matched to the desired result and your situation. Your dentist will explain all the options to you extensively during a thorough consultation and answer your questions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Will my health insurance cover the costs of the restoration?

bloecke.text: Part of the costs, such as for root canal treatments or simple dentures, is usually covered by statutory health insurance, depending on the insurer and indication, especially where it is medically necessary. The costs of higher-quality care and aesthetic measures are always associated with out-of-pocket contributions. The exact proportion varies according to individual circumstances. Your dentist will inform you transparently about the costs and help you complete the necessary applications for reimbursement.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I have my teeth restored without it looking artificial?

bloecke.text: Yes – if you want to have your teeth done, it's above all about a result that suits you and doesn't look artificial. What matters most is careful planning, high-quality materials and a harmonious interplay of proportions, surfaces and colour. The experts at KU64 will advise you thoroughly on this and work with you to find the solution that best suits your smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is treatment possible for anxious patients too?

bloecke.text: If you're one of the anxious patients, you're in the best hands at KU64! We make sure you feel understood and can go through the necessary treatment steps at your own pace. Treatment under general anaesthetic can – depending on the scope and medical circumstances – be an option, which we discuss individually.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How do I keep my result looking good in the long term?

bloecke.text: For your teeth to keep shining in the long term after restoration, regular prevention appointments, good care at home and sensibly coordinated check-ups with your dentist at the practice are all part of it. This applies to natural teeth just as much as to dentures – because well-cared-for transitions and healthy gums make the biggest visual difference. We advise and support you in preserving your newly regained smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How do I get in touch if I still have questions?

bloecke.text: If you still have questions, you can easily get in touch with us – by phone, online or in person at the dental practice – and arrange a suitable appointment.

faltenbehandlung.titel: Wrinkle Treatment in Berlin at KU64

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What methods of wrinkle treatment are there?

bloecke.text: Aesthetic medicine offers numerous ways to smooth wrinkles in a targeted manner and rejuvenate the appearance of the skin – entirely without surgery. Depending on age, skin type and desired outcome, different methods of wrinkle filling or firming procedures may be suitable. Which wrinkle treatment is best for you depends on your individual needs and physical prerequisites.
Our specialists are happy to advise you in detail to find the optimal solution for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Wrinkle treatment with botulinum toxin

bloecke.text: Our facial expressions make our face lively and individual – but over the course of a lifetime, they leave behind forehead lines, frown lines or crow's feet. This is where wrinkle treatment with botulinum toxin, also known as Botox, comes in: through targeted injection of this muscle relaxant, certain facial muscles can be relaxed. This eases existing wrinkles and helps prevent new ones from forming.

The treatment takes only a few minutes and quickly delivers the desired result. Botulinum toxin is a proven method especially for reducing deep expression lines gently. Our goal is a natural, aesthetic result according to your wishes. That's why, following a personal consultation, we naturally tailor the dosage precisely to your needs.
More about botulinum toxin treatments at KU64

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Wrinkle treatment with hyaluronic acid

bloecke.text: Over the years, the skin loses moisture and firmness. This means the face appears less fresh and wrinkles form more quickly. Targeted wrinkle filling with a filler such as hyaluronic acid can offset this effect by restoring lost volume and smoothing fine lines. This method is particularly popular for treating nasolabial folds, marionette lines and lip lines. It is also suitable for gentle contouring of the lips, cheeks or chin.

Hyaluronic acid is a natural component of the body and is well tolerated by the skin. The filling procedure is minimally invasive. This means you can look forward to a quickly visible improvement in your skin's appearance – with no downtime at work or in your private life. Hyaluronic acid can also be combined with other aesthetic procedures such as thread lifting for harmonious, sculpted results.
More about hyaluronic acid treatments at KU64

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Mesotherapy

bloecke.text: Many patients want more than treatment of individual wrinkles: they want themselves and their skin overall to look brighter and fresher. For this, the skin above all needs more moisture, nutrients and improved regenerative capacity.

Mesotherapy is an innovative method that addresses exactly this: through micro-fine injections, individually tailored active ingredients such as hyaluronic acid, vitamins and antioxidants are introduced directly into the skin. This stimulates cell regeneration, firms the tissue and visibly revitalises the skin.
This aesthetic treatment is particularly suitable for fine dehydration lines and tired, dull skin. It can be applied to the face as well as the neck, décolletage or hands.
Following an in-depth consultation, our doctors tailor the combination of active ingredients individually to your skin's needs, so that you achieve the radiant result you wish for.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Collagen boosters

bloecke.text: Collagen is a key structural protein in the skin that keeps it firm and elastic. As we age, the body's own collagen production slows down – the skin loses firmness and wrinkles form. Collagen boosters are a method to specifically slow this process down and stimulate your skin's natural regeneration.

Injection with special active ingredients such as poly-L-lactic acid or calcium hydroxylapatite stimulates collagen formation over the long term. The effect: a gradual firming and a naturally looking lift that sustainably improves your skin quality. This method is particularly suitable for deeper wrinkles, sunken cheeks or slack areas of skin.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Thread lifting

bloecke.text: Has your skin lost firmness, and would you like a natural lift without surgery? Thread lifting is a gentle alternative to plastic surgery. This method uses threads that are inserted under the skin, producing an immediate firming effect. At the same time, they stimulate collagen production, so your skin's appearance continues to improve over the following weeks and months. The threads are absorbable. This means they dissolve on their own after a certain time and do not need to be removed.
Thread lifting is particularly suitable for treating sagging or drooping cheeks as well as mild wrinkles in the area of the chin, neck or décolletage.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: PRP treatment

bloecke.text: PRP treatment, also known as the vampire facial, is an innovative method to make your skin look fresh and radiant again without any artificial additives.

Instead of synthetic fillers, this treatment uses your own blood, which is processed and injected into the skin in a targeted manner. The PRP (platelet-rich plasma) it contains is rich in platelets. These stimulate the body's own collagen and cell production and support the skin's natural regeneration.

This aesthetic method is particularly suitable for tired, dull skin, early wrinkles or generally improving skin quality in the area of the face, neck and décolletage. PRP wrinkle treatment can also be combined with other procedures such as injectable fillers or thread lifting to intensify skin firming.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Wrinkle treatment with chemical peels

bloecke.text: Chemical peels are a proven method for counteracting skin ageing, sun damage and environmental stress, giving the skin renewed freshness and an even, radiant complexion.

Through the targeted application of special acids – such as fruit acid, trichloroacetic acid (TCA) or salicylic acid – dead skin cells are gently removed from the surface of the skin and from within the pores. In addition, cell renewal is stimulated and collagen production is boosted. Depending on the intensity, a chemical peel can work mainly on the skin's surface or reach deeper skin layers.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Microdermabrasion

bloecke.text: Many people find unevenness, fine wrinkles or acne scars bothersome. Dermabrasion is an effective aesthetic method for correcting such surface imperfections. During dermabrasion, the upper layer of skin is specifically removed, stimulating skin renewal. Fine, rotating abrasive heads gently smooth your skin, while pigmentation irregularities are evened out and wrinkles are reduced.
This treatment is particularly suitable if you wish for visible skin rejuvenation but prefer natural regeneration over a filler, an injectable treatment or thread lifting.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Carboxytherapy

bloecke.text: One effect that occurs as we age is that blood circulation in the skin slows down. As a result, oxygen supply decreases and the tissue loses firmness. Carboxytherapy aims to counteract this process: through the targeted injection of medical carbon dioxide (CO₂) into the skin, circulation is stimulated, oxygen supply is improved and the body's own collagen production is activated.

This treatment is an option if you would like to reduce fine lines or dark circles, or firm and rejuvenate slack skin on the face, neck and décolletage. In addition, the improved skin regeneration achieved through carboxytherapy can help improve stretch marks and scars.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Laser therapy

bloecke.text: Similar to collagen or PRP treatment, laser therapy is also about stimulating the skin's natural regeneration, giving you an even and fresh complexion once again. Using modern laser technology, deeper layers of skin can be stimulated and collagen production encouraged.

Laser therapy is suitable for treatment on the face, neck and décolletage. Thanks to its precision, it is also possible to specifically reduce fine lines, scars or skin irregularities in various areas of the body.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Beautiful all over: these are the areas where you can have wrinkles treated

bloecke.text: Wrinkles form where the skin is particularly stressed by facial expressions, sun exposure or the natural ageing process. While some lines give your face character, especially deeper wrinkles can make you look tired or tense.

Whatever area of your face or body you wish to have treated for wrinkles: a range of modern aesthetic procedures are available to gently smooth, firm and regenerate your skin. At KU64 in Berlin, we always place great importance on tailoring wrinkle treatment precisely to your wishes and needs, achieving a natural result that highlights your personality.
We are happy to advise you on which method is best suited for you. Why not book an appointment right away?
For most people, the first wrinkles appear on the forehead. They form mainly due to facial movements, exposure to UV rays from sunlight, and the natural, age-related loss of skin elasticity.

If you would like to reduce forehead lines, you have several options. A particularly well-established and popular method for effectively smoothing forehead lines is targeted wrinkle filling with botulinum toxin (Botox). The muscle relaxant reduces the activity of the forehead muscles, smoothing existing lines and preventing new ones from forming. For deeper wrinkles, an additional injection with hyaluronic acid can be carried out to compensate for lost volume.

The frown line, also known as the glabellar line, forms between the eyebrows and can make your face look tense or stern – even when you are completely relaxed. These vertical lines form through repeated contraction of the forehead muscles, for example when concentrating or in bright light.

As with forehead lines, targeted injection with botulinum toxin is also the most effective method for reducing the frown line. If you suffer from a very deep frown line, an additional wrinkle filling with hyaluronic acid can be useful to gently plump up the tissue.

The fine lines at the outer corners of the eyes, also known as crow's feet due to their typical shape, form over the years through smiling and blinking. As the skin around the eyes is particularly thin, it loses firmness more quickly than in other areas during the ageing process. This makes it easier for wrinkles to become established and deepen.

If you wish for a gentle smoothing of crow's feet to enjoy a fresher, more open-eyed look again, you can opt for targeted wrinkle filling with botulinum toxin or hyaluronic acid, or for wrinkle treatment with your own blood (PRP). This method is particularly suitable for you if you wish for a treatment using your body's own substances and your crow's feet are not yet very pronounced.

Marionette lines run from the corners of the mouth downwards towards the chin and can make you look grumpy or sad. Due to the age-related loss of firmness and volume, these lines deepen over time. Smoking additionally encourages and intensifies marionette lines.

If you would like to plump up marionette lines, wrinkle filling with hyaluronic acid is an effective method. Wrinkle treatment with your own fat is also a good alternative for achieving particularly long-lasting results.
If you would also like to firm the sagging skin around the corners of the mouth, thread lifting can be a useful addition. This way, your smile will once again be as lovely as you wish.

Nasolabial folds run from the sides of the nose down to the corners of the mouth and are among the most prominent wrinkles on the face. They become more pronounced due to the natural loss of elasticity and volume in the skin, as well as facial movements when speaking and smiling.

As with marionette lines, injection with hyaluronic acid is a proven method for plumping up nasolabial folds. In some cases, wrinkle treatment with your own fat can also be useful for restoring volume to the area between the nose and mouth over the long term.

For more comprehensive firming, you can also consider thread lifting or a collagen booster to sustainably improve your skin structure. We are happy to advise you on all options and which wrinkle treatments are most promising for you personally.
Nose wrinkles, also known as 'bunny lines', are fine lines that form on the sides in the middle area of the nose. They become especially visible when laughing or wrinkling the nose.

If these fine lines bother you, wrinkle filling with botulinum toxin (Botox) is helpful for smoothing them and preventing new nose wrinkles. For deeper lines, additional injection with hyaluronic acid is an option to plump up the wrinkles and improve the skin structure in this area overall.

Do you have fine lines around your mouth that make you look older? Lip lines, also known as smoker's lines, can be reduced using various methods. At the same time, your lip contours can be naturally enhanced.

Wrinkle treatment with hyaluronic acid evens out and improves the appearance of the skin in the lip area overall while also giving your lips more volume again. If you would like to do even more for a youthful smile, you can combine the injection with a collagen booster or laser therapy. This strengthens the structure of your lip skin over the long term.
As we age, fine lines can first form on the chin, later even deeper chin wrinkles. These signs are often accompanied by an uneven surface texture.

To smooth chin wrinkles, many patients opt for wrinkle filling with botulinum toxin. If the focus is on balancing volume and contours, injection with hyaluronic acid or your own fat can help make your facial features look more harmonious again. For deeper firming and definition, thread lifting or a collagen booster can also be a useful addition.

Besides the forehead, the neck is often one of the first areas where the natural ageing process becomes noticeable. As collagen breakdown progresses, neck wrinkles develop in the form of fine lines or deeper horizontal folds. In addition, sagging areas of skin can affect the contour of your neck.

There are various methods for firming and rejuvenating the skin on the neck. If you want to ease fine wrinkles, wrinkle filling with hyaluronic acid can help. For deeper wrinkles or a sagging skin structure, thread lifting or a collagen booster stimulate the body's own regeneration and provide long-term firming.

The décolletage is a sensitive area of skin that is often exposed to the sun and loses elasticity comparatively quickly. Décolletage wrinkles form due to the natural ageing process, repeated movements during sleep, or insufficient skin care.

A proven method for gently smoothing and revitalising the décolletage is wrinkle filling with hyaluronic acid. The treatment provides moisture, improves the skin structure and reduces fine wrinkles. For deeper regeneration, PRP treatment or mesotherapy can help stimulate the body's own collagen production and strengthen the skin structure.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are the risks of wrinkle treatment?

bloecke.text: As with any medical treatment, wrinkle filling and other non-invasive or minimally invasive procedures carry certain risks, which vary depending on skin type and method. In most cases, modern aesthetic treatments are well tolerated and safe when carried out by experienced specialists. Immediately after treatment, mild side effects such as redness, swelling or small bruises can occur, but these usually subside quickly.

With injections of hyaluronic acid, your own fat or botulinum toxin, asymmetric results or allergic reactions can occur in rare cases. Thread lifting and collagen boosters also carry a small risk of infection or temporary skin irregularities.

Unlike surgical procedures in plastic surgery, such as liposuction or a tummy tuck, the risks of gentle skin rejuvenation methods in aesthetic medicine are low. At our practice on Kurfürstendamm in Berlin, we place great importance on a thorough consultation before every treatment, so we can discuss any possible risks with you individually.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Anti-ageing starts in everyday life: how you can prevent wrinkles

bloecke.text: The formation of wrinkles is a natural process that becomes visible in all of us over the years. Alongside genetic factors, individual lifestyle and environmental influences also play a decisive role in how early and how quickly the signs of time appear. By taking preventive measures early on, you can slow down the skin ageing process and keep your skin firm and fresh for longer.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A balanced diet and plenty of fluids

bloecke.text: Antioxidants, vitamins and unsaturated fatty acids support collagen production and thus protect your skin from premature wrinkle formation. Omega-3 fatty acids from fish, nuts and avocados in particular contribute to improved skin elasticity. Vitamin C (for example from citrus fruits or peppers) and vitamin E (found, among other things, in green leafy vegetables and plant oils) protect the skin from harmful free radicals. With the right diet, you can therefore contribute a great deal to keeping your skin healthy and youthful for longer.

Adequate fluid intake is also essential: water helps transport toxins out of the body and supplies the skin with moisture. A lack of fluids, on the other hand, can make the skin look dull and cause fine lines to appear more quickly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Avoiding smoking and alcohol

bloecke.text: Smoking and alcohol consumption impair the oxygen and nutrient supply to the skin. As a result, they are among the biggest accelerators of skin ageing.

Smoking damages the collagen and elastin fibres responsible for firm skin. In addition, smokers often develop pronounced lip lines as well as deeper lines around the mouth and eyes. Even aesthetic methods such as wrinkle filling or a collagen booster can only compensate for the negative effects of smoking to a limited extent.

Alcohol has a dehydrating effect and deprives the skin of essential nutrients. As a result, it loses firmness, and fine lines become visible more quickly. Over the long term, increased alcohol consumption can also lead to skin redness, dilated blood vessels and an uneven skin appearance.
To slow down skin ageing, avoiding smoking and alcohol is therefore one of the most effective measures – and you will also be doing your general health a great favour!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Getting enough sleep

bloecke.text: The much-quoted beauty sleep is no myth: while you sleep, your skin regenerates. It repairs cell damage and produces new collagen, which provides firmness and elasticity. In addition, your body increases blood flow to the skin, supplying it with oxygen and nutrients.

Anyone who consistently gets too little sleep risks not only signs of tiredness such as dark circles and dull skin, but also a loss of firmness and faster wrinkle formation. So if you want to do something good for your skin, why not simply go to bed a little earlier.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Reducing stress

bloecke.text: Under stress, your body releases cortisol. This hormone accelerates the breakdown of collagen and elastin, causing your skin to lose firmness and wrinkles to form. In addition, blood circulation is restricted, which impairs your skin's regeneration and makes it look more tired and dull.

A balanced lifestyle therefore contributes not only to your general wellbeing, but also to keeping your skin healthy and youthful. Relaxation techniques such as meditation, yoga or breathing exercises can help lower stress levels and slow down skin ageing. Regular exercise in fresh air also promotes blood circulation and supports your skin in regenerating.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Using sun protection

bloecke.text: UV radiation is one of the main causes of premature skin ageing and the formation of wrinkles. It causes damage in both the upper and deeper layers of the skin and promotes the breakdown of collagen and elastin. This leads to reduced skin elasticity and premature wrinkle formation. If you want to keep your skin young and healthy for as long as possible, you should therefore apply sun protection daily – regardless of the weather or season.

A broad-spectrum sunscreen with at least SPF 30 protects not only against sunburn and skin cancer, but also against pigmentation spots and light-induced skin ageing. Particularly sensitive areas of skin such as the face, neck and décolletage benefit from good, regular protection.

Good to know: even aesthetic treatments such as wrinkle filling can only achieve their optimal effect if you also protect your skin from UV radiation. So there are many good reasons to make sun protection a fixed part of your daily routine.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about wrinkle treatment
How much do wrinkle treatments cost?

bloecke.text: The cost of wrinkle treatment varies depending on the method and treatment area. Wrinkle filling with hyaluronic acid or botulinum toxin usually starts at around €200. More elaborate procedures such as thread lifting or PRP treatment can involve higher costs. Following an individual consultation, in which we discuss the optimal treatment together with you, you will of course receive a transparent and detailed cost breakdown at KU64.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which wrinkle treatment lasts the longest?

bloecke.text: How long the result of a wrinkle treatment lasts depends on various factors, above all the method chosen. But individual characteristics such as your skin type and metabolism also play a role.
Unlike plastic surgery, non-invasive or minimally invasive treatments cannot deliver permanent results. In return, they are gentle and do not require long recovery times.
Botulinum toxin reduces expression lines for around 3 to 6 months, while wrinkle filling with hyaluronic acid can last between 6 and 18 months, depending on the treatment area.
Even more long-lasting results are offered by thread lifting, for example, as it can stimulate the body's own collagen production and sustainably improve the skin structure – for up to 2 years.

A particularly long-lasting method is fat filling, in which your own fat, often taken from a previous liposuction procedure, is used to fill wrinkles. This technique can achieve effects lasting for years. Non-invasive laser treatment can also strengthen your skin structure over the long term and thus rejuvenate the appearance of your skin.
Our specialists are happy to advise you in detail on which treatments are suitable for your desired result and how to achieve a natural, long-lasting outcome.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I have liposuction on my face as well?

bloecke.text: Liposuction on the face is possible, but it is not the first choice for facial contouring. A gentler alternative is the fat-dissolving injection (injection lipolysis), which specifically breaks down fat cells that are then naturally eliminated by the body. This method is particularly suitable for smaller fat deposits, for example on the cheeks or chin.
A complementary wrinkle treatment, such as wrinkle filling or laser treatment, can additionally firm your skin and define your facial contours.
Please feel free to contact us for a personal consultation to clarify which method best suits you and your needs!

feste-zahnspange.titel: WIN Lingual Systems – The Alternative to a Brace

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Lingual brace: invisible tooth correction with lingual technology

bloecke.text: Put your smile in the spotlight, not your brace! With lingual technology, even pronounced misalignments can be corrected almost invisibly. The lingual brace is therefore a discreet alternative to a conventional fixed brace – ideal for teenagers and adults with high aesthetic expectations for tooth correction.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Discreetly to a radiant smile with the inner-lying WIN brace

bloecke.text: Lingual means "facing the tongue". The ultra-flat brackets of the lingual brace are attached to the inside of the teeth rather than the outside. This means the lingual brace is invisible to onlookers. Thanks to their perfect fit, lingual technology can treat both minor and complex misalignments just as effectively as a conventional visible brace. Patients in professional life who require treatment lasting several years benefit in particular from this almost invisible technique. After treatment, the dentist or orthodontist removes the brackets of the lingual brace from the teeth without leaving any residue.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tailor-made for optimal treatment success

bloecke.text: The WIN braces used by KU64 Berlin, made by DW Lingual Systems, are individually crafted and manufactured in Germany. Every single component, such as brackets or archwires, is adjusted to the millimetre to fit the patient's personal tooth and jaw shape. This bespoke manufacturing guarantees a high degree of long-term stability and functionality for the tooth correction. Unlike a conventional outer brace from mass production, this ensures that the teeth remain in their new position in the long term even after the lingual brace has been removed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For a straight bite: areas of application for the lingual brace

bloecke.text: Like any other fixed brace, the inner-lying brace can be used to correct the following tooth misalignments:
Open bite Even with the mouth closed, there is a gap between the upper and lower teeth.
Crowding The teeth are rotated or crooked because they do not have enough space in the jaw.
Frontal bite There is a large gap between the front teeth of the upper and lower jaw.
Overbite With an overbite, the upper jaw protrudes. It is too large in relation to the lower jaw, or the lower jaw is too small.
Crossbite With a crossbite, the chewing surfaces of the teeth no longer meet correctly when biting down; instead, the upper teeth sit behind the lower teeth.
Gaps between teeth There is too much space in the jaw, causing gaps to form between the teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: More than just invisible: advantages of the WIN lingual brace

bloecke.text: The lingual brace offers numerous advantages compared to conventional fixed braces, is in no way inferior in terms of treatment results, and ensures long-term straight teeth.
Suitable for teenagers and adults
Corrects almost all bite positions and tooth misalignments
Almost invisible from the outside
Ultra-flat brackets for high wearing comfort
Low breakage rate and high adhesive strength
Optimal hygiene capability
Barely affects speech (a slight lisp may occur initially during the adjustment phase)
Lower risk of tooth decay and demineralisation of the tooth surfaces due to constant contact with saliva
Individually precise manufacturing of all components for stable tooth correction
No risk of allergy thanks to biocompatible materials

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fast treatment with lingual technology

bloecke.text: Depending on the patient and the degree of jaw and tooth misalignment, treatment with lingual technology can take anywhere from a few months to several years. Initial improvements in the tooth misalignment are usually visible after just a few weeks. More extensive tooth corrections, however, often require more time. In these cases, treatment can take up to four years. Following treatment, the lingual brace is replaced with a retainer, which ensures the long-term stability of the new tooth position.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs
Who covers the cost of the lingual brace?

bloecke.text: The cost of the lingual brace ranges between 5,500 and 10,500 euros – depending on the material of the brackets. It is not covered by statutory health insurance and must be paid for privately by the patient.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How is the lingual brace attached?

bloecke.text: The brackets of the fixed lingual brace are bonded to the inside of the teeth, either directly or using a transfer tray. The archwire is then firmly attached to the brackets. At regular intervals, the dentist or orthodontist adjusts the wire according to treatment progress, gradually guiding the teeth into their new position.

The dentists and orthodontists at KU64 Berlin will be happy to advise you personally about the many possible applications and give you tips on oral hygiene and caring for your lingual brace. Dental aesthetics | Bleaching (tooth whitening) | Digital Smile Design (DSD)

aligner.titel: Invisalign® Or Spark® Treatment In Berlin

bloecke.text: KU64 has 15 years of experience when it comes to invisible dental correction aligners. Our ELITE partner status bears witness to this!

At the KU64 dental practice, our orthodontists offer the crystal-clear and almost invisible braces from INVISALIGN®, which offer a high degree of subjective wearing comfort compared with conventional braces. Our specialist dentists for orthodontics enrich the range of treatments at KU64 with this innovative method from the USA and are on hand to offer you comprehensive information and individual advice. The invisible aligners from INVISALIGN® give you the chance to conjure up an attractive smile and get straight teeth without having to put up with the stigma of wearing braces!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Advantages OF Invisalign®:

bloecke.text: almost invisible appearance
removable, e.g. before important appointments
easy hygiene – thanks to the flexibility and absence of metal wires, teeth can be brushed and flossed regularly with INVISALIGN®
comfortable to wear
overlapping teeth can be corrected without wearing brackets and wires – also suitable for minor misalignments, for both teenagers and adults
smile whenever and as much as you like

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW Does Invisalign® Work?

bloecke.text: Similarly to a treatment with conventional braces, if you opt for the invisible INVISALIGN® solution, we first take photos, X-rays and impressions of your dentition at our practice and draw up a treatment plan. This data is then sent to Align Technology, the manufacturer of INVISALIGN® braces, and converted there into a 3D digital representation. This allows our orthodontists to create a 3D simulation of the entire treatment, which helps to visualise the planned results individually. In other words, with INVISALIGN® technology, your smile can become a “designer smile” too!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Use OF Invisalign® FOR Teenagers AND Adults

bloecke.text: Once we have determined the course of your treatment together with you virtually at our practice, you will see the movement of your dentition in a 3D animation. A series of so-called invisible or transparent “aligners” (from the English “to align” – to bring into a straight line, to arrange) is then custom-made for you based on the data obtained. The aligners for each INVISALIGN® set are made separately for the upper and lower jaw from lightweight plastic material and fit precisely onto your teeth. The INVISALIGN® aligners are worn for at least two weeks and then exchanged for new ones, with each aligner differing slightly from the previous one – this is how INVISALIGN® gently moves your teeth into the desired position: you will be proud of the results and your new smile!

The length of treatment with the invisible or transparent INVISALIGN® braces, which the treating dentists and orthodontists determine at the start of treatment, varies in duration and cost depending on the level of difficulty of the specific case. As a rule, treatment with INVISALIGN® takes between six and 18 months.

Wearing time: 22 hours daily. The INVISALIGN® aligner should only be removed for eating and cleaning your teeth. Approximately every two to three weeks, you receive a new aligner (for each jaw) until the treatment goal is achieved. Afterwards, as with treatment using fixed braces, we recommend a retainer to maintain the result achieved with INVISALIGN® on a lasting basis.

The invisible or transparent INVISALIGN® aligner is also suitable for teenagers from the age of eleven who no longer have any milk teeth. However, some teeth may still be coming through. This is taken into account accordingly when the aligner is made. INVISALIGN® also delivers particularly good results for relapse cases, partial orthodontic treatments, and resolving crowding, where not all teeth need to be fitted with fixed braces.

Getting used to it: this only takes a few days, after which INVISALIGN® is generally well tolerated. For teenagers (adapted treatment with INVISALIGN Teen®), there is a colour-coding system that shows whether the aligner has been worn for the required number of hours or days.

The KU64 dental practice is an official INVISALIGN® provider and has been awarded Platinum status for frequent use of the INVISALIGN® method. We are happy to explain how Invisalign® works! Please get in touch with us if you have any questions about INVISALIGN® treatment. Our orthodontists are also happy to help with any questions not answered in the INVISALIGN® FAQs!
