fissurenversiegelung.titel: Fissure Sealing in Berlin for Children

bloecke.text: There is a sensible and effective preventive measure in the fight against tooth decay – especially for kids and teenagers, but also for adults. Fissures are small gaps, grooves, pits or notches in the chewing surfaces of the back teeth. Food remnants and bacteria tend to collect in these grooves, which can be up to 1 mm deep and 0.05 mm narrow, and are difficult to remove even with excellent oral hygiene. Particularly at the back of the mouth, thorough cleaning of the teeth is almost impossible, and the risk of decay is above average. To avoid irreversible damage to permanent teeth caused by decay, we recommend a simple but sensible preventive measure for you and your family: fissure sealing for children.

Children's teeth that have been sealed develop decay far less often and are also considerably easier to clean. Even in childhood, shortly after the permanent back teeth have come through, and for healthy, decay-free teeth in adults, this preventive measure is a worthwhile investment in your health.

Under certain conditions, fissure sealing is a treatment supported by statutory health insurance providers. We, the dental specialists at KU64, provide competent advice and support: from choosing the best dental measure to protect your teeth (or your children's teeth) through to professional treatment and responsible aftercare, we are by your side.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Technique and materials used in fissure sealing for children

bloecke.text: The working procedures and materials used in sealing the fissures of permanent teeth are considered well-established and highly reliable. The specialist team at KU64 makes use of the latest developments and research findings in dentistry in this regard. Today, the filling material generally consists of a high-quality, thin-flowing resin that is hardened with light and supplies the tooth with fluoride to strengthen it. Only occasionally is a special dental cement used for fissure sealing, which has good fluoride-releasing properties but does not last as long.

Applying the sealing material generally requires a thoroughly cleaned and dry tooth. For optimal adhesion of the sealant, the fissures are conditioned with a special acid, cleaned and dried again, and then filled precisely. The filling is then hardened with a UV-like light matched to the particular resin, which is directed at specific points on the treated tooth. The entire treatment, which is completely pain-free, takes 15 to 30 minutes. From this point on, the problematic pits in the chewing surfaces are filled. This makes the chewing surface and the tooth smoother, more resistant, and easier to clean with a toothbrush.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 30 minutes of fissure sealing for years without toothache

bloecke.text: Fissure sealing for children, which significantly reduces the risk of decay, particularly in the back teeth, is one of those treatments that requires no invasive steps and causes no toothache.

Fissure sealing does not damage the tooth structure. To take away your child's fear of this sensible sealing of the fissures and to make future visits to the dentist easier for them, the team at KU64 places great emphasis on being child-friendly in every respect. Even the waiting room resembles a children's playroom.

Here, the joy of exploring replaces the usual boredom, providing distraction and relaxation. Our offer of laughter gas for anxiety-free treatment under mild sedation gives restless and nervous patients a feeling of lightness and reassurance, is guaranteed to bring a Big Smile to their face, and thus takes away the fear of the next visit to the children's dentist. This is because follow-up after fissure sealing is of great importance. Sealed fissures last around 7 to 10 years and must be checked continuously to ensure they remain intact. Repairing a damaged filling is straightforward and, like the whole treatment, free of side effects. Good dental care, however, plays a major part in how long a fissure sealing lasts!
Get in touch with us! Our children's dentists and preventive care assistants will be happy to advise you on fissure sealing and all our other services for children's dental care!

knochenaufbau.titel: Bone Augmentation for Implants in the Jaw

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Sinus Lift AND Bone Augmentation FOR AN Implant

bloecke.text: For implants to be used successfully and for the long term, a good supply of bone needs to be present. As a general rule: the stronger the bone, the better the hold for the implant. However, if the bone doesn't meet the necessary requirements, the quality of the jawbone or the maxillary sinus can be improved before the actual implantation using various bone augmentation procedures, such as a sinus lift. The effort and cost involved can vary considerably from one procedure to another.

Bone loss in the jawbone is usually caused by periodontitis, tooth loss, or the high chewing pressure placed on the sinus floor by dentures. Factors such as genetic predisposition, general medical conditions, medication, age and smoking, for example, also influence the extent of the bone loss.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bone Augmentation FOR AN Implant: Requirements

bloecke.text: For an implant to have optimal hold, sufficient bone height is required, and depending on the implant, sufficient bone width in the jawbone is needed too. Reconstructing bone width tends to be less problematic than increasing bone height.

As a rule, the lower jaw generally has a higher bone density and quality than the upper jaw, which increases the chances of a successful implantation. In the upper jaw, however, the curved shape of the maxillary sinus often means there isn't enough natural bone to securely anchor a dental implant. In this case, a so-called sinus lift can help.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: External Sinus Lift & Internal Sinus Lift

bloecke.text: A sinus lift is the general term for the surgical thickening or raising of the floor of the maxillary sinus, and a distinction is made between an external and an internal sinus lift. A sinus lift can only be carried out on the upper jaw, where the patient's own bone or a bone substitute material is surgically placed beneath the maxillary sinus. This creates greater bone height, which, after a healing period of around four months, provides sufficient hold for a dental implant.

The external and internal sinus lift differ in that the external sinus lift is the more involved procedure, since it is only used when the existing bone height is very low and several millimetres of bone height need to be gained. To do this, the wall of the maxillary sinus has to be exposed with the greatest precision and care, so that the bone material can then be placed in the cavity between the mucous membrane and the bone.

An internal sinus lift is a minimally invasive procedure in which access to the floor of the maxillary sinus is gained through the drill channel for the later implant. The advantage here is that no second surgical site needs to be opened. However, this method also requires patience and a high degree of precision, particularly since visibility through the drill hole can sometimes be very limited.

zahnarztangst.titel: Dental anxiety a thing of the past dentist for nervous patients in Berlin

bloecke.text: We, the specialists at KU64, give your anxiety – or your child's anxiety – no chance!

Through our extraordinary feel-good ambience, our service team, who will welcome you warmly, and a specialised, experienced team of dentists, assistants and prophylaxis staff, we want to make your and your children's stay at our practice a pleasant one – with a separate play waiting area.
"Modern dentistry is far more pleasant and much less frightening than it was in past decades," says Dr Stephan Ziegler from the KU64 dental practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What can be done about anxiety?

bloecke.text: The secret: a mixture of various approaches, well-trained staff and innovative ideas. It all begins with the practice's interior in warm yellow-orange tones, or the fragrance columns that create a pleasant atmosphere. For mild cases, a glass of sparkling wine at the KU64 reception before treatment can help. Warm, caring staff who look after the patient – for example, holding their hand during treatment – combined with particularly short waiting times at the practice, further reduce anxiety. Patients respond very well to the overhead monitors. Here, patients have the chance to watch a film during treatment – so they completely forget about the injection! Following the motto "out of sight, out of mind". But generally speaking, instruments and syringes simply have no place within the patient's field of view, as they only provoke anxiety!

Part of KU64's practice concept is a numbing gel applied before the injection – something patients particularly appreciate. The special gel, available in six different flavours (from piña colada to mint), is applied to the gum and gently massaged in. The actual needle prick is barely noticeable!

"We have done away with everything that causes patients fear and panic during treatment," says Dr Stephan Ziegler, dentist and owner of the Berlin dental practice KU64. The practice's ambience on the Kurfürstendamm is based on the latest psychological findings. According to these, the colour orange is said to create a pleasant mood and actively counteract stress. Compared to white walls, orange appears noticeably warmer. With its sunny, sandy colours, Ziegler's practice therefore resembles a dune landscape, evoking a beach-like feeling.

For patients whose anxiety is so great that they have already put off urgently needed treatment, KU64 also offers treatment under general anaesthetic. Only modern and effective anaesthetics are used to prevent pain. When treatment takes place under these conditions, the sensation of pain is switched off.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Anxiety-free treatment for children

bloecke.text: Your children are also well looked after. Since 2010, through the entrance at Kurfürstendamm 64, we have had a separate children's reception area on the 4th floor that leaves nothing to be desired. Time passes playfully, often faster than some little ones would like.
Our 4 paediatric dentists and 3 paediatric prophylaxis assistants take plenty of time for the children, speak their language, and in doing so playfully take away their anxiety.
Should treatment turn out to be more extensive after all, there is still the option of treatment under laughing gas, twilight sleep, or general anaesthetic.
Do you have any further questions? Then please get in touch with our dental specialists or our KU64 service team for a personal consultation.

knirscherschiene.titel: Bite Splint – A Grinding Splint Protects AGAINST Teeth Grinding

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Anti-grinding splints help!

bloecke.text: Anyone who feels pain in the jaw or jaw joint after a night's sleep may have been clenching or grinding their teeth heavily during the preceding hours. According to studies by American researchers, around 30 per cent of all people clench and grind their teeth at night – in dentistry, this is known as bruxism. The causes are often stress and emotional strain, which are, of course, very common nowadays. Even children and young people grind their teeth. Sometimes the grinding is really loud. In most cases, however, it is a silent clenching, which is no less destructive.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The consequences of nighttime teeth grinding

bloecke.text: The following consequences are cause for concern for patients:
Wear of the teeth
Loosening
Destruction of dental restorations
Morning pain in the jaw or jaw joint
Headaches
Muscle tension in the neck and shoulder area

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What helps against teeth grinding?

bloecke.text: Medication can ease the symptoms but does not remove their causes. An effective symptomatic therapy is a bite splint, also known as an anti-grinding splint or grinding splint. This splint resembles a boxer's mouthguard and effectively protects your teeth from grinding damage. Although the bite splint does not stop the teeth grinding itself, it significantly reduces the damage bruxism causes to your teeth. What has been spared from your teeth can often be seen on the splint after just a few weeks or months!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: THE Bite Splint AS an Individual Piece

bloecke.text: To make the anti-grinding splint, impressions of the upper and lower jaw are required. The splint is then individually made by the dental technician and fitted. During the first 7–10 nights, the anti-grinding splint is usually felt to be irritating, as the familiar ritual (nighttime clenching and grinding) doesn't work with the splint in place. However, this changes after 7–10 nights. At that point, the so-called engram in the chewing muscles is erased, and you sleep noticeably more relaxed.
From then on, at least your valuable teeth are protected by the bite splint. However, such a splint does not replace the long-term treatment of the (underlying) problem.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treating causes rather than symptoms

bloecke.text: Psychological or psychotherapeutic treatment can also be considered (in combination with a bite splint) to get to the bottom of nighttime teeth grinding. Stress in family or work settings could well be the cause. Talk to us about this – we are happy to advise you on all questions relating to functional diagnostics and craniomandibular dysfunction (CMD).

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is meant by craniomandibular dysfunction (CMD)?

bloecke.text: CMD refers to a disrupted interaction between the teeth of the upper and lower jaw and the jaw joint, which can affect the entire body.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: serious health problems caused by cmd

bloecke.text: Toothache, jaw joint pain, and pain in the face, head or neck area, as well as tension and pain in other parts of a patient's musculoskeletal system, right through to tinnitus, can often be traced back to CMD. Here you can find out more about craniomandibular dysfunction and our treatment concept.
Our practice team is happy to advise you on protective splints and how you can permanently banish the troublesome issue of teeth grinding from your life.

inlays-onlays.titel: Inlays in Berlin: Aesthetic Tooth Repair with a Stable Fit

bloecke.text: Inlays are a high-quality and extremely long-lasting restoration for damaged teeth, individually made for you in our dental laboratory. An inlay is very well suited to larger areas of damage to a tooth and lasts longer than a filling. It can also be used when a filling would no longer be sufficient. At KU64 we offer gold inlays and, as the top aesthetic option, computer-made ceramic inlays using the modern CEREC method in just one sitting. We are very happy to advise you on the possible applications, costs and alternatives in a personal appointment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Table of Contents

bloecke.text: The most important facts at a glance When damage gets bigger: Why an inlay can offer more stability than a filling Your advantages with inlays at KU64 What materials are available for inlays? An inlay gives you many advantages This is how treatment with an inlay works at KU64 Are there also disadvantages? Dentistry you can rely on Our specialists for inlays Your inlay is in the best hands with us Already read? FAQs – Frequently asked questions about inlays

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The most important facts at a glance
Preserving your tooth to the highest standard

bloecke.text: When fillings are no longer sufficient and as much natural tooth as possible should be preserved at the same time, inlays are the perfect choice before dentures become necessary. Especially in the back teeth, they offer a precise and aesthetic solution that combines the function and natural look of the teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Stability and longevity

bloecke.text: Inlays are robust, well tolerated and designed for long-term care. They help to stabilise a damaged tooth rather than placing unnecessary strain on it. They also give you a secure feeling in everyday life when chewing, speaking and smiling.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Precise treatment with CEREC

bloecke.text: At KU64 you benefit from modern CEREC technology for particularly accurate planning and a precisely fitting treatment for your inlays on the very same day. Using the virtual impression on the computer, your inlay can be precisely matched to your existing tooth structure, which ensures the best possible result.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When damage gets bigger: Why an inlay can offer more stability than a filling

bloecke.text: When a tooth is more badly damaged, you often notice this not only when looking in the mirror but also in everyday life. Perhaps you suddenly chew more carefully on one side because a tooth no longer feels as strong as before. Perhaps you have an older filling that no longer seals the tooth quite as reliably, or food frequently gets stuck there. At this point, many patients don't just want a quick repair. They want a treatment that stabilises the tooth, looks natural and works reliably in the long term.

Once a hole has formed in a tooth, classic fillings aren't always enough if the resulting damage is already too great. This is exactly where an inlay can offer advantages over a classic filling. While fillings cope well with smaller defects, an inlay offers a precisely fitting, load-bearing and long-lasting restoration even for larger areas of damage in the back teeth. H2: What is an inlay?

An inlay is an individually made insert filling used to precisely treat your damaged tooth. Unlike a classic filling, it is not modelled directly and freely within the tooth, but is made, fitted and then firmly placed outside the mouth in our in-house laboratory. It is therefore also known as an indirect filling. This is exactly where the great advantage lies: the inlay can be very precisely matched to the defect and, especially for larger areas of damage in the back teeth, offers more stability and a higher-quality treatment than a conventional filling. And best of all: unlike a filling, an inlay often lasts a lifetime.

Inlays therefore come into consideration in dentistry above all when a tooth needs more than a simple filling can provide, but is not yet so badly damaged that a crown is immediately required. They thus serve to preserve the tooth and close the gap between a direct filling and a larger reconstructive treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Filling, inlay, onlay, overlay, partial crown – what's the difference?

bloecke.text: When it comes to treating a damaged tooth, this fortunately often doesn't require a full denture. The natural tooth can be preserved through restoration. Here we distinguish between different aesthetic dental measures according to the extent of restoration required for your tooth:
A filling is placed directly into the tooth at the practice and is mainly used for smaller defects.

An inlay is a precisely fitting so-called indirect filling made in the laboratory for larger areas of damage within the tooth structure, usually on the chewing surface or in the space between teeth. It is considered a high-quality alternative to a direct filling, especially when the defect is larger and the contact point with the neighbouring tooth needs to be precisely reconstructed.
Onlays and overlays are variants of the inlay that go a step further: they don't just treat a defect within the tooth but also cover large parts of the chewing surface.

The partial crown is more extensive still. It is used when a tooth is more badly damaged and the entire chewing surface or several cusps need to be reconstructed, without covering the whole tooth as with a full crown.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Your advantages with inlays at KU64
Precise planning with modern technology

bloecke.text: For your new ceramic inlay, KU64 uses the gentle and quick CEREC method. This makes high-quality restorations possible in just one sitting!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Specialised dentists for high-quality inlays

bloecke.text: Our dentists specialise in high-quality, long-lasting restorations and continually further their training. This means you benefit from the best materials and gentlest treatment methods.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Experience for long-lasting results

bloecke.text: With over 20 years of experience, we ensure that your inlays are functional, stable and aesthetically convincing – from the choice of material through to the final fitting.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment tailored to you

bloecke.text: Our interdisciplinary and multilingual team offers you not only advice in your mother tongue but also treatment tailored to you individually, so you feel completely well looked after at all times.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What materials are available for inlays?

bloecke.text: Inlays can be made from different materials. Which material suits you best depends mainly on how large the defect is, how much strain the tooth is under, what aesthetic expectations you have and which solution makes sense in the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Ceramic inlays

bloecke.text: Ceramic inlays are today the preferred choice for many patients when aesthetics, tooth preservation and high-quality treatment are the priorities. Their colour can be matched very well to the natural tooth structure, which makes them particularly inconspicuous. They are long-lasting, resistant to chewing forces, colour-stable and well tolerated biologically.

Especially in the back teeth, ceramic inlays combine a natural look with high precision. This makes them particularly suitable for people who want a functionally reliable treatment. This is combined with the advantage that they blend harmoniously into the tooth at the same time. They can be particularly well combined with digital technology and a virtual impression via CEREC, and can therefore often be made and fitted in just one sitting.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gold inlays

bloecke.text: Gold inlays are considered particularly robust and long-lasting. Gold is regarded as a very resilient material that also withstands strong chewing forces well. At the same time, it is soft enough not to place unnecessary strain on the opposing tooth through abrasion.

From a functional point of view, gold inlays are therefore still a very high-quality solution, used mainly in the heavily loaded back teeth. Visually, however, they are noticeably more visible than ceramic. For patients for whom longevity and stability are the main priorities, gold can nevertheless be a very good choice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Composite inlays

bloecke.text: Composite inlays play a minor role in dentistry, as they cannot match ceramic or gold in terms of durability.

For some situations, composite inlays can nevertheless be a sensible option, for example when a rather simple or more cost-conscious treatment is desired. Whether they are advisable in an individual case depends on the strain on the tooth, the size of the defect and the long-term expectations of the treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: An inlay gives you many advantages

bloecke.text: An inlay is more than just a treatment for a damaged tooth. It is a high-quality solution when a defect has become too large for a classic filling, but the tooth should nevertheless be preserved.
These are the biggest advantages:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Precise fit

bloecke.text: An inlay is individually adapted to your tooth and then precisely fitted. This means the defect can be treated very precisely. Especially with larger areas of damage in the back teeth, this precision is an important advantage over normal fillings, as it contributes to a secure fit and a natural chewing feeling.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Great stability for larger defects

bloecke.text: When a tooth needs more than a classic filling, an inlay can offer more stability. It is especially suitable when the defect is already larger but enough healthy tooth structure is still present to preserve the tooth at a high quality. This means the tooth can be given a load-bearing treatment without immediately having to choose a more extensive solution such as a crown.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The best possible contact point between teeth

bloecke.text: A well-made inlay from our dental laboratory helps to restore the natural contact with the neighbouring tooth as precisely as possible. This is important so that food residue doesn't get stuck as easily, the tooth remains well integrated functionally, and your bite feels harmonious again in everyday life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Natural aesthetics and good tolerability

bloecke.text: Ceramic inlays in particular convince with a natural tooth appearance and a very harmonious match to your existing teeth. At the same time, high-quality materials such as ceramic are considered well tolerated. This means you benefit not only from stability but also from a treatment that blends aesthetically unobtrusively into your smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Long-lasting treatment with a focus on preserving the tooth

bloecke.text: An inlay is designed for long-term treatment and durability. It helps to supplement damaged tooth structure at a high quality and preserve the natural tooth for as long as possible. This idea of tooth preservation fits particularly well with the modern, precise and tissue-sparing dentistry practised at KU64.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: This is how treatment with an inlay works at KU64

bloecke.text: Treatment with an inlay at KU64 follows a clear process with your dentist. The aim is to treat the damaged tooth precisely, preserve as much healthy tooth structure as possible, and give you back a stable, natural feeling when chewing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Examination and planning

bloecke.text: First, we check how large the defect is and whether an inlay is the right treatment for your tooth. We look carefully at how much healthy tooth structure remains, how much strain the tooth is under, and which solution makes sense medically and aesthetically.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Removal of decay or old filling

bloecke.text: In the next step, the affected tooth is carefully cleaned. Our dentist removes decay, leaking areas or an old filling so that a stable basis can be created for the new treatment. This lays the foundation for a precisely fitting, long-term treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Digital scan or impression

bloecke.text: We then record the shape of your tooth precisely using a digital scan or, depending on the situation, a classic impression. This precision is crucial so that the inlay later sits functionally, tightly and comfortably.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Manufacture of the inlay

bloecke.text: Based on the recorded data, your inlay is individually made. Our laboratory creates a precisely fitting reconstruction, matched to your tooth, your bite and the natural shape of your row of teeth. With ceramic treatments, the focus is not only on stability but also on aesthetic adaptation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 5. Fitting and check-up

bloecke.text: As soon as the inlay is ready, we can place it in the tooth and secure it firmly. With CEREC, ceramic inlays are usually available on the very same day! We then check carefully whether everything fits perfectly, whether the contacts with the neighbouring teeth are correct, and whether your bite feels natural.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are there also disadvantages?

bloecke.text: An inlay is a high-quality, long-lasting treatment, but it is not automatically the best solution in every situation. What matters is always how large the defect is, how much healthy tooth structure remains, and what functional and aesthetic goal is to be achieved. Precisely because inlays are precisely and individually made, alongside many advantages there are also a few further points to consider.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Not always the best choice for every defect

bloecke.text: An inlay is especially sensible when a defect is too large for a filling but not yet large enough for a crown. For very small areas of damage, a normal filling is often the simpler and more affordable solution. If, on the other hand, the tooth is already badly weakened, a partial crown or crown may be medically more sensible. This is exactly why your treating dentist always checks individually which treatment is best for your tooth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Higher costs than a filling

bloecke.text: An inlay is more elaborate than a classic filling because it is individually made and precisely fitted. As a result, the costs are usually significantly higher than for a direct filling. For many patients, this is nevertheless worthwhile if they want a more stable, more precise and longer-lasting treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Often two appointments required

bloecke.text: A classic filling can be placed directly in one sitting. In many cases, two treatment appointments are needed for an inlay; only with the CEREC method using ceramic inlays is the treatment very often possible in just one appointment. However, the additional effort serves the precise fit and the high-quality treatment, which also has a significantly longer durability than a direct filling.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – Frequently asked questions about inlays
What does an inlay cost in Berlin?

bloecke.text: The cost of an inlay in Berlin depends mainly on the material, the size of the defect and the dental technical effort involved. As such, no general amount can be given.

Important to know: statutory health insurers generally do not cover inlays as a full standard benefit. Insured patients are only entitled to a co-payment-free standard filling, usually made of self-adhesive materials in the back teeth. If you choose an inlay instead, the insurer usually only contributes an amount equivalent to the comparable standard treatment, or a small subsidy. You bear the remaining amount yourself. Whether and to what extent a subsidy is possible always depends on your individual findings and treatment plan.

Before treatment begins, we provide you with an individual treatment and cost plan. This shows you transparently which costs your health insurer covers via the fixed subsidy and how much your own contribution will be.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What's the difference between an inlay, onlay and overlay?

bloecke.text: Inlays repair larger holes and damage within the tooth, while onlays also replace larger parts of the upper part of the tooth. Onlays are thus a particular variant of inlays that can preserve the tooth in cases of larger damage, when it doesn't yet need to be fully crowned. If onlays replace the entire upper area of the tooth like an artificial cap, this is referred to as an overlay.

Inlays, onlays and overlays are ultimately the same type of treatment within holistic dentistry: indirect fillings that come from the laboratory. Dentists therefore often use the terms inlay and onlay interchangeably.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does an inlay last?

bloecke.text: An inlay is designed for long-term treatment and, with good care, can work stably for many years – often even a lifetime. How long it lasts in an individual case depends mainly on the material, the precision of fit, the strain during chewing, and your oral hygiene. Gold inlays are considered particularly long-lasting; ceramic inlays, however, are convincing due to their natural aesthetics and high tolerability, with almost the same longevity.

Regular check-ups help preserve the treatment in the long term and protect the tooth from diseases such as decay. Especially compared to a classic filling, an inlay can therefore often be the higher-quality and more durable solution.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is an inlay better than a filling or a crown?

bloecke.text: That depends on the size of the defect and the remaining tooth structure. An inlay is usually the better choice when a defect is too large for a classic filling, but the tooth is not yet so badly damaged that a crown is already necessary.

Compared to a filling, an inlay can offer more stability and precision for larger defects, as it is precisely made outside the mouth and then fitted. This makes it particularly suitable for the back teeth. A classic filling, on the other hand, is usually more sensible when the defect is smaller and can be built up directly in the tooth.

Compared to a crown, an inlay has the advantage that in many cases more natural tooth structure can be preserved. A crown is more appropriate when the tooth is already so badly weakened or destroyed that a partial treatment is no longer sufficient.
In summary: the inlay is the treatment of choice between a filling and a crown – higher quality and more load-bearing than a filling, but more tissue-sparing than a crown.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does the treatment hurt?

bloecke.text: Worrying about pain is completely understandable, especially if you come to the dentist with unpleasant past experiences or an uneasy feeling. The good news is: an inlay can be treated very well under local anaesthetic. The local anaesthetic works quickly and enables painless treatment. During treatment, many people therefore feel more pressure or vibration rather than actual pain.

If you are an anxious patient, simply talk to us. Our staff are specially trained in dealing with dental anxiety and are there for you with understanding. The dentists at KU64 ensure a calm process during treatment, in which nothing happens unexpectedly and every step is explained transparently and thoroughly.

kinderprophylaxe.titel: Children's Preventive Dentistry in Berlin – The KU64 Premium Prophylaxis for Children and Young People

bloecke.text: Dear parents, dear children,

We want every person to have healthy teeth and gums for life. To achieve this goal, children need to learn the right approach to dental care from an early age, with parents and dentist working together.
This includes:
daily dental care
a healthy diet
regular preventive check-ups and
a tailored prevention programme for kids with our charming tooth fairies.

For children, preventive measures are still largely covered by statutory health insurance. However, a professional teeth cleaning such as the KU64 Premium Children's Prophylaxis is not included in the statutory health insurance benefits catalogue, even for children, and must be paid for privately. As a rule, this costs children only 40 to 80 euros.

Professional teeth cleaning takes longer in special cases, such as for those wearing brackets, with black tartar, or discolouration caused by medication, etc. In these cases, we charge an additional 5 euros for every 5 minutes required.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Professional teeth cleaning for children and young people – it's an educational treatment!

bloecke.text: First, we carry out what is known as an oral hygiene assessment in our practice: plaque is stained with a special agent to make it clearly visible. This allows us to show your child in the mirror where they need to brush better. We note down the number of tooth surfaces with plaque and the areas where the gums bleed on contact. At later check-ups, this makes it easy to see whether brushing habits have improved.

abschnitte.ueberschrief: Brushing your teeth – but doing it properly!

bloecke.text: To motivate your child and help them better understand the treatment as well as proper tooth brushing, we show the plaque in our unique cavity cave. Once stained, the clearly visible plaque is carefully and gently removed by our specially trained prevention staff, and the tooth surfaces are polished to a mirror-smooth finish. Each tooth is then coated with a highly effective protective varnish, which protects the teeth from decay for up to three months. For longer-term protection, we recommend having a fissure sealant applied at our practice. However, there is no fixed recommendation as to the age at which such a sealant should be applied, as tooth development varies from child to child.
From the age of three, we also show your child how to brush their own teeth as effectively as possible, to prevent plaque from building up again.

All of this takes place in a relaxed and friendly atmosphere, focused solely on your child's dental health. The child should come to understand that they are responsible for their own dental health and develop a genuine enjoyment of dental care. For us paediatric dentists, this is the most important task of all!

weisheitszaehne.titel: Wisdom Tooth Removal in Berlin – Professional Wisdom Tooth Surgery from One of Our Specialists

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gentle wisdom tooth removal by our experienced oral and maxillofacial surgeons

bloecke.text: The removal of wisdom teeth is one of the most common operations in dentistry. The so-called "eights" are removed in almost every second person in Germany before the age of 30. The most common reason: there simply isn't enough room in the jaw for the wisdom teeth. The wisdom teeth then remain trapped within the jawbone. Dentists and oral surgeons refer to this as "retention of the wisdom tooth".

abschnitte.ueberschrief: Wisdom teeth often cause problems in the mouth and jaw

bloecke.text: A wisdom tooth can lead to inflammation, abscesses or cysts. Thanks to the use of antibiotics, however, these severe complications are now extremely rare. The main cause of this inflammation is the formation of a hood-shaped gum pocket, which, although accessible to the germs in the mouth, is difficult or impossible to clean properly. An acute wisdom tooth infection is usually accompanied by swelling, difficulty swallowing and severe pain. This kind of inflammation is the most common reason for removal.

But it doesn't have to come to inflammation in the first place. Modern surgery already offers a kind of early detection. Through an examination and a panoramic X-ray, which shows the position of the wisdom teeth and the surrounding anatomical structures, your dentist can already assess whether a preventive removal of the wisdom teeth makes sense. If recurring inflammation occurs directly at the wisdom tooth or in its surrounding area, the tooth should be removed from the mouth. Other reasons for removing the "eight" include tooth decay or even root infections, cysts or other pathological changes, or signs of resorption affecting the neighbouring tooth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Surgery without general anaesthetic

bloecke.text: The surgical removal of wisdom teeth is normally carried out as an outpatient procedure under local anaesthetic. For particularly anxious patients, the operation can be performed under general anaesthetic – however, this must be paid for privately by patients with statutory health insurance. In the first few days after tooth removal, swelling of the cheek, difficulty swallowing and pain in the area of the surgical site are to be expected. These symptoms should, however, disappear after three to five days.

behandlung-in-narkose.titel: Anaesthesia – Pain-free Treatment While Asleep Under General Anaesthetic at the Dentist

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Anaesthesia and General Anaesthetic for Dental Treatment

bloecke.text: At KU64, you and our young patients have the option of "sleeping through" your treatment with us. Fear of dental treatment, lengthy restorative work or operations are all good reasons for treatment under anaesthesia/general anaesthetic. Some anaesthesia methods are carried out by our dentists, others by qualified anaesthetists. An external, highly competent team of anaesthetists, with whom we have worked closely for many years, ensures our patients are looked after in the best possible way before, during and after treatment. Our reception team will be happy to arrange an appointment for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Types of Anaesthesia at KU64:

bloecke.text: Pre-numbing: with a fruit-flavoured gel that makes the subsequent needle prick seem completely harmless.
Local anaesthesia: with this method, we achieve complete pain relief in over 95% of cases.

Nitrous oxide: a lovely solution for children as well as older, anxious patients. The benefits of nitrous oxide treatment are that any gag reflex is greatly reduced or eliminated entirely, and the perception of pain is significantly lessened.

Twilight sleep: with so-called twilight sleep, a special "feel-good cocktail" – usually Dormicum and Propofol – is administered intravenously. The advantage of this type of anaesthesia is that it places less strain on the body than a general anaesthetic, and as a patient you remain responsive, without being able to fully remember the treatment afterwards.

General anaesthetic: ITN (intubation anaesthesia) is generally used for operations or in the treatment of children. Whether it's for several hours or just a minor procedure, our anaesthetists combine many years of experience with the very latest medical technology.
By the way:
If you wish, we can even administer an antidote at the end of the treatment, which makes the numb feeling wear off more quickly!

They help to relieve strain on the body and preserve quality of life. At KU64 in Berlin, we develop your personal Longevity concept for tooth preservation, prevention, aesthetics and long-term oral health.

bloecke.text: Healthy teeth and healthy gums don't just create a radiant smile – they also form the basis for your long-term, holistic health.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Why Longevity begins at the dentist

bloecke.text: When people think about Longevity, they usually think first of nutrition, exercise, sleep, supplements or skincare. At KU64, we think one step further: about your teeth and your gums.

Because oral health is not a nice-to-have. It's an important building block for long-term health, quality of life and wellbeing. Chronic inflammation in the mouth can put a strain on the body and increase health risks. Healthy gums, stable teeth and good chewing function, on the other hand, support what really matters in everyday life: eating, laughing, speaking and feeling good, without a second thought.

At KU64, we combine modern preventive care, precise diagnostics and sustainable treatment concepts into a Longevity approach for your oral health. Our aim is to detect inflammation early, preserve tooth structure for the long term, maintain function and aesthetics, and act as far ahead as possible – before small risks turn into bigger problems.

Because true beauty doesn't begin with teeth that merely look perfect on the surface. It begins with dental health that lasts. For us, Longevity at the dentist means: taking sensible precautions today, so that your smile stays strong, healthy and confident tomorrow too.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does Longevity mean?

bloecke.text: The term Longevity means roughly the same as long life. But this isn't just about living as many years as possible. The main focus is on the question of how long we stay healthy, active and capable. That's why, in connection with Longevity, a distinction is made between lifespan and healthspan: lifespan describes the sheer length of life, while healthspan describes the healthy years within that lifetime. Longevity, as a concept, therefore stands for all the measures and methods that make a long and good life possible.

However, Longevity is clearly distinct from concepts that aim to slow down or disguise ageing, for example through cosmetic surgery or other purely cosmetic measures. Healthy ageing doesn't mean halting the natural ageing process. Rather, it's about preserving physical, mental and social health for as long as possible through suitable measures and a conscious, mindful way of living. The World Health Organization (WHO) describes Healthy Ageing as a process in which functional abilities are maintained and developed that enable wellbeing in old age.
Modern Longevity concepts focus on prevention, healthy lifestyle habits, early diagnostics and individual strategies to identify risks in good time and preserve quality of life over the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Oral health as the basis for a long and good life

bloecke.text: The mouth is not an isolated part of the body. Teeth, gums, oral flora and jaw function influence how we eat, speak, laugh, present ourselves and feel in everyday life. At the same time, there is a close connection between oral health and general health. The WHO points out that oral and general health are linked – among other things in relation to diabetes, inflammatory conditions such as periodontitis, nutrition and caries risk.

This is exactly where Longevity in dentistry comes in: it means keeping your teeth, gums, bite and oral flora healthy, stable and functional for as long as possible. It's not about short-term repairs, but about a forward-looking strategy for tooth preservation, freedom from inflammation, aesthetics and quality of life.

That's why, at KU64, we don't wait until problems arise to look at your oral health. We want to spot risks early, prevent inflammation, preserve tooth structure, stabilise chewing function and keep your smile healthy and naturally beautiful in the long term. In this way, dentistry becomes an important part of your personal Longevity routine – for strong teeth today and a healthy tomorrow.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dentistry you can rely on
Nervous patients welcome

bloecke.text: Dental anxiety is no obstacle at KU64. We support you with calm procedures and empathetic explanations, so that your Longevity treatment is as pleasant as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: All specialists under one roof

bloecke.text: Longevity in dentistry puts a holistic view of your oral health centre stage. At KU64, dentists, implantologists, orthodontists and periodontists work hand in hand. This gives you fully coordinated, sustainable care.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Here for you 7 days a week

bloecke.text: Our practice is open seven days a week. Book your appointments for your Longevity treatment whenever they fit into your everyday life, without long waiting times.

Longevity in dentistry also means proper dental care. In our Prophylaxis Shop, you'll find specially selected products for your individual oral health, so that you keep a beautiful smile for a long time.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Who is the Longevity treatment at KU64 suitable for?

bloecke.text: Longevity dentistry makes sense for people of all ages who don't want to leave their oral health to chance. The focus is not just on individual complaints, but on your long-term health: stable teeth, healthy gums, a functioning bite and a naturally beautiful smile. The Longevity approach at KU64 is particularly suitable if you want to take early precautions, identify risks and keep your teeth healthy for as long as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For health-conscious people with high standards

bloecke.text: Do you pay attention to nutrition, sleep, exercise and prevention, and want to strategically include your dental health in your overall health concept too? Then Longevity dentistry is a particularly good fit for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For patients with bleeding gums or a periodontitis risk

bloecke.text: Bleeding gums, bad breath, receding gums or loose teeth shouldn't be dismissed as unimportant. They can be signs of inflammatory processes in the mouth, for example an early or existing periodontitis. This is exactly where Longevity dentistry comes in: we want to identify inflammation early, stabilise the gums and preserve your natural teeth for as long as possible. The earlier risks become visible, the more precisely we can counteract them.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For people who want to keep their own teeth for a long time

bloecke.text: Your own teeth are valuable. That's why tooth preservation is at the heart of what we do at KU64: through precise diagnostics, regular preventive care, gentle treatments and a clear strategy for your oral health. Longevity in dentistry means taking small changes seriously before they turn into bigger damage.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For older patients who want to secure their quality of life

bloecke.text: Chewing, laughing, speaking and enjoying life: healthy teeth are an important part of an active quality of life. As we get older, it becomes ever more important to have teeth, gums, dentures, implants and bite checked regularly. The Longevity approach helps keep existing restorations stable, prevent tooth loss and secure chewing function in the long term. The aim is for you to feel confident, well cared for and self-assured in the future too – in everyday life, while eating and while smiling.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For aesthetic patients

bloecke.text: Anyone who wants veneers, whitening or high-quality reconstructions first needs a healthy foundation. A beautiful smile only looks harmonious in the long run if the gums, tooth structure and bite are stable. That's why, at KU64, we combine aesthetic dentistry with prevention and functional planning. This creates a result that not only looks beautiful, but also suits your oral health, your face and your everyday life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For people with stress, grinding or muscle complaints

bloecke.text: Stress often shows up in the teeth too. Grinding, clenching, tense chewing muscles, headaches, jaw joint complaints or worn-down teeth can all be signs that your bite is under constant strain. That's why the jaw joint, muscles and tooth structure are also part of the Longevity view. At KU64, we check whether functional strain is putting your teeth at risk in the long term, and which measures can help to relieve the bite, muscles and teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The KU64 Longevity Check: how we analyse your oral health
1. Personal medical history and health profile

bloecke.text: Our Longevity Check begins with a holistic look at your individual situation. We take the time to record your personal medical history in detail. In this first step, we note your current lifestyle as well as any relevant pre-existing conditions and medications you're taking. Aspects such as your stress level, eating habits and daily oral hygiene also play a key role in our understanding of your oral health. We also discuss your current concerns and your aesthetic goals, so that together we can lay the foundation for your personal treatment plan.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Tooth and gum status

bloecke.text: In the next step, we build up a detailed picture of your oral health. This includes a precise examination of your teeth, gums and the entire periodontium. We check existing fillings, crowns and implants for stability and function, and assess the health of your mucous membranes. This thorough assessment forms the basis for identifying potential risks early and creating a tailor-made plan to preserve your dental health in the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Preventive care and caries risk analysis

bloecke.text: With our Prophylaxis 4.0, we use the most up-to-date methods to take your oral health to a new level. This includes a thorough professional dental clean, in which we gently remove biofilm and plaque even from hard-to-reach areas. We also use modern techniques such as Air-Flow for a radiant smile. Using scientifically based saliva tests, we determine your individual caries risk, so we can focus prevention exactly where it's needed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Bite, CMD and functional strain

bloecke.text: A healthy bite is the basis for chewing and speaking without complaints. That's why, as part of our Longevity Check, we look closely for signs of overload – for example, abrasion (loss of tooth structure), night-time grinding or clenching. We examine how your jaw joints and chewing muscles work together, in order to identify functional problems early. This ensures that teeth, jaw and muscles work together in harmony.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 5. Aesthetic analysis of your smile

bloecke.text: An aesthetic smile is an expression of vitality and wellbeing. That's why we look at your smile holistically: we don't just consider tooth colour, shape and position, but also assess the condition of existing restorations and how well they blend into your overall look. Our aim is a harmonious aesthetic that corresponds perfectly with your lip line and facial symmetry – for a smile that not only feels healthy, but looks it too.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 6. Individual Longevity plan

bloecke.text: We bring all the findings together into an individual Longevity plan, tailored precisely to your needs. This plan not only defines your ideal preventive care rhythm, but also gives clear treatment recommendations – from tooth preservation measures to aesthetic options. Together, we decide how to secure your dental health in the long term and support you on your way to a lastingly healthy smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Our range of services for your long-term dental health

bloecke.text: Longevity in dentistry is not a single treatment step, but an interplay of prevention, diagnostics, function, aesthetics and tooth preservation. Depending on your starting point, different services may be useful to prevent inflammation, stabilise teeth, relieve the bite or keep your smile healthy and naturally beautiful for the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Professional dental cleaning

bloecke.text: Professional dental cleaning is an important foundation for long-term healthy teeth and gums. We remove plaque, biofilm and staining, even from areas that are hard to reach at home. This treatment can help prevent caries and gum inflammation, and specifically improve your oral hygiene.
All information on professional dental cleaning

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Whitening

bloecke.text: Whitening can visibly lighten discoloured teeth and make your smile look fresher. Before whitening, we check whether your teeth and gums are healthy, so that the treatment can be planned safely and harmoniously. This way, aesthetics becomes part of a healthy foundation, not just a short-term beauty effect.
All information on whitening

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Night guard for grinding

bloecke.text: A night guard can protect your teeth if you grind or clench at night or during the day. It helps relieve strain on tooth structure, fillings, crowns and jaw joints. Particularly with stress, tension or worn-down teeth, it's an important building block for long-term tooth preservation.
All information on night guards for grinding

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Braces

bloecke.text: Braces can correct misaligned teeth, improving not only aesthetics but also function and the ability to clean the teeth properly. Crowded or overlapping teeth in particular make oral hygiene more difficult and can increase the risk of plaque, caries or gum problems. Orthodontic treatment can therefore also contribute to long-term oral health.
All information on braces

abschnitte.ueberschrift: CMD treatment

bloecke.text: CMD stands for craniomandibular dysfunction and describes problems in the interplay of teeth, jaw joints and chewing muscles. Signs can include a clicking jaw, headaches, neck tension, toothache with no clear cause, or a permanently tense bite. Our CMD treatment can help identify uneven strain and relieve teeth, muscles and jaw joints in the long term.
All information on CMD treatment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Osteopathy

bloecke.text: Osteopathy can be a useful addition to dental treatment when problems don't just arise locally in the teeth, but are linked to muscles, posture, jaw joints or patterns of tension. This holistic view of the body can be particularly helpful with CMD, grinding or chronic tension, to better understand the functional connections.
All information on osteopathy

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dentosophy

bloecke.text: Dentosophy looks at the functional interplay of teeth, jaw, breathing, tongue and posture. It can be particularly helpful when the bite, mouth function, jaw development or muscles are out of balance. As part of our Longevity concept, this treatment supports the idea of identifying functional causes early, rather than just treating symptoms.
All information on Dentosophy

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Periodontitis treatment

bloecke.text: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammation of the periodontium and, if left untreated, can lead to receding gums, bone loss and tooth loss. Periodontitis treatment aims to reduce inflammation, clean periodontal pockets and stabilise the periodontium for the long term. For Dental Longevity, it's one of the most important services if you experience bleeding gums, bad breath or loose teeth.
All information on periodontitis treatment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Caries risk assessment

bloecke.text: Caries risk assessment helps to identify your personal risk of new decay at an early stage. This can take into account, among other things, oral hygiene, diet, saliva, existing fillings and individual findings. This allows prevention to be planned more precisely, before damage to the tooth structure occurs.
All information on caries risk assessment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Caries treatment

bloecke.text: Caries treatment should be carried out as early and as gently as possible. The smaller the defect, the more healthy tooth structure can be preserved. Our modern approach to caries treatment therefore isn't just about filling a hole – it's about keeping the tooth stable, functional and aesthetically pleasing in the long term.
All information on caries treatment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Root canal treatment

bloecke.text: Root canal treatment may become necessary when the inside of a tooth becomes inflamed. The aim is to preserve the natural tooth despite deep inflammation, wherever possible. This is especially important for Dental Longevity, since keeping your own teeth is often the most sustainable solution – provided the tooth can be treated so that it is stable and free of inflammation.
All information on root canal treatment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fillings

bloecke.text: Fillings close minor to moderate tooth defects and protect the tooth from further damage. High-quality, well-fitted fillings support the stability, function and appearance of the tooth. In our Longevity concept, this isn't just about repair – it's about substance-sparing treatment and long-term tooth preservation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – Frequently asked questions about Longevity in dentistry
Which therapy is part of Longevity dentistry?

bloecke.text: The right Longevity therapy always depends on your personal starting point. At KU64, we don't develop a standard plan from this, but an individual treatment concept for tooth preservation, freedom from inflammation, function and aesthetics.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do veneers fit in with a Longevity concept?

bloecke.text: Yes, if the foundation is right. Veneers can improve the appearance of teeth, for example with discolouration, minor shape corrections, slight misalignments or unharmonious front teeth. However, for a beautiful long-term result, the gums, tooth structure and bite need to be healthy and stable. That's why, before any veneer treatment, we always check whether prevention, periodontitis therapy, caries treatment or a functional analysis should come first.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What role does denture/prosthetic work play in Dental Longevity?

bloecke.text: Dentures or prosthetic work can be an important part of Longevity dentistry when teeth are badly damaged or already missing. However, a fixed part of the Longevity concept is tooth preservation before tooth replacement, so that with forward-looking treatment, we do our best to ensure that, ideally, you never need dentures in the first place.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What benefits does the service at KU64 offer me?

bloecke.text: Longevity works best when prevention, diagnostics and therapy can be planned well and fit smoothly together. That's why the service at KU64 includes a large interdisciplinary team, modern diagnostics, long opening hours, online appointment booking, short distances between different specialist areas, and our own in-house dental laboratory.

lachgas.titel: Nitrous Oxide Sedation – Ideal for Kids and Nervous Patients

bloecke.text: Among the special features of the KU64 children's dentistry team are children's hypnosis, little bits of magic, and treatment with nitrous oxide – so that both little ones and grown-ups simply love coming to our dental practice!

More than 100 years ago, nitrous oxide was introduced as a method perfectly suited to treating nervous patients. In a low concentration, which thanks to today's technology cannot exceed 50 or 70 per cent, nitrous oxide is not only odourless but also completely safe for the patient.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which patients is nitrous oxide suitable for?

bloecke.text: Treatment with nitrous oxide is suitable for patients with dental phobia or dental anxiety, as well as for tense patients. It is also an ideal solution for children, allowing treatment to be carried out in a relaxed way. The benefits of nitrous oxide treatment are that any gag reflex is greatly reduced or completely switched off, and the perception of pain is also significantly reduced.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How nitrous oxide is used

bloecke.text: The nitrous oxide-oxygen mixture is given to you via a nasal mask, with the proportion of nitrous oxide gradually increased. In this way, you drift into a twilight state without losing consciousness. A pleasant feeling of relaxation sets in, and once treatment is complete, this twilight state slowly fades away as the oxygen level is raised back up to 100 per cent. Nitrous oxide must not be used if your nasal breathing is impaired or if you suffer from a condition involving shortness of breath.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are there any risks with nitrous oxide treatment?

bloecke.text: As we, the dental specialists at KU64, use only modern high-tech equipment and are excellently trained in nitrous oxide treatment, sedation with nitrous oxide is the safest form of calming a patient. To date, no side effects or risks are known, especially since you remain conscious throughout and all your reflexes remain intact. So if you have been diagnosed with dental anxiety, nitrous oxide treatment is ideally suited and, moreover, risk-free.
Do you have questions about nitrous oxide treatment? Then please get in touch with our (paediatric) dental specialists for a personal consultation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Holistic Dentistry Means Dentistry That Takes The Whole Body Into Account

bloecke.text: Holistic dentistry represents a form of therapy that goes beyond the mere treatment of symptoms. The mouth, with its teeth, is part of the human body and therefore has various interactions with it. To get to the root of certain (dental) conditions, holistic dentistry is recommended.
If periodontitis (a disease of the tooth-supporting structures) is present, the risk of cardiovascular disease, strokes or premature births may be increased.
Head, neck, shoulder and back pain, as well as tinnitus – so-called CMD symptoms – can have their cause in the jaw joints or in a misaligned bite.
Intolerances to materials – various gold alloys, amalgam, plastics – can be responsible for tiredness, exhaustion and a general feeling of being unwell.
Chronic inflammation in the teeth and jaw area leads to an increased build-up of bacteria in the blood and can impair performance as well as weaken the immune system.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Health Begins In The Mouth

bloecke.text: Our specialised dentists at the KU64 practice are the right point of contact for you. Following a holistic analysis of the mouth and body, and taking into account all your health questions, risks and wishes, we will work together with you to find the optimal treatment concept. Our practice also offers a network of competent doctors from many specialist fields relating to holistic dentistry, with whom we work closely together. Conventional medicine, naturopathy and biological medicine are combined here holistically for our patients.

Do you have further questions or would you like more information about holistic dentistry? You can also reach us quickly and easily online via our appointment form. Or simply send us an enquiry by email to info@ku64.de – we would be happy to get back to you!
Once active treatment has finished, the time begins for stabilising the tooth movement that has been achieved.

Taking this fact into account and drawing the necessary conclusions is essential to any orthodontic effort aimed at long-term success in achieving straight teeth. We therefore consider it essential to encourage our patients to help ensure the long-term stability of the treatment result themselves.

The removable retention appliances must be worn every night and, in some cases, during the day as well. The fixed retainer wire often used in the front tooth region provides additional stabilisation that does not depend on the patient's cooperation. The wire is bonded comfortably from the inside and is worn invisibly from the outside. A visit to the practice to reattach it is only needed if the bonding comes loose.
According to current knowledge, in a great many orthodontically treated cases, a significant part of the good aesthetics and correct alignment of the teeth is lost without stabilising measures.
This unfavourable movement of the teeth occurs not only after orthodontic treatment, but also in untreated cases with a harmonious dental condition.
Ultimately, everyone must decide for themselves how long this measure is acceptable. However, anyone who does not want to jeopardise the result of years of effort should not refuse these measures.
As long as appliances are being worn, we should see each other at least once a year, unless otherwise agreed, in order to assess the course of late retention and, if necessary, repair the appliances.

In some adult patients, the jaws are positioned incorrectly in relation to one another. A satisfactory correction can often only be achieved in these patients through a combined orthodontic-jaw surgery treatment.

During this treatment, the jaws are repositioned into the correct position in a single operation. This extensive operation is carried out exclusively by experienced oral and maxillofacial surgeons in hospital and takes between 3 and 6 hours.

Orthodontic pre-treatment is required before the operation in order to align the dental arches. After the operation, both jaws are fixed with wires for about 1 week, during which time the patient can only take nourishment through a straw. Orthodontic fine-tuning begins after around 3-4 weeks.

The repositioning of the jaws will change your appearance. Please be aware that your facial features will change as a result of the procedure. Some patients have always wished for this change, while for others it can indeed be a concern.
