zahnbruecken.titel: Fixed Dental Restorations: Dental Bridges Precisely Fitted FOR Every Gap FROM Specialist KU64 Berlin

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WITH Dental Bridges REGAIN Your Radiant Smile

bloecke.text: Most people find it hard to smile brightly with a gap in their teeth. But a gap in our dental arch doesn't just affect the aesthetics of our face. When a tooth is missing, our chewing function is limited and our bite no longer works perfectly. Even the stability of the surrounding teeth is at risk. With a dental bridge, gaps in the mouth can be closed gently and permanently – without any loss of appearance. This is because dental bridges are now indistinguishable from natural teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is a dental bridge?

bloecke.text: Gaps in the teeth not only look unattractive without dental restoration, they also have far-reaching effects on our dental health and the balance of our entire body. The following impairments and risks can arise as a result of a gap in the teeth:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Consequences of gaps in the teeth

bloecke.text: Biting down firmly: with a gap in the teeth, this is often only possible to a limited extent. Food frequently cannot be chewed as finely as with a healthy set of teeth. Over time, this can affect the entire digestive process.
Chewing and biting stimulate the bone mass of the jaw – similar to a muscle, it is preserved in this way. The jawbone in the area of a gap receives far less stimulation and can consequently recede.

Every tooth has an individual function within the set of teeth. If a tooth is missing, the neighbouring teeth take over its function. The remaining teeth are put under greater strain and wear down more quickly. The tooth reacts with heightened sensitivity and can even break entirely.

When speaking, our tongue normally touches our closed rows of teeth. This helps us articulate words. If the row of teeth is interrupted by a gap, this can change pronunciation – especially where front teeth are missing. Lisping or other speech problems can result.

Without a bridge or tooth, the remaining teeth in the jaw no longer have sufficient support. They shift, which can lead to misalignment within the set of teeth. Under certain circumstances, there is a risk of losing healthy teeth due to destabilised roots. Furthermore, "migrating" teeth can damage the gums and cause pain.

An imbalance in the bite is often also noticeable in the joints: a disrupted bite places uneven strain on the chewing muscles and jaw joints. Teeth grinding and jaw pain can result, extending to chronic pain in the head and neck area.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Strong and deeply rooted: dental bridges need firm support

bloecke.text: With a dental bridge, the gap between two teeth can be closed with a precise fit. The adjacent teeth serve as bridge pillars and stable anchor points. Your dentist attaches the bridge to them using special dental cement. However, not all teeth are suitable as pillars.
For the bridge to last a long time, the following conditions should be met:
Your pillar teeth should have strong, healthy roots.
The teeth serving as bridge pillars should also be free of fillings.
You should have a healthy jawbone without major defects.

Molars are best suited as bridge pillars: due to their three roots, they are particularly strong, resilient and stable as pillars. Incisors, on the other hand, have only a single small root and offer far less support for a dental bridge. A prerequisite for this type of dental restoration is healthy pillar teeth free of fillings.
By the way: it's not just natural teeth that can support a dental bridge. Dental implants can also take on the function of pillar teeth and be fitted with a crown.
It's never too late for a confident smile with well-cared-for teeth: in principle, individual missing front or back teeth can be replaced with a dental bridge at any age.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A gap-free smile for a lifetime thanks to long-lasting durability

bloecke.text: With your new dental bridge, you'll go through life with a radiant smile for a long time to come. This is because dental bridges have a high durability: with good care, you can wear this dental restoration for up to 15 years before it needs to be replaced. This means conventional dental bridges last far longer than removable dentures. However, the more missing teeth that need to be bridged and replaced, the shorter the bridge's lifespan tends to be.

Despite a precisely fitted construction, as you get older it can happen that parts of the dental bridge come loose or break off. In this case, get in touch with your dentist at KU64 Berlin straight away!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental bridges: advantages and disadvantages

bloecke.text: Closing a gap in the teeth with a dental bridge differs significantly from treatment with a dental implant or denture. Dental bridges have numerous advantages, but also disadvantages, compared with other forms of dental restoration. Your dentist at KU64 Berlin will be happy to explain the particular features of a dental bridge to you in a personal conversation. During an initial examination, your dentist will also determine whether a bridge is the right form of dental restoration in your case.
Advantages
+ chewing and speech function are restored
+ existing rows of teeth are stabilised
+ dental and facial aesthetics are reconstructed
+ short treatment period of just a few weeks
+ straightforward dental treatment with local anaesthetic
+ no healing phase
+ costs covered by health insurance funds
Disadvantages
– damage to neighbouring teeth from grinding down healthy tooth structure (grinding trauma)
– a maximum of three to four teeth can be bridged
– overloading of the load-bearing pillar teeth
– possible loss of jawbone in the area of the bridge
– more difficult to clean and care for
– risk of decay forming at the edges of the bridge

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The right bridge for every gap: types of dental bridges

bloecke.text: At KU64 Berlin, you can choose from a wide variety of dental bridge types: because there's a suitable bridge for every gap. Which dental bridge is right for you depends on the size of the gap and its position within your set of teeth. Not every bridge, for example, is suitable for the front tooth area. The experienced dentists at KU64 Berlin will determine the ideal dental restoration for you through a comprehensive diagnostic assessment. Whether it's an implant-supported bridge, an adhesive bridge or a cantilever bridge – you're in excellent hands with us!

The classic dental bridge is known as a fixed bridge. It consists of two bridge anchors and the bridge units in between that close the gap. The bridge anchors are attached with crowns to the pillar teeth on either side, giving the dental bridge its stability.

A cantilever bridge is used for gaps that have a pillar tooth on only one side. For good stability, cantilever bridges are often attached to several prepared pillar teeth. Nevertheless, your gap should not be too long, as very strong forces act on the pillar teeth and, due to the one-sided attachment, can jeopardise the stability of the bridge.

An adhesive bridge is used above all for missing front and side teeth and is a very gentle method of dental restoration. Your dentist attaches the artificial tooth to the back of the healthy neighbouring teeth using adhesive wings. This requires only a very small amount of tooth structure to be removed from the back of the pillar teeth. The gums are also spared. The adhesive bridge is a good choice, particularly for young patients with missing or congenitally absent front teeth.
With a combination bridge, your natural teeth and an implant jointly support the dental restoration. In this way, two adjacent teeth can be replaced.

A temporary bridge serves as a provisional dental restoration to bridge the time until the permanent restoration is fitted. Short-term plastic temporaries can generally be worn for several days to weeks. For longer treatments, such as the placement of implants, your dentist will make a long-term temporary. This protects the treated teeth from external stimuli for several months and closes gaps for an aesthetically pleasing appearance.

If only four to six of your own teeth remain, a telescopic bridge can fill extensive gaps. Of all bridge types, the telescopic bridge offers the greatest flexibility in use: it does not require healthy pillar teeth for attachment. Instead, the existing teeth are fitted with telescopic crowns, onto which the bridge is placed. If further teeth are lost over time, your dentist can extend the bridge. You can remove the telescopic bridge without any trouble in order to clean both your own teeth and the bridge. At the same time, removing and inserting it strengthens the muscles as well as the remaining teeth.

For large gaps or unstable pillar teeth, an implant-supported bridge can bridge the missing teeth. Unlike conventional dental bridges, the implant-supported bridge is not attached to your own teeth but to an implant. If several teeth are missing, several dental implants are placed as pillar teeth. The multi-unit dental bridge is fitted with a crown onto the pillar teeth, closing the gaps in between.

A pontic bridge (Schwebebrücke) is used primarily in the non-visible side tooth area of the lower jaw. Unlike a classic dental bridge, the bridge unit in a pontic bridge does not touch the jaw. The bridge units can be flushed underneath and cleaned optimally. For aesthetic reasons, the pontic bridge is not used in the front tooth area.

With an inlay-retained bridge, gaps can be closed without crowning the neighbouring teeth. Instead, the bridge is attached to an inlay, which serves as the bridge pillar. The inlay can be made from metal or all-ceramic material. For a natural shape and appearance, metal inlays can be veneered with tooth-coloured ceramic. Inlay-retained bridges are a tooth-conserving and aesthetically pleasing alternative to the classic dental bridge, as the pillar teeth only need to be ground down minimally. If your pillar teeth already have a filling, your dentist can replace it with the inlay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Choose from high-quality materials

bloecke.text: Every dental bridge consists of one or two bridge anchors (the dental crowns) and the artificial tooth in between, known as the free-floating bridge unit. The bridge anchors form a crown that is placed onto the ground-down pillar teeth. Depending on the size of the gaps, we can make your bridge with up to three bridge units. The larger the gap to be bridged, the more stable the material should be. This is because your dental bridge is exposed to strong chewing forces in everyday life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gold dental bridges: biocompatible and long-lasting

bloecke.text: Gold has been used in dentistry for many thousands of years. The ancient Egyptians attached artificial teeth to existing neighbouring teeth with a gold thread. Even though the form of dental bridges has evolved over the years, the advantages of classic materials such as gold in dentistry are still valued today: gold dental bridges not only have high stability and long durability, but are also particularly biocompatible for your body.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Ceramic bridges: natural appearance and highly resilient

bloecke.text: All-ceramic bridges look virtually identical to your natural teeth. This is because our dental technicians can match ceramic bridges almost perfectly to your individual tooth colour. Similar to gold dental bridges, ceramic bridges are particularly stable, resistant to wear and well tolerated by the body. For particular requirements, we make dental bridges from zirconium oxide ceramic. Due to their high stability, they are especially suitable as a professional solution for larger gaps in the side tooth area. Thanks to their precise fit and material purity, they guarantee you a particularly comfortable wearing experience.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Metal bridges: affordable and visually noticeable

bloecke.text: Full-cast metal dental bridges are now only very rarely used in dentistry. As they are not tooth-coloured, they tend to catch the eye, making them less attractive to many patients and not an aesthetically high-quality solution. Full-metal bridges can cause a metallic taste and trigger allergic reactions, and are not suitable for people with allergies. A metal dental bridge is the most affordable option and is classed as a standard service by statutory health insurance funds.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Composite bridges: cost-effective and aesthetically pleasing

bloecke.text: A cost-effective alternative to all-ceramic bridges are dental bridges made from a combination of different materials. With this type of dental bridge, the bridge framework is generally made from a precious metal, which is veneered with ceramic or composite resin. Composite bridges have proven their worth in dentistry and have been in use for more than 50 years. The advantage: due to its metal framework, the bridge is very stable and, thanks to its tooth-coloured veneer, can be matched very well visually to your existing set of teeth. The disadvantage: after several years, discolouration can appear on the gums and teeth if the metal ions dissolve.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Our own dental laboratory: precision and quality at every step

bloecke.text: Every dental bridge is made individually for each patient with the utmost precision in our in-house dental laboratory in Berlin. This is because the precise fit determines the wearing comfort of the dental bridge. The design of the dental bridge is carried out on a computer. Our digitally controlled milling machine then shapes the finished bridge from the design. For an optimal aesthetic result, the dental bridge is perfectly matched to your natural tooth colour. Our dental technicians even take into account nuances and individual features of your teeth when making your bridge. All dental bridges made by KU64 Berlin meet the highest quality standards and come with an above-average length of warranty. Please note that this warranty obligation does not exist for dental restorations made abroad!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Four steps to your new dental bridge: how the treatment proceeds

bloecke.text: Regardless of which type of dental bridge you choose: the treatment process is similar for most types of dental bridge. We plan each dental bridge carefully in advance and then make it individually in our in-house dental laboratory. Depending on the size of the bridge and the condition of your teeth, several sessions are required for treatment.
The process takes place in four steps:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Preliminary examination and taking an impression

bloecke.text: The durability of a bridge depends significantly on the state of health of the existing teeth, the jawbone and the gums. In a preliminary examination, your dentist therefore first checks the condition of the surrounding teeth in order to identify potential risks in good time. For this, they take an X-ray of the upper and lower jaw. Loose or decayed pillar teeth are first treated to ensure the stability of the bridge. Inflammation of the tooth roots or jawbone must also be treated before the bridge is fitted. Your dentist then takes an impression of your teeth and uses it to make a temporary.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Grinding down the teeth

bloecke.text: Before the crown is fitted, the so-called pillar teeth are ground down and thus prepared for the bridge to be fitted. Unlike conventional bridge treatment, the teeth bordering the gap are only pre-treated and gently prepared on the barely visible tooth surfaces and in the area of the enamel. This procedure preserves the natural hard tooth structure almost entirely. Until your bridge is completed, you will receive a plastic temporary that protects your pillar teeth and already covers the gap.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Making and fitting the bridge

bloecke.text: At KU64 Berlin, aesthetics and a natural look come first, even with dental restorations. Before the dental bridge is made, the dentist determines the appropriate shape and tooth colour. Using the impression and tooth colour, the dental technician makes a framework for the bridge in the in-house laboratory. In a further session, the bridge framework is fitted and adjusted to your teeth. Any areas causing problems are ground down. Only once the bridge sits well on the jaw are the veneers made in the laboratory and the bridge completed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Fitting and follow-up examination

bloecke.text: At a further treatment appointment, the bridge is fitted onto the teeth. For this, the new, artificial crowns are cemented onto the pillar teeth. These hold the bridge elements, which are thus firmly anchored in the mouth. After fitting, your dentist checks the shape and fit of the dental bridge at a further follow-up appointment. This gives you the opportunity to discuss any concerns and clarify any remaining questions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Care: how to keep your dental bridge looking radiant

bloecke.text: As a wearer of a dental bridge, you should pay particular attention to your oral hygiene. Clean the fixed dental bridge thoroughly and regularly, just like your other teeth, at least twice a day. There is an increased risk of decay forming, especially at the crown edge of the crowned pillar teeth. Using interdental brushes and dental floss, you can free the sensitive spaces between teeth from food residue and plaque. With thorough oral hygiene, you protect your new smile not only from decay but also from periodontitis. The team at KU64 Berlin will be happy to give you tips at your next appointment for the professional cleaning and care of your dental bridge.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Contact: we're building a bridge to your new smile

bloecke.text: We do everything for your oral health. Our team of dental specialists will be happy to answer any questions and provide further information on quality dental restorations such as dental bridges made in Berlin, the various types, as well as the process and costs! Our practice team is here for you seven days a week.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQ
Which Dental Restoration IS Better: Bridge OR Implant?

bloecke.text: Which dental restoration is better doesn't just depend on the costs, but on many individual factors and the patient's wishes. There's no universally valid guide. Implants are anchored in healthy jawbone and thus offer very stable support.

Unlike with a bridge, no healthy tooth structure needs to be sacrificed with an implant. While implants can even be used in a toothless jaw, dental bridges, by contrast, can only replace three to four teeth. Healthy natural neighbouring teeth are needed to anchor the bridge stably with the crown.

Implants require a surgical procedure. The treatment duration and healing time for implants are therefore longer compared with bridges. Implants and bridges also differ in durability: the durability of implants, at up to 20 years, is longer than that of bridges.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which Material IS Best FOR Dental Crowns?

bloecke.text: The different materials offer various advantages. Alongside appearance, durability and tolerability also play a role. And, ultimately, of course, the cost as well. Ceramic crowns are very popular as dental restorations due to their resemblance to natural teeth and high tolerability.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW Much DO Dental Bridges Cost?

bloecke.text: The costs of dental bridges vary quite considerably. They depend on the number of teeth to be replaced as well as the material used. The location – whether upper or lower jaw, front or back tooth area – also affects the cost. Metal bridges are the most affordable option, while all-ceramic dental bridges cost considerably more. The KU64 Berlin team will be happy to advise you in detail on the subject of dental restorations, their materials and costs.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is A Dental Bridge Paid FOR BY Health Insurance?

bloecke.text: You don't have to bear the cost of your dental restoration alone. Dental bridges are part of the standard service provided by statutory health insurance funds. For you as a patient, this means: the health insurance fund pays a fixed subsidy of 50 per cent towards your dental bridge. If you have kept your bonus record (Bonusheft) up to date for five or ten years, the subsidy increases to 60 or 65 per cent respectively. With supplementary dental insurance, you can significantly reduce your costs. Depending on the tariff, the supplementary dental insurance may cover the full cost of your bridge.

Full, well-shaped lips, firm skin and defined facial features are considered symbols of attractiveness and youthfulness. They give the face expressiveness and harmony – but as we age, lip volume can diminish, skin becomes less firm and taut, and the contours of the cheeks, chin and nose can become less defined.

This is where hyaluronic acid fillers come in: a minimally invasive procedure and a safe method to smooth fine lines, gently plump the lips and create a harmonious overall appearance. Hyaluronic acid can be dosed individually and delivers natural, aesthetic results.

As a specialist for beauty treatments in Berlin, KU64 stands for the highest quality and the most modern techniques. Our experienced team combines medical precision with a feel for aesthetics to achieve harmonious, long-lasting results. Arrange a no-obligation consultation and find out how a hyaluronic acid treatment can highlight your natural beauty.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is hyaluronic acid?

bloecke.text: Hyaluronic acid is a true all-rounder when it comes to the beauty and health of the skin. As a natural component of the body, it plays a crucial role in retaining moisture, elasticity and volume. Particularly in the lip area, hyaluronic acid has established itself as a gentle and effective method for creating volume, defining contours and reducing dryness. But what exactly makes hyaluronic acid so special?

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Hyaluronic acid – a natural component of the skin

bloecke.text: Hyaluronic acid is a substance naturally produced by the body that can bind large amounts of water – up to 6,000 times its own weight. In the skin, it provides firmness, moisture and suppleness. However, as we age, the skin's natural hyaluronic acid content decreases, which can lead to volume loss, dryness and fine lines.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Cross-linked and non-cross-linked hyaluronic acid

bloecke.text: Both cross-linked and non-cross-linked hyaluronic acid are used for beauty treatments. Both forms differ in structure and longevity, and each offers benefits for different areas of application.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Cross-linked hyaluronic acid: volume and targeted correction

bloecke.text: This form of hyaluronic acid is stabilised through chemical processes, giving the molecules a firmer, gel-like structure. As a result, it is broken down more slowly by the body and remains in the tissue for longer. It is mainly used for the following treatments:
Filling wrinkles (e.g. nasolabial folds, marionette lines)
Lip augmentation and defining the lip contour
Cheek and chin augmentation
Nose correction
Filling deep skin folds and building volume

As cross-linked hyaluronic acid is firmer, it is particularly suitable for areas where structure, volume and longer-lasting results are desired. Depending on the product and individual metabolic activity, the effect can last between 6 and 18 months.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Non-cross-linked hyaluronic acid: moisture for radiant skin

bloecke.text: This form is more liquid and is broken down more quickly by the body, as it is not chemically stabilised. It has a primarily moisturising effect and improves skin texture without creating volume. It is used for:
Skin booster treatments for skin rejuvenation
Moisturising mesotherapy for the face, neck and décolletage
Reducing fine lines (e.g. around the eyes or on the neck)
Non-cross-linked hyaluronic acid is often applied over several sessions to sustainably improve skin quality. As it is broken down more quickly by the body, it usually lasts between 3 and 6 months.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Benefits of hyaluronic acid fillers for the lips and skin

bloecke.text: Injecting hyaluronic acid is one of the safest and most popular methods in aesthetic medicine. There are many reasons for this:
Natural, individual results: with a tailored dosage and treatment, our specialists achieve exactly the result you wish for.
Moisture and suppleness: dry or chapped lips become full and supple again. Tired skin looks fresh and radiant once more.
Minimally invasive procedure with immediately visible results: the treatment only takes around 20–30 minutes, after which you will quickly see an effect.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The hyaluronic acid treatment

bloecke.text: At KU64 in Berlin, we place great importance on individual consultation and tailored treatment, so that the result matches your expectations 100 per cent.

bloecke.text: In a detailed consultation, we discuss your wishes and expectations and analyse your individual facial features. Together, we determine which lip shape, cheek or nose correction suits you best.

Good to know: the first results of a hyaluronic acid treatment are visible immediately. The final result appears after 3 to 5 days.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When is a hyaluronic acid treatment suitable?

bloecke.text: Hyaluronic acid fillers are a popular and proven method for accentuating the contours of the lips or face, plumping the skin and providing moisture.
Thin or asymmetrical lips: precise injection techniques can harmonise and proportionally balance the lips.
Age-related loss of lip volume: hyaluronic acid can gently correct volume loss, making your lips look fuller and more youthful again.
Nasolabial folds or wrinkles around the eyes: the plumping effect of hyaluronic acid also softens pronounced wrinkles.
Nose correction: targeted hyaluronic acid injections make it possible to balance out irregularities, gently correcting the shape of the nose and giving it a more symmetrical appearance.
Cheek and chin augmentation: loss of elasticity in the cheeks and chin can be balanced out with hyaluronic acid, gently sculpting and defining the facial contours.

Whether you would like a subtle refresh of your skin or lips, or an expressive face with clear contours and voluminous lips – at KU64 in Berlin, we offer individual advice and focus on a treatment that suits your natural facial features perfectly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When is a hyaluronic acid treatment not suitable?

bloecke.text: In certain cases, wrinkle filling or lip augmentation with hyaluronic acid is not advisable, or should at least be postponed, in order to minimise possible risks.
Acute infections or inflammation: in cases of herpes, wounds or other skin irritations, hyaluronic acid treatment should only be carried out once healing is complete.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding: aesthetic procedures such as hyaluronic acid fillers are not recommended during these sensitive periods, as there is insufficient safety data available.
Allergies or intolerances to hyaluronic acid: people with a known intolerance to hyaluronic acid or the additives it contains should consider alternative methods.

At KU64 in Berlin, we place the highest value on thorough consultation and individual analysis in order to offer you the best possible treatment. Arrange a no-obligation consultation and find out how we can optimise your face and lips harmoniously and aesthetically!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Results of a hyaluronic acid treatment

bloecke.text: The effect of a hyaluronic acid treatment is not permanent, as the body gradually breaks down the injected hyaluronic acid over time. The result usually lasts between 6 and 12 months, depending on the treatment area and individual factors such as your metabolism and lifestyle. If you would like to maintain the volume of your lips or the defined contours of your chin or cheek area for longer, you can easily have a top-up treatment.

Immediately after the injection, the skin in the treated area may swell slightly, which is completely normal and subsides within a few hours to a few days. The final result appears after around 3 to 5 days, once the hyaluronic acid has fully spread through the tissue and any swelling has gone down.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: These temporary side effects may occur:

bloecke.text: Mild swelling & redness: swelling or slight redness may occur immediately after the injection, which usually subsides within 24 to 48 hours.
Bruising: small bruises or haematomas at the injection sites are possible but usually disappear after a few days.
Asymmetry: in rare cases, slight unevenness can occur, which can be gently corrected with a follow-up treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The right aftercare following hyaluronic acid treatment

bloecke.text: Avoid pressure: in the first few days after treatment, try to avoid putting pressure on the treated areas so that the hyaluronic acid can distribute evenly.
Drink enough water: hyaluronic acid binds moisture – adequate fluid intake supports the result and keeps your skin and lips supple.
Gentle cooling: if mild swelling occurs, careful cooling with a soft cooling pad can help support the healing process.
Moderate temperatures: visits to the sauna or solarium, or excessive cooling, for example with ice cubes, can affect healing.
With the right aftercare, the result can be optimised and its longevity extended.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: No need to fear a “duck face”: the right technique is key

bloecke.text: Many patients are particularly hesitant about lip treatment with hyaluronic acid because they fear the unnatural-looking “duck face”. These overly voluminous and often uneven lips are usually the result of incorrect injection technique or too much hyaluronic acid in the wrong area.

At KU64 in Berlin, we place great importance on a harmonious and natural aesthetic – both when treating the lips and when performing nose correction and wrinkle filling in all areas. Our experienced doctors use precise injection techniques for lip augmentation to gently optimise the shape of the lips without altering the face's natural proportions. By using lip fillers in moderate amounts in a targeted way, the lips are subtly plumped while retaining a natural look that suits your individual facial features.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about hyaluronic acid treatments
How long does a hyaluronic acid treatment take?

bloecke.text: Depending on whether you are having wrinkles, lips, a nose correction or one or more other areas treated, hyaluronic acid treatment usually takes 20 to 40 minutes. Thanks to modern methods and, if necessary, numbing, the treatment is almost painless and you can return to your everyday routine without any downtime. The first results are visible immediately after the injection, while the final result appears after 3 to 5 days, once any swelling has gone down.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much hyaluronic acid is used in a treatment?

bloecke.text: The amount of hyaluronic acid depends on the area being treated and your desired result. For a subtle lip enlargement, mild fine lines or gentle correction of facial contours, treatment often starts with a smaller amount, with further adjustments made later if needed. Our experienced specialists always ensure a natural look and harmonious proportions that suit your face.
Some guideline values for different treatments:
Lip filler: 0.5 – 1 ml
Cheek augmentation: 1 – 3 ml
Chin sculpting: 1 – 2 ml
Nose correction: 0.5 – 1 ml
Wrinkle filling: 0.5 – 1 ml per treated area
We determine the exact amount for you precisely, based on a thorough consultation tailored to your individual wishes.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is treatment with hyaluronic acid painful?

bloecke.text: Treatment with hyaluronic acid is generally only mildly uncomfortable. Most patients feel, at most, a slight prick or brief pressure at the injection site. Very fine needles are used for the injections, which reduce the sensation of pain. In sensitive areas such as the lips, a numbing cream can be applied before treatment.

Slight redness or a feeling of tightness after treatment is normal and usually disappears within a few hours. Overall, hyaluronic acid injection is a nearly painless, quick and low-risk method for aesthetic correction.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I go back to work straight after a hyaluronic acid treatment?

bloecke.text: Yes, you can go straight back to work and continue with your usual daily routine after treatment. Mild swelling, redness or small bruises at the injection sites are possible but usually disappear within 24 to 48 hours. However, to avoid affecting the result, you should avoid strenuous physical activity, hot drinks and visits to the sauna or solarium for the first 24 hours. If mild swelling occurs, careful cooling with a soft cooling pad can help.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I apply lipstick after lip augmentation?

bloecke.text: After a lip filler treatment with hyaluronic acid, you should avoid applying lipstick or lip gloss for at least 24 hours. The skin on the lips is more sensitive than usual immediately after treatment, and make-up products can cause irritation or infection. We recommend caring for your lips gently and only using moisturising, fragrance-free lip balm. Once the initial healing phase is complete and there is no more redness or swelling, you can apply make-up as usual again.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I exercise after a hyaluronic acid treatment?

bloecke.text: After a hyaluronic acid injection, you should avoid sport and strenuous physical activity for at least 24 to 48 hours. The increased blood flow during exercise can lead to greater swelling, bruising or uneven distribution of the hyaluronic acid. After a few days, the healing process is complete and you can resume your usual sporting activities.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long do lip fillers last?

bloecke.text: A lip filler treatment with hyaluronic acid usually lasts between 6 and 12 months. As your body naturally breaks down the hyaluronic acid, regular top-ups can help maintain the desired volume and lip shape over the long term.

In people with a fast metabolism or very active facial expressions, hyaluronic acid may break down more quickly, while the result lasts longer in others. The experts at KU64 Berlin are happy to offer individual advice on the ideal treatment frequency for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which lip fillers are the best?

bloecke.text: There are various methods for shaping the lips and achieving more volume or definition. Which method is best suited depends on your individual wishes and your natural lip shape.
Hyaluronic acid fillers: hyaluronic acid is the most popular lip filler. It provides moisture, adds volume and can be used in a targeted way to accentuate the lip contours.

Botulinum toxin: with this method, the lips are not directly enlarged; instead, the muscles around the mouth are specifically relaxed. This causes the upper lip to move slightly outward, creating the impression of more volume.

Fat transfer: with this method, the body's own fat is taken from another area of the body, processed and injected as a lip filler. This method offers longer-lasting results than hyaluronic acid but is also more invasive.

Thread lift: with this method, fine threads are inserted into the lips to gently lift them and define their contours. It is particularly suitable for people who place less importance on volume but especially want a firmer lip contour.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is hyaluronic acid treatment safe?

bloecke.text: Yes. Hyaluronic acid is a substance naturally found in the body that is responsible for binding moisture and maintaining the skin's elasticity. As it is a biodegradable substance, the injected hyaluronic acid is naturally absorbed by the body over time – usually within 6 to 12 months.

Modern hyaluronic acid fillers are specifically developed for aesthetic treatments and are very well tolerated. They contain no animal-derived ingredients and are generally free from allergy-triggering substances. This means the risk of intolerances or side effects is very low.

At KU64 in Berlin, we use high-quality, certified hyaluronic acid preparations and place the utmost importance on precise application by experienced professionals, who tailor the treatment to the individual wishes and needs of our patients.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: From what age can you have your lips augmented?

bloecke.text: In principle, lip augmentation with hyaluronic acid is possible from the age of 18. Younger patients can only undergo the treatment with written consent from a parent or legal guardian. In addition, we carry out an individual consultation before every treatment. In doing so, we not only clarify expectations and wishes but also check whether lip augmentation is an active decision and appropriate in the individual case.
At KU64 in Berlin, we place great importance on a professional, safe treatment as well as natural, harmonious results that suit your individual aesthetic.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is CEREC?

bloecke.text: CEREC stands for "Chairside Economical Restoration of Esthetic Ceramics" – roughly translated: ceramic restoration made directly at the treatment chair. The method was developed at the University of Zurich in 1980 and has fundamentally changed the way dental restorations are made.

The technology combines three steps in one continuous digital process: instead of a traditional tray impression, a digital camera captures your teeth with precise 3D images – contact-free and completely gentle. The CEREC software then analyses these images and calculates suggestions for possible restorations. The camera does not touch the teeth at any point during the scan. This means you experience a gentle impression-taking process without any gagging or unpleasant taste in the mouth. Our milling unit then produces your restoration directly in the practice – without any detour via an external laboratory.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The right material for your CEREC restoration

bloecke.text: For your restoration, we use only high-quality, metal-free and biocompatible materials in the CEREC method – individually matched to the colour of your natural teeth. Depending on the diagnosis and requirements, the following materials are used:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: All-ceramic (lithium disilicate)

bloecke.text: Lithium disilicate is a high-quality glass ceramic material that, thanks to its natural translucency, comes visually very close to real tooth enamel. It stands out for its high aesthetics and solid stability, and is particularly suited to inlays, crowns and veneers in the visible front tooth area.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Zirconia

bloecke.text: Zirconia is a high-strength material that impresses with its exceptional hardness and fracture resistance. It is the first choice for heavily loaded back teeth, larger restorations and multi-unit bridges.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Hybrid ceramic

bloecke.text: Hybrid ceramic is made from a combination of ceramic and resin components, which makes the material lighter and more elastic than pure ceramic. It's gentle on the opposing tooth and cushions chewing forces.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Feldspar ceramic (porcelain)

bloecke.text: Feldspar ceramic is the classic dental porcelain that has been used in dentistry for decades. It stands out for its particularly natural light refraction and excellent aesthetics, and is used mainly for veneers and facings in the front tooth area, where the highest visual standards are required.
We'll discuss with you which material is best suited to your tooth before treatment begins.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fast, gentle, aesthetic – your advantages with CEREC at a glance

bloecke.text: Restorations made using the CEREC method offer the following advantages compared to a conventionally lab-made restoration:
Fast production: partial and single crowns, veneers and inlays are ready in one sitting. This significantly shortens the treatment time.
No impressions, no gagging: the conventional taking of impressions with impression material and trays at the dentist is no longer needed.
No temporary restoration: wearing temporaries for several days or weeks is not necessary. As a result, there's no exposed tooth for food, drinks and germs to get into.
Biological compatibility: ceramic is very similar to natural tooth enamel, making it well tolerated by the body and suitable even for those with allergies.
No interactions: all-ceramic restorations are metal-free. There are no interactions with metals, for example in bridges, crowns or inlays.
Durability and long-term stability: ceramic is very stable, wear-resistant and long-lasting. All-ceramic restorations therefore keep their precise fit even after years.

Natural aesthetics: thanks to its high translucency, ceramic restorations look like a real tooth. Ceramic keeps its aesthetic appearance and does not discolour, even over many years. Dark crown margins, as seen with restorations made from other materials, do not occur.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Step by step: how your CEREC treatment works

bloecke.text: At KU64, we create your dental restoration quickly, precisely and entirely digitally – in just one appointment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Consultation and preparation

bloecke.text: First, we determine the individual shade of your tooth and the neighbouring teeth together. For a perfectly aesthetic result, we recommend having stubborn discolouration removed beforehand with a professional teeth cleaning. We then prepare your tooth for the restoration: we carefully remove old restorations and decay, and reshape the tooth where necessary. In doing so, we preserve as much healthy tooth structure as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Digital 3D scan

bloecke.text: Instead of a traditional tray impression with impression material, our high-resolution intraoral camera captures your prepared tooth, the neighbouring teeth and your entire bite – completely contact-free and in a fraction of a second. The camera scans the tooth surface with the highest precision and transmits the data to the screen in real time. This creates a detailed digital 3D model of your teeth, which serves as the precise basis for planning your restoration. You experience the entire impression-taking process comfortably in the treatment chair (chairside) – without gagging, without an unpleasant taste in the mouth, and without a long wait for impression material to set.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Planning and milling

bloecke.text: Based on the 3D data, the CEREC software calculates the exact shape of your restoration – taking into account your individual tooth shape, the neighbouring teeth and your bite. Your dentist checks and refines the digital model on screen before production begins. Our milling unit then mills your crown, inlay, bridge or veneer directly in the practice from a high-quality ceramic block, with a precise fit – accurately, quickly and without any detour via an external laboratory. Milling usually takes only 15 to 20 minutes. You can spend this time relaxing in our waiting area.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Fitting and fine adjustment

bloecke.text: As soon as your restoration is finished, we first check the fit, colour and bite directly in the treatment chair. If necessary, we make fine adjustments on the spot. We then permanently bond it in place using special cement and polish the surface for a pleasant feel. You can use your teeth as normal straight afterwards.

Find out what modern CAD/CAM technology can do for your dental restoration. Get in touch – we'll support you from the first examination right through to the finished restoration, and remain available to you at any time after your CEREC treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When is CEREC right for you, and when isn't it?

bloecke.text: CEREC is a versatile technology that offers an ideal solution for most patients with damaged teeth or teeth in need of restoration. Nevertheless, there are situations in which a different approach makes more sense. At KU64, we advise you individually, so that you receive the care that's really right for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: CEREC is well suited to you if …

bloecke.text: your tooth has a larger defect that goes beyond what a direct filling can treat
the remaining tooth structure is still largely stable
your tooth is exposed to heavy chewing forces and needs a particularly stable restoration
you have a metal intolerance and need a completely metal-free restoration
for professional, family or health reasons, you would like or are only able to attend a single appointment – for example, due to dental anxiety, limited mobility or a busy schedule

abschnitte.ueberschrift: CEREC is less suitable if …

bloecke.text: the tooth is so badly damaged that there is no longer enough tooth structure left to serve as a stable base, meaning a post-and-core build-up or preliminary treatment is needed first
the planned restoration is very extensive, for example with large multi-unit bridges, where conventional laboratory fabrication offers the more precise solution
the transition between the prepared tooth and gum lies so deep that a conventional impression offers greater precision
there are acute inflammations of the tooth or gum that require periodontal treatment or root canal treatment
complex bite abnormalities are present that first require orthodontic treatment
an implant or bone graft is needed first
you decide on a gold restoration, since this material cannot be processed using the CEREC method
Once the relevant step has been completed, we will also make your restoration using the CEREC method.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What to bear in mind after your CEREC treatment

bloecke.text: After treatment, you can generally use your new restoration straight away – nevertheless, there are a few things to bear in mind in the first hours and in the longer term, so that your CEREC restoration lasts as long as possible.

Straight after treatment: wait to eat until the anaesthetic has completely worn off. This helps you avoid accidentally biting your tongue or cheek. In the first few hours, we recommend avoiding very hard, chewy or sticky foods, so that the bonding cement can fully set.

Long-term care: brush your teeth thoroughly as usual. Your CEREC restoration can be cared for in exactly the same way as your natural teeth. Regular professional teeth cleaning is particularly recommended, as it keeps the margins of your restoration clean and significantly extends its lifespan.

A note for teeth grinders: if you grind or clench your teeth at night, we recommend a custom-made protective splint – it protects your restoration from excessive strain and considerably extends its lifespan.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – Frequently asked questions about CEREC
What kinds of restoration can the dentist make using the CEREC method?

bloecke.text: In our dental practices in Berlin and Potsdam, we use the CEREC method to create the following restorations: multi-unit bridges, all-ceramic inlays/onlays, veneers (ceramic shells), fillings, partial crowns and crowns for front and back teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does it take to make a crown with CEREC?

bloecke.text: From the examination through the 3D scan and digital design to the finished crown, the whole treatment usually takes place in just one sitting, rather than two or three appointments. Treating a tooth with a crown therefore takes only around two hours in total. Thanks to chairside production – meaning the restoration is made directly at the treatment chair – there's no need to go via an external laboratory at all, and you leave our practice with your finished restoration on the very same day. Especially with extensive dental restorations, the CEREC method allows us to significantly reduce the number of treatment appointments needed at our dental practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much does a CEREC treatment cost?

bloecke.text: The cost of a CEREC restoration depends on which restoration is needed for your tooth and how large the defect is. An inlay is generally less expensive than a crown, while a multi-unit bridge is correspondingly more involved. At KU64, we discuss the costs transparently with you before treatment begins, so you know exactly what to expect.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much does a CEREC crown cost?

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much does a CEREC bridge cost?

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much does a CEREC inlay cost?

Anyone who specifically wants a gold restoration will also need a different approach, as CEREC only processes ceramic and zirconia. At KU64, we'll give you honest advice on whether CEREC is the best solution for your tooth or whether a different restoration would better suit your situation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Amalgam: from standard care to a modern alternative

bloecke.text: Dental amalgam was the standard care in dentistry for decades for repairing cavities and was already in use over 100 years ago – particularly for fillings in the back teeth. There were pragmatic reasons for this: amalgam is considered very durable and long-lasting as well as comparatively inexpensive. The mixture of various metals with mercury as the main component (over 50 per cent), along with silver, tin and copper, could also be reliably processed even when it was difficult to achieve absolute dryness in the tooth. This made it reliably suitable even for larger defects in molars.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Amalgam and the environment: the 2025 ban

bloecke.text: At the latest with the 2025 amalgam ban, many patients experience a change in perspective at the dental practice: it consists of over 50 per cent mercury, and this is a highly problematic substance. It is toxic to humans and animals and may therefore no longer be used in products, so that it does not enter the environment and accumulate there. From there it can also enter the bodies of humans and animals via food. However, within the finished filling, it very rarely poses a danger due to the extremely small quantity involved.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Aesthetics and modern alternatives: your teeth in a new light

bloecke.text: Alongside environmental and health considerations, aesthetic significance is playing an increasingly important role today. Amalgam fillings are clearly visible in the mouth. In photos, a dark 'silvery' spot stands out and detracts from the appearance of the teeth. At the same time, numerous modern alternative filling materials are now available in natural tooth colours and without risks to people or the environment, which are functionally stable and noticeably less conspicuous aesthetically.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Why is the use of amalgam now banned?

bloecke.text: The reason for the ban on amalgam in the European Union (EU) is not that there are new findings about the dangers of amalgam fillings in the mouth. In its processed state, it is considered largely harmless and safe.

Rather, it is about environmental and precautionary policy surrounding mercury. Dental amalgam is over 50 per cent a mercury-containing material. The metal is classified worldwide as a problematic pollutant because it can accumulate in the environment and – depending on its transformation – enter the organisms of humans and animals via the food chain. It can then damage the nervous system, the immune system and kidney function.

The EU therefore aims to reduce mercury emissions throughout the entire product life cycle: from processing in products, through use, to disposal. It was therefore decided to largely end the use and export of mercury-containing dental amalgam from 1 January 2025 – with narrowly defined exceptions where it is medically essential in individual cases.
The ban on its use in dental practices was overdue, as mercury-free alternatives made of composite resin or ceramic for repairing tooth defects have long been available in very many situations.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: KU64: amalgam-free since day one

bloecke.text: Did you know? Not a single amalgam filling has ever been placed at the KU64 practices. Long before most other practices, we were clear: we do not want to use filling materials with questionable aesthetics and problematic ingredients. Instead, KU64 has specialised in safe amalgam remediation and has removed over 100,000 amalgam fillings since our founding.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Replacing amalgam fillings: how to make the right decision

bloecke.text: Removing amalgam fillings can make sense for various reasons. At KU64, we support you in making the right decision by offering you clear criteria for when removal is necessary or advisable.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When should you have amalgam removed?

bloecke.text: Defective fillings: if your filling has cracks or breaks and no longer fulfils its function.
Secondary caries: if decay develops under or around the amalgam filling.
Aesthetic reasons: if the visible dark colour of the amalgam filling bothers you and you wish for a more aesthetic solution.
Tooth sensitivity: if unpleasant sensations or pain indicate a leaking area.
Health complaints: if you have headaches, tiredness or other symptoms that are suspected to be connected to possibly damaged amalgam fillings.
Allergies: if proven allergies to amalgam or metals exist.
Certain conditions: if autoimmune diseases such as rheumatism, lupus, multiple sclerosis or Hashimoto's thyroiditis are present, in order to reduce mercury exposure.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When should you not have amalgam removed?

bloecke.text: Intact fillings: if an amalgam filling is still intact and functional.
Not medically necessary: if the amalgam filling causes no complaints such as pain or sensitivity.
During pregnancy: if you are pregnant or currently breastfeeding.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Amalgam removal with triple protection at KU64

bloecke.text: The health of our patients is especially important to us. That is why we offer you amalgam removal with triple protection. This ensures optimal safety during amalgam removal, as dust and vapours can no longer be inhaled. This is because, when drilling out an amalgam filling, tiny amalgam particles can enter the oral cavity and thereby transfer mercury into the body via the mucous membranes. At the same time, toxic mercury vapours are released, which carry the risk of mercury entering the body through breathing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How our triple protection works during amalgam removal

bloecke.text: Rubber dam: your dentist first isolates the tooth to be treated from the oral cavity and the neighbouring teeth using a special stretch rubber sheet.

Suction cannula: at the same time, a special plastic cap (Clean-Up system from Sweden) surrounds the tooth and is connected to a powerful suction unit that safely removes mercury vapours and particles.
Oxygen: a nasal cannula supplies you with fresh oxygen during treatment, so that you do not inhale any toxic vapours.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What happens after amalgam removal?

bloecke.text: At KU64, our experts provide you with complete amalgam remediation. This means: on the same day as the amalgam removal, a new restoration with high-quality, harmless and aesthetic filling material is usually carried out. In most cases, composite resin is used, which we match as closely as possible to the natural colour of your teeth.
If the tooth damage is so extensive that composite would no longer be stable enough, we make ceramic inlays in our own in-house dental laboratory.
Whether and to what extent costs for the new filling apply to you is something we discuss with you beforehand.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Holistic aftercare at KU64: naturopathic support for your healing

bloecke.text: After amalgam removal, we support you at KU64 with holistic aftercare. Our naturopathic practitioner accompanies you, on request, with naturopathic care and promotes your recovery. This includes, for example, detoxifying the body or strengthening the immune system through targeted herbal medicine.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What your amalgam removal costs at KU64

bloecke.text: The cost of your amalgam removal at KU64 depends on the scope of treatment, the number of affected teeth and the replacement materials chosen. As a rule, the cost of amalgam removal ranges between 50 and 150 euros per tooth. Added to this are the costs for the filling material you choose. Composite fillings represent a more affordable alternative to ceramic or gold inlays, which are usually among the most expensive options. At KU64, you will of course receive a detailed and transparent breakdown of costs before treatment begins.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does health insurance cover the costs?

bloecke.text: Health insurance usually only covers the cost of amalgam removal if it is medically necessary. This can be the case with allergies or an intolerance to amalgam. If you wish for the replacement for aesthetic reasons, you will usually have to bear the costs privately. At KU64, we inform you in advance about which services are covered by health insurance and which costs you must pay yourself.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about amalgam removal
Why do so many people have amalgam in their mouths?

bloecke.text: Amalgam was standard care in dentistry for decades and was used particularly for molars because it is robust and long-lasting. This is why many patients today still carry older amalgam fillings.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does amalgam really contain mercury?

bloecke.text: Yes, dental amalgam consists of over 50 per cent mercury. This is precisely why many people want to have their fillings checked and to be advised about contemporary alternatives. Feel free to get in touch with us regarding this, or book an appointment online around the clock.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does the amalgam ban affect me and my fillings?

bloecke.text: Since 2025, the use of new amalgam fillings in dentistry has largely been prohibited in the EU (with exceptions). However, existing amalgam fillings do not automatically have to be removed as a result – what matters is the findings, any complaints, and your wish for a tooth-coloured alternative.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does amalgam remediation mean?

bloecke.text: Amalgam remediation refers to the structured renewal of older amalgam fillings – often step by step, depending on the priority of the teeth. The aim is a functionally stable and aesthetic restoration using safe materials.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When is amalgam removal medically advisable?

bloecke.text: Removal is particularly advisable when the filling is defective, the margins are leaking, or there is a suspicion of secondary caries. Whether replacement is necessary for your teeth is clarified by your dentist based on the findings.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What fillings are available as a replacement, and what is aesthetically best?

bloecke.text: As a rule, tooth-coloured composite fillings or ceramic inlays/onlays come into consideration. In cases of very extensive tooth damage, dental restorations such as crowns may also be necessary. Which materials are aesthetically and functionally best suited depends on the size and position of the fillings as well as your bite situation. We discuss all associated costs with you calmly and in detail.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How does the treatment proceed at the dental practice?

bloecke.text: First, the dentist thoroughly examines the fillings in your mouth and discusses the content and scope of the appropriate therapy with you. The old filling is then removed in a controlled manner, and the tooth is subsequently built up with a suitable new restoration.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What protective measures are there during removal?

bloecke.text: During amalgam removal, protective measures are important to reduce escaping toxic particles and to make the process safe. KU64 relies on triple protection during amalgam removal, consisting of a rubber dam to isolate the tooth, a suction cannula to reduce mercury vapours and particles, as well as a nasal cannula that supplies you with fresh oxygen. We will explain transparently which measures are appropriate in your particular case before treatment begins.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How many appointments do I need – and how long does an appointment take?

bloecke.text: This depends on how many amalgam fillings need to be removed and what restoration is planned afterwards (filling, ceramic, dental restoration). In most cases, a single session at our dental practice is sufficient for amalgam remediation. We discuss the content, duration and suitable appointments for the treatment with you calmly beforehand.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What do I need to bear in mind after removal?

bloecke.text: Immediately after treatment, you should be gentle with the numbed area and only eat once the anaesthetic has worn off.

bloecke.text: KU64 is accessible at central locations in Berlin and Potsdam, so the journey there can usually be planned well. Details on how to get there (public transport, parking, location) can be found on the website under Contact/Locations.

parodontitis-behandlung/laserbehandlung.titel: Laser treatment for teeth in Berlin – gentle and low-pain

bloecke.text: Inflamed gums, bleeding or an uncomfortable feeling of pressure are typical signs of periodontitis. With laser treatment for teeth, we at KU64 offer you a modern, particularly gentle treatment option: bacteria can be specifically reduced with the dental laser without unnecessarily stressing healthy tissue. The treatment is low-pain, vibration-free and causes less irritation to the gums than drilling. Our specialists integrate laser treatment into individual periodontitis concepts – for greater comfort during treatment and a noticeably better feeling afterwards.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The key facts at a glance
Targeted support for periodontitis

bloecke.text: Dental lasers precisely reduce the germs in the mouth that cause inflammation, making them the ideal complement to modern periodontitis therapies.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gentle procedure

bloecke.text: The high precision of laser use protects healthy tooth tissue to the greatest possible extent and thereby supports good natural wound healing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Low-pain treatment

bloecke.text: Laser treatment is low in vibration and noise, and patients find it noticeably more pleasant than drills and scalpels – especially with sensitive gums.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Lasering instead of drilling: light energy for healthy gums

bloecke.text: Lasers are increasingly used in dentistry and, for certain procedures, partly or even completely replace scalpels and drills. Thanks to modern laser therapy, dental treatment is possible with almost no pain. The dentists at KU64 use hair-fine dental lasers for particularly precise and gentle treatment. Unpleasant drilling noises or vibrations are a thing of the past. Instead, as a patient you benefit from less bleeding and swelling as well as faster wound healing than with conventional procedures. Depending on the type of laser, the treated areas are also cooled.

The laser is a true all-rounder: it can be used for surgical incisions in the gums or teeth as well as to stimulate wound healing. Laser treatment can also reduce bacteria and germs in the mouth and seal off blood vessels. Swelling or bleeding generally occurs significantly less often after laser treatment.

Thanks to these advantages, we at KU64 use the laser for gentle and low-pain treatment of periodontitis. In the past, we also used lasers for treating tooth decay and in surgery – for example, for root canal treatment. Over time, however, other methods have proven more effective and gentler for tooth decay and surgical procedures – which is why at KU64 we now deliberately rely on more modern, established methods rather than the laser in these areas.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What are laser beams?

bloecke.text: Put simply, laser beams are strongly focused, high-energy light. During treatment, these very short pulses of light hit the tissue in the mouth and are converted into heat. Depending on the radiation dose and the speed of the light pulses, different effects can be achieved.

The advantages: laser beams reach areas in the mouth that your dentist can only reach with difficulty, or not at all, using conventional instruments. In addition, the laser allows precise treatment: your dentist can treat diseased tissue with pinpoint accuracy without damaging adjacent healthy tissue.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Where are laser treatments used at KU64?
Intensive dental cleaning: Prophylaxis Plus Laser

bloecke.text: The revolutionary professional intensive dental cleaning Prophylaxis PLUS Laser is the future of dental care. Experience the next generation of dental cleaning at KU64 Berlin-Charlottenburg and KU64 Berlin-Mitte! Our innovative method combines sound theoretical training with practical expertise – professionally carried out by our dental hygienists and laser experts Adina Mauder or Aisegkioul Netzip Oglou-Housein at our branch on the Kudamm, and our experienced prophylaxis assistant Nurcan Sahin at our branch in Berlin-Mitte.

The advanced laser treatment serves to effectively prevent conditions such as tooth decay and periodontitis, as well as to prepare for treatments such as bleaching or the fitting of dentures by specifically reducing the bacterial load in the mouth.

Whether an intensive dental cleaning with laser treatment makes sense is determined individually using the so-called aMMP8 test. This test measures specific enzymes that indicate inflammatory processes and can impair the natural barrier protection of your oral mucosa.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Course of treatment

bloecke.text: First, a classic professional dental cleaning (PDC) is carried out, including pocket measurement. If probing depths (the distance between the gum margin and the base of the pocket) of 3 to 4 millimetres with bleeding are found, together with a noticeable MMP8 value, we recommend our Prophylaxis PLUS Laser treatment as a targeted, supportive measure. This is because enlarged pockets are an early warning sign of periodontitis.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Advantages of the treatment

bloecke.text: With this innovative therapy:
bacteria that cause inflammation are effectively destroyed with a gentle laser beam
the healthy oral flora is sustainably strengthened with probiotic lozenges
good bacteria can be specifically rebuilt
your mouth is perfectly prepared for further treatments such as bleaching or dental implants

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Laser treatment of periodontitis

bloecke.text: Compared with conventional periodontitis therapy, the dental laser offers numerous advantages in combating painful and pathological gum inflammation. For patients, laser procedures are gentler and generally free of side effects. The dentists at KU64 have therefore been using EmunDo therapy in combination with lasers for periodontitis treatment in their practice for many years. EmunDo is a biocompatible dye that marks bacteria on the teeth and in the gum pockets. The dentist then punctures the teeth and gum pockets with the laser.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Course of treatment

bloecke.text: The laser light destroys the disease-causing bacteria and germs. The dentist then uses an even finer laser to remove the inflamed tissue. This prevents new bacteria from settling. At the same time, this speeds up healing and, thanks to the precise technique, protects the surrounding tissue. As a patient, you do not lose any root substance. The cleaned gum pockets close up again after treatment. You can eat and drink again shortly afterwards.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Advantages of the treatment

bloecke.text: Laser therapy is particularly suitable for patients with severe periodontitis, as it is especially effective at destroying 99.9 per cent of bacteria. Antibiotics or other additional medications for accompanying treatment are not necessary. Therapy with EmunDo is also a suitable alternative for people with allergies, as it works without iodine. Local anaesthetic can also be dispensed with.
If inflammatory gum disease is treated at an early stage, you may be able to avoid the long-term need for dentures such as veneers, implants, bridges or crowns.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Laser treatment of peri-implantitis

bloecke.text: Very rarely, following implantation, the gum tissue and bone around the dental implant become inflamed. This is referred to as peri-implantitis. When cleaning inflamed dental implants, precise modern laser technology at our dental practice replaces classic surgical methods.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Course of treatment

bloecke.text: Similar to periodontitis treatment, the dentist uses the laser to remove the disease-causing bacteria and inflamed tissue around the denture. In doing so, the laser exposes the implant without cuts or pain – and without the soft gum tissue receding. The laser penetrates the inflamed tissue in a targeted manner, reduces the bacterial load and promotes healing at the same time – all without a scalpel and almost pain-free.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Advantages of the treatment

bloecke.text: The laser works like a modern antibiotic without side effects. Bone and mucous membrane can heal more quickly after laser treatment, and the healthy tissue once again encloses the implant.
KU64's implantology experts are happy to advise you in detail about the effects and individual steps of laser therapy.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dentistry at world-class level
Anxious patients welcome

bloecke.text: Gentle, low-pain and noiseless laser treatments are particularly suitable for anxious patients. KU64 accompanies you with a calm process and clear explanations, all the way to a radiant smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Open 7 days a week

bloecke.text: Do without long waiting times and flexibly fit your laser treatment appointment around your job, family and life – thanks to our opening hours, seven days a week.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Family appointments with a play paradise

bloecke.text: Simply combine your laser treatment with your children's check-up appointment – thanks to family appointments and our spacious, lovingly designed KU64 play paradise.
Support the long-term success of your laser treatment for healthy gums with suitable products from our in-house prophylaxis shop.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: All the advantages of laser treatment

bloecke.text: Laser dental treatment is one of the most innovative and gentlest methods in dentistry. The dentists at KU64 use laser treatment as an effective complement to conventional treatments for periodontitis. As a patient, you benefit from the following advantages:
precise and careful treatment that protects healthy tissue
generally no local anaesthetic required
lasting reduction of bacteria and germs in the mouth, thereby minimising inflammation
fewer antibiotics and medications needed after treatment
less swelling and bleeding, as the blood vessels are sealed off at the same time
non-invasive treatment with no stitches or scars
contact-free treatment with no vibrations or drilling noise on the tooth
shorter treatment time and almost no pain
quick, uncomplicated healing phase
aesthetic results
eating and drinking is possible immediately after treatment

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Who is laser treatment suitable for?

bloecke.text: Laser treatment is possible for almost every patient and carries no greater risk than conventional dental treatment. On the contrary: this gentle, modern treatment method is also suitable for people taking blood-thinning medication, as the procedure involves almost no bleeding.

For people with pre-existing conditions who should avoid anaesthetic or general anaesthesia, laser treatment is a suitable alternative. Patients with pain in particular value the safety and comfort that laser treatment offers. Feelings of pressure and the disruptive noise and vibration of the drill on the tooth are eliminated with laser treatment. The prospect of pain-free treatment also means that anxious patients can take a seat in the dental chair feeling more relaxed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does a laser dental treatment cost at KU64?

bloecke.text: Laser treatments are not services required by law and are not reimbursed by statutory health insurance. As a patient, you generally bear the costs of your laser treatment yourself. Whether your private health insurance or a supplementary insurance policy covers the costs depends on the tariff you have chosen.

In the case of acute procedures, pregnant and breastfeeding women may, under certain circumstances, have the costs of laser treatment reimbursed by statutory health insurance if it is medically indicated.

The cost of laser treatment varies depending on the type of treatment. The decisive factor is how many teeth are treated. The dentists at KU64 in Berlin and Potsdam are happy to discuss the individual steps with you in detail and draw up a personalised treatment and cost plan for you. This means you already know what costs to expect before treatment begins.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about laser treatment of teeth

bloecke.text: Our everyday practice shows that many patients are often very reluctant to visit the dentist for fear of pain. Noises, vibrations and smells during treatment often heighten this fear of the dentist.

The use of the laser can help patients overcome their fear. The new experience of pain-free treatment with no noises or feelings of pressure can dissolve existing patterns of anxiety and take away the breeding ground for fear of the dentist. Anxious patients then become increasingly willing to undergo more complex dental procedures too, such as root canal treatment. With laser technology, we guarantee our patients gentle, optimal treatment and the best possible outcomes.

In medicine, a distinction is made between hard lasers, soft lasers and mid-power lasers. Hard lasers have high power and are particularly suitable for cutting and removing tissue. They are used for root canal treatments as well as in the therapy of periodontitis. Soft lasers, on the other hand, have lower power and generate no heat during treatment. Owing to their low power levels, they are used to activate tissue. This stimulation reduces pain and inflammation during treatment and promotes blood circulation. Mid-power lasers operate at a medium power level but achieve a similar effect to soft lasers.
At KU64 in Berlin and Potsdam, we use the A.R.C. Laser for treatments. This is a diode laser (soft laser), which has been on the market in Germany since 1981.
