kinderzahnarzt/karies-bei-kindern.titel: Tooth Decay in Children – Children's Laughter Instead of Cavities

bloecke.text: Tooth decay, also known as caries or dental caries, is a common dental disease caused by the harmful effects of acids on tooth enamel. These acids are produced by bacteria in the mouth that feed on sugar and other carbohydrates. Tooth decay leads to the breakdown of enamel and the formation of holes or cavities in the teeth.

Proper care of milk teeth and attention during children's early years lays the foundation for a healthy smile later in life and in the years to come. Identifying these caries risk factors and implementing appropriate preventive measures is crucial for protecting children's oral health. With the right education and care, parents can help minimise their children's risk of tooth decay and secure a healthy smile for the future.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Easy for Children to Understand – What Is Tooth Decay?

bloecke.text: Here's a simple way to explain tooth decay to children:

Tooth decay is like a little army of tiny monsters attacking your teeth. Your teeth are like castles that you need to protect. These monsters love to eat sugar, and when they eat sugar, they make acid. The acid attacks the castles – it makes small holes in your teeth, and that's called tooth decay. But don't worry, you can protect your castles! You need to brush your teeth well to keep the monsters away. Use your toothbrush and toothpaste like your shield and sword to keep the monster acid away. And don't forget to eat fewer sweet things, so the monsters have nothing to nibble on.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: KU64 – Your Children's Dentist in Berlin

bloecke.text: Early detection of tooth decay is enormously important, especially for children who will live with their teeth for longer and, later, with their permanent teeth, and who therefore need to be taught proper dental hygiene in good time. It is all the more crucial that the child associates positive feelings with the dental visit, and doesn't think of unpleasant toothache when they hear the word "dentist". Our children's dentists at KU64 are attuned to the needs of their youngest patients and aim to make each little one's visit as pleasant as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Increased Risk of Tooth Decay in Children?

bloecke.text: There are several factors that increase the risk of tooth decay in children. Parents should be aware of these and ensure that their children's dental health is promoted and risks are kept as low as possible in order to prevent the development of tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Eating Habits

bloecke.text: A sugar-free diet is considered one of the main factors that increase the risk of tooth decay. Children who frequently consume sugary foods and drinks are more susceptible to tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Inadequate Oral Hygiene & Dental Care

bloecke.text: Children who do not brush their teeth regularly and thoroughly have a higher risk of tooth decay. Neglecting oral hygiene allows plaque and bacteria to build up on the teeth, leading to the formation of tooth decay. Parents should take the care of their children's milk teeth seriously, as this can also have a positive effect on the health of the permanent teeth and dental care in the years to come.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Mouth Breathing

bloecke.text: Predominantly breathing through the mouth can also be a risk factor for tooth decay. The resulting dry mouth conditions increase the risk of tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 4. Fluoride Deficiency

bloecke.text: Fluoride is an important component for strengthening tooth enamel. Children who do not get enough fluoride from toothpaste or drinking water have an increased risk of tooth decay. For this reason, choosing the right toothpaste is essential for children's dental health.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 5. Insufficient Dental Visits / Check-ups

bloecke.text: Regular dental examinations are crucial for detecting and treating tooth decay early. Children who do not have regular dental visits miss out on important preventive and early detection measures.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 6. Tooth Decay from Prolonged Sucking

bloecke.text: So-called prolonged sucking is a factor to be taken seriously, as it promotes the development of tooth decay. Baby bottle tooth decay, also known as bottle caries, is a dental condition that very commonly occurs in toddlers and infants. This type of tooth decay develops through frequent and prolonged sucking on a bottle or dummy filled with sugary liquids such as juices. This contact between the teeth and sugary drinks, particularly before bedtime, can lead to baby bottle tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Tooth Decay Develops in Children

bloecke.text: Tooth decay does not affect a tooth from one moment to the next or overnight, as there is a process behind it that ultimately leads to the disease:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Infection by Bacteria

bloecke.text: Tooth decay is a contagious dental disease caused by bacteria. Tooth decay can be transmitted through direct contact with infected saliva or by sharing cutlery, drinking vessels, or kissing. These bacteria, in particular Streptococcus mutans, are responsible for breaking down sugar. This leads to the formation of acid, which can damage tooth enamel. As their immune systems are still developing and they often have close contact with one another, children are frequently more susceptible to catching tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Multiplication of the Bacteria

bloecke.text: The bacteria that play a decisive role in tooth decay multiply through various mechanisms, such as food intake. The consumption of many sugary substances, such as drinks or sweets, causes the bacteria to multiply even further and, as a by-product of their metabolism, to produce acids that attack tooth enamel. The bacteria stick to the milk teeth and form a sticky substance called plaque. Within this plaque, bacteria can accumulate in large numbers and continue to multiply. This is a recurring cycle. If no measures are taken to stop this process, it leads to the development of tooth decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Holes Form

bloecke.text: Holes caused by tooth decay, also known as carious lesions or cavities, form as a result of the harmful process described above, which attacks tooth enamel. The acids attack the hard enamel by dissolving minerals out of it. This process, known as demineralisation, weakens the enamel and makes it increasingly susceptible. If the process is not stopped, the acids continue to penetrate, creating a lesion or cavity and, thus, permanent damage. This cavity is what we commonly refer to as a hole in a tooth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth Decay in Children – Treating Milk Teeth

bloecke.text: Treatment of tooth decay in milk teeth generally depends on the severity of the decay. Here are the common treatment options for tooth decay:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fissure Sealing

bloecke.text: In the early stages of tooth decay, the dentist may apply a fissure sealant. This is a thin layer of resin applied to the chewing surfaces of the teeth to protect them from further decay.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fillings

bloecke.text: In cases of deeper decay that has already damaged the tooth, a filling may be necessary. The dentist removes the decayed area of the milk tooth and fills the hole with a tooth-coloured filling material, such as composite resin or amalgam.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Root Canal Treatment

bloecke.text: In severe cases, when the decay has reached the pulp and thus the interior of the tooth, pulp therapy or root canal treatment may be necessary. In this procedure, the infected or damaged pulp is removed and the tooth is then filled.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth Extraction

bloecke.text: If the decay is so advanced that the tooth can no longer be saved, the dentist will carry out an extraction. This involves removing the affected milk tooth. This is done to prevent the infection from spreading to neighbouring teeth.

A local anaesthetic is usually used during treatment to minimise pain and discomfort. The choice of treatment depends on the individual situation of the child and the severity of the decay. It is important to visit the dentist early on to treat tooth decay in milk teeth. Untreated tooth decay not only causes pain but can also affect the growth of the permanent teeth and lead to long-term problems. So make an appointment with us at the practice today.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prevention – These Measures Help Prevent Tooth Decay
1. The Right Brushing Routine

bloecke.text: A child-friendly tooth-brushing routine is crucial for promoting children's oral health. It is important to make brushing a positive experience for children and to introduce them to good habits that will benefit them for a lifetime.
Easy Brushing Technique for Children – A Guide
Demonstrate the correct brushing motion by holding the brush at a 45-degree angle to the teeth. Make small, gentle circular movements.
Emphasise thorough cleaning of the chewing surfaces of the molars and the front teeth.
Make sure your child also gently brushes the tongue and palate to remove plaque and bacteria.
Brush gently along the gums to remove plaque and bacteria. This should not be painful. Be sure to clean the tongue and palate as well.
Children should brush their teeth, or have their teeth brushed, at least twice a day, ideally in the morning and before bedtime. The recommended brushing time is two minutes.
Child-Friendly Equipment

In addition to proper technique, the right equipment is an important prerequisite for healthy oral hygiene. When it comes to dental care for children in particular, it is important to choose a child-friendly toothbrush with soft bristles. Electric toothbrushes are often very effective, but a manual toothbrush can work just as well if used correctly. To spark your child's interest, brushes with a playful, motivating design are also a great choice. A pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste for children should be used for brushing. From the moment the milk teeth start to touch one another, you should begin flossing to remove plaque and food particles between the teeth. There are also special interdental brushes that are easy to use and can be suitable for children.
Positive Reinforcement and Rewards

Make brushing a pleasant routine by encouraging your child to have fun with it. This can be achieved by playing music, telling stories, or using an hourglass to time the brushing. Reward your child with praise and small rewards for brushing regularly and thoroughly.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Attend Early Detection Check-ups

bloecke.text: Another important measure for preventing tooth decay is attending regular check-ups and dental visits for prevention and early detection of tooth decay. It's important to know that in its earliest stage, the formation of tooth decay can be reversible, provided the demineralisation has not progressed too far.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Preventing the Spread of Tooth Decay

bloecke.text: Children are more susceptible to catching tooth decay, as their immune systems are still developing and they often have closer contact with one another. However, the spread of tooth decay can be minimised through good oral hygiene practices, such as regular tooth brushing and avoiding sharing cutlery or crockery.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Tooth Decay in Children – Act Quickly!

bloecke.text: Tooth decay is often underestimated, but at KU64 we understand the dangers of decay damage and its consequences, and we act immediately. That's why we thoroughly check even seemingly healthy teeth – this is the only way to identify decay in time, carry out its removal, and prevent serious complications at the right time. Depending on the extent of the damage, the appropriate treatment is chosen.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Book an Appointment Now!

bloecke.text: For more information about the services offered by our practice for all-round healthy, beautiful teeth, visit our social media channels Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and Instagram.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQ: Frequently Asked Questions About Tooth Decay in Children
What Symptoms Indicate Tooth Decay In My Child?

bloecke.text: Symptoms that may indicate tooth decay in your child include pain or sensitivity in the teeth, particularly when eating hot, cold, sweet, or sour foods. Discolouration or dark spots on the teeth are also a sign. In more advanced stages, your child may have visible holes or defects in the teeth. Bad breath, difficulty chewing, and gum problems can be further indicators. However, please note that tooth decay does not always cause pain, especially in its early stages. This is why regular dental check-ups are important for detecting and treating tooth decay early. If you notice any of these symptoms, you should see a children's dentist straight away.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can Tooth Decay In Children Be Stopped?

bloecke.text: The good news is that tooth decay in children can be stopped or, in many cases, even reversed. However, the most important prerequisite for this is that the decay is detected and treated early. Treatment of tooth decay in children may include measures such as fillings, sealants, and, in some cases, root canal treatments, depending on the severity of the decay. In addition to treatment, prevention of tooth decay is crucial. The causes of tooth decay in children are inadequate care of milk teeth and excessive consumption of sugary foods and drinks. Parents should ensure that their children brush their teeth regularly, encourage a balanced diet with limited sugar consumption, and support dental visits for check-ups and cleanings.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Quickly Does Tooth Decay In Children Need To Be Treated?

bloecke.text: The earlier tooth decay in young children is treated, the lower the risk of complications and pain for the child. If left untreated, tooth decay can spread and cause damage to the teeth. This results in pain and larger, more expensive procedures. Regular dental check-ups are essential for detecting tooth decay in good time.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: At What Age Is Tooth Decay Normal?

bloecke.text: Tooth decay can occur at any age, though it is more common in children, as their milk teeth are more susceptible to decay. As a rule, the first teeth develop from around six months of age, and tooth decay can occur from this age onwards, particularly if dental care is neglected. For this reason, it is important to establish good dental habits as early as possible.

zahnimplantate/implantate-und-rauchen.titel: Dental Implants and Smoking: What You Should Know

bloecke.text: Smoking is not only harmful to blood vessels, the heart and the lungs. It also endangers the health of your teeth, gums and jaw. As a result, placing and maintaining an implant long-term carries particular risks for smokers. In this guide, we've put together the most important aspects of dental implants and smoking for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Table of Contents

bloecke.text: The most important points at a glance Your path to stability and a smile that lasts Why smoking limits bone stability Why smoking delays wound healing after implantation Why smoking increases the risk of implant loss Benefits of quitting smoking for your dental health What do I need to consider as a smoker regarding the operation? Advice on dental implants and smoking at KU64 Conclusion: Active measures minimise the risk smoking poses to implants FAQs – Frequently asked questions about dental implants and smoking

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The Most Important Points at a Glance
Limited Bone Stability in Smokers

bloecke.text: Smoking increases the risk of periodontitis and thus jawbone loss. The stable bone needed for implants is lost.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Delayed Wound Healing After Implantation

bloecke.text: Nicotine and harmful substances in tobacco smoke can promote inflammation and delay or complicate the healing of the implant. You should therefore avoid smoking for as long as possible after the procedure.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Our Goal: Long-Term Success

bloecke.text: We won't leave you on your own. As a smoker, we'll support you with individual strategies for preparing for and looking after your new dental implant, to help it last for the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Your Path to Stability and a Smile That Lasts

bloecke.text: You're a smoker and would like to have firm, secure teeth. Sometimes a diseased tooth simply can't be saved and has to be removed. To close the gap in your mouth with a confident smile, you want the reliable quality and aesthetics of an implant – but you're unsure because you smoke and the treatment involves considerable cost? This is exactly where our support begins. We'll talk you through, on equal footing, how nicotine can affect healing and which steps really matter before and after the operation.

We don't lecture. Every story is different. It's clear that giving up smoking altogether would be best for your health. But sometimes the time isn't right for big changes. Becoming a non-smoker can be a long process that takes a great deal of energy. Or, for whatever personal reasons, you may simply not aim for that at all. Even small, realistic changes at the right moment can do your health some good and give your implant the best possible chance to heal in well.

At KU64, we take the time to listen to your questions, concerns and goals. Together, we develop a plan that fits your everyday life – from manageable smoking breaks around the procedure, to gentle surgical planning, to structured aftercare. This turns uncertainty into a clear path towards your goal: medically sound, carefully supported and delivered with genuine warmth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Why Smoking Limits Bone Stability

bloecke.text: Let's start with the disadvantages of smoking for your new implant. According to scientific studies, heavy smokers have a six times higher risk of inflammatory diseases of the tooth-supporting structures than non-smokers, due to the toxins they absorb. This applies to tooth decay, but especially to periodontitis. This disease leads to the breakdown of the jawbone and the connective tissue in the mouth.
Nicotine also impairs the body's absorption of calcium, which is essential for strong, healthy bones. As a result, smokers often have poorer bone quality than non-smokers.

However, successful implant placement requires a sufficiently stable bone bed, so that the implant can gain enough support in the bone. If the bone doesn't offer enough support, it can be built up surgically using a sinus lift. This, however, brings additional surgical risks.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Why Smoking Delays Wound Healing After Implantation

bloecke.text: Placing an implant is a more involved procedure compared with conventional forms of tooth replacement, such as a crown. During implantation, the surgeon opens the gum at the chosen implant site and prepares the jawbone with a drill for the future implant. The implant, which has a screw thread, is then inserted into the bone.

Over the course of three to six months, the implant naturally fuses with the surrounding jawbone and becomes firmly anchored in the jaw, just like a real tooth root. If you smoke during this healing phase, it can lead to complications in the healing process of the dental implant. This is because the harmful substances in tobacco smoke promote inflammatory processes in the mouth, making wound healing more difficult.

Our implantology experts therefore strongly advise against smoking immediately before and after implant placement. They will take the time to give you tips and strategies before and after the operation, to help your new implant heal in as well as possible.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Why Smoking Increases the Risk of Implant Loss

bloecke.text: Anyone who continues to smoke after the implant has healed in should be aware that implants tend to last less time in smokers than in non-smokers. The increased risk of implant loss arises, for example, because smokers more often develop inflammation of the tissue around the implant (peri-implantitis). If this inflammation cannot be stopped, it can, in the worst case, lead to the loss of the implant.

For smokers, the risk of peri-implantitis is increased because nicotine is a nerve toxin and narrows the blood vessels. Blood flow in the mouth, particularly around the gums, deteriorates, and with it the immune system. This creates an ideal breeding ground for bacteria, which can spread more easily than in non-smokers, causing inflammation at the neck of the implant and in the surrounding tissue, and can even reach the jawbone.

A review study from 2020 found that, across all the studies analysed, smokers have a significantly higher risk of implant loss than non-smokers. The risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Benefits of Quitting Smoking for Your Dental Health

bloecke.text: Are you a smoker looking to use your upcoming implant treatment as an opportunity to quit smoking? As a future non-smoker, you'll protect your dental health and benefit in many ways:
A radiant smile: You protect your valuable replacement teeth and your newly regained smile. Staining of the teeth, lips or tongue caused by nicotine or tar becomes a thing of the past.
Healthy teeth: You'll suffer from tooth decay far less often than people who smoke. What's more, smokers tend to build up more tartar on their teeth than non-smokers.

Less inflammation and pain: Smoking increases sensitivity to pain throughout the mouth. As a non-smoker, you reduce your risk of inflammation in the mouth and throat, such as periodontitis, along with the exposed, sensitive tooth necks that come with it.

Stronger teeth: Any inflammation of the gums and tooth socket can weaken the structures that hold the teeth in place. The result: teeth can fall out. Studies confirm that smokers lose their teeth more often than non-smokers.
Fresher breath: The build-up of bacteria that causes unpleasant breath and bad breath also decreases when you stop smoking.
Lower cancer risk: Smoking increases the risk of developing cancer of the mouth, throat and larynx. The good news: your cancer risk gradually returns to normal once you quit smoking.

Even if you've smoked for many years, it's never too late to quit. The benefits of not smoking for oral health are often noticeable immediately, and continue to be felt in the long term. Aids such as nicotine patches can help by easing the physical withdrawal symptoms. Acupuncture or hypnotherapy with a suitably qualified practitioner can also help with quitting smoking. We're happy to advise you on further options for a smoke-free life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Do I Need to Consider as a Smoker Regarding the Operation?

bloecke.text: The period immediately before and after implantation is crucial for successful healing. To reduce the risks of smoking to a minimum and give your dental implant the best possible conditions to heal in, it's important to follow some specific guidelines around the procedure:
The implantologists at KU64 recommend not smoking for 14 days before and after any bone augmentation, as well as 14 days before and after implant placement.

Dentists also advise against using nicotine-containing chewing gum or lozenges after implantation. While these can make quitting easier and don't contain the combustion residues found in tobacco smoke, they do deliver the cellular toxin nicotine directly onto the teeth, oral mucosa and gums. This significantly increases the risk of gum inflammation, periodontitis and other infections such as peri-implantitis or peri-implant mucositis during the healing phase after the operation.

In the longer term, smokers should pay attention to getting enough vitamin C in their diet after implant placement. Our dental health specialists are happy to advise you on the right, healing-supportive diet after the procedure.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Advice on Dental Implants and Smoking at KU64

bloecke.text: Are you a smoker considering an implant? We're happy to advise you on your options for the long-term maintenance of implants and the optimal care of your new replacement teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Fast Appointment Booking with Your Implantology Specialists

bloecke.text: Get in touch with us! Call us on +49 308647320, send us a message, or book an appointment online directly with our two implantology specialists, Dr Surian Herrmann and Jiotis Hondralis, for a detailed personal consultation on implants and smoking.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Conclusion: Active Measures Minimise the Risk Smoking Poses to Implants

bloecke.text: As a smoker, your wish for a firm bite with dental implants is entirely achievable. Although smoking brings risks for bone stability and wound healing, active measures such as a smoking break around the procedure, and above all our professional, individual advice and support, can help you secure the long-term success of your implant as well as possible. We're here for you, with advice and hands-on help!
Written by: Dr Stephan Ziegler
Last updated on 10.12.25

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – Frequently Asked Questions About Dental Implants and Smoking
Are Dental Implants Possible Despite Smoking?

bloecke.text: Yes, this is possible following an individual risk assessment. What matters most is your general state of health, how well your teeth heal, and taking a smoking break around the procedure to improve the implant's chances of success.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Why Does Smoking Encourage Peri-Implantitis?

bloecke.text: Peri-implantitis is an irreversible inflammation of the tooth socket that causes bone loss. If left untreated, it can lead to the loss of the implant and, in some cases, of healthy neighbouring teeth too. Peri-implantitis can also develop many years after implants have been placed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Can I Prevent Peri-Implantitis as a Smoker?

bloecke.text: Regular preventive check-ups combined with professional teeth cleaning at the dentist can help prevent tooth decay and peri-implantitis. Our implantology specialists are trained to spot and treat bacterial build-up around implants at an early stage.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Does Implant Placement Work?

bloecke.text: After diagnosis and planning, you'll be given a clear timeline with a date for surgery and follow-up care. Treatment involves placing the implant under local anaesthetic, followed by structured check-ups.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Long Should I Avoid Smoking After Implant Surgery?

bloecke.text: We strongly recommend taking a break from smoking around the procedure, so the operation can be carried out well and the implant can heal in safely. You should avoid smoking for two weeks before implant placement and two weeks afterwards – so four weeks in total without smoking.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Will I Need Bone Augmentation as a Smoker?

bloecke.text: If there isn't enough bone available in the lower jaw, we recommend bone augmentation to secure the stability of the implant. Smokers are more likely to need prior bone augmentation. Whether this is really necessary in your case will be determined by a dental examination.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Complications Can Occur?

bloecke.text: Smokers have an increased risk of possible complications from surgery. Rarely, swelling, secondary bleeding or infections can occur; in the longer term, peri-implant complications (inflammation around the implant) are possible. Good oral hygiene, smoking breaks before and after implant placement, and regular check-ups significantly reduce this risk.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Do Implants Support Oral Health?

bloecke.text: Implants are the gold standard for replacing missing teeth. High-quality tooth replacements such as implants make dental care easier and support your oral health. As a rule, you'll benefit from advantages for both aesthetics and oral hygiene, even though maintaining an implant long-term is more demanding for smokers due to the risk factors involved in smoking. Professional preventive care and consistent oral hygiene are essential. This way, your new replacement teeth will last you a long time.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Do Implants Cost?

bloecke.text: The cost of dental implants depends on the complexity of the treatment, the materials used, any bone augmentation required, and laboratory work. Your dentist will set out all the individual items transparently in a treatment and cost plan – from the surgical step through to the final replacement tooth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Who Will Support Me Through the Process?

bloecke.text: Our team of experienced oral and maxillofacial surgeons and preventive care specialists will support you before, during and after the operation. We'll explain everything to you step by step and stay with you throughout the procedure and aftercare, so your replacement teeth remain in good condition for the long term.

Healthy gums are the foundation for beautiful, healthy teeth – and for a carefree smile. When the gums recede, this is not only aesthetically unsettling but also leads to sensitivity in the exposed tooth necks. It also increases the risk of serious damage. The good news: with modern, gentle methods, gum rebuilding to reconstruct the areas that have been lost is possible in our practice. This restores the protection for your teeth, along with the good feeling of being able to smile with confidence again.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: This is why gum rebuilding is so important

bloecke.text: Gums play an important role in preserving your teeth. They hold the teeth firmly in the jaw, protect them from harmful bacteria and ensure that eating, speaking and laughing function normally.

Gum recession can be triggered by various mechanical and biological factors. The most common causes are incorrect tooth brushing and a pathological inflammation of the gums, periodontitis. If the protection of the teeth is weakened as a result of gum recession, this can have far-reaching consequences: teeth appear longer, tooth necks are gradually exposed and become sensitive to pain. The lack of protection from the gum tissue makes them more susceptible to diseases such as tooth decay. In the worst case, tooth loss can even occur.

Using modern methods, we regenerate the lost substance of this protective layer through gum rebuilding and restore your smile's natural appearance. For the perfect result, you can combine the gum reconstruction with gentle bleaching.

In our practice, your wellbeing is at the centre of everything we do. Our team takes the time to provide sensitive advice to our patients. We explain each treatment step to you and work together with you to find the solution that best suits your situation. In this way, we not only ensure healthy gums but also renewed self-confidence and quality of life.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When is gum rebuilding treatment needed?

bloecke.text: Any gum recession should be examined and monitored by a dentist to determine the exact cause and rule out possible negative consequences for the whole organism.

Mild gum recession that causes no discomfort or increased risk of tooth decay usually does not require additional gum rebuilding from a medical point of view. However, affected patients should attend regular dental check-ups and address the causes of the developing recession with medical support so that it progresses as little as possible.

The recession can be triggered by incorrect oral care, meaning you should adjust your daily tooth cleaning routine. However, it can also result from periodontitis, sometimes in combination with periodontal pockets. This must be treated as quickly as possible by the specialist in our periodontology department. Natural teeth are not the only ones affected. Recession caused by inflammation can sometimes also be observed around dental restorations such as dental implants.

Advanced gum recession with exposed tooth necks causes pain when eating and drinking, impairs oral hygiene and encourages inflammation, making treatment through gum rebuilding necessary. As the recession progresses, the teeth also gradually lose their grip, which can lead to tooth loss.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What methods are available for gum rebuilding?

bloecke.text: At the first signs of gum recession, the treating doctor or dentist will initially try to improve the condition of the gums using various conservative methods, stopping any inflammation and periodontitis. Our team uses the most modern methods for this. These include medicinal therapy against the inflammation, deep-cleaning procedures to remove plaque and tartar, and laser therapy to remove inflamed tissue and bacteria. Important: conservative methods do not restore gum tissue that has already been lost. However, targeted measures prevent further gum recession and secondary conditions.

If conservative treatments are not enough to resolve gum recession and restore oral health, a surgical procedure for gum rebuilding is required at our dental practice. This calls for precise planning and comprehensive aftercare. Only in this way is it possible to ensure the successful integration of new tissue and to maintain oral health in the long term.

There are various surgical methods that can be used depending on the extent and severity of the recession. The choice of the appropriate surgical method depends on the individual patient's situation, the severity of the damage and the dental recommendations.
In addition to the surgical procedure, we use medications such as growth hormones where necessary to promote the regeneration of the affected areas in the mouth after the procedure.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gum transplantation

bloecke.text: Gum transplantation is a common, gentle microsurgical method for treating gum recession. For the transplant, the surgeon takes healthy gum tissue from another area of the mouth and transfers it to the areas at the tooth necks affected by recession. Gum tissue is usually taken from the palate area for this. Meanwhile, there are also the first successful treatment options using artificial gum tissue from the laboratory, which makes the procedure even gentler.

The transplanted gum tissue regenerates the gums at the receded areas within a few weeks of the transplant and protects the exposed tooth necks. The aesthetic appearance also improves through gum transplantation, restoring your beautiful smile. The aesthetic improvement is particularly noticeable when the front teeth are affected.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gum flap surgery

bloecke.text: Flap surgery with gum correction is another common surgical method for gum rebuilding. As long as there is still enough tissue available, no gum transplant is needed. The surgeon lifts the gum flap to clean the underlying structures and restore the bone.

The gum tissue is then laid back over the teeth to support healing and, depending on the situation, can be remodelled with a gum correction to better protect the tooth neck and enclose it firmly again.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bone rebuilding

bloecke.text: If gum recession is accompanied by bone loss in the chewing apparatus, bone rebuilding may be necessary in addition to gum transplantation. In this procedure, artificial bone substitute materials are surgically placed at the affected areas of the jaw to regenerate the bone tissue and secure the stability of the teeth.

The reconstructive materials heal completely into the bone and are not visible from the outside. In this way, they form a new foundation for the tooth and the surrounding gum tissue. The surgeon can then, if necessary, transplant tissue from another area of the palate.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does treatment for gum rebuilding cost?

bloecke.text: Gum rebuilding is an investment in your health, your smile and your wellbeing. It is not possible to name exact costs in general terms, as they depend heavily on the individual situation. Among other things, the following are decisive:
Extent of treatment – does it affect only one tooth or are areas around several teeth affected?
Method and technique – depending on whether the body's own tissue is used or modern substitute materials are applied.
Time required and aftercare – a more complex treatment situation for the teeth also means a longer treatment period.

As a rule, statutory health insurance does not cover the costs of gum rebuilding, as the treatment is primarily regarded as improving aesthetics. However, all costs for the treatment steps required in this context for periodontitis treatment are covered by insurance.
Private health insurance and supplementary dental insurance may – depending on the contract – reimburse part of the costs for the treatment. This depends on your individual tariff.

So that you have certainty in your planning, we create an individual treatment and cost plan for you at our practice with all the information, which we go through with you step by step together. This way, you know exactly what costs you will incur and what options exist for cost coverage through your health insurance.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Aftercare: keeping your gums healthy

bloecke.text: After successful gum rebuilding treatment, it is important to protect the result achieved and to preserve the reconstructed gum tissue in the long term. Your gums now need attention and gentle care so that the new tissue can develop stably and further procedures do not become necessary in the first place. With a combination of professional support and proper care, you secure the results of the gum rebuilding for the long term – and above all, the joy of your carefree smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How to behave after treatment

bloecke.text: Follow the individual recommendations from your dentist – for example, regarding rest, special oral care or rinses.
Avoid hard or very hot foods in the first few days after the operation.
You should avoid smoking and alcohol as much as possible during the healing phase, as they significantly delay regeneration.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Correct tooth brushing

bloecke.text: Brush gently: use a soft toothbrush or an electric brush with pressure control so that the gums are protected.

The right brushing technique: circular motions rather than scrubbing with a manual brush, and gliding from the gum towards the tip of the tooth with an electric brush – your dentist or preventive care specialist will be happy to show you the right brushing technique.
Clean between the teeth: dental floss or interdental brushes can remove bacteria from places the brush cannot reach.
Diet is part of dental care: plenty of fresh vegetables, little sugar and sufficient water support oral health.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Regular dental check-ups

bloecke.text: Six-monthly check-up appointments with preventive care help your dentist to detect changes at an early stage and take countermeasures if necessary.
We recommend professional teeth cleaning (PTC) twice a year. This keeps the gums free of inflammation and gives deposits no chance to build up.
Stress, teeth grinding or smoking are risk factors for gum recession – we will advise you on how best to reduce these.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about gum rebuilding
Who needs gum rebuilding treatment?

bloecke.text: Treatment by rebuilding gaps in or missing gum tissue makes sense when the tooth necks are exposed. This is because sooner or later, sensitivity to cold, heat, acidic or sugary foods and drinks will occur.

However, natural teeth are not the only ones affected – recession is also known in implantology. It often occurs around dental restorations, with dental implants being particularly affected. Since no pain sensation occurs at the tooth in this case, you should have your dental restoration regularly checked by a specialist dentist in our implantology department. Gum recession can also occur unnoticed under veneers. Special attention should therefore also be paid to veneers.

Especially when a disease of the gums, possibly in combination with periodontal pockets, is the cause of the recession, treatment should be started immediately in our periodontology department. This prevents periodontitis from spreading further.
In rare cases, braces can be the cause of the recession. Regular orthodontic check-ups can prevent this from happening, and the braces will be adjusted or paused if necessary.

In addition to dental health, dental aesthetics also suffer from exposed tooth necks. By reconstructing the gums, you also regain your natural smile. Combine the treatment with gentle bleaching for the perfect result.
It is best to contact us directly and have us clarify at our dental practice whether action is needed in your case.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does gum rebuilding cost?

bloecke.text: The costs depend on the method, the extent and the number of teeth affected. As a rule, statutory health insurance cannot cover the costs of the treatment. Private insurance and supplementary insurance cover part or all of the costs depending on the tariff. We will inform you transparently about all options and costs beforehand.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does gum rebuilding treatment hurt?

bloecke.text: No. Thanks to modern, gentle methods and reliable anaesthesia, you will not feel any pain during the treatment. After the procedure, usually only very mild discomfort occurs, and any pain can be well managed with pain relief medication.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What should I do if I am afraid of the procedure?

bloecke.text: It is important to talk openly about your fear. Speak to the dentist about your concerns. We specialise in caring for anxious patients with sensitivity and creating a relaxed atmosphere. We work at your pace, explain every treatment step and ensure that anxious patients feel safe. Thanks to modern, gentle methods and reliable anaesthesia, you will not feel any pain during the treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are there any risks or side effects with gum rebuilding?

bloecke.text: As with any minor procedure, slight swelling or sensitivity may occur after treatment. However, serious complications are rare. We will explain everything to you calmly beforehand and accompany you until everything has fully healed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How long does healing take after gum rebuilding?

bloecke.text: You will already see the first results of the reconstructed gum tissue after a few days. However, it takes a few weeks for the gums to heal completely. During this time, we are here for you and will give you tips on the right care and behaviour until healing is complete.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do the results of gum rebuilding last?

bloecke.text: With proper oral hygiene and regular professional teeth cleaning, the results of the treatment will remain with you for the long term. It is important to avoid risk factors such as smoking or incorrect brushing technique. As part of the treatment, we will give you all the information you need for this, and we are happy to support you in implementing our recommendations.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I prevent gum recession?

bloecke.text: Yes! A correct and gentle brushing technique, regular preventive check-ups at the practice and controlling risk factors help to keep the gums healthy – often for a lifetime. We also recommend having professional teeth cleaning carried out regularly.

implantat-prophylaxe/periimplantitis.titel: Peri-implantitis – Inflammation Around the Dental Implant

bloecke.text: Have you decided on an implant when it comes to replacing a missing tooth? A great choice! Dental implants are the highest-quality form of tooth replacement, barely distinguishable from a real tooth either in appearance or feel. And ideally, they last a lifetime. However, problems can occasionally arise around implants that may affect how long they last – above all, peri-implantitis. Here you can find out exactly what this is, how to prevent it, and which therapy we use at KU64 Berlin to treat it, so that your dental implant continues to serve you reliably for many years to come.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT IS Peri-implantitis?

bloecke.text: Peri-implantitis is an inflammation of the tissue around a dental implant. In this respect, it resembles periodontitis (gum disease), which can occur around natural teeth. Peri-implantitis initially affects the gums, but in an advanced stage it can also affect the jawbone surrounding the implant. Early detection and treatment are very important, as the inflammation typically leads to bone loss over time and, in the worst case, to loss of the implant.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW COMMON IS Peri-implantitis?

bloecke.text: There is a considerable body of research on peri-implantitis. Studies show that around 20% of people with implants develop peri-implantitis over the years. The precursor to peri-implantitis, peri-implant mucositis, occurs in up to 50% of implant wearers.

But there's no need to panic: this doesn't mean your personal risk of peri-implantitis is automatically 20%. Factors such as the quality of your oral hygiene, smoking, or systemic conditions like diabetes play a significant role. Studies also show that the risk increases the longer you have had the implant. So regular dental check-ups become no less important over the years – quite the opposite, in fact. Come and visit us at one of our locations in Berlin!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW DOES Peri-implantitis Develop? Causes AND Risk Factors

bloecke.text: Peri-implantitis usually develops as a result of a bacterial infection in the tissue surrounding dental implants. The main cause is plaque build-up on the implant surfaces, similar to periodontitis affecting natural teeth. If this plaque isn't removed regularly, it can harden and turn into tartar, which further fuels the inflammation. Over time, the inflammation can spread to the jawbone.
There are several risk factors that can encourage the development of peri-implantitis:

If implants aren't cleaned thoroughly enough, plaque builds up. This encourages the growth of bacteria that cause inflammation. Since plaque and bacteria collect especially at the point where the implant meets the gum, using dental floss, interdental brushes and antibacterial mouthwash is particularly important for implant wearers – though of course, your natural teeth will benefit too!

Nicotine consumption impairs blood flow to the gums and weakens the immune system. This means the tissue around implants is less able to regenerate. Studies show that the risk of peri-implantitis is up to 50% higher for smokers than for non-smokers.
Correct positioning is crucial in implantology. If the implant hasn't been placed optimally, this can make cleaning more difficult and encourage the accumulation of bacteria.

Patients who have previously had periodontitis are at higher risk of developing inflammation after an implant has been placed. If you have such a history, you should pay particular attention to thorough oral hygiene and regular check-ups with your dentist to minimise your risk of peri-implantitis.
Weak bone substance can increase the risk of problems following dental implantation. This is because peri-implantitis can then lead to bone loss more quickly and is harder to stop.
Excessive strain on the implant caused by too much biting pressure can irritate the surrounding tissue and trigger inflammation.

Conditions such as diabetes mellitus can impair the tissue's ability to heal and increase the risk of peri-implantitis. If blood sugar is well controlled, the risk remains manageable. However, if diabetes is poorly controlled, the risk can increase significantly. In our practice in Berlin, we also offer a diabetes test as part of your preventive care, on request. Do feel free to ask us about it!

The development of peri-implantitis is a gradual process that often only begins and progresses months or even years after implantation. Regular follow-up check-ups with your dentist and careful oral hygiene – from brushing to mouthwash – are essential to minimise the risk.

Our implantology specialists at KU64 Berlin ensure that your implant is placed optimally. After that, we naturally place great importance on thorough aftercare and will explain exactly how to look after your implant properly, so that it stays with you for many years to come.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW DOES Peri-implantitis Present? Diagnosis AND Symptoms

bloecke.text: With peri-implantitis, early treatment is absolutely essential. However, patients often only notice clear symptoms once the inflammation has already progressed. This makes it all the more important to watch out for early signs and see a dentist quickly. These are typical symptoms of peri-implantitis:
Redness and swelling of the gums: At the start of the condition, there is often slight redness and swelling of the gums around the implant, similar to gum inflammation (gingivitis).
Bleeding when brushing or touching the area: A common sign of peri-implantitis is bleeding gums, which can occur under pressure and points to inflammation.
Bad breath: Chronic inflammation in the mouth can lead to persistent bad breath that doesn't go away even with thorough, regular oral hygiene.
Sensitivity to pain: If you feel pain around the implant when touching it or chewing, this already indicates advanced inflammation that should be treated by a dentist as soon as possible.

Gum recession: Over time, the gum around the implant can recede and partially expose it. This recession is triggered partly by the inflammation itself, and partly because the gum loses its support as the jawbone is broken down.
Pus formation: In severe cases, pus can form around the dental implant, which is a clear sign of an advanced infection.

Loosening of the implant: This is a particularly alarming symptom. It indicates that the jawbone has already been significantly broken down by the inflammation. If the implant loses its hold as a result, the peri-implantitis is already at a late stage.

Please take these symptoms seriously and, if in doubt, feel free to book an appointment in addition to your regular check-ups. Our dentists at KU64 can tell you whether it is indeed peri-implantitis and, if necessary, treat it and save your implant – the earlier, the better and the more straightforward!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW IS Peri-implantitis Treated? Modern Treatment Methods

bloecke.text: How best to treat peri-implantitis depends on how severe and advanced the condition is. The aim of treatment is to control the inflammation, allow the tissue to regenerate, and prevent further bone loss. As a general rule: the earlier peri-implantitis is detected, the easier it is to treat. In dentistry, there are various approaches for different stages of the condition:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Non-surgical treatment

bloecke.text: Peri-implantitis at an early stage can usually be treated without surgical intervention. The following methods may be used:

Professional cleaning: Dental implants need to be thoroughly cleaned to remove plaque and tartar. At KU64 Berlin, we use modern laser technology, which removes bacteria and inflamed tissue with particular precision and gentleness – without any pain or unpleasant noises!
Antibacterial therapy: Antibacterial rinses or gels can help reduce the bacterial load and combat the inflammation.

Improving oral hygiene: With the right oral hygiene and correct use of aids such as interdental brushes, you can prevent plaque from building up again. Our team is happy to take the time to show you everything step by step.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Surgical treatment

bloecke.text: If peri-implantitis has progressed to the point where bone has already been lost, surgical treatment may become necessary. This usually looks as follows:
Curettage and cleaning: The gum is opened to gain access to the implant and the surrounding tissue. The inflamed area is then thoroughly cleaned and infected tissue is removed.

Bone grafting: If bone has already been lost, a bone graft can be carried out. Either the patient's own bone or a substitute material is used to rebuild the bone and give the implant renewed stability.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Implant replacement

bloecke.text: In particularly severe cases, where peri-implantitis and bone loss have progressed so far that the implant no longer has any stability, removal of the implant is often the only option. Once the area has healed, a new implant can be placed.

Whichever type of treatment is right for you, good, regular aftercare and prevention are crucial to its success. Together with you, we're happy to plan regular check-ups and professional teeth cleaning, so that peri-implantitis doesn't stand a chance of returning.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Professional Preventive Diagnostics

bloecke.text: At our practice at Kurfürstendamm 64 in Berlin, we offer you modern diagnostics for ideal prevention. Our specialists in oral and maxillofacial surgery, implantology and oral surgery assess your individual potential risks before implantation. This allows them to advise and treat you optimally right from the start.
More about dental implants at KU64 Berlin

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Innovative Prophylaxis 4.0

bloecke.text: With our prophylaxis system 'Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT)', which so far only a few dental practices in Germany offer, professional teeth cleaning is gentler, more effective and more pleasant for our patients than ever before. No pain, no scraping, no loud noises – just clean, healthy teeth.
More about GBT at KU64 Berlin

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW CAN Peri-implantitis Be Prevented?

bloecke.text: Preventing peri-implantitis starts with consistent oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups. Here are a few tips to help your implant stay with you for as long as possible:

Thorough oral hygiene: The most important step in preventing peri-implantitis and other conditions is careful daily oral hygiene. As well as thorough brushing, this includes cleaning between the teeth. Using dental floss, interdental brushes or special implant brushes helps you remove plaque even from the hard-to-reach areas around the implant. Antiseptic mouthwashes can help reduce bacteria and support gum health.

Regular cleaning and check-ups: Regular visits to the dentist are important not only for professional teeth cleaning, but also for the early detection of problems such as peri-implantitis. During cleaning, plaque and tartar are removed. Our dentists also check the health of your implant and the surrounding tissue. If necessary, they clean the implant surface directly, so that inflammation doesn't get the chance to develop in the first place.

Avoiding smoking: Smoking is one of the biggest risk factors for peri-implantitis. Tobacco use impairs the immune system and blood flow to the gums, which increases the risk of inflammation and slows healing. So having a dental implant is another good reason for smokers to consider quitting!

A balanced diet: A healthy diet is well known to contribute to overall health – including the health of your mouth. Sugary and heavily processed foods encourage plaque formation and can increase the risk of inflammation. A balanced diet with plenty of fruit, vegetables and key nutrients, on the other hand, supports the immune system and gum health. And you'll feel fitter for it too!

Avoiding excessive strain: Implants need to be evenly loaded so the tissue isn't placed under excessive strain. Avoid putting too much pressure on the implant. If you grind your teeth at night, a special dental splint can help distribute the biting pressure. We at KU64 Berlin are happy to advise you!

Treating periodontitis before implantation: For patients who currently have, or have previously had, periodontitis, we pay particular attention to ensuring that the inflammation has fully cleared before we place an implant. A healthy oral environment before implantation minimises the risk of peri-implantitis developing later on.

Early treatment of inflammation: Should you notice early signs of gum inflammation, such as redness or bleeding, please don't hesitate to contact us straight away. Prompt treatment can prevent the inflammation from developing into peri-implantitis and spare you a more extensive procedure.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Conclusion

bloecke.text: If you keep a few things in mind, your dental implant can last a lifetime. Thorough oral hygiene, together with regular professional teeth cleaning and dental check-ups, form the basis for tooth replacement that stays in perfect condition long-term. This is because inflammation that is detected early can be treated easily and successfully, meaning it never progresses to bone loss in the first place.
Whether you had your tooth replacement done with us at Kurfürstendamm 64 in Berlin or at another practice, we're happy to help look after your dental implant!

zahnimplantate/zahnimplantat-kosten.titel: Dental Implant Costs: WHAT Does A Dental Implant Cost?

bloecke.text: A patient who needs a dental prosthesis will quite quickly start thinking about the costs of dental implants. One advantage implants have over other types of dental prosthesis is their long lifespan, though this does come at a price. The cost of implants depends on many factors, which we will describe in more detail below. For this reason, we cannot give a blanket statement here about the actual costs of individual dental implants, but we can give you some pointers as to how implant costs are made up and which factors influence the prices. The overall cost depends to a large extent on the scope of the treatment, the type of dental implant and the materials used.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental Implants: Costs AND HOW THEY Are Made Up

bloecke.text: Naturally, the cost of dental implants depends heavily on the difficulty and complexity of the implantation process for the prosthesis, and on whether bone augmentation, such as a sinus lift, is needed beforehand. However, the costs of implants, which may at first seem very high, should be seen in relation to the longevity and high success rate of an implant. When you consider that 90% of all implants are still completely intact even 10 years later, the price of a worry-free dental prosthesis quickly falls into perspective, especially since, unlike with a conventional bridge, no healthy teeth need to be sacrificed. Prices for dental implant treatment also cannot be stated as a blanket figure because the cost of an implant is made up of many different cost factors. Naturally, there are material costs for the dental implant itself, which depend on the implant material, as well as costs for surgical consumables, drills and, where necessary, bone substitute material. If, for example, bone augmentation is needed because the dental implant would otherwise not find sufficient support in the jawbone, this also increases the price. So, to be able to state the actual cost of a dental implant, the first step is a consultation with the dentist.

The cost of dental implants is therefore not just a question of materials. We should also not forget the costs for the implantologist who fits the artificial tooth. They are directly involved in every step of the treatment, from diagnostics and planning through to the actual implantation, the fitting of the prosthesis and any bone augmentation or sinus lift required. The costs may seem high at first. However, it should be borne in mind that quality should never be compromised when it comes to dental implants, in order to ensure long-term compatibility and durability. An experienced expert makes sure that nothing can easily go wrong with the implants and that the artificial tooth still holds firm even after many years.

Finally, the costs for the dental technology, or rather the dental laboratory, meaning the production of the prosthesis, as well as, for example, the production of a 3D drilling guide, also factor into the final cost of implants. Since our practice has its own fully equipped dental laboratory, you save on additional costs that would otherwise arise, for example, from having your implant sent off elsewhere. Here, of course, the question is what kind of prosthesis the patient wants. High-quality ceramic teeth look particularly natural, but are correspondingly more expensive than more affordable options. The rule here is: a good tooth should not only look natural, but should also be made from stable materials.
In short, the cost of implants depends on the following factors:
Whether bone augmentation (e.g. a sinus lift) and the corresponding bone substitute material are needed
The material of the dental implants (titanium, etc.)
The material of the prosthesis (ceramic for ceramic implants, etc.)
Surgical consumables for the implant treatment
The implantologist's fee for their services (diagnostics, implantation (fitting the implant), etc.)
Production of the implants in the dental laboratory

Another factor affecting the price is whether you need an implant to anchor a back tooth or a front tooth. Implants intended to carry a new front tooth are somewhat more expensive, as visual factors also need to be taken into account here. With, for example, an upper back molar, it is less of an issue if the transition from the silvery implant to the crown is slightly visible than it would be with a front incisor. If you have any questions about the cost of dental implants, we are happy to offer you comprehensive, no-obligation advice. You are also welcome to request a no-obligation quote from us.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental Implants: HOW MUCH OF THE Cost Is Covered BY Health Insurance?

bloecke.text: How much of the cost of dental implants you have to cover yourself depends on your own insurance status. With special supplementary dental insurance for implants, the cost of dental implants may be partially or even fully covered. Cover through statutory health insurance, on the other hand, does not provide for the full cost of dental implants to be covered. This does not mean, however, that members of statutory health insurance have to bear the entire cost of dental implants on their own. For those with statutory insurance, for example, there is a fixed subsidy for the prosthesis, depending on the condition of the jaw. However, it is not the implant itself that is subsidised, but rather the prosthesis later fitted onto the implant (crown, etc.). Here, too, the quality of the prosthesis you want makes a difference. High-quality ceramic implants, which look particularly natural, cost more accordingly.

In addition to advice from your treating implantologist and dentist, our administrative staff, who regularly update their knowledge on the latest developments in cost reimbursement by health insurers, will provide you with an individual quote for your treatment and cost plan for dental implants. We work closely with all major statutory health insurers and, if you have any questions about reimbursement, we are also happy to speak directly with your private or statutory health insurer on request. For privately insured patients, KU64 patients also receive, in cooperation with the service provider DOC PKV, a free insurance check, in which it is assessed even before treatment begins whether an optimisation of your insurance tariff is necessary and possible. The aim here is to secure full cost coverage from your private health insurer or a reduction in the amount you have to pay yourself for the prosthesis.

As an additional service, we also offer, in cooperation with the service provider BFS, convenient instalment payment plans (payment by instalments) for your personal contribution. The terms of this financing arrangement can be tailored individually to suit you.
More information here:
https://meinebfs.de/sie/patienten/neupatienten-zahnarztpraxis-ku64/

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental Implant Costs ABROAD: Saving AT THE Expense OF Quality?

bloecke.text: In order to save on the cost of implants, more and more patients are choosing to have an implant fitted abroad. Eastern European countries in particular are popular for dental implants, as providers there offer lower costs compared with Germany. However, patients should bear in mind that the quality of dental implants cannot be guaranteed to the same extent there as in Germany, and that the process therefore carries certain risks. Anyone who nevertheless wants to have an implant fitted into the jawbone abroad should find out beforehand about the quality of what is on offer. Is bone augmentation offered alongside the implant? Is this included in the cost? Is the material used of high quality? Who is the manufacturer of the dental implants? Do the dentists hold the same qualifications as dentists in Germany? How good is the medical care before and after the operation? All these questions should be clarified in advance, and online reviews can also be consulted to help assess whether implants from abroad can be fully trusted. A comparison (including a price comparison) with national implant providers is always worthwhile.

To be completely on the safe side when it comes to quality and service for implant patients, it is better to go straight to a specialist for dental implants who is certified to German standards for your dental treatment. These dentists and implantologists offer worry-free implant treatment, with implant costs becoming increasingly affordable. In particular, providers who handle the production of the dental implant and prosthesis, the fitting of the prosthesis into the jaw, and support throughout the subsequent healing phase all under one roof can offer patients comparatively good value alongside high quality. At KU64, you receive all these services under one roof at our practice in Berlin Charlottenburg. Implant production, fitting and aftercare can be offered as affordably as possible, so that the cost of dental implants does not dampen your enjoyment of your new teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Implants, Crowns, Prostheses – An Explanation Of Terms

bloecke.text: As a patient, it is not easy to tell the various forms of dental prosthesis apart. Terms are often used interchangeably, even though they refer to completely different procedures. They differ not only in terms of the type of prosthesis, but also in terms of cost. So that there is no more confusion between terms such as dental implants, prostheses, crowns and bridges, here is an explanation of the terms:

Prosthesis: prosthesis is the umbrella term for all forms of artificial teeth. This can include the familiar artificial denture, various types of crown, or indeed the more complex dental implant. The complexity and durability of a prosthesis varies, as do the costs patients face and the procedure used to fit it.

Dental implant: a dental implant, or simply an implant, is an artificial tooth (dental prosthesis) that is fitted into the jawbone. Implants are usually made of titanium (a non-magnetic metal that is well tolerated by the body) and serve as an artificial tooth root. Implants can be fitted in both the lower and upper jaw. There are various types of dental implant for every situation, each with a different cost.

Bone augmentation: depending on the implant system, bone augmentation may be necessary. This is the case when the implant cannot be sufficiently anchored in the jawbone. Using special material, the jaw is, so to speak, "built up" so that the dental implant has firm support. Bone augmentation adds extra cost to the implant treatment.

Crown: a crown, or implant crown, is the visible part of the implant, designed to mimic the natural tooth. Ceramic is usually used for this (ceramic implant), as it is particularly stable and long-lasting, and also looks very natural. The cost to the patient varies depending on the quality and appearance of the crown.

Fixed prosthesis: depending on the implant system, it is possible to fit either fixed or removable implants into the jaw. Fixed implants are used primarily for single-tooth implants. With these, the crown and artificial root are permanently joined together.

Removable prosthesis: removable dental implants are implants in which the ceramic crown is not permanently attached to the actual titanium implant. This is achieved, for example, through what is known as a telescopic denture. This is a common approach for full implants.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental Implant Costs: Your Personal Consultation AT KU64

bloecke.text: The cost of dental implants is often one of the first questions patients ask when considering an implant. Personal, tailored advice is of the utmost importance here. We are happy to take the time to draw up an individual cost plan with you and discuss all the important factors relating to implant treatment and dental implants in general. The KU64 practice also offers you the advantage that our in-house dental laboratory, along with the treating dentist and oral surgeon, can coordinate the overall planning of the implant procedure "under one roof". This saves you unnecessary trips from one doctor to another and lets you benefit from the close collaboration of our implantology specialists. This ensures that implant treatment is as cost-effective as possible, and that you need not worry about hefty transport or storage costs for the prosthesis or dental implant.

Would you like more information on the cost of dental implants, the implantation process itself, medical aftercare, or the possible fixed subsidy? Contact us by phone on +49308647320, send us an email, or arrange an appointment directly with our implantology specialists for your personal consultation. We will find the right solution for you. And should any problems arise, we are happy to help. You can also find further information on the cost and reimbursement of implants in our "Cost Information" section. Feel free to find out more there, with no obligation.

prophylaxe-4-0/prophylaxe-4-0.titel: Prophylaxis 4.0 in Berlin – the most modern professional teeth cleaning

bloecke.text: Healthy teeth are the foundation of a beautiful smile and an attractive appearance. For many people, regular dental care is as much a part of daily life as eating and sleeping. Yet brushing your teeth every day isn't always enough to maintain good oral health. With regular prophylaxis, including professional teeth cleaning (PZR), at KU64 Berlin, you actively prevent tooth decay and gum inflammation (periodontitis) and keep your teeth healthy for life – because prevention is the best protection!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Wellness for your teeth – the benefits of professional teeth cleaning in Berlin at KU64

bloecke.text: Our goal is your goal too: healthy teeth and a beautiful smile for life.

KU64 has 25 years of experience in the field of prophylaxis. In the summer of 2017, we were also one of the first practices in Germany to introduce the pioneering, innovative prophylaxis system 'Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT)'. This advanced prophylaxis treatment offers greater protection for the mouth.

With prophylaxis (professional teeth cleaning), you actively prevent tooth decay and gum inflammation (periodontitis) and can achieve this goal with ease – because prevention is the best protection! Our specialist team at our practice on Berlin's Kurfürstendamm draws on 25 years of experience. This experience benefits all our patients. The use of magnifying loupes is as standard for us as ongoing training, so our prophylaxis assistants and dental hygienists always work to the most up-to-date scientific standards.

Tooth decay and periodontitis (inflammation of the gums and the tissues supporting the teeth) are infectious diseases that can lead to tooth loss. According to scientific studies, these are not hereditary but the result of insufficient prevention. The germs need a certain type of nourishment and a certain amount of time to cause damage to teeth and gums. Through various tests, we can determine your individual risk of tooth decay and periodontitis and protect you through targeted measures.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Your benefits and advantages with KU64 prophylaxis:

bloecke.text: Professional teeth cleaning at KU64 is gentle, pleasant and thorough, and it doesn't hurt.
It protects against tooth decay and periodontal disease.
The prophylaxis team at KU64 Berlin works with GBT technology and the EMS staining method. Scraping with sharp instruments is no longer necessary.
Your dentist can carry out the subsequent examination of your teeth more precisely and quickly, as neither tartar nor plaque obstructs their view.
Professional teeth cleaning protects your dental restorations. Implants, fillings, crowns, inlays and veneers last significantly longer thanks to polishing.
Professional teeth cleaning very effectively eliminates bad breath, 90 per cent of which comes from bacteria in the oral cavity, leaving your mouth feeling fresh and clean.

Professional teeth cleaning reduces bacteria in the gum pockets and, according to scientific studies, thereby lowers the risk of heart attacks and strokes, premature births, diabetes, arthritis, rheumatism and gastrointestinal diseases.
Professional teeth cleaning removes the sticky base layer, plaque, from your teeth, making at-home oral hygiene easier too.
Teeth become brighter again through the thorough removal of all discolouration caused by food and drink such as nicotine, tea, red wine, beetroot and so on.
Professional teeth cleaning eliminates bleeding gums and prevents bacterial gum inflammation and periodontitis.
Thanks to deep fluoridation and enamel hardening, professional teeth cleaning effectively protects teeth from acids and makes tooth necks less sensitive.

It reduces tooth decay by an average of 80 to 90 per cent, thereby preventing fillings and tooth loss. This saves you from expensive dental restorations and lets you keep your own teeth well into old age!
Professional teeth cleaning not only gives you a radiant smile but also makes kissing more enjoyable!

Early detection of periodontitis is particularly important for dental implant wearers. To ensure our prophylaxis programme is as successful as possible for your implants, it makes sense to also check bone metabolism. This is negatively affected by possibly undetected diabetes and a low vitamin D level. We can now test for both.
We charge 64 euros for the Implant Safe test, 49 euros for the vitamin D test, and also 49 euros for the diabetes test.
If you are interested, please mention this at your next prophylaxis appointment.

bloecke.text: Even those who brush their teeth thoroughly twice a day don't always reach every spot with a toothbrush. The spaces between teeth in particular are a popular breeding ground for bacteria, which even dental floss or small brushes – so-called interdental brushes – cannot fully remove. This is precisely where professional teeth cleaning (PZR) comes in! This treatment by a dentist supports your daily dental care but cannot replace it.

remineralisation of early-stage defects

valuable tips for optimising your at-home oral hygiene – you'll receive the right tools to take home straight away

bloecke.text: From implantology to root canal treatment to prophylaxis: the most modern treatment methods and precision come first at KU64 Berlin. abschnitte.ueberschrift: For even more protection: Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT)

bloecke.text: In the summer of 2017, KU64 Berlin was also one of the first practices in Germany to introduce the pioneering, innovative prophylaxis system 'Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT)'. This advanced prophylaxis treatment offers greater protection for the mouth, for the best possible health. Here's how Guided Biofilm Therapy works at KU64 Berlin:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Making bacteria visible

bloecke.text: To make bacteria visible, the dentist stains the teeth and gums using a solution called 'total mouth disinfection'. This exposes the bacteria and plaque, allowing the highly effective Guided Biofilm Therapy to work to maximum effect. As a bonus, you can see which areas you have been brushing well and which you haven't, so you can improve your oral hygiene in future.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Cleaning gums and tongue

bloecke.text: As part of Guided Biofilm Therapy, the dentist cleans the gums and tongue using EMS's Erythritol Plus powder – a renowned quality brand in dentistry from Switzerland. During cleaning with the AirFlow method, the water is warmed for the first time to a temperature you can actually feel.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Removing tartar

bloecke.text: To clean gum pockets and remove tartar, the dentists at KU64 Berlin use the new Piezon No Pain ultrasound device from EMS with fine PS tips.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Arranging a follow-up appointment with your dentist

bloecke.text: After Guided Biofilm Therapy, you arrange a new recall appointment with your dentist so we can ensure a long-term improvement in your oral hygiene.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Detecting periodontitis faster with PerioSafe

bloecke.text: Tooth decay and periodontitis, the inflammation of the gums and the tissues supporting the teeth, are infectious diseases that can lead to tooth loss. According to scientific studies, these are not hereditary but the result of insufficient prevention. The germs need a certain type of nourishment and a certain amount of time to cause damage to a tooth or the gums. As part of prophylaxis, the dentists at KU64 Berlin carry out various tests to determine your individual risk of tooth decay and periodontitis and protect you through targeted measures. As one of the first dental practices in Berlin, KU64 offers the PerioSafe rapid test. This allows your dentist to detect undiscovered periodontal inflammation before tissue breakdown occurs in the structures supporting the teeth and possibly leads to tooth loss.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: We carry out a diabetes test for you on the spot

bloecke.text: As part of a prophylaxis session at our branch at Hausvogteiplatz 14, we are able to determine a particularly important health indicator for you!

HbA1c stands for haemoglobin A1c, a sugar-bound component of red blood pigment. A value above 6.5% indicates diabetes mellitus. The HbA1c value provides a long-term overview of blood sugar levels, making day-to-day measurements unnecessary. This value is particularly important for assessing the risk of future progression of periodontitis. You'll find out your HbA1c value within minutes – for a small fee and with just a small drop of blood. Please ask for our dental hygienist Peggy Bofinger-Hofmann.
