kinderzahnarzt/erster-besuch-bei-ku64.titel: Before Your Child's First Visit to the KU64 Children's Dentist

bloecke.text: Dear Parents,

It is our heartfelt wish that your child comes to us with a smile and leaves our practice with a smile too. That's why we've put together a little guide with tips to help you prepare your child for their first visit to the dentist:
1. Please try, right from the start, to announce the dental visit in a cheerful mood:
a. "Yes, today you get to go to the dentist!" puts your child in a positive mood,
b. "Oh dear, today we have to go to the dentist with you!" makes your child expect something negative right from the start, as feelings of fear are passed on from parents to children.

2. Only share your own positive experiences of the dentist. If you don't have any, it's better not to say anything. Make it clear to your child that they shouldn't take other people's negative stories too seriously, and talk these stories through at home.

3. Avoid negatively charged words such as fear, pain, hurting, drilling, injection and similar terms — including negations of these. In sentences like "You really don't need to be afraid, it won't hurt at all", the subconscious only registers "afraid" and "hurt", which is exactly what puts the idea into your child's head that something bad might happen at the dentist! Likewise, statements like "You have to be very brave and courageous!" trigger negative expectations.

4. False promises lead to mistrust: "You won't even notice it" or "It'll be over in no time" are things we unfortunately can't always guarantee. Your child will "notice" even the gentlest, most pain-free treatment, and a thorough examination or careful therapy sometimes does take a little longer than "in no time". Young children also don't yet have a real sense of time. This means we children's dentists can only end up disappointing — and losing their trust!

5. Promising rewards afterwards leads your child to believe that something terrible is about to happen, since big rewards are usually associated with bad experiences. And the feeling of having to earn something in advance increases the pressure beforehand. Statements like "Mummy will hold your hand" also lead your child to expect that they will need comforting.

6. It helps to say things like "Today your dentist is going to count your teeth and check that they're all healthy." As no treatment takes place during the first visit with us, we prepare your child for everything that follows. If, unfortunately, pain is the reason for the first dental visit, it's best to say: "Today your dentist is going to help you feel better afterwards."

7. Children's books on the topic of "a visit to the dentist" are also a great way to prepare. They help illustrate the upcoming event for your child. You can also act out the dental situation at home with cuddly toys and other favourites, and practise it that way.
8. If your child is no longer very small, encourage them to go into the treatment room on their own. Experience has shown that this often works out better.
9. Let your child answer our questions themselves, as your child should be at the centre of the whole experience and should feel that too.
10. Praise your child after the treatment. This builds self-confidence and encourages them to try new things.
That's how the first dental visit becomes a real success!
Please bear in mind that at our KU64 Youngstars Club, quite a few things are different to what you might remember from your own childhood. Child-friendly, pain-free treatment is our top priority!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Documents You Should Have Ready for Your First Visit

bloecke.text: We want everything to run smoothly at your first appointment. So that we can advise you fully, we need a few documents from you when you check in. Please bring the following along to your initial examination:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Your Insurance Card

bloecke.text: Your health or insurance card proves your membership of a statutory health insurance scheme. All your personal details are stored on the chip. If you have private insurance, please bring your identity card instead.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Registration and Risk Assessment Questionnaire

bloecke.text: Before your first dental examination, we ask you to fill in a registration form. Through this registration and medical history form, we collect your contact details as well as information about your general state of health. This includes illnesses, allergies and any medication you take that could affect dental treatment. This information allows us to identify risk factors early on and prevent complications. You'll receive the registration form from our dental assistants at reception during your first visit.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bonus Booklet

bloecke.text: Your bonus booklet gives us an overview of the preventive dental check-ups you've had so far. You'll receive another stamp in your bonus booklet after your initial examination with us. To keep the booklet complete without any gaps, you need to attend at least one preventive check-up per year — children even need two per year. If you haven't missed a preventive appointment within five to ten years, your health insurer will give you a bonus contribution towards dentures or other tooth replacement. We take this information into account when drawing up your individual cost and treatment plan.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Examination Records

bloecke.text: Have any X-rays or 3D images, so-called CBCT scans, been taken of your teeth within the last few years? Please ask your dentist to make these available to you if possible. Our dentists can take these images into account when assessing your dental health, meaning additional X-rays may not be needed. Please also bring your X-ray record card to the check-up, if you have one.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treatment and Cost Plans

bloecke.text: Has another dentist already drawn up a treatment and cost plan for your care? We recommend bringing this along to your first dental examination. It contains details of your dental status, the proposed care, the planned therapy and the expected costs, and our dentists can use it as a guide for any further treatment plans.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Medication Record and Cardiac Device ID

bloecke.text: Please let us know if you are currently taking, or regularly take, any medication. A look at your medication record or the patient information leaflet for your medicines helps us to anticipate and assess any unwanted interactions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Implant Card

bloecke.text: Do you already have dentures, prostheses or other implants, such as a pacemaker? Please let us know, and bring your device ID card, if you have one, to your initial examination at our practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Allergy Card

bloecke.text: Do you have allergies and have you been given an allergy card by your doctor? A properly functioning immune system is an important factor, particularly with dentures and tooth replacements. Your allergy card allows us to rule out, or take into account, any potential contact allergies to denture materials during our treatments.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Referral

bloecke.text: If you've received a referral from your dentist to one of our specialists, please also bring this along to your initial examination. This means your regular dentist will subsequently be informed of the findings from our examination.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Toothbrush

bloecke.text: If you haven't had time to brush your teeth beforehand, you can simply do so at our practice before your appointment. Toothbrushes and toothpaste are available for you to use. However, if you use a special toothpaste, please remember to bring it along. Please also allow a few extra minutes for brushing your teeth at our practice.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Happens During the Initial Examination?

bloecke.text: During your first visit to our dental practice, no specific treatment generally takes place unless you have particular complaints. During the initial examination, our dentists first take a look at the state of your dental health. They check:
your teeth for plaque, tartar and decay, as well as for cracks, damaged fillings and reduced vitality
your gums for signs of periodontitis
the condition of any existing dentures or tooth replacements
the position of individual teeth and your tongue
your jaw joint and chewing muscles for imbalances and misalignment
your oral mucosa, lips and lymph nodes, as well as
your throat, face, head and neck for swelling, redness and tissue changes as possible signs of cancer
In individual cases, we take photographs to document the state of your teeth and dentition. To better detect gaps and holes between your teeth, additional X-rays may also be required.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Individual Advice on All Dental Services

bloecke.text: Should further appointments be needed as a result of the initial examination, we'll inform you of your treatment options in a personal consultation. You're welcome to ask questions at any time. In consultation with our colleagues from the fields of implantology, periodontology, oral surgery, orthodontics and aesthetic dentistry, we then draw up a treatment plan covering all the further steps involved. This means we can always tell you exactly what's been achieved so far and roughly how much longer the treatment is likely to take.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Full Service Under One Roof

bloecke.text: This guarantees you short waiting times and high quality: we make your dentures and tooth replacements in our own in-house, high-tech dental laboratory. We work with all common materials, including CEREC, titanium, gold, acrylic and ceramic. On request, our dental technicians will even come right to your treatment chair to restore your radiant smile permanently, by hand.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prevention for a Lifelong Smile

bloecke.text: Even if no further treatment is needed, we recommend that our patients arrange regular check-ups with their dentist following their initial examination. This allows us to spot and treat general health conditions early, before they get worse. Poor diet, eating disorders, inadequate oral hygiene, stress or an incorrect jaw alignment can also affect your health in the long run. During your first examination, we give you specific information and tips for healthy teeth, and tell you all about prevention and professional teeth cleaning. All of this helps not only to prevent complex procedures, but also to reduce your treatment costs in the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Nervous Patients Are in Safe Hands With Us

bloecke.text: Just the thought of the dentist is enough to fill many people with dread. That's why we take particular time and care with our nervous patients. We're delighted that you've found the courage to get in touch with our practice. Patients with dental anxiety get an appointment at KU64 at very short notice and don't have to wait long. The first appointment is purely for getting to know each other. We're happy to answer your questions in full, giving you our undivided attention.

We also hold your hand throughout the treatment itself. Unpleasant smells and sounds can quickly raise stress levels even before treatment begins. We know this. We counter it with special relaxation techniques, autogenic training or acupuncture. To block out disruptive noises from the dental instruments, we offer you music or audiobooks. For longer treatments, you can watch a film using video glasses. We also break the treatment itself down into small steps, allowing for plenty of pauses in which we can explain the next step.

We promise you: pain during a visit to the dentist is a thing of the past at KU64 Berlin. Our practice has many years of experience with sedative and calming agents. On request, we can also carry out your treatment under general anaesthetic.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What Does an Initial Examination at KU64 Berlin Cost?

bloecke.text: For patients with statutory health insurance, the cost of the initial examination is covered by their health insurer. Private patients cover the cost of the check-up themselves.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Long Are the Waiting Times at KU64 Berlin?

bloecke.text: If you've booked an appointment for an initial examination at our dental practice, you'll hardly have to wait at all. If you have acute tooth pain, you can also visit our practice without an appointment. In this case, please contact us in advance. This allows us to plan your pain treatment better and reduce your waiting time.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How Long Does the Initial Examination at KU64 Berlin Take?

bloecke.text: Depending on what's needed, the initial examination usually takes between 30 minutes and an hour.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Children's Dentist Ahoy – Waiting Room Goodbye!

bloecke.text: The world of KU64 Berlin, home of holistic dentistry for children and young people, offers plenty of room for play, fun and a relaxed appointment with the children's dentist. Little ones can stay amongst themselves with us, as we have created a whole, very futuristic and playful floor especially for them, with great attention to detail.

The dentists at KU64 Berlin, who are attuned to children's needs, welcome young and old alike on the fourth floor in a colourful children's play paradise complete with a children's cinema, Playstation and X-Box, a cavity cave, an oversized game of Jenga, an aquarium and formicarium, wonderful books, a painting station and much more. That way, visiting the dentist is fun right from the very first appointment!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: THE First Visit TO THE Children's Dentist

bloecke.text: The first visit to the children's dentist ideally takes place when the first tooth breaks through. Children's teeth and the permanent teeth of young people need particularly sensitive treatment. We treat toddlers, children and young people up to the age of 18, as well as expectant mothers. Children are born with a healthy mouth, and together with parents, we want to keep it that way.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW DOES THE Children's Dentist Approach Treatment?

bloecke.text: Our team of children's dentists don't just advise you from a dental point of view – our young patients also experience us as committed and caring confidants. After the initial consultation at our dental practice, which among other things serves to get to know one another, and a thorough examination, an individual treatment and prevention plan is drawn up. When examining tooth structure, tooth position, gums, oral mucosa and the development of the bite, our dentists always keep in mind that this mouth belongs to a young personality. Our dentists also pay attention to tooth position at every examination. Working together with our orthodontic specialists, they ensure that a crooked tooth is guided back into a straight, harmonious position within the bite. Naturally, our dentists explain their approach in detail at every stage of treatment and are always happy to answer any questions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT'S THE Secret Of Our Practice?

bloecke.text: At Berlin's largest children's dental practice, your children are taught the correct tooth-brushing technique in an impressive and child-friendly way – so that tooth decay never gets a chance to develop in the first place. We take anxious patients gently by the hand and actively work against feelings of anxiety in the treatment room: our treating dentists delight our young stars with music, stories, talking hand puppets and little bits of magic. Anyone who wishes may watch a film during treatment.

A tasty numbing gel, laughing gas, calming syrup and child hypnosis are further ways of making your child's visit to the dentist as pleasant and pain-free as possible, whilst at the same time avoiding a general anaesthetic or sedation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A Magical Treatment JUST FOR Kids

bloecke.text: Another special feature of our children's dentists: the entire dental practice team has been trained in Therapeutic Magic, a combination of magic and hypnotherapy, by expert Annalisa Neumeyer. Our children's dentists and their assistants have mastered a great many wonderful magic tricks, allowing children and families to enjoy relaxed, anxiety-free treatment and an entertaining stay at KU64 Berlin!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: OUR Pedagogical Approach

bloecke.text: We also make no secret of our twenty years of dental experience and our team of specialists in the fields of prevention and orthodontics.
Quite the opposite: with us, even the very youngest learn how to look after their teeth in the best possible way and receive practical tips for their daily tooth-brushing routine at home.

Unlike adults, young children first have to get used to the dentist. The dentists at our children's dental practice therefore know exactly how to handle them in order to build trust, and they take plenty of time over treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Welcome TO THE KU64 Young Stars Doctor School Berlin

bloecke.text: At the KU64 Young Stars Doctor School, children's awareness of dental health is nurtured. At our children's dental practice, children learn not only how to brush their teeth, but also how to "ride lying down", experience "sun and wind", get to "show their teeth", feel "tooth shine" and have fun with the "mouth washing machine". Afterwards, there are fun little stamps on their very own certificate – and the dental treatment for children can begin.
Through this pedagogical approach, the dentist conveys to the child, early on and firmly, just how important the health of their teeth and a proper diet are.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Our Services Especially FOR Kids

bloecke.text: Standard isn't good enough for us. At KU64 Berlin, we offer our patients treatments that go far beyond the standard services provided by statutory health insurers:
individual, pain-free tooth decay risk check based on the latest dental findings, saliva test, etc.
regular professional teeth cleaning, which also cares for the areas that even the best toothbrush can't reach, including polishing
removal of discolouration and pigment deposits
fissure sealing, including for premolars and milk teeth
temporary fissure sealing
frequently repeated enamel hardening through targeted deep fluoridation
special treatments for anxious patients
special treatments against bad breath
toothbrush check – recommendation of the right toothbrush for the relevant age
text message reminder one day before every appointment
free tooth-brushing products and sugar-free sweets
KU64 tooth certificate with the prevention fairy seal for children
gentle, child-friendly diagnostic procedures

bloecke.text: The design of the dental practice comes from the renowned GRAFT architects: the floor on the fourth level for our young patients blends seamlessly into the overall design of the KU64 Berlin dental practice. Since opening in January 2010, we have offered young patients a very special kind of visit to the dentist.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A Dental Visit FOR THE Whole Family Thanks To Extensive Opening Hours

bloecke.text: The first appointment at the dentist can bring plenty of excitement for children and parents alike. That's why at KU64 Berlin, we offer an appointment for the whole family. At these family appointments, children and adults are treated at the same time or one after the other. This not only helps the little ones feel more relaxed, but is also practical and saves time.

We know that family life often means juggling lots of appointments. That's why our children's dental practice offers treatment seven days a week. Book an appointment now during our opening hours: Monday to Friday from 8am to 8pm, Saturday from 9am to 7pm, and Sunday from 10am to 6pm.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQ

bloecke.text: Parents can play a significant role in making the first visit to the dentist a positive experience, so that children even look forward to their next visit. If you stay calm before the first examination, this often transfers automatically to your child. This applies to fears and worries too, by the way. Your child will intuitively sense whether you yourself are afraid of the dentist. Instead, try to spark curiosity and enthusiasm for the dental examination, and avoid promises that "it won't hurt". A reward after the visit to the dentist usually isn't necessary either.

Tooth care generally begins with the very first milk tooth. Parents should clean their child's milk teeth regularly in the evening with a cloth or cotton bud. By the age of two at the latest, the cotton bud can be swapped for a toothbrush. Dentists recommend brushing milk teeth twice a day with a fluoride children's toothpaste. Parents should brush thoroughly before or after their child, to make sure every area of the mouth has been reached. Once the permanent teeth come through, children should ideally use a toothpaste with a higher fluoride content. We're happy to give you tips on the correct brushing technique and a balanced diet that supports oral health at your next check-up appointment.

Regular prevention and professional teeth cleaning for children is worthwhile from as early as the third year of life. Combined with regular check-ups, prevention helps with the early detection of tooth decay and gum diseases such as periodontitis.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prophylaxis 4.0 – gentler, more pleasant and more effective!

bloecke.text: KU64 is one of the first practices in Germany to introduce the pioneering and innovative prophylaxis system 'Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT)'. This advanced prophylaxis treatment offers greater protection in the mouth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What's it all about?

bloecke.text: For you as a patient, the new KU64 prophylaxis becomes gentler, more pleasant and more effective. Until now, professional cleaning involved a lot of scraping and polishing to smooth the roughened surface again as best as possible. Both the airscaler ultrasound and the hand instruments leave anything but a smooth tooth surface, and quite a bit of substance is worn away in the process. With our new professional cleaning, the aim is no longer to scrape away as much as possible, but rather to clean and disinfect as gently as possible — also known as biofilm management. That's why, from now on, a new powder is being used for the AirFlow. This powder is a 4-valent sugar alcohol called erythritol. It's related to xylitol, but better. Better, because in addition to its mechanical cleaning action, it also has a chemical effect on the germs that weren't removed, for example in the root cementum. It inhibits the metabolism of these germs and thereby renders them largely harmless. With this wonderful technique, we remove the entire disease-causing biofilm from the mouth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: This has a fundamental effect on how the new prophylaxis works:

bloecke.text: Teeth and gums are stained using an agent called 'total mouth disinfection'. This is done so that our highly effective therapy can be applied with maximum precision. Very much in keeping with the motto: 'the enemy — that is, bacteria and plaque — is first exposed and made visible.' A nice side effect: we show you where you've brushed well and where you haven't, so you can improve your oral hygiene.

Gum and tongue cleaning with Erythritol Plus powder from EMS (a renowned quality brand in dentistry, from Switzerland). For the first time, the water in this AirFlow device is warmed to a temperature you can actually feel.
Further cleaning of the pockets and removal of tartar using the new Piezon No Pain ultrasound device from EMS with fine PS tips.
Together, we arrange a new recall appointment so we can ensure a long-term improvement in your oral hygiene.

By the way: as one of the first dental practices in Berlin, KU64 offers the rapid PerioSafe test, allowing us to detect undiscovered periodontal inflammation before it leads to tissue breakdown in the supporting structures of the teeth and possibly tooth loss.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: KU64 prophylaxis – what are the benefits?

bloecke.text: * it is gentle, pleasant, thorough and doesn't hurt * protects against tooth decay and periodontal disease * with EMS's GBT technology and staining method, work is carried out with precision, without unnecessary scraping using sharp instruments * the dentist can carry out the check-up more precisely and quickly, as no tartar or plaque obstructs the view * restorations (fillings, crowns, inlays and veneers too) last longer

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does Dr Stephan Ziegler, KU64 owner and dentist, say about the introduction of the new prophylaxis system?
An effective weapon deployed against dangerous bacteria

bloecke.text: Over the course of a lifetime, people of all ages repeatedly complain of toothache or bleeding gums. 'Patients often ignore these early warning signs, with fatal consequences,' says Dr Stephan Ziegler, senior dentist and founder of the KU64 dental practice in Berlin. He warns: 'From the age of 35 onwards, the risk of developing periodontitis — that is, inflammation of the tissue supporting the teeth — also increases, which in the worst case ends in tooth loss and damages organs.' However, a new type of prophylaxis system, so-called Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT), offers effective protection in the fight against harmful germs.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The gum margin as a weak point

bloecke.text: Usually caused by inadequate hygiene, microorganisms in the mouth multiply extremely quickly. Hidden in hard-to-reach spaces between the teeth, on the tongue, or under loose-fitting dentures, they lie in wait for food, which they then break down. In this process, also known as metabolic activity, these tiny organisms excrete acids that quite literally attack the hard substance of the teeth. The gum margin reacts particularly sensitively to the resulting layer of bacteria, also known as plaque, with inflammation. Patients often don't notice this gradual and largely painless process, which is accompanied by typical symptoms such as bleeding gums. 'These are perfect conditions for inflammatory pathogens, which penetrate the organism through the weakened tissue and can even increase the risk of heart attack and stroke,' explains Dr Ziegler.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Stifling germs before they take hold

bloecke.text: When doctors identify a bacterial infection, they fall back on conventional methods such as professional teeth cleaning with sharp polishing pastes, ultrasound, or, in more serious cases, even curettage — the surface removal of germs using a sharp scraping instrument. 'With conventional polishing, many problem areas are not reached, and the gingiva, that is, the gums, are unnecessarily injured. This kind of traditional cleaning is often very unpleasant for patients, sometimes even painful, meaning follow-up appointments are missed,' says Dr Ziegler. In cases of advanced periodontitis with deep gum pockets, the dentist scrapes the microorganisms out of the pockets using a fine instrument. However, this also results in the removal of important root cementum. This outer layer of tissue between the tooth and gum serves an important protective function. Without it, bacteria penetrate more quickly. 'What's more, both approaches, as well as cleaning with conventional ultrasound devices, leave a rough surface behind. Dangerous pathogens find ideal hiding places here and continue to multiply,' emphasises the KU64 expert.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Prophylaxis isn't just prophylaxis

bloecke.text: To stop uncontrolled bacterial growth, experts turn to an advanced version of the well-known powder jet technique, also called Air-Flow. Dr Ziegler of KU64 in Berlin is one of the first to use it in Germany and explains the new principle: 'In the first step, the biofilm — that is, the layer of bacteria — in the mouth is made visible using a colouring solution. The novel powder-water-air mixture made of erythritol then removes existing pathogens. Unlike its predecessor xylitol, this sugar substitute has improved properties. On the one hand, it increases the mechanical cleaning effect, which is tailored to the individual mouth situation using a finer or coarser spray. On the other hand, it disinfects and inhibits the metabolism of remaining bacterial strains in the root cementum. This perfect combination polishes the tooth surface eight times more effectively, thereby shortening the treatment time to just 45 minutes. Even the skin of a tomato remains undamaged by this gentle procedure. A further benefit: patients now find the tempered water jet, at 40 degrees, pleasant.' Regular check-ups using the new GBT maintain dental health and prevent disease.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Minimising the risk of periodontitis

bloecke.text: Early detection of periodontitis is particularly important for those with dental implants. For our prophylaxis programme to be as successful as possible for your implants, it makes sense to also check bone metabolism. This is negatively affected by undetected diabetes and too low a vitamin D level. We can now test for both.
We charge 64 euros for the Implant Safe test, 49 euros for the vitamin D test, and 49 euros for the diabetes test as well.

wurzelkanalbehandlung/endodontie-fuer-ue.titel: Information for Patients Referred for Endodontic Treatment by the Specialists at KU64

bloecke.text: Your own dentist has entrusted us with saving your tooth – thank you for this vote of confidence! It's a good choice, as our referral practice has more than 20 years' experience in modern endodontics (root canal treatment). Before your upcoming appointment, we'd like to give you some helpful information.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WE SAVE YOUR TOOTH AND FREE YOU FROM PAIN

bloecke.text: At our practice, we offer professional, high-quality root canal treatment with three particularly well-qualified colleagues:
Dr Sabine Gousetis, DGET-certified specialist in endodontics
Dr Frank Schreiber, specialised in endodontics as a focus of his work

Their many years of experience and ongoing training in endodontics guarantee the best possible treatment for your teeth and provide gentle care in a pleasant atmosphere. It goes without saying that we carry out all treatments according to the latest knowledge and using the most modern technology, to achieve long-term success. That's why our endodontists have been examined and certified by the DGET, the German Society for Endodontics and Dental Traumatology. This postgraduate training requires a high level of commitment and skill – and as a patient, you benefit from this, with us even threefold, for the good of your teeth!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHY ARE YOU IN GOOD HANDS WITH US?

bloecke.text: Our dentists don't just have years of experience (they have already carried out countless root canal treatments, freeing patients from their pain) and comprehensive training in endodontics. They also use strongly magnifying loupes with integrated LED light and a high-tech surgical microscope for root canal treatment. This guarantees precise, safe treatment without unpleasant after-effects. What's more, at KU64 you get fast, flexible appointments – even at weekends.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT IS THE PROCESS FOR ENDODONTIC TREATMENT?

bloecke.text: According to current knowledge, no compromises should be made when it comes to root canal treatment. If the treatment isn't carried out absolutely thoroughly, this inevitably worsens the prognosis for the affected tooth. So what does a good root canal treatment actually involve?

With these professional measures used in modern root canal treatment, we achieve the greatest possible freedom from bacteria within the root canal system, giving the best prospects for long-term success:
Creating a sterile working field with rubber dam protection, using sterile, single-use rotary instruments made from highly flexible nickel–titanium
Instrumentation using a computer-controlled step motor that measures and optimally adjusts torque 300 times per second
Ultrasonically activated cleaning of the root canal to clear side canals
Use of additional medical, disinfecting rinsing solutions to loosen and flush out organic residue in the root canal
Additional electronic measurement of root canal lengths, to prevent under- or over-filling of the canals

Root filling: once the root canals have been cleaned, elaborate filling techniques are used, such as lateral condensation or thermal filling with gutta-percha, a natural material obtained from the sap of the gutta tree

abschnitte.ueberschrift: HOW LONG DOES ROOT CANAL TREATMENT TAKE?

bloecke.text: Modern treatment today is far more comfortable and gentle than in the past. Even so, root canal treatment usually takes place over several sessions, each lasting a good hour or longer.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT ARE THE CHANCES OF SUCCESS WITH ROOT CANAL TREATMENT?

bloecke.text: By using all the means available to us in modern root canal treatment, there is a very good chance that the affected tooth can be kept healthy and free of infection in the long term. In rare cases, a root canal may be S-shaped, branch off, or otherwise make mechanical preparation impossible. Unfortunately, such cases cannot be entirely ruled out before treatment is carried out.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT HAPPENS AFTER ROOT CANAL TREATMENT?

bloecke.text: Once treatment is complete, your dentist receives a detailed treatment report, and further care of the tooth can continue with them as usual. As part of our regular follow-up checks (recall), our endodontists check that the treatment has been successful and also inform your dentist accordingly.

The tooth is already considerably weakened by the root canal treatment itself and becomes somewhat more brittle, which is accompanied by a more or less pronounced grey discolouration. For this reason, these teeth should always be fitted with a crown or partial crown, which offers the best protection both against the tooth breaking apart and against reinfection with bacteria.

Please bear in mind: a tooth that has been optimally root-treated by our specialists and subsequently fitted with a ceramic restoration by your own dentist can go on to do its full job in your mouth for a lifetime, without becoming a source of trouble. Further surgical measures, such as an apicoectomy, are also highly unlikely to be necessary.
You'll find further information about our root canal treatment here!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHEN IS AN APICOECTOMY NECESSARY?

bloecke.text: Why have a tooth extracted if you have inflammation at the root tip? WE CAN SAVE YOUR TOOTH!
With a microscope-assisted apicoectomy, many teeth can be saved when a revision (repeat) of the root filling isn't possible.
When are you in the right place with Dr Marlies Herrera?
If you have a referral from your dentist for an apicoectomy!
If you're due to have a tooth extracted because of inflammation or a cyst at the root tip, and a repeat root canal treatment isn't possible!
If an instrument has broken off inside a root canal and can't be removed!
If an X-ray has revealed a foreign body in the jawbone at a root tip!
If any of these apply to you, we'd be happy to give you detailed advice on the most up-to-date and modern ways of preserving your tooth long-term through a minimally invasive oral surgery procedure.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: BOOK YOUR APPOINTMENT NOW!

bloecke.text: Do you have questions about root canal treatment, or would you like more information about endodontic treatment and to speak to a dentist? Get in touch now and contact our dental specialists at KU64. We offer you the chance to have an individual consultation, in which you'll learn more about modern methods in endodontics. Our endodontists (root canal specialists) will explain the possible costs and treatment steps to you, and take away any worries you may have.

cmd-behandlung/craniomandibulaere-dysfun.titel: Craniomandibular Dysfunction and Functional Diagnostics – CMD Treatment Berlin

bloecke.text: Functional pre-treatment for jaw joint complaints, CMD symptoms or before dental restorations (tooth replacement).

Functional diagnostics serves to examine and assess the chewing system. This involves examining how the teeth and jaws interact with each other, with the musculature, with the skull and with the whole body. This examination is usually carried out using manual techniques and can be usefully supported by imaging procedures (OPTG) or special technical analysis methods.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is Craniomandibular Dysfunction (CMD)?

bloecke.text: CMD refers to a disrupted interaction between the teeth of the upper and lower jaw and the resulting faulty bite position. As the jaw joints cannot work optimally in this condition, the surrounding musculature is subjected to unnaturally high strain, which can lead to a wide range of health problems.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Serious health impairments caused by CMD

bloecke.text: There are many different causes of craniomandibular dysfunction. Biological, psychological and social factors can all play a role. Common causes include genetics, hormones, developmental disorders of the jaw joint, postural problems or emotional stress.

Pain in the teeth and jaw joints, in the face, and in the head and neck area can often be traced back to CMD. But tension and pain in other parts of the musculoskeletal system, and even tinnitus, frequently have their origin in CMD as well.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Treating CMD Through Functional Diagnostics and Therapy

bloecke.text: Early treatment is important, as the malfunction of the bite and the strain on the jaw joint continue to progress, considerably worsening the prospects of a cure over time. Comprehensive diagnosis of the complaints mentioned above requires cross-disciplinary collaboration between doctors and specialists from a wide range of fields. At KU64, we work on the basis of a holistic concept together with dentists (functional diagnostics), dental technicians, orthodontists, radiologists, orthopaedists, ENT specialists, alternative practitioners, osteopaths and physiotherapists. In this way, our practice offers optimal conditions for our patients. This also means that the analysis and subsequent manual therapy of complex jaw joint problems, and the associated complaints and pain, are no problem for us.

For this reason, we work together with a number of external specialists on your behalf! We do not reduce our patients to their oral cavity; our focus is on the whole person as a system. For us, interdisciplinary (dental) medicine also means that everyone involved is well informed at all times. CMD can only be treated successfully in the long term if specialised doctors and therapists develop a suitable treatment concept on the basis of joint diagnostics.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Therapy With The Dros® Splint

bloecke.text: DROS® splint therapy is the first concept in CMD treatment that can fully take the results of diagnosis into account through standardised working steps. The splint is made individually and to a high standard by our own in-house certified dental laboratory, SMILE DESIGN. Unlike other splints (thermoformed splints, night guards), the DROS® splint is not a protective splint, as its use serves a clearly defined therapeutic goal. Protective splints, on the other hand, are often bitten through after a very short time and do not contribute to solving the actual problem.

The standardised procedure of DROS® therapy provides orientation throughout the entire course of treatment and, in most cases, makes it possible to limit the treatment period to seven to ten weeks. The focus of treatment by the certified DROS® therapist (a specialist in functional diagnostics and therapy) is the assessment and optimisation of the occlusion of the teeth. For this, the DROS® splint, fitted as an upper jaw bite splint, is used:

It eliminates the problematic premature contacts between the upper and lower teeth, which can cause a wide range of CMD symptoms, and, through its biomechanical principle, enables the individually optimal physiological position of the lower jaw. This creates a stable starting point for subsequent orthodontic and/or prosthetic treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Definition And Mode Of Action Of The Dros® Splint

bloecke.text: DROS® stands for Diagnostic Relaxing Orientating Stabilising bite splint: The diagnostic phase at the beginning of treatment is followed first by a relaxation phase, which primarily aims to relax the myogenic structures of the masticatory organ. The subsequent orientation phase then enables the reorientation of the mandible (lower jaw). The final stabilisation phase then achieves the actual goal of the therapy: a stable condylar position (SCP).

Here we would like to inform you about the various types of fixed braces and about the course of orthodontic treatment at the KU64 dental practice. A multibracket appliance (MB) – the fixed brace – consists of brackets and bands, which the orthodontist bonds onto the teeth that need to be moved. All the teeth are then connected with an archwire. Thanks to its elastic tendency to spring back into shape, the archwire exerts a force on the teeth concerned and pulls the tooth into the correct position.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The brackets of a brace

bloecke.text: The materials used by the orthodontist when fitting fixed braces with brackets range from unprogrammed stainless steel brackets to almost invisible ceramic brackets. Brackets can also be bonded to the inside of the teeth, so that the fixed brace cannot be seen at all. In this way, in some cases the orthodontist has the option of fitting an almost invisible brace using conventional means. However, if it is important to you to wear a truly invisible brace, you should find out about the “Invisalign” brace, which our practice also offers.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Brace with stainless steel brackets

bloecke.text: With unprogrammed stainless steel brackets (also known as metal brackets), the archwire is held in place with a rubber ring or fine wires (ligatures). These brackets are quite large, and the areas between the rubber rings or ligatures are harder to clean.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Braces with mini brackets

bloecke.text: Mini brackets require less bonding surface on the tooth, are therefore less noticeable and do not create as strong a feeling of a foreign body in the mouth as is the case with conventional braces.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Brace with SL brackets

bloecke.text: Self-ligating brackets (SL brackets, Damon Q) are fitted with a small clip closure that holds the archwire in the bracket slot. The wire is therefore not held in place with rubber rings or wires. The advantage of braces with self-ligating brackets is that the archwire can slide freely within the bracket slot. The archwire of the brace does not have to overcome any frictional resistance. This makes the transfer of forces more efficient and shortens the length of orthodontic treatment. Self-ligating brackets are made from both metal and ceramic.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Braces with ceramic brackets

bloecke.text: Ceramic brackets (Damon Clear) are tooth-coloured and less noticeable. The material is more brittle and harder. For this reason, patients' teeth can wear down if they bite onto a ceramic bracket. In some cases, ceramic brackets have to be laboriously ground off the tooth when the brace is removed.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The wires of a brace

bloecke.text: A distinction is made between steel wires and superelastic or thermoelastic wires.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Steel wires vs. superelastic wires in a brace

bloecke.text: Steel wires can be bent well, but they tire quickly and then no longer exert as much force on the teeth. For this reason, superelastic wires were developed in orthodontics. Superelastic wires cannot be bent out of shape but have great springiness. With these braces, the force acting on the tooth over a long period is very gentle, yet constant. This is easy on the tissue and makes the necessary bone remodelling easier. The risk of side effects such as root damage is reduced. At the same time, the length of treatment can be drastically shortened.

The forces that a modern superelastic wire exerts on the periodontium fall within a range that modern orthodontics considers gentle on the teeth. As a result, many of the drawbacks of the fixed braces of earlier times are no longer found today. When the most modern materials are used and current medical standards are observed, the MB appliance harms neither the teeth nor the periodontium. The use of the most up-to-date techniques and materials has been standard practice in our practice since it was founded. However, proper oral hygiene at home remains, and will always remain, essential.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Advice on fixed braces

bloecke.text: Whichever of the many brace options offered at our practice you decide on, in consultation with the orthodontist, you will be making a good choice. After all, healthy teeth and a friendly smile considerably improve quality of life.

Do you have any questions? Get in touch with us. Our team of qualified orthodontists will be happy to answer all your questions and provide further information on orthodontics and all types of braces (fixed braces, invisible aligners from Invisalign and Spark or WIN)!

Whether a bridge or an implant is generally the better option cannot be answered in general terms. Both types of dental replacement have their advantages and disadvantages, and depending on several factors, each can achieve better results for certain patients.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bridge Instead Of Implant – Bridges AS "gap fillers"

bloecke.text: If one or more teeth are missing, they should be replaced not only for aesthetic reasons, but also to prevent misaligned teeth, gum disease and problems with the jaw joint.

Unlike an implant, a bridge has long been considered the most common treatment for a gap in the teeth. However, this also has the disadvantage that, to fit a bridge, the healthy neighbouring teeth have to be ground down, since — unlike with a dental implant — the adjacent teeth are used as anchors. This is why bridges have become increasingly unpopular in recent years, as patients have to sacrifice healthy tooth substance for a secure fit. A bridge therefore makes the most sense when the neighbouring teeth are also affected, as these are automatically crowned as part of the treatment anyway, which can help save costs.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Implants: Replacing A Tooth Permanently

bloecke.text: Implants stand out because, unlike other forms of tooth replacement, no other healthy teeth need to be ground down and used as supporting pillars. Instead, a completely new artificial tooth root is anchored in the jaw, to which a crown can then be attached. After successful implantation and healing, dental implants particularly impress with their longevity. Studies from the last 20 years show that around 90% of all implants are still completely intact even 10 years later.

However, the longevity of dental implants also depends on several important factors. Fundamentally, the patient's state of health determines whether implantation is possible. Diabetes, cancer, metabolic disorders, cardiovascular conditions or blood disorders can be risk factors for the successful placement of implants. Regularly taking medication or smoking can also affect how long dental implants last. Studies have shown that dental implants in smokers last only half as long as in non-smokers.

Furthermore, there must be enough space for the implant, as well as dense, stable jawbone. If this is not the case, the bone may need to be built up or reinforced with bone graft material. However, with a thorough initial examination, consultation and planning by our jaw and implantology experts, these risks can be weighed up in advance, so that you can ultimately make the right decision between an implant and a bridge.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bridge Or Implant: A Conclusion

bloecke.text: Weighing up all these advantages and disadvantages, it can be summarised as follows: a dental implant involves higher costs than a bridge, and a solid amount of bone as well as good general health are basic requirements. However, unlike a bridge, an implant offers a reliable tooth replacement for which no healthy tooth substance has to be sacrificed, and which, in the best case, remains firmly anchored in the jaw for life.

A classic bridge offers a cheaper and less involved alternative to an implant, especially when the requirements for a dental implant are not met and the teeth adjacent to the bridge are already crowned. In this case too, a bridge can achieve very good aesthetic and functional results.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: "Implant Or Bridge?" – Advice AT KU64

bloecke.text: If you would like to know whether a bridge or an implant is better suited to you, our jaw and implantology experts are happy to advise you.
Contact us by phone on +49308647320, send us an email, or arrange an appointment directly with us for a detailed personal consultation.

Put simply, a dental implant performs the function of an artificial tooth root and can therefore be used as a particularly durable base for dental prosthetics, such as a bridge or crown. Since the 1980s, titanium has been the standard material used for dental implants.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Implant Material: Well-tolerated AND Long-lasting Titanium Implants

bloecke.text: Before titanium implants became the norm, ceramic implants were commonly used up until the 1980s. Whilst these were known for good tolerability and swift integration, the material properties of ceramic also meant that the implant frequently became brittle very quickly. This short lifespan of ceramic implants has meant that dental implants made from titanium have remained the most popular and reliable implants for years.

Dental implants are made from pure titanium, which, unlike the titanium alloys often used in orthopaedics, does not trigger allergies or foreign body reactions. Titanium implants are also tissue-friendly (“biocompatible”) and, thanks to their slightly rough, natural surface, anchor firmly into the jawbone as though they were part of the body.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental Implant Durability: Lasting Peace of Mind WITH A Titanium Implant

bloecke.text: With a healing success rate of over 95%, the implantology of titanium dental implants represents one of the most reliable dental procedures of all.

Studies from the last 20 years also show that, following successful implantation and the healing phase, around 90% of all implants are still fully functional even 10 years later. Single crowns and conventional bridges, by contrast, have only a 70-80% chance of still being fully intact 10 years after healing. A titanium dental implant therefore represents a worthwhile investment that, with the right care, will stay with you for a lifetime.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Factors AFFECTING THE Durability OF Dental Implants

bloecke.text: How long a dental implant lasts depends not only on the experience of the implantologist but also on the condition of the jawbone. The patient must have good bone quality and a sufficient amount of bone so that the implant in question has enough space and is therefore more resilient. Should the patient not have enough bone volume, a so-called sinus lift can help, among other methods — a surgical procedure in which the floor of the maxillary sinus is thickened.

Following successful implantation and the implant's healing phase, the dental implant, like a natural tooth root, becomes surrounded by a ring of gum tissue, which minimises the risk of later infections. To maintain this condition in the long term, sufficient oral hygiene must, of course, be observed.

Any inflammation of the gums caused by plaque, tartar or bacterial deposits can lead to an infection which, in the worst case, can reach as far as the bone in which the implant is anchored. In addition to your everyday dental care, we therefore recommend having a professional teeth cleaning or preventive treatment carried out by one of our specialists 2-3 times a year.
Other factors, such as smoking, diabetes, radiation during the course of chemotherapy, or taking medications that disrupt bone metabolism, can also affect the longevity of your implant.

If you snore regularly and perhaps also suffer from occasional apnoea, or from sporadic pauses in breathing during the night, a custom-made anti-snoring splint from your dentist – also known as a snoring guard – may be able to help.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Sleep apnoea – what is it?

bloecke.text: Sleep apnoea, also known as sleep apnoea syndrome, is a condition in which pauses in breathing cause the body to be undersupplied with oxygen. This usually triggers a recurring waking response as an alarm signal for the lack of oxygen. However, the patient doesn't necessarily notice this waking directly, as the reaction doesn't lead to full wakefulness. Instead, the body is put into a kind of "working mode", for example through an increased pulse rate. This process leads to a considerable loss of sleep quality. As a result, someone affected by sleep apnoea is very tired and exhausted in the morning or throughout the entire day.

An individually made anti-snoring splint is well suited to counter sleep apnoea, the snoring that almost automatically comes with it, and further health consequences. It helps you enjoy your sleep and your nights once again.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How does an anti-snoring splint work?

bloecke.text: The dental splint is made from transparent plastic and produced entirely individually for each patient. It consists of two parts, one fitted to the upper jaw and the other fitted precisely to the lower jaw. The two parts are connected by two straps attached at the sides in such a way that the lower jaw is forced to sit relatively far forward.

The anti-snoring splint therefore provides a considerable widening of the throat area. The air breathed in can no longer flow in as quickly, and the noise-causing fluttering of the soft tissue in the throat – what's usually perceived as snoring – no longer occurs. Jaw movements are still possible even with the splint in place, which most wearers find very comfortable. However, the anti-snoring splint prevents the lower jaw from sinking back and retracting.
Clinical studies have shown that this relatively simple aid considerably reduces snoring in around 80 per cent of all patients. The risk of apnoea is even reduced by a remarkable 50 per cent.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Benefit from our in-house dental laboratory!

bloecke.text: We, the dental specialists at KU64, naturally want you to feel as little disturbed as possible by the anti-snoring splint while you sleep. That's why we place particular importance on making it as delicate as possible and ensuring a precise fit. Alongside many years of experience, we offer our patients the most modern examination methods and techniques, such as completely pain-free digital 3D X-rays. Any slight tension you may feel in your mouth after wearing the anti-snoring splint disappears quickly. Compared with the dangerous consequences of a pause in breathing, this is, in any case, only a very minor impact on your wellbeing.

If you have any further questions or would like more information on sleep apnoea, snoring and the anti-snoring splint, please get in touch with us. You can send us an e-mail, for example, or call us directly at our practice on the Kurfürstendamm in Berlin: 030 – 864 73 20.

knochenaufbau/sinuslift.titel: Sinus Lift AND Bone Augmentation FOR AN Implant

bloecke.text: For implants to be used successfully and to last a long time, there needs to be a good supply of bone. As a general rule: the stronger the bone, the better the implant will be held in place. If the bone does not meet the necessary requirements, however, various bone augmentation procedures - such as a sinus lift - can be used before the actual implantation to improve the quality of the jawbone or the maxillary sinus. The effort and costs involved can vary drastically from one procedure to another.

Bone loss in the jaw is usually caused by periodontitis, tooth loss, or the high chewing pressure exerted on the sinus floor by a denture. Other factors such as genetic predisposition, general health conditions, medication, age and smoking also influence the extent of bone loss.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Bone Augmentation FOR AN Implant: Requirements

bloecke.text: One of the prerequisites for optimal implant support is having sufficient bone height, and, depending on the implant, sufficient bone width in the jawbone. Reconstructing bone width tends to be less problematic than increasing bone height.

The lower jaw generally has a higher bone density and quality than the upper jaw, which increases the likelihood of implant success. In the upper jaw, however, the sinus cavity often means there isn't enough of the patient's own bone to securely anchor a dental implant. In this case, a so-called sinus lift can help.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: External Sinus Lift & Internal Sinus Lift

bloecke.text: A sinus lift generally refers to the surgical thickening or raising of the sinus floor, and a distinction is made between an external and an internal sinus lift. A sinus lift can only be performed in the upper jaw, where the patient's own bone or a bone substitute material is surgically placed beneath the sinus. This creates a greater bone height, which, after a healing period of around 4 months, provides sufficient support for a dental implant.

The difference between the external and internal sinus lift is that the external sinus lift is the more involved procedure, as it is only used when the existing bone height is very low and several millimetres of bone height need to be gained. This requires the sinus wall to be exposed with the greatest precision and care, so that the bone material can then be placed in the cavity between the mucous membrane and the bone.

An internal sinus lift is a minimally invasive procedure in which access to the sinus floor is gained through the drill channel for the later implant. The advantage here is that no second surgical site needs to be opened. However, this procedure also requires patience and a high degree of precision, particularly as visibility through the drill hole can sometimes be quite limited.

aligner/sos-zahnspangen.titel: SOS Braces – Is Your Brace Broken?

bloecke.text: Arrange an SOS appointment with us straight away so we can refit it. In the meantime, you can try to solve the problem as follows:

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For fixed multiband appliances
a) Bracket or band is loose:

bloecke.text: If the bracket or band (metal ring) has come away from the tooth but is still attached to the wire, leave everything as it is.
If the band (metal ring) has come away from the tooth, try cleaning the tooth with a toothbrush and slide the band back onto the tooth.
If a bracket or band has come away completely and is no longer connected to a wire, try to remove the piece carefully. Please keep it and bring it with you to your next appointment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: b) Wire has come loose or is poking

bloecke.text: Try to fit the wire back into the bracket or band (for example, using tweezers). If it's rubbing, a little wax can be used to cover the area causing irritation.
We strongly advise against using wire cutters or any other tools inside the mouth! Wire ends that spring off could cause soft tissue injuries.

You can try carefully bending or pressing down the end of the wire, for example with your finger or the handle of a spoon. If this isn't possible, protective wax from your orthodontist can help. If you don't have any wax to hand, you can also temporarily cover the area with sugar-free chewing gum.
Arrange an SOS appointment with your orthodontist for a repair!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: c) A fixed appliance in the area of the palate or tongue has come loose

bloecke.text: If a band has come loose, try sliding the band back onto the tooth and arrange an SOS appointment straight away! The appliance shouldn't cause any further irritation after that.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For problems with removable braces

bloecke.text: If the appliance is pressing on or irritating the gum, arrange an SOS appointment with your orthodontist. In the meantime, small sharp edges on the plastic can be smoothed down yourself using a nail file.

If the removable brace or a wire on the brace has broken, please arrange an SOS appointment with your orthodontist. If the appliance still fits and doesn't cause any pressure points when worn, please keep wearing it until your SOS appointment!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: For problems with Invisalign aligners

bloecke.text: Please let your treating dentist know, and they will help you straight away.

If you lose an invisalign® aligner: if you had only just started wearing the new invisalign® aligner, go back to your previous invisalign® aligner if possible and keep wearing that one. If you had already been wearing the invisalign® aligner for a few days, try moving on to your next invisalign® aligner and continue wearing it as prescribed.
If your invisalign® aligner has broken, arrange a check-up appointment straight away and try to keep wearing your broken invisalign® aligner in the meantime. This usually doesn't cause any problems.
Our orthodontists are happy to advise and treat you!

dvt-3d-roentgen/praeimplantationsdiagnos.titel: Patient Information: Preventive Implantation Diagnostics (PID) – FOR an Optimal Implantation

bloecke.text: By diagnostics for individual risk minimisation prior to implantation, we mean the assessment of immunological (inflammatory), osteological (bone-related) and genetic risks that may jeopardise long-term implant success. Modern preventive medicine offers the possibility of identifying at-risk patients through differentiated diagnostics and treating them with individually tailored treatment concepts.
The following factors influence the success of implantological measures:

Bone metabolism If the bone's regenerative capacity is reduced, the healing of an implant is at risk. Bone build-up and breakdown processes can be assessed on the basis of genetic predispositions as well as the current metabolic activity of the bone. For example, in cases of existing or expected osteoporosis, the long-term preservation of the implant is at risk.

Material compatibility Every implant is a foreign material to the body. Although modern implant materials generally show very high biocompatibility, immunological sensitisation reactions (allergies) can occur in individual cases in sensitive patients. Immune reactions against the implant material can lead to local or systemic complaints, up to rejection of the implant. Individual compatibility can be clarified using new, highly sensitive testing procedures.

Immune status/inflammation Implantological measures require an intact immune system. In the case of an immune deficiency, there is a risk that pathogens cannot be fully eliminated by the body. An overactive immune defence, on the other hand, for example in acute or chronic infections, intensifies breakdown processes in the bone via inflammatory mechanisms. The individual immune and inflammatory situation can be reliably determined using laboratory tests.

Periodontitis In cases of periodontitis or gingivitis, the success of the implantation is put at risk by bacterial load and individual susceptibility to inflammation. Targeted elimination of pathogens, following prior characterisation of the bacteria and analysis of the inflammatory disposition, allows for an optimised and targeted treatment strategy (full mouth desinfection).

Due to the risk factors mentioned above, PID is recommended for every patient prior to extensive and costly implant treatment. The changes aimed for with PID are not only sensible with regard to the implantation but also lead to a reduced risk of osteoporosis and coronary heart disease. Modern pre-implantation diagnostics and therapy can therefore contribute to an improved quality of life far beyond the actual restoration of dental function and aesthetics.

Depending on your individual risk factors, we will draw up a treatment concept tailored specifically to you, in order to ensure a successful implantation. For example, the bone's regenerative capacity can be improved with the help of a change in diet or through hormonal or micronutrient preparations. A weakened immune system is regenerated through immune-stimulating therapy, while anti-inflammatory preparations help in cases of increased inflammatory activity (so-called high-responders). Incompatible materials can be ruled out beforehand.

cmd-behandlung/osteopathie.titel: Osteopathy Treatment – AND THE Blockages Are GONE!

bloecke.text: Osteopathy is a holistic, manual therapy used to treat functional disorders and pain, and to release blockages throughout the body. It addresses various structures such as bones, muscles, tendons and organs. Osteopathy is not only practised for acute or chronic conditions, but also has a preventive effect.

Osteopaths know the mechanisms that can counteract misalignment of the teeth. They use manual techniques to help structures with impaired function return to their original movement and to release blockages. Osteopathy is an interdisciplinary approach to treating jaw joint complaints, as it looks at and treats the body as a whole.
Our CMD and orthodontic specialists will be happy to advise you!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: WHAT IS Osteopathy?

bloecke.text: Osteopathy is still a relatively young field of medicine. It was developed over 130 years ago by the American doctor Andrew Taylor Still (1828-1917) and is based on the following idea: “Any change in mobility within the musculoskeletal system, whether hypo- (too little) or hyper- (too much) mobility, leads to a functional disorder, which in turn can trigger a clinical condition.”

The osteopath treats patients, not clinical pictures – gently and without pain: using only their hands, they release blockages in the body and thereby ease discomfort and pain. In practice, osteopathy has proven its worth in many disciplines, including dentistry.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Craniosacral Osteopathy

bloecke.text: This fascinating area of osteopathy deals with the treatment of the complex interplay between the bones and membranes of the skull, and the connective tissue that links directly to the sacrum. The starting point for diagnosis and treatment is the craniosacral rhythm, which, like the heart and breathing rhythms, is an independent rhythm of the body. The osteopath works with this rhythm both in diagnosis and in treating disorders of the body and organs. Osteopathy (craniosacral therapy) is even used with infants and young children, for example with babies who cry excessively or who have skull asymmetries caused by a narrow maternal pelvis during birth, or by a forceps or ventouse delivery. Asymmetries, tension or compression in the skull can place increased strain on the dura mater (the tough protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord), which extends down to the sacrum and coccyx. Conversely, problems in the pelvic area can extend up into the head and cause discomfort there.
Relief or healing through craniosacral osteopathy generally does not come from simply correcting a finding, but from supporting and mobilising the body’s own self-healing powers.

Many people only go to the dentist once they have toothache or notice black spots on their teeth themselves! Most don't know that, as part of preventive care, it's possible to have a caries risk assessment carried out, thereby protecting their teeth from decay and keeping them healthy in the long term. The test is child's play, completely painless, gives reliable warning of decay, and is quick to carry out.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How KU64's risk assessment works

bloecke.text: Our dentists at KU64 simply take a saliva sample from you. Using this sample, our specialists can identify acid-producing bacteria and mutans streptococci (lactobacilli) and give you an assessment of how at risk your teeth are of being affected by harmful bacteria. Your risk is increased if you already have old or defective fillings in your mouth. You are also at higher risk of harmful bacteria if you already have plaque, as this provides a breeding ground for bacteria.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: We at KU64 have the right help on hand for you

bloecke.text: Should the caries risk assessment show that you are at risk, we can offer you the right support to help you avoid elaborate (and costly) procedures. We're happy to give you a few easy-to-follow tips on oral hygiene and diet. Should this not be enough, we also recommend using a tongue scraper as well as an ultrasonic toothbrush to optimise your daily oral care. Both of these care products have shown very good results, particularly when it comes to removing critical and stubborn plaque. Take precautions in good time and prevent the worst from happening.
We at KU64 are very happy to help you with our knowledge and, if you wish, with our products too.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Selective Therapy

bloecke.text: The dye EmunDo works precisely and locally, as it only attaches itself to inflamed areas. At the same time, the staining of the plaque and inflamed areas shows where further laser treatment is needed. EmunDo is activated by the laser and effectively kills all periodontal pathogenic bacteria – and only these.

Treatment with EmunDo is painless, free from side effects and can be repeated at any time. During laser treatment, a local and purely thermal process (caused by heat) takes place with a bactericidal effect. Due to the low power used, there is neither thermal tissue damage nor photothermal removal through burning or evaporation. Nor does the dentine become glazed, as the treatment is carried out at extremely low power and only acts on the bacteria marked with EmunDo.

zahnersatz.titel: Dental Restorations in Berlin: High-Quality Inlays, Crowns, Bridges, Dentures, Implants and Veneers

bloecke.text: Missing, damaged or heavily worn teeth affect not only your smile but also your chewing, speaking and self-confidence. At KU64 in Berlin, you receive high-quality dental restorations – from veneers and inlays to crowns and bridges, right through to dentures and implant-supported solutions – individually planned, aesthetically matched and crafted by master hand in our own dental laboratory. Often on the very same day!

Veneers offer an aesthetically outstanding, tooth-friendly solution for minor defects and discolouration. They are not restorations in the classic sense, but wafer-thin facings that are placed onto the existing front teeth. Our specialist dental technicians create the veneers individually for you, and the dentist bonds them to the tooth surface with a special adhesive. For this, we only need to prepare the teeth minimally. With the innovative Flowable Injection Technique, even this preparation is no longer necessary, allowing us to restore your perfect smile in an even more tooth-friendly way.
All information on veneers

For individual missing teeth, dental bridges are a widely used, cost-effective way to close the gap in the tooth row again. To fit a bridge, your dentist gently prepares the neighbouring teeth on their barely visible surfaces and in the enamel area. A bridge in the front or back teeth can replace missing teeth at any age. Good bridge stability requires a sufficient number of healthy abutment teeth without fillings.
All information on bridges

At KU64, you receive bespoke, high-quality dental restorations – often in just one appointment! Thanks to the advanced CEREC procedure, our dental technicians produce veneers, inlays, fillings, multi-unit bridges and crowns from ceramic in our own laboratory, gently and with a precise fit. Depending on the diagnosis, we can often carry out the entire treatment in just one day.
All information on CEREC

Inlays are suitable for larger defects in a tooth that can still be preserved, meaning a full restoration is not yet necessary. They are robust and long-lasting, and are made individually for each patient by our dental technicians. At our KU64 dental practice in Berlin, we offer inlays made of gold or ceramic.
All information on inlays

When several teeth are missing in the upper or lower jaw, various types of dentures are the standard, cost-effective option for restoring the dental arch. Chewing and speaking function almost as well as with natural teeth, which is not the case with gaps in the teeth. Thanks to modern technology, dentures are now barely distinguishable from natural teeth. They are available as removable or fixed solutions. All dentures at KU64 are made in our own dental laboratory.
All information on dentures

Crowns, used as restorations in the upper and lower jaw, are fitted when a tooth is already badly damaged but its root does not need to be removed. A crown restores the entire visible part of the tooth. To fit the crown, the dentist prepares the natural tooth all the way around, down below the gum line. The crown can then be placed on top. In this way, an artificial crown helps to preserve the patient's natural tooth structure.
All information on crowns

An implant is the highest-quality option for replacing a missing tooth. It is an artificial tooth root that the dentist places into the jaw. Once it has fused with the bone, an artificial tooth can be attached to it. Unlike bridges, there is no need to prepare the healthy neighbouring teeth. Implants are barely distinguishable from natural teeth in function and appearance. With proper preventive care, they can last a lifetime.
All information on implants

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Gaps in your teeth and their consequences

bloecke.text: Gaps in your teeth change more than just the appearance of your smile and face. Many patients only realise in everyday life just how unsettling a missing tooth can be when chewing, speaking or laughing. At the same time, it's understandable if you hesitate to start treatment because of cost, treatment duration or dental anxiety. H3: Risk to general health

Untreated gaps in the teeth can have far-reaching consequences for the entire chewing system and your overall health. If a tooth is missing, neighbouring teeth lose their lateral support and may gradually shift or become loose. The opposing tooth can grow further out because it no longer has natural contact when biting down. This changes the bite, distributes chewing load unevenly, and can put greater strain on the jaw joints and chewing muscles. Speech, chewing function, bone stability and oral hygiene can also suffer as a result. This often leads to teeth grinding and a reduction in jawbone volume over time.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Get expert advice
