abschnitte.ueberschrift: FAQs – Frequently asked questions about dental restorations in Berlin
How long does treatment with a dental restoration take?

bloecke.text: The duration depends on whether you're receiving a crown, bridge, denture or implant-supported restoration. At KU64, individual ceramic restorations can sometimes be planned digitally and even completed on the same day. For more complex restorations, we plan several steps across multiple appointments.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How much does a dental restoration cost?

bloecke.text: The cost of prosthetics varies depending on the number of teeth, the type of restoration and the material chosen. While a crown is relatively inexpensive, bridges and implants tend to be more costly by comparison. Depending on your insurance, this can mean a significant personal contribution. Your dentist at KU64 Berlin will prepare a treatment and cost plan showing the itemised costs before any treatment begins.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Does statutory health insurance cover the cost of dental restorations?

bloecke.text: As a rule, your statutory health insurance provider contributes a fixed subsidy towards the cost of your restoration. This amounts to 60 percent of the actual costs incurred, based on standard care. If you have kept an unbroken bonus record for ten years, the subsidy rises to 75 percent, reducing the patient's personal contribution accordingly. For those on a low income, statutory insurers cover 100 percent of the cost of standard care.
To claim reimbursement, the health insurance provider needs a treatment and cost plan, which your dentist at KU64 will prepare before treatment begins.

With supplementary dental insurance, you can close the coverage gap, topping up your health insurance benefits to up to 100 percent. In some cases, supplementary dental insurance may also cover teeth that are already missing. The exact terms and included benefits depend on the insurance conditions and vary between providers.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What can I do about dental anxiety if I need a restoration?

bloecke.text: Some patients feel uneasy just thinking about dental restorations. But don't worry – we make the whole process as comfortable as possible for you. The dentists at KU64 specialise in treating anxious patients, thanks to relevant further training and our uniquely comforting environment. The oral surgery team at KU64 supports you sensitively before, during and after your treatment.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What is the difference between a crown, a bridge and an implant?

bloecke.text: A crown encases a badly damaged tooth and restores its shape and stability. A bridge replaces one or more missing teeth and is attached to neighbouring teeth or dental implants. An implant replaces the artificial tooth root in the jawbone and can later support a crown, bridge or denture.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are dental implants always the best type of restoration?

bloecke.text: Dental implants can be particularly worthwhile when individual teeth are missing and you want to avoid preparing healthy neighbouring teeth. Especially for larger gaps, implants offer better stability, comfort and security, and with careful care they can last a lifetime. In dentistry, they are therefore considered an aesthetic and long-lasting solution for tooth replacement. This does require sufficient bone volume, or the option to build up the bone beforehand.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I get a dental restoration straight away?

bloecke.text: As a state-of-the-art dental practice, we can plan, produce in our own laboratory and fit a restoration within a single appointment. Depending on the diagnosis, however, it may be necessary to properly prepare the existing teeth and jaw for treatment beforehand. This is because a long-standing gap can cause neighbouring teeth to shift, making the gap smaller. In that case, there may no longer be enough room in the jaw for the restoration. Orthodontic treatment with braces can bring the bite back into its original shape, creating enough space for the restoration. The orthodontists at KU64 are happy to explain the treatment process to you in detail.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I wear braces with a dental restoration?

bloecke.text: Yes. Existing restorations such as crowns or implants are not an obstacle to orthodontic treatment. If your existing restoration is stable and the crowned teeth are healthy, you can wear braces without any concerns.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can I still get a restoration if I'm missing several teeth?

bloecke.text: Yes. If you're missing several teeth, various solutions are available: bridges, dentures, dental implants, or implant-supported restorations such as All-on-4. This can even restore the entire dental arch if no natural teeth remain at all. For larger gaps, we plan especially carefully, so that aesthetics, chewing function, stability and ease of care work well together in the long term.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Can a dental restoration look natural?

bloecke.text: Yes. High-quality restorations can look very natural today. What matters is the material, colour, shape, translucency and the exact match to your remaining teeth. Ceramic restorations in particular can be designed to look especially natural and harmonious.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do I have to choose between aesthetics and function?

bloecke.text: No. Good dentistry combines both: your restoration should look attractive, but it should also sit securely, withstand daily use well and feel natural in everyday life. With dental restorations, it's important to consider not just the visible tooth shape, but also your bite, chewing function, ease of care and longevity.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Is root canal treatment an alternative to a dental restoration?

bloecke.text: We always try to preserve a tooth for as long as possible. If an inflamed or badly damaged tooth can still be saved, root canal treatment is often a way to preserve it. It's only when the tooth is no longer stable enough, or the inflammation cannot be properly controlled, that a restoration such as an implant, bridge or denture becomes necessary.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Do I need a crown after root canal treatment?

bloecke.text: Yes, a tooth that has had root canal treatment is often stabilised with a crown afterwards. After root canal treatment, the tooth is often weakened, especially if a lot of tooth structure has been lost. A crown can protect the tooth, restore its shape and help you chew with confidence again.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What happens if I wait too long to get a dental restoration?

bloecke.text: If gaps in the teeth are left untreated for a long time, neighbouring teeth can tilt, opposing teeth can grow further out, and the bite can change. Chewing, speaking and the jaw joints are also put under strain by the gap. That's why it's a good idea to talk to your dentist at KU64 early on, to work out which solution suits your dental situation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: How do I find out which type of restoration is right for me?

bloecke.text: The best way is through a personal consultation with a thorough examination. During this, we at KU64 check which teeth can be preserved, whether root canal treatment or orthodontic treatment should come first, and which restoration options are available to you. You will then receive a detailed treatment plan setting out the process, alternatives and costs.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Frequently asked questions about aesthetic medicine
What does aesthetic medicine mean?

bloecke.text: Aesthetic medicine encompasses medical treatments that improve or correct outward appearance without requiring surgical intervention. It focuses on gentle, minimally invasive procedures for skin rejuvenation, wrinkle reduction and the harmonisation of facial features.
Typical aesthetic medicine treatments include:
wrinkle treatments to gently smooth facial features
lip enhancement for more volume and contour
laser therapies for skin rejuvenation or the removal of pigment spots and scars.

Unlike plastic surgery, aesthetic medicine does not require surgical procedures, such as rhinoplasty, liposuction or breast augmentation, and enables naturally looking results with short recovery times.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What does aesthetic dermatology mean?

bloecke.text: Aesthetic dermatology is a branch of dermatology concerned with beautifying and rejuvenating the skin. It combines medical skincare with modern, minimally invasive procedures to improve skin texture, colour and elasticity. The focus is on maintaining a healthy and aesthetically pleasing complexion, usually without surgical intervention.
Aesthetic dermatology treatments also make use of procedures such as laser, medical peels, microneedling or PRP (platelet-rich plasma therapy).

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What's the difference between aesthetic medicine and plastic surgery?

bloecke.text: The difference between aesthetic medicine and plastic surgery lies mainly in the procedures used, the invasiveness of the treatments, and the aim of each intervention.
Aesthetic medicine includes non-surgical treatments to improve outward appearance. It aims to reduce wrinkles, optimise contours or improve the complexion.

Plastic surgery involves operative procedures that permanently alter deeper layers of tissue or structures. Typical examples are liposuction, rhinoplasty and breast augmentation. Such procedures can be carried out for both aesthetic and reconstructive reasons, for example following accidents.

Invasive procedures are usually carried out under general anaesthetic in a clinic. Anyone opting for plastic surgery must therefore expect treatment and healing phases that can be considerably longer. As with any operation, you should also thoroughly inform yourself about the risks beforehand and receive comprehensive information from your treating doctor.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: What training does a doctor for aesthetic medicine have?

bloecke.text: There is (as of January 2025) no independent specialist qualification for aesthetic medicine. A doctor for aesthetic medicine generally has basic medical training followed by specialised further training in non-surgical aesthetic procedures.

Unlike plastic surgeons, who complete specialist training in plastic and aesthetic surgery, there is no uniformly regulated training for aesthetic medicine. The basic requirement for aesthetic medicine is a completed degree in human medicine and a licence to practise. Many doctors for aesthetic medicine also have specialist training in dermatology, plastic surgery, oral surgery or other medical fields. To be permitted to offer aesthetic treatments, licensed doctors must also qualify through further training.
All our specialists at KU64 Berlin undergo regular further training and have expertise in their field, so our patients can always rely on treatment and results of the highest quality.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Are aesthetic medical treatments paid for by health insurance?

bloecke.text: Aesthetic medical treatments, as well as plastic surgery, are generally not covered by health insurance, as they are classed as cosmetic procedures and do not serve a medically necessary purpose. You will therefore usually need to cover the costs yourself.
There are, however, exceptions in which statutory or private health insurance covers the cost of an aesthetic treatment. These include:
medically necessary reconstructive treatments following accidents or illnesses
psychological distress documented by a medical report
functional or health-related limitations, for example if drooping eyelids severely restrict field of vision.

Purely cosmetic treatments such as wrinkle reduction, lip augmentation or skin rejuvenation are not covered by statutory health insurance. Some private health insurance tariffs may cover certain treatments. If you have private insurance, ask your insurer under what circumstances they cover particular costs and what data and evidence you need to submit for this.

Interested in an aesthetic facial treatment? At KU64 Berlin, we'll of course provide you in advance with a detailed cost plan containing all the relevant data and information, so you can decide in your own time whether and which treatment you'd like to have.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Which areas is aesthetic medicine suitable for?

bloecke.text: Aesthetic medicine is suitable for various areas of the face and body. It usually focuses on harmonising facial features and correcting small imperfections.
Wrinkle treatments are frequently carried out on the forehead and around the eyes.
In the lip area, volume can be built up or contours accentuated.
Further treatment areas for aesthetic medicine include the neck, décolletage and hands, as well as areas of the body affected by cellulite, pigment spots or skin irregularities.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The Consequences of Misaligned Teeth

bloecke.text: Misaligned teeth and jaws often affect overall health and are frequently the cause of chronic conditions. These include, among others:
Stomach and digestive complaints caused by poor chewing and biting function
Postural problems and resulting back pain
Facial asymmetry
Headaches caused by tension

Protruding teeth are particularly at risk, for example in a fall. Crowded teeth are difficult to clean properly, which can lead to tooth decay, gum disease and other dental problems. A deep bite can damage the periodontal tissue. An incorrect bite function, such as a crossbite, can lead to facial asymmetry and imbalance throughout the whole body. With orthodontic treatment methods such as braces, our orthodontic team in Berlin Charlottenburg helps prevent these conditions from developing.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Straight Teeth: Your Very Own Calling Card

bloecke.text: Beautiful teeth and a healthy set of teeth are everyone's calling card. The first thing people notice is your face, which of course includes your mouth – so why not correct misalignments if you have the chance? Well-cared-for, straight teeth and a lovely smile contribute significantly to a warm and confident appearance and boost self-confidence at any age. With the near-invisible Invisalign® braces in particular, there's no longer any reason to go without a beautiful smile.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: An Orthodontist You Can Trust

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Diagnostic Examination: The Foundation of Successful Treatment

bloecke.text: Diagnosis requires a complete medical and dental history, a clinical examination, dental impressions, special X-rays and photographs. For the best possible treatment outcome, we also examine your overall constitution as well as the interplay between jaw muscles, tongue and breathing. On the basis of the data gathered in this way, the orthodontist or dentist can decide whether orthodontic treatment is advisable in your particular case. If so, our specialists then draw up an individual treatment plan with the right services for the patient.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: When Should You See an Orthodontist?

bloecke.text: Misaligned teeth and jaws can affect your overall health. The dentists at KU64 Berlin recommend orthodontic treatment for:
Overbite – the upper front teeth protrude too far over the lower teeth.
Underbite – here, the lower jaw's teeth sit too far forward, or the upper teeth too far back.
Open bite – there is a gap between the cutting edges of the front teeth and/or the chewing surfaces of the back teeth when the back teeth are brought together.
Asymmetrical midline – when the centre of the upper front teeth does not line up with the centre of the lower front teeth.
Spacing – gaps between the teeth caused by a missing tooth or teeth that do not fill the jaw.
Crowding – when there isn't enough room on the jaw ridge for the teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Braces: Your Near-invisible Companion to a Radiant Smile

bloecke.text: For many years, braces had a poor image. Metal wires fixed firmly to the teeth, glinting whenever you smiled, put many working people off having their teeth straightened. But times have changed: fixed braces are no longer the only way to straighten crooked teeth. These days, children, teenagers and adults can choose from a wide range of braces – fixed or removable, visible or invisible. These appliances gently move the teeth by applying light pressure to the jaw and teeth. They allow the muscles to adjust and influence jaw growth. Depending on the type and severity of the particular misalignment, the orthodontist will determine which treatment promises the greatest success in each case. Our orthodontists in Berlin Charlottenburg are happy to advise you on the advantages, features and costs of the various braces for children, teenagers and adults. By the way, braces – known as snoring splints in this context – can also help as part of snoring therapy.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Multi-bracket Appliances

bloecke.text: The best-known type of orthodontic brace is the multi-bracket appliance (fixed brace), made up of brackets, bands and wires. Bands are attached to the back teeth and serve as anchors for the appliance, while brackets are usually bonded to the front of a tooth. In our practice in Berlin Charlottenburg, we use the DAMON Q+ and Clear systems for orthodontic treatment with fixed braces.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Invisalign®

bloecke.text: Misaligned teeth can also be treated without conventional braces. Invisalign® treatment achieves excellent results for correcting gaps in the front teeth, crooked teeth and a narrow dental arch. Our orthodontists produce two crystal-clear removable splints, known as aligners, for this purpose. Every two weeks, the aligners are exchanged for a new pair, gradually moving the teeth into the desired final position.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Retainers

bloecke.text: Retainers help maintain your new tooth position in the long term after active orthodontic treatment. Retainers come as removable or fixed retention appliances and are worn for the first one to two years after treatment. Whether brackets, Invisalign®, Spark (Ormco) or WIN – the dentists at our orthodontic practice will find out which option from the range of orthodontic treatments is best for you. We also offer composite bonding – what is that? Composite bonding is a minimally invasive tooth-beautification method in which a ceramic-reinforced composite material is applied to the tooth surface. This material is tooth-coloured, durable and precisely shaped to correct gaps, discolouration or minor tooth damage – with no drilling and no pain! The benefits: fast results, a natural look, gentle on the teeth and affordable. A perfect smile in just one session! 🌟

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Veneers & Inlays

bloecke.text: Nowadays, ceramic veneers – so-called VENEERS (ceramic shells) – are used on individual teeth in the front tooth area. A veneer is as wafer-thin as a contact lens and extremely robust! Wherever possible, we also work with hand-layered NON-PREP VENEERS. These preserve your existing tooth structure to the greatest possible extent. They are used for:
Tooth beautification through tooth lengthening, for example in the case of chipped teeth
Small positional corrections of crooked teeth
Balancing out different tooth sizes – for example, in the case of peg teeth
Closing small gaps between teeth
A solution or alternative in cases of receding gums
Discoloured teeth, for example due to congenital or acquired enamel defects, or discolouration caused by medication, and much more

Smaller defects are therefore treated by your dentist in a minimally invasive way, using tiny composite fillings or veneers. We always take care to preserve your existing tooth structure as far as possible. If the defects are larger, or if aesthetic corrections are needed, there are full-ceramic options available:
Composite fillings
Ceramic veneers – VENEERS
Ceramic inlays and full-ceramic dental restorations (partial crowns/crowns) from the specialists in dental aesthetics/tooth beautification at KU64

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Dental Crowns & Bridges for Aesthetic Teeth

bloecke.text: For larger defects or the reconstruction of chewing surfaces in the back teeth, your dentist will use full-ceramic inlays (inlay fillings), full-ceramic partial crowns or crowns.

This type of dental restoration is made in our SMILE DESIGN laboratory from high-quality ceramic to the highest standard, individually layered and painted to match your tooth colour and shape. Your KU64 dentist stays in close contact with your dental technician to achieve the best possible result!
The advantages of ceramic include:
High biocompatibility of the material, meaning it is also ideally suited to patients with allergies or intolerances
Long durability
A colour of your choice, with no discolouration
A chameleon effect, which ensures that the ceramic blends in excellently with your existing tooth colour

For patients who are particularly short of time, or who may only be in Berlin for a single day, the KU64 practice offers the so-called CEREC method for producing ceramic veneers, inlays or partial crowns.

In this process, the prepared tooth is scanned digitally in three dimensions, and the data is transmitted to the milling unit, which then mills the inlay with the utmost precision from a block of ceramic.

Our dental specialists work with high-magnification loupes or microscopes to ensure the most accurate diagnosis and the best possible therapy for you. Our root canal specialists also use a special microscope to precisely analyse and optimally treat every root canal.
At KU64, you receive a guarantee of up to 10 years on high-quality dental restorations such as implants, crowns, bridges, and veneers – significantly longer than legally required.

With high-resolution video simulation, we give you a realistic impression of what your new smile will look like even before treatment begins. Thanks to the innovative Digital Smile Design method, we develop a digital 3D sketch of your future smile based on X-rays and photographs. Whether it's orthodontic correction with INVISALIGN® or high-quality dental restorations – you can see in advance what aesthetic result to expect.

Our entertainment options don't end in the waiting lounge – they accompany you right into the treatment room. Every treatment chair is fitted with a ceiling-mounted monitor, providing a pleasant atmosphere, especially during longer sessions.

You can rely on us for the highest hygiene standards – for your health and a safe treatment. All instruments, turbines, and hand and contra-angle pieces are freshly reprocessed after every treatment, so you are always treated with sterile equipment. Disposable items are disposed of in an environmentally sound and proper manner, so that you can feel fully protected.

In our prophylaxis shops, you can find dentist-tested and recommended preventive care products – tailored to your individual needs. Get advice from our dental care professionals and benefit from lower prices than at the pharmacy. Thanks to short distances, you can take your dental care products with you straight after treatment – without any extra effort.

Our team of dentists, dental nurses, and dental hygienists continually undergo further training and always work in line with the latest developments in dentistry – for the highest quality and the most modern treatment methods. Your contribution to the further-training budget directly benefits you in the form of high-quality treatment.

Thanks to state-of-the-art technology, you receive high-quality dental treatments in the shortest possible time. With the computer-assisted CEREC method, we produce precise, well-fitting dental restorations – in just one appointment, with no long waiting times. You don't have to wait long for a radiantly white smile either: our express teeth whitening delivers visibly brighter teeth in just 90 minutes.
We remove mercury-containing amalgam fillings exclusively using a protective rubber dam, to ensure a safe and gentle treatment.

With us, you receive safe and gentle dental care – thanks to tested, low-allergy, and biocompatible materials. We only use materials that, according to current knowledge, are safe for your health and the environment. So you can be sure: no amalgam, no palladium, no formaldehyde-containing materials – for safe, gentle, and sustainable dental care.
Through interdisciplinary collaboration with highly qualified external colleagues, we ensure that your treatment is considered holistically – for the best possible health and optimal results.

We do everything we can to bring your teeth into perfect condition and to maintain them for a lifetime. With our certified prevention system, you receive highly effective and gentle preventive care that, with consistent use, can prevent over 90 per cent of tooth decay and periodontitis.

Our individual preventive care is precisely tailored to your needs and combines 25 years of experience with the latest Swiss technology. We use the Guided Biofilm Therapy method by EMS, a gentle and effective no-pain prevention method that largely does away with hand instruments, brushes, and polishing paste. An investment that pays off for you in the long run.

Benefit from over 30 years of experience in aesthetic dentistry. Our dentists trained their craft at KU64 on Ku'damm, Berlin's largest and best-known dental practice, and apply their knowledge with the utmost care for you.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: In-house dental laboratory: perfection without detours

bloecke.text: A dental laboratory of your own within the practice? What is the exception elsewhere is standard at KU64. In our exclusive in-house dental laboratories in Berlin-Charlottenburg and Potsdam, we produce bridges, crowns, veneers, and CEREC ceramic inlays to German master craftsmanship standards – precise, individual, and in direct coordination with our dentists and dental technicians. For you, this means shorter waiting times, a perfect fit, and the highest quality.

In our state-of-the-art laboratories, experienced master dental technicians work who can produce and fit numerous dental technical items on the very same day – for fast and excellent results. Benefit from the following advantages:

With us, the master dental technician comes directly to your treatment chair to assess your case in person. Your wishes and ideas are conveyed exactly as intended, so you receive professional suggestions and input directly from dental technology experts. This also reflects our specialist concept: every step of the process is carried out by an expert in their field – for a perfect result.
Thanks to state-of-the-art high-tech machines (CAD/CAM), your new teeth are made with the highest precision – faster than in any laboratory in the Far East, and still at a fair price.
You receive warranty periods of up to 10 years – significantly more than legally required, and a sign of our high standard of quality.
Every dental restoration is a highly individual, custom-made piece produced specifically for you – a perfect fit, aesthetically pleasing, and precisely tailored to your needs.

We produce your dental restorations to German master craftsmanship standards – using a stereo microscope for exact workmanship and perfect attention to detail. This ensures every dental restoration meets the highest functional dental guidelines.
Your high-quality dental restorations are made exclusively by selected top dental technicians and specially trained professionals – no trainees, as is often otherwise the case.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Flexibility without compromise: here for you 7 days a week

bloecke.text: At KU64, you receive first-class dental care – seven days a week. Thanks to our patient-friendly opening hours, we are here for you Monday to Friday from 8am to 8pm, and on weekends and public holidays from 9am to 7pm (except on Christmas holidays, New Year's Day, and Easter).
With an experienced team of numerous dentists, we guarantee you quick appointments and short waiting times, even for complex procedures. Because we know: toothache doesn't stick to opening hours.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Experiencing dental health playfully from the very start

bloecke.text: Your child should feel completely at ease at the dentist too – which is exactly why we have created an environment that inspires trust and curiosity. Exciting play areas with a slide, ball pool, children's cinema, cavity cave, Xbox, and PlayStation, as well as a fascinating mini zoo with Brazilian leafcutter ants and fish, turn a visit to the dentist at KU64 into a positive experience.

From gentle fillings for children and fissure sealants to relaxing nitrous oxide treatments: our experienced team of paediatric dentists, orthodontists, speech therapists, and prevention experts look after your child's dental health with great patience and empathy. In this way, your child playfully loses any fear of the dentist.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Sensitive dentistry for anxious patients

bloecke.text: A visit to the dentist can be a major challenge for many people – at KU64, you are not alone in this. We pay particular attention to our anxious patients.

We take the time to address your fears and carry out every treatment in small, easy-to-follow steps – so you always feel safe. On request, we use gentle sedation methods such as nitrous oxide or medication to help you relax as much as possible. If your anxiety is especially severe, you can even have your treatment under monitored sedation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Aesthetics in perfection – beyond the smile

bloecke.text: At KU64, aesthetics is about more than just beautiful teeth – it's a holistic concept that puts your wellbeing at the centre. Our premium beauty and cosmetic treatments, using the most modern methods, give you a fresh, radiant look – from innovative skin rejuvenation treatments to professional lip and facial treatments or waxing. As with our dentistry, you also benefit here from the highest quality, the latest technologies, and an experienced team of experts who bring out your natural beauty. Because true aesthetics begins where perfection meets individuality.

hilfsprojekt-suedafrika.titel: Westcoast Kids – Volunteering in South Africa for Healthy Teeth in Nursery and Primary School

bloecke.text: In many areas of South Africa, medical care is limited. Most children have acute dental treatment needs. With the aid project “Westcoast Kids”, KU64 Berlin provides support on the ground. Since 2009, a ten-person team has treated around 300 children from the local primary school and nursery in Paternoster on the west coast of South Africa each year, volunteering for a week and a half.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: About the project not far from Cape Town, South Africa

bloecke.text: In 2009, a team led by Dr Stephan Ziegler, consisting of three dentists, four dental assistants and two prophylaxis specialists, travelled for the first time to the small fishing village of Paternoster, 160 kilometres from Cape Town. Their mission: to promote and maintain the oral health of the children there. Since then, the dental team has set up a temporary children's dental surgery every year in the hall of St Augustine Primary School. Their patients are children aged between four and 16. Home visits to parents in pain, as well as visits to the Paternoster nursery “St Christophorus”, are also part of the schedule during their ten-day stays.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The school hall serves as a treatment room

bloecke.text: The treatment room in Paternoster has little in common with the modern dental practice on Berlin's Ku'damm. A reception area with a play and waiting zone is set up in the school hall. The treatment area is equipped with three treatment stations and is separated only by a privacy screen. The noise level is correspondingly high. The washroom next door serves as a prophylaxis room, where the children learn how to brush their teeth.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Challenging working conditions call for improvisation

bloecke.text: For the KU64 team, the working conditions in Paternoster are demanding. The dentists sit on stacked garden chairs. A sun lounger serves as the treatment chair. The treatment light and suction are weak. There is no X-ray machine, nor any drawers in which to store the treatment instruments. A small steriliser cleans the equipment after treatment. Unlike in Berlin, where the dentists document every procedure digitally, in Paternoster reports and important data are recorded by hand on index cards.

Almost all of the practice equipment for the social project comes from Germany and is stored on site until the next visit. At the end of each treatment week, the team draws up an inventory list and counts all the materials that have been used up. This quickly shows what needs to be restocked and brought back from Germany for the projects the following year.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: On dental health in South Africa

bloecke.text: According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), almost every second child in South Africa between the ages of five and 15 requires treatment for tooth decay. However, many people live in poverty in townships, for whom treatment is often too expensive. In addition, in certain areas of South Africa there is only a single district dentist. The options for dental care on the ground are therefore limited for many people. Through its treatments, the KU64 team supports children and families who are not reached by the social projects of the large aid organisations and who, without help, remain trapped long-term in bleak living conditions.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The “Westcoast Kids” aid project in South Africa shows early success

bloecke.text: Around 200 fillings, 120 extractions and countless fissure sealants: the dental team's first visit to Paternoster in 2009 was a real treatment marathon. Due to the limited time on the ground, the team focuses mainly on preserving permanent teeth – only rarely can baby teeth also be treated. Most three-year-old children in Paternoster have already lost all their baby teeth. In some cases, Dr Ziegler's team treated children with up to nine decayed teeth.

A great deal of sensitivity is repeatedly called for when treating the young patients. Many children have had traumatic experiences from previous dental treatments, as in South Africa decayed teeth are usually extracted rather than saved. Added to this is an “intercultural issue”, whereby young girls approaching puberty often have their front teeth removed. In this country at the southern tip of Africa, this is regarded by the population as a sign of female maturity. In the meantime, KU64 Berlin's social project has paid off. A change in thinking has taken place in the region not far from Cape Town. Thanks to projects like this one from KU64 Berlin, more and more people recognise the importance of healthy teeth. This is evident on repeat visits: a remarkable number of fillings from previous years remain intact in the young patients. The risk of tooth decay has also decreased more than expected in almost all of the children.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Three steps to healthy teeth: the content of the “Westcoast Kids” project

bloecke.text: With school starting at eight o'clock in the morning, the treatment day begins for the KU64 team. Children are brought out of lessons in small groups to the temporary dental surgery. While some children draw, craft and play in the “waiting room”, others have brushing lessons scheduled in the prophylaxis area – because effective oral hygiene is the best protection against tooth decay and gum disease in South Africa too.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 1. Prevention: tooth-brushing training for a smile full of confidence

bloecke.text: The dental team invests a great deal of attention and time in tooth-brushing training – a real adventure for the children. Many kids in Africa do not own a toothbrush or do not know how to use one correctly. The trained prophylaxis assistants use a gel to colour the children's teeth in order to make plaque visible. The pupils then learn the correct brushing technique using a fabric crocodile. Together with the dental assistants, they explore their own mouths as thoroughly as possible with a toothbrush and learn how to reach even the difficult spots when brushing. The aim is to actively motivate the children to brush their teeth daily, giving them a good foundation for their future oral hygiene. Tips for a healthy diet are also part of the education provided.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 2. Education: prophylaxis presentations deepen understanding

bloecke.text: To sustainably strengthen the children's motivation for regular oral hygiene, additional prophylaxis talks are held. For these, the dentists bring well-known stars such as Shakira onto the screen. In their presentations, they show the singer with and without teeth. This helps the children understand that dental care plays a major role in academic success, later choice of partner, and self-confidence – and thus their future. Local dental hygienist Karen Paulse translates the presentation by KU64 dentists Dr Stephan Ziegler and Juliane Kottenhagen into Afrikaans, as children in the small coastal town only begin learning English from the second grade.

“Help people to help themselves” is KU64 Berlin's motto. That is why the dentists also offer dental training for local teachers and childcare workers as part of their projects. This way, once the dental team has left, they can answer children's questions and impress upon them the importance of proper dental care.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: 3. Preserving teeth: removing decay and strengthening teeth

bloecke.text: After the prophylaxis training, the day continues in the treatment room. Fillings are placed and the teeth are fluoridated to make them more resistant to decay. Decayed teeth are only extracted in rare cases. In their work, the team places great importance on carrying out treatments as gently and carefully as possible in order to help the children overcome their fear of the dentist. Providing patience and comfort is also part of the volunteer dentists' role. To treat as many patients as possible, the dental team works for as long as the school is open, usually from 8am to 4pm. There are no fixed breaks; instead, power cuts lasting several hours a day cause unplanned interruptions to the volunteer work.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The project partners: working hand in hand for healthy teeth

bloecke.text: Numerous partners have supported KU64 Berlin dental practice for many years in its mission in the coastal town near Cape Town. The work on the ground takes place as part of the Laureate Foundation's “Westcoast Kids” project and in collaboration with the charitable association BIG SMILE e.V.

From 21 January to 1 February 2012, KU64 dentists treated pupils in South Africa on a voluntary basis for the third time: smiling faces, healthy teeth and happy children were the best reward for the new dentists and prophylaxis assistants from the KU64 dental practice on Berlin's Ku'damm.

In the small, lively fishing village of Paternoster, around 160 kilometres from Cape Town in South Africa, lives 7-year-old Naobi, a cheerful pupil. She gets good marks at school, has lots of friends and wants to become a doctor one day. But the truth is that Naobi would have tooth decay and no front teeth left were it not for BIG SMILE e.V., a charitable association that looks after the dental health of disadvantaged children worldwide.

Since 2009, BIG SMILE e.V. has been sending a ten-person team from the partner dental practice KU64 in Berlin to South Africa to examine the teeth of around 200 to 300 children within a week. “We have been able to demonstrate remarkable success over the past years,” says Dr Ziegler, owner of the KU64 dental practice in Berlin, who personally travels along every year to give something back from his own success.

“Big Smile e.V. doesn't just aim for short-term dental health success; its top priority is the long-term impact of projects and aid,” explains Boschmann, project manager at BIG SMILE e.V. “The association is grateful for any kind of help: whether it's a donation, an idea for how the association can help in future, or spreading the vision of creating a world free of tooth decay,” Boschmann enthuses, looking forward to the seventh charity trip in January 2017. Naobi will also be there again, proudly showing off her teeth, which wouldn't be the same without BIG SMILE e.V.
In order to finance a further modern mobile dental unit in a suitcase format, KU64 staff are launching a South Africa flea market from their own belongings.

Under the motto “Shopping for a good cause”, KU64 staff sell their own treasured items, such as Aunt Uschi's old porcelain cup. In return, visitors can give Gemenicio in Paternoster a smile with their purchase.

For the sixth time, as part of the WESTCOAST KIDS aid project, ten members of staff from the KU64 dental practice will treat around 200 primary school children from 18 to 25 January in Paternoster, 160 kilometres from Cape Town.

The project is supported by the charitable BIG SMILE e.V. foundation as well as the charitable Laureate Foundation. A large number of partners from the dental sector have supported the venture with generous donations in kind, including Smile Design Dentallabor, Voco GmbH and Henry Schein Dentaldepot. The Swiss company CURADEN/CUPRAPROX provided the prophylaxis materials (children's toothpaste and toothbrushes) for the primary school children. Non-medical companies such as Villas La Baleine also support the project, providing KU64 with three houses in which the team is accommodated.
The results of the KU64 aid project in South Africa: 7 days, 100 children, 50 adults, 200 fillings, 120 extractions and many beaming, smiling faces.

The KU64 team is sharing the many memories from this time with everyone interested as part of a large exhibition – featuring wonderful photos by Andreas Schwarz and the kind support of Fotostudio Urbschat.
The pictures can be purchased for a good cause in exchange for a donation from 30 euros. All proceeds go towards the South Africa project.

Right in the heart of Kurfürstendamm, KU64 has created a world beyond the classic dental practice: a place that offers more than functionality and an exceptionally aesthetic design. Behind KU64 lies a spatial concept that builds trust, takes away fear and conveys a sense of security. Inspired by nature and open space, KU64 has been welcoming patients since 2005 in a dental spa that set new standards across Germany. Often copied, yet never matched, KU64 remains the original to this day. An architectural statement by the GRAFT trio of architects for a new generation of dental practices – human, bold and unmistakable.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Like a holiday for the senses: a practice design that helps you relax

bloecke.text: In the middle of Berlin's Kurfürstendamm, KU64 welcomes its visitors in surroundings with an almost otherworldly touch: a sunny, sandy dune landscape stretches across two floors and 2,700 square metres, filled with warm light, the scent of freshly brewed coffee and relaxed lounge music. Transparent surfaces open up unusual perspectives, while floor and ceiling form wave-like shapes into a dynamic sculptural space. The environment feels organic and expansive, carried by amorphous imagery, acoustic accents and a thoughtful lighting concept that connects spaces fluidly with one another.

The design consistently follows the idea of "Zahnarzt on the Beach": summer, sand, water and openness form the creative foundation of a concept that deliberately breaks with convention. Instead of classic treatment rooms, an aesthetic environment emerges that feels more like a stylish wellness resort than a dental practice. And anyone enjoying a cappuccino in the deckchairs on the sun terrace, above the rooftops of Kurfürstendamm, won't be surprised when, in the evening, a fireplace brings a touch of romance to the dental practice's waiting lounge.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The vision

bloecke.text: Anyone who steps into KU64 quickly notices: this practice follows a different idea. The vision behind it is as clear as it is extraordinary – a dental practice that people don't visit only when something hurts, but a place where people are happy to come and happy to stay.

"I wanted to create spaces that calm rather than deter – open, welcoming and free of the classic sense of distance. Not sterile functionality, but an environment that allows trust to develop." – Dr Stephan Ziegler

Dr Ziegler found this particular understanding of space and atmosphere in the Design Hotel Q! – one of the first major projects by the internationally renowned architecture firm GRAFT. Convinced by the formal language, the lighting concept and the clear, emotional aesthetic, his vision of an entirely new type of dental practice began to take shape. Just a few months later, construction work began at KU64 – with GRAFT as the architectural partner at his side.
The result was a practice that only reveals itself as such on second glance, and at first glance simply feels like a place where people feel at ease.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Arrive, feel at ease, come back

bloecke.text: Today, the vision has become lived reality: patients visit KU64 regularly and with a good feeling. Waiting times are not seen as a burden, but as a welcome pause in everyday life.
Even dentists from other practices refer their anxious patients to KU64 and see that treatment becomes possible where uncertainty once prevailed.

Children, too, love coming to KU64 – so much so that some parents struggle to get them to leave after their appointment. This turns the dental visit into a little outing that many families are happy to make time for.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Environmental Healing

bloecke.text: "Architecture can be more than beautiful. Buildings and interiors can relieve fear and even support healing processes. This is called Healing Architecture," says Thomas Willemeit of GRAFT – the architects behind KU64. The design of the practice on Kurfürstendamm follows this same principle: spaces that calm, colours that radiate warmth, lighting concepts that provide orientation.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Architecture as part of treatment

bloecke.text: As far back as the 1980s, studies in American hospitals found that a pleasant environment can influence the healing process. At the time, many children's hospitals began decorating walls with oversized graffiti, setting up small play areas and painting rooms in individual, colourful designs. They found that this was not only well received but that children recovered more quickly. This eased the burden on children, parents and the American healthcare system alike.

The Technical University of Berlin also studies the effect of architecture in medical facilities and how it can influence the healing process (Healing Architecture). Do patients recover more quickly when atmosphere and building design are right? What influence do shapes, light, plants, scents or colours have? Scientists agree that the environment also has a positive effect on the healing process. Around a thousand studies exist worldwide on this topic. They show that patients who recover in a pleasant hospital environment need fewer medications, for example. Their blood pressure also drops, their heart rate decreases, and they experience less stress.

A further Healing Architecture study conducted in Danish intensive care units demonstrated that architecture and design in hospitals influence both positive and negative processes and behaviour among patients, relatives and staff.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The minds behind the vision

bloecke.text: The award-winning design of KU64 unmistakably bears the signature of GRAFT. Founded in 1998 by Wolfram Putz, Lars Krückeberg and Thomas Willemeit, the firm, with offices in Berlin, Los Angeles and Beijing, has long been among the internationally influential names in contemporary architecture. Known for visionary spatial concepts, an emotional architectural language and the courage to combine unusual materials and colours, GRAFT creates spaces that go far beyond classic functionality. At KU64 too, form, atmosphere and experience come together into a design concept that sets new standards – entirely in keeping with the GRAFT philosophy.

The firm, working across architecture, urban planning, exhibition design, music and the "pursuit of happiness", also gained international attention through its collaboration with Brad Pitt and the Make It Right Foundation he founded, for which they designed sustainable homes in New Orleans following the devastation of Hurricane Katrina.
For the innovative spatial concept of KU64, GRAFT was honoured with the Archip Award 2008 (1st Prize, Public Interior/Innovation category).
Notable GRAFT projects:
Design Hotel Q! in Berlin: With its wave-like lines and freestanding bathtubs, Hotel Q! is considered one of the "50 coolest hotels of the World" (Condé Nast Traveller).

Stack Restaurant & Bar, Mirage Hotel Las Vegas: For the Stack restaurant and bar, the GRAFT architects designed organically shaped wooden installations reminiscent of the canyons of the Grand Canyon, giving the space a futuristic, nature-inspired atmosphere.

Intensive care unit at Charité Berlin: For the intensive care unit of Berlin's Charité hospital, GRAFT created a spatial concept specifically designed for emotional impact and to support healing – an example of architectural "Environmental Healing".

abschnitte.ueberschrift: A building with history – KU64 on Kurfürstendamm

bloecke.text: In the 1950s, a thriving fashion industry and great interest in fashion and design developed in West Berlin. The first fashion shows and major fashion houses followed. The ECO-Haus is built at Kurfürstendamm 64/65 – a modern commercial building that becomes home to numerous Berlin clothing manufacturers. Over 1,000 employees work here.

Haute couture moves out, cinema moves in: the "Hollywood" cinema opens in the ECO-Haus. At the opening, the usherettes appear in elegant costumes, presenting themselves and the building as a unified whole – what we would today call corporate design. Unusual for the time was the fact that visitors could watch the projectionist at work through a large window. The interior design, too, was anything but ordinary: audiences could follow the performance from romantic double seats fitted with a small table. The walls of the cinema hall bore the emblems of famous film studios.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Early 1990s

bloecke.text: After an extensive renovation, the cinema gets a new look. The foyer is redesigned in the style of a French café, with decorative ceiling elements and light-filled details – a place between cinematic art and architecture.

The "Hollywood" stands empty. Berlin dentist Dr Stephan Ziegler recognises the building's potential – and develops the vision of a practice in which specialists from different fields work together under one roof. The idea: a dental practice that combines design and function in a new way.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Summer 2005

bloecke.text: The upper two floors are brought back to life: KU64 – Die Zahnspezialisten open their practice in extraordinary surroundings. The name is a deliberate nod to the history of the place and marks the beginning of a new chapter on Kurfürstendamm.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The support and aid projects of the dental specialists at KU64

bloecke.text: Year after year, the dental specialists at KU64 support a number of charitable projects (social responsibility projects) in Berlin, in Germany and abroad. These projects are not conceived as one-off support and aid actions, but as long-term undertakings. If you would like to support us, please see the note at the end of this page!
Our South Africa Project

One of our most important projects is the treatment of an entire school in Paternoster, South Africa, every January. The project WESTCOAST KIDS (www.westcoastkids.co.za) was initiated by our patient and LAUREATE foundation director Simone Jacke, in cooperation with the charitable association BIG SMILE E.V. (Internationales Institut für Kariesprophylaxe e.V.) from Hamburg and the dental specialists at KU64. “Sustainability is indeed a declared aim of the project,” says dentist and KU64 owner Dr Stephan Ziegler. “After all, we want to make a valuable contribution to the lasting dental health of children in, for example, South Africa.” Accordingly, tooth preservation and prevention take top priority in our treatments. And so the children are also taught proper toothbrushing – because, even at this end of the world, effective oral hygiene is the best protection against tooth decay and gum disease.
More information about our South Africa project.
A big thank you to our partners

It goes without saying that an undertaking of this kind is only possible with the help of strong partners: numerous partners from the dental sector have supported KU64's commitment with generous donations in kind, including Henry Schein Dentaldepot, MIP GmbH, Smile Design Dentallabor, Voco GmbH, the companies 3M Espe, Curaprox, Onedroponly, Camlog, MIP, multi-com.biz and Resorba, as well as Ivoclar Vivadent GmbH. But non-medical companies are also among the supporters of the initiative, such as Handelsplan AG, or Strandloper Sea Villas, who sponsored the 3 houses in which the KU64 team was accommodated for the entire duration of the treatment.
We would also like to thank our donors, large and small, as every contribution benefits the children. Special thanks go to our generous donor RSD REISE SERVICE DEUTSCHLAND GMBH.
A selection of KU64 aid projects

Beyond our commitment in South Africa, the KU64 dental specialists also support children's aid projects at a local level, for example for the Arche and the Laughing Hearts initiative, as well as for the children's and youth departments of numerous children's sports clubs.

bloecke.text: Effective cleaning for removable dentures and much more!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: The innovative ultrasonic cleaner for brilliantly clean results

bloecke.text: Discover the latest treasure for the optimal cleaning of your removable dentures, splints, sports guards and much more – the brand-new ultrasonic cleaner, now available exclusively at KU64 in Potsdam! With our unbeatable RRP of just €99, you can now effortlessly ensure a spotless and thorough clean.

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Superior cleaning technology for your dentures

bloecke.text: The ultrasonic cleaner uses advanced technology to remove even stubborn deposits and impurities that have built up on your removable dentures over time. The ultrasonic waves create tiny yet powerful vibrations in the water, cleaning thoroughly even in hard-to-reach areas. Say goodbye to annoying residue and smile with renewed confidence!

abschnitte.ueberschrift: Versatility for various applications

bloecke.text: Our ultrasonic cleaner is suitable not only for dentures but is also ideal for cleaning splints, sports guards and other removable dental products. Whether you're a sportsman or sportswoman, wear an orthodontic splint, or simply use removable dentures – this cleaner is the perfect solution for hygienic cleanliness.

abschnitte.ueberschrief: Ultrasonic Cleaner – Simple and safe to use

bloecke.text: Operating the ultrasonic cleaner couldn't be simpler. Just fill the tank with water and place your denture or splint into the device. Switch on the ultrasonic cleaner and let the technology do its work. In no time at all, you'll get a brilliantly clean result. The cleaner has been designed with a particular focus on safety, so you needn't worry – your dental products are in good hands.
